items.title: Embodied AI Fails the Mirror Test: How a Simple Mirror Breaks Robot Policies
items.summary: Can a simple mirror expose the limitations of today's robotic manipulation policies? Inspired by the mirror self-recognition test in animal cognition, we investigate whether robot policies can reliably manipulate physical objects in scenes containing their reflections. items.abstract: Can a simple mirror expose the limitations of today's robotic manipulation policies? Inspired by the mirror self-recognition test in animal cognition, we investigate whether robot policies can reliably manipulate physical objects in scenes containing their reflections. We introduce RoboDojo-Mirror, a benchmark built on RoboDojo that preserves task objectives, success criteria, and policy checkpoints while comparing a mirror-free baseline with single-mirror, dual-mirror, and mirrored-tabletop conditions. Across five policies spanning Vision-Language-Action models, World Action Models, and agentic policies, every mirror condition reduces aggregate success rates: averaged over the three conditions, the drop ranges from 10.8 to 56.7 percentage points across policies, and it reaches 62.5 points on the mirrored tabletop. Because a mirror is also a physical obstacle, we compare it against geometrically matched non-reflective panels; 50--88\% of mirror-specific failures occur without recorded robot--panel contact, so direct collisions alone do not explain the degradation. Trajectory and contact analyses instead reveal recurring behaviors consistent with phantom targeting of reflected objects and spatial mislocalization of real ones. Targeted diagnostics further characterize grasping near reflections, policy-dependent pushing progress, and physical-target interaction under main-camera occlusion. Real-robot experiments with π_{0.5} and FastWAM also show lower overall success rates under the upright-mirror and mirrored-tabletop conditions. These findings reveal a shared vulnerability to reflective environments across diverse robot policies and motivate reflection-aware evaluation of embodied intelligence. Code is available at https://github.com/iPPLab/robodojo-mirror.

items.abstract: Models read a book, an hour of video, or an image in one forward pass. As the context grows, this pass slows down, loses accuracy, and stops at the context window. Sparse attention is efficient, but keeps the other two limitations. Grid probing, a recent training-free method, recovers the accuracy and extends the reach by asking a frozen model the same question about short local and strided spans of the input, but every question repeats the whole computation, since each span is encoded again. Our insight is that grid probing is emulated attention, an attention pattern reproduced from outside the model through prompts, since each probe only restricts which part of the input the question can see. We introduce Factorized Context Attention (FCA), a training-free block-sparse attention that runs the same pattern natively, as the attention of the model itself. FCA encodes the input once into a KV cache, reads all spans as masked sequences in one batched forward, and uses a stair position schedule to keep every span inside the trained position range. Across long video understanding, long-context text inference and image grounding, FCA matches the accuracy and the reach of grid probing at a fraction of its cost. It gains about 10 points over the single pass on long video and 9 to 14 points on long novels, finds needles in videos of over a thousand frames and in texts four times the length of the window, and answers a later question about the same input in as little as a tenth of the time of grid probing. Native attention thus keeps what emulated attention gains without its cost, all with existing frozen language and vision-language models.

items.title: VenusOCR2.0: Towards Efficient and Effective Document Parsing

To continuously improve recognition quality without self-training collapse, we build a bounded recursive self-improvement (RSI) data engine where the model acts strictly as a weakness probe, while external multi-expert medoid consensus, VLM…
items.abstract: We present VenusOCR2.0, a compact 1B-parameter vision-language recognizer designed for both high-accuracy and high-throughput document parsing across text, tables, and formulas. To continuously improve recognition quality without self-training collapse, we build a bounded recursive self-improvement (RSI) data engine where the model acts strictly as a weakness probe, while external multi-expert medoid consensus, VLM visual verification, and factorized synthesis supply reliable supervision across pretraining, curated SFT, and RLVR. VenusOCR2.0 couples a dynamic-resolution SigLIP2 encoder and 2x2 spatial token merging with a Qwen3-0.6B decoder, adopting compact atomic OTSL tokens to shorten table sequences and reduce structural errors. To further eliminate the autoregressive decoding bottleneck, we introduce PTPv2, a lightweight (sim67M) decoupled parallel draft module that combines frozen multi-layer verifier conditioning, a standalone learned mask, and block-causal all-position next-token prediction. On OmniDocBenchv1.6, VenusOCR2.0 achieves an overall score of 96.45 and a state-of-the-art 98.57 formula CDM, substantially outperforming massive general-purpose VLMs such as Gemini-3-Pro (92.91) and Qwen3-VL-235B (89.78). Deployed in vLLM on a single H20 GPU, PTPv2 delivers a 2.96x single-request speedup and up to 2.36x higher batched throughput while guaranteeing lossless, token-for-token equivalence with standard autoregressive decoding.

items.title: Reinforcing Diffusion Models by Instantaneous Trajectory Distribution Matching
items.summary: Forward diffusion reinforcement learning (RL)---enabling deterministic ODE sampling without trajectory backpropagation---has grown increasingly popular for efficiently aligning diffusion models. items.abstract: Forward diffusion reinforcement learning (RL)---enabling deterministic ODE sampling without trajectory backpropagation---has grown increasingly popular for efficiently aligning diffusion models. However, we reveal that existing methods essentially rely on signed reward-weighted regression (RWR), regressing the trainable policy velocity onto rollouts from a behavior distribution. Unbiased baseline subtraction implicitly assumes that the policy velocity equals the behavior marginal velocity---an idealized assumption violated under classifier-free guidance (CFG) rollouts, offline/off-policy updates, and imperfect online self-consistency. This behavior--policy mismatch breaks baseline invariance and injects baseline-induced gradient drift, destabilizing training. To resolve this issue, we propose Instantaneous Trajectory Distribution Matching (iTDM), taking the infinitesimal limit of Trajectory Distribution Matching toward a time-local reward-guided target via the posterior-score identity to yield a sample-level gradient anchored at the behavior velocity without learning an additional reward-tilted target score. Tracking this velocity with an online auxiliary denoiser guarantees exact baseline invariance at the auxiliary optimum, effectively suppressing baseline drift across both online and offline RL. Extensive experiments across compositional generation, text rendering, and preference alignment show that iTDM achieves state-of-the-art in-domain and out-of-domain performance across group-wise online/offline RL and pairwise offline RL. Notably, on the challenging GenEval2 benchmark, iTDM converges nearly 3\times faster than competing methods while scaling smoothly to 0.87 without collapse. Furthermore, iTDM scales effectively to the 5.6B FLUX.3 model, achieving better performance across both in-domain and unseen metrics. Code is available at https://github.com/Luo-Yihong/iTDM

items.abstract: People reason with pictures as well as words. Interleaved multimodal reasoning gives models a similar way to solve problems by creating intermediate images and using them to guide further reasoning. Training models with this ability usually relies on task-specific demonstrations, which are difficult to collect. We introduce ThinkMorph-SSL, a two-stage training recipe that uses images themselves as a source of supervision. The first stage, pretext reasoning, converts visual pretext tasks, such as image colorization and denoising, into instruction-free interleaved traces. Models describe a corrupted or transformed image, generate a restored or canonical image, and interpret the result. The second stage uses automatically constructed demonstrations for question-driven instruction tuning. At the same instruction-tuning budget, models trained with pretext reasoning outperform those trained with instruction tuning alone. The full recipe improves over the base model by an average of 11.33 accuracy points across twelve benchmarks. These results show that supervision derived from images can build the visual skills needed for interleaved reasoning and improve learning from task-specific demonstrations.

We introduce Qwen-Image-HD, which adapts Qwen-Image 2.0 to high-resolution synthesis through local training and blockwise autoregressive generation. Each prediction covers a target tile at 1K scale, conditioned on high-resolution upper and left neighbors and a compressed historical thumbnail. These conditions provide adjacent fine-scale structures and an overview of the scene generated so far. To integrate these complementary cues, we map both forms of history and the target to a shared canvas coordinate system to express their spatial relationships and scale differences. On Qwen-Image-Bench at 4K, Qwen-Image-HD achieves stronger overall evaluation performance than direct 4K generation with FLUX-3-Image-Klein. Compared with full-image 4K supervised fine-tuning of the same backbone, it achieves better generation quality with lower training compute and higher inference efficiency, while exhibiting fewer unnatural repetitive stripes in original-resolution comparisons. We further introduce a Wavefront-AutoRegressive inference schedule that generates tiles on the same anti-diagonal concurrently across GPUs to reduce single-image latency.

items.abstract: Real-time interactive video generation allows users to change the prompt during generation to steer the evolving video. However, existing streaming models, which generate videos chunk by chunk, often keep following the previous prompt after a switch. We trace this failure to context inertia, where the previous chunk acts as a strong prior that suppresses the new prompt. Furthermore, we find that this inertia persists even when the cache retains only the previous chunk, yet discarding the context breaks visual continuity, which limits approaches that edit the cache. Rather than editing the cache, we propose Residual Guidance (RG), a simple, training-free method that counteracts context inertia with a correction measured outside the cache. Specifically, RG denoises the re-noised previous chunk once under the new prompt without the cache and adds the resulting residual to the early denoising steps of the next chunk, where its content is largely decided and the new prompt is most suppressed. Across settings ranging from a single switch to long multi-switch generation, RG substantially improves prompt switching capability on existing streaming models, including those with dedicated switching mechanisms, while largely retaining visual quality. As it requires no training or per-model tuning and adds only one forward pass per chunk, RG can be easily integrated into existing real-time video generation pipelines.

items.abstract: While text-driven body motion generation has matured, pure-hand synthesis remains bottlenecked by data. Existing datasets often treat hands as rigid end-effectors, lack fine-grained captions, or are too limited in scale to support robust generalization. We introduce RoMo Hands, an in-the-wild, text-paired dataset of ~542K sequences (884 hours, 95.5M frames at 30 fps) which is an order of magnitude larger than prior work. To ensure high-quality supervision, a stringent dexterity filter discards low-articulation sequences, focusing the distribution on complex bimanual movement. Each clip is paired with five captions at increasing granularities from global semantic tags to atomic finger states, organized under a hierarchical taxonomy. To bridge the gap between body and hand architectures, we propose a novel 393-D bimanual representation that adapts redundant body-motion paradigms to the high-DoF kinematics of hands. Systematic benchmarking of diffusion, masked-token, and autoregressive generators reveals distinct trade-offs under these hand-specific adaptations, including a sharp divergence between semantic alignment and kinematic plausibility. Our dataset, representation, and benchmark establish a rigorous foundation for the next generation of dexterous motion synthesis. Project page: https://romodataset.github.io/romo-hands/.

items.abstract: Multi-reference image generation requires a model to preserve the appearance of selected subjects while arranging them according to an instruction. Despite recent progress in reference-based generation and compositional control, reliably organizing selected subjects into the intended scene remains challenging. Although existing methods provide various forms of compositional guidance, the planned relationships are not always explicitly instantiated for inspection and refinement before image synthesis. To address this limitation, we introduce MAGPIE, which represents the intended composition as a simplified 3D scene defined by an executable Blender program. A coding agent links each scene instance to its reference, checks the geometry and rendered view against the instruction, and revises the program to correct discrepancies. The final proxy rendering serves as a visual plan for the image generator. Using MAGPIE-Instruct-3K, we train the generator to follow this plan while drawing each subject's appearance from its reference. MAGPIE improves both Qwen and FLUX on DreamOmni2 and SconeEval. With FLUX, it improves overall success on DreamOmni2 by 28.21 percentage points over the original backbone and achieves the highest overall score among the models evaluated on SconeEval.

items.abstract: Games, especially modern AAA games, challenge language models to perceive complex scenes, control actions, and make decisions over long horizons. Existing game benchmarks primarily test language models as computer-use agents that query a language model throughout play, incurring repeated inference cost and, in real-time games, acting while the environment continues to evolve. We ask whether coding agents can learn from game interaction to develop standalone game-playing programs that run without language model inference. We thus introduce Coding4Games, a benchmark for evaluating whether coding agents can develop standalone programs that play modern games through visual observations and standard game inputs. Coding4Games has three defining features: 1) Diverse Modern Games, covering 15 games with diverse visual, strategic, and control demands; 2) Development-Test Separation, in which a coding agent uses a sandbox and the standard player interface to iteratively develop a program, after which the selected program is frozen and independently tested without language-model inference; and 3) Outcome and Process Evaluation, which measures not only game performance and reliability but also how agents use feedback, revise programs, and resolve problems during development. Across 15 games, the best program per game outscores the strongest GUI baseline on 13 and ties it on one. The human player outscores all agents on 10 games. We additionally examine the effects of development budgets. Coding4Games evaluates whether coding agents can turn their understanding of complex interactive environments into programs that work reliably on their own.

items.summary: We propose LoopDVR, a framework for converting pretrained Transformer-based dense visual recognition models into parameter-efficient looped networks. Rather than reducing the network width or depth directly, LoopDVR reuses Transformer blocks across layers in both the ViT backbone and Transformer decoder, reducing the number of parameters while retaining the original computational structure. items.abstract: We propose LoopDVR, a framework for converting pretrained Transformer-based dense visual recognition models into parameter-efficient looped networks. Rather than reducing the network width or depth directly, LoopDVR reuses Transformer blocks across layers in both the ViT backbone and Transformer decoder, reducing the number of parameters while retaining the original computational structure. However, naively sharing parameters can disrupt the distinct transformations learned at different depths. To address this challenge, we identify suitable sharing groups based on inter-layer representation dissimilarity and keep the final backbone block independent for multi-scale feature construction. We then initialize each shared backbone block with the pretrained weights of its group's terminal layer to better preserve the learned representations. An independent Loop Adapter at each layer further helps retain depth-specific transformations within shared blocks. Subsequently, we distill visual representations into the looped backbone and integrate it with a looped decoder for task-specific training. Experiments demonstrate that LoopDVR achieves the best accuracy--parameter trade-offs across dense recognition tasks. Compared with the reference models, it reduces parameters by approximately 28% while maintaining competitive accuracy. Notably, LoopDet-S achieves 50.9 box AP with only 7.0M parameters, highlighting its effectiveness in compact models.

items.title: PartAgent: Agentic 3D Part Segmentation via Expert Integration and Closed-Loop Refinement
items.summary: Segmenting a 3D object into semantically meaningful parts requires joint reasoning about geometric structure and semantic context. Pretrained 3D experts provide spatially grounded region proposals, while 2D experts provide semantic cues for identifying object parts. The challenge is to integrate these complementary capabilities into a framework that can both produce meaningful part segmentations and progressively…
items.abstract: Segmenting a 3D object into semantically meaningful parts requires joint reasoning about geometric structure and semantic context. Pretrained 3D experts provide spatially grounded region proposals, while 2D experts provide semantic cues for identifying object parts. The challenge is to integrate these complementary capabilities into a framework that can both produce meaningful part segmentations and progressively refine them. We present PartAgent, a training-free agentic framework for 3D part segmentation built upon two complementary modules: (i) Structural-Semantic Expert Integration combines regions predicted by the 3D expert with multiview semantic evidence from the 2D expert through image-to-surface correspondences, constructing compositional part partitions at multiple granularities. (ii) Observation-Driven Closed-Loop Partition Refinement observes the current partition and its supporting evidence to select targeted inspection, evidence repair, composition, or reselection actions. It verifies proposed changes and uses the updated state and action outcomes to guide subsequent decisions. On PartObjaverse-Tiny-WT, PartAgent achieves 68.41 mIoU, outperforming the strongest competing method by 8.53 points. Across 3DCoMPaT200, PartNeXt, PartNetE, and PartObjaverse-Tiny, PartAgent achieves the highest mIoU on each dataset, averaging 69.36 across the four datasets, 7.28 points above the highest mean among competing methods.

items.abstract: Spatial reasoning in hospitals requires tracking look-alike equipment, interpreting patient-relative directions, and judging passage widths, yet existing benchmarks provide limited coverage of these abilities. We introduce Clinical3D-Bench, a simulated benchmark with 3,368 questions of eight types on egocentric walkthroughs of 373 hospital-room layouts. Layouts follow hospital design guidelines, answers are computed from the 3D scenes, and paired scene states test whether models change their answers when relevant evidence changes. Videos are photorealistic, and ten physicians screened the layouts. Among 35 multimodal large language models (MLLMs), the best open and proprietary models reach 45.7% and 53.6% macro accuracy, against 40.8% for an answer prior and 79.0% for physicians on a subset, and 27 of 32 open models score below 40% on two-way patient-relative directions. Fine-tuning on Clinical3D-45K, our 44,750-question training set, lifts two MLLMs 16-20 points above the best proprietary model. 3D maps given to the fine-tuned MLLM as input go largely unused: replacing them with another video's, even when they are ground truth, barely changes its accuracy. The proposed GeoJeV instead lets the MLLM compute with 3D: it reconstructs a scene memory from each video, selects 3D operations and their arguments from the MLLM's question state, and adds their evidence to its option scores. It achieves the highest accuracy of all evaluated models, narrowing the gap to physicians.

items.abstract: A single electroencephalographic (EEG) recording can support multiple decoding tasks. Fixed-label tests cannot show how EEG foundation models handle changing questions or options. We introduce EEGJev, a fast decision model that scores candidate answers in one pass. Our benchmark, EEGJev-Bench, covers six question types across 19 public EEG sources. We held the recording and options fixed while switching between questions about attributes paired during training, such as facial expression and the hand participants were asked to use. Across 13 test sources, EEGJev selected a label for the requested attribute with 99.70% accuracy (49.20% under uniform choice). Balanced accuracy for the specific answer was 62.04%. Its 95th-percentile response time was shorter than NeuroLM's on matched validation questions answered individually. EEGJev lets users switch decoding targets by changing the question. With EEGJev-Bench, researchers can test whether new decoders follow the question more reliably, identify the correct answer more often, or both.

items.summary: Inferring gene regulation from single-cell data is difficult because observational measurements cannot distinguish correlation from causation and access to perturbational data, especially with multiple modalities, remains limited. items.abstract: Inferring gene regulation from single-cell data is difficult because observational measurements cannot distinguish correlation from causation and access to perturbational data, especially with multiple modalities, remains limited. Here we present the Cross-Modal Causal Variational Autoencoder (CMC-VAE), which learns a network linking genes and proteins (gene-gene, protein-protein and gene-protein) in the latent space and maps each connection back onto measured features. Trained on 809,130 observational CITE-seq profiles, CMC-VAE recovers co-expression, transcription factor regulons and immune signalling programs, and learns a sparse cross-modal map enriched for transcript-protein cognate pairs. On three CRISPR screens used during development, it ranks knockout-responsive genes better than correlation and latent-VAE baselines. Fitted to a screen's unperturbed control cells, without perturbation labels, the model translates measured knockout RNA responses into protein responses better than a correlation map and cognate transcripts. The direction of gene-to-gene regulation, however, is not recovered from observational data. On the CITE-seq screens, fine-tuning only the latent network improves held-out response correlation, mainly by learning a response shared across knockouts. On larger Perturb-seq screens, with about 1,000 training perturbations, fine-tuning the latent network learns gene-specific effects that transfer to held-out genes, more so than a gene-level causal model fine-tuned on the same cells, and in simulation, such interventions also restore edge orientations that observational training leaves unresolved.

items.abstract: Progenitor-exhausted CD8+ T cells (Tex-prog) are essential for sustaining T-cell-mediated immunity during chronic infection and cancer and therefore offer a promising immunotherapy target. Synthetic cis-regulatory elements (CREs) could enable selective transgene expression in Tex-prog cells, but whether they can distinguish this population from closely related CD8+ T-cell exhaustion states remains unclear. Here, we integrated publicly available paired single-cell ATAC-seq and single-cell RNA-seq datasets from mouse infection and tumor models and identified an ATAC-defined Tex-prog-like population (C1). We used the CREsted framework to fine-tune a pretrained Borzoi model to predict chromatin accessibility across C1 and ten comparator populations. We then used CREsted to design candidate synthetic CREs with predicted preferential accessibility in C1. The fine-tuned model achieved an average precision of 0.242 for identifying C1-selective regions on chromosomes held out from fine-tuning, approximately tenfold higher than the random-ranking baseline. Sequence optimization generated 196 1,000-bp designs with at least twofold higher predicted accessibility in C1 relative to the strongest competing population across eight DNA backgrounds. Motif enrichment and sequence-attribution analyses identified sequence patterns associated with AP-1, NFAT, POU, EGR, and TCF/LEF transcription factor families. Together, these findings identify candidate synthetic CREs with predicted preferential accessibility in a Tex-prog-like CD8+ T-cell population and provide a foundation for future experimental evaluation of their functional enhancer activity and cell-state specificity.

items.abstract: Deep learning methods that predict spatial transcriptomics from histology offer scalable molecular profiling of clinical cohorts. However, conventional correlation metrics overstate prediction quality across whole sections by crediting models for recognizing broad tissue regions, and understate fine-scale prediction quality because sampling noise dominates sparse RNA counts. To resolve this, we introduce the reproducible-signal correlation (RSC) metric. RSC randomly splits RNA counts into two halves to separate reproducible signal from sampling noise across spatial scales and within tissue regions or cell classes. Across 12 spot-level and three single-cell methods, RSC revealed that most models capture broad tissue patterns but largely miss differences between neighboring spots or cells, which whole-section correlation overlooks. Within malignant cells, RSC distinguished methods that genuinely capture part of the cell-to-cell heterogeneity from those whose scores across all cells were inflated by cell-type composition. Guided by RSC, we designed a pairwise difference loss between neighboring spots that improved fine-scale predictions on average across 11 models. RSC thus provides a foundation for benchmarking predictions, guiding model design and determining which spatial analyses histology can support.

items.abstract: Abstract Influenza A virus (IAV) remains a serious global public health threat. Andrographolide, the predominant bioactive component of Andrographis paniculata, exerts broad-spectrum antiviral effects. Nevertheless, the molecular targets and mechanisms underlying its anti-IAV activity remain unclear. This study intended to identify the key functional target of andrographolide and elucidate its immune regulatory mechanism against IAV infection. Bulk transcriptome sequencing, protein interaction network analysis and multiple machine learning methods were integrated to screen key functional genes regulated by andrographolide during IAV infection. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations were used to verify the binding affinity between andrographolide and the hub gene, while single-cell transcriptomic analysis and virtual gene knockout assays were performed to explore cell-specific functional mechanisms. TLR3 was screened and confirmed as the core hub gene, and andrographolide could stably bind to TLR3. Single-cell results showed that TLR3 was specifically enriched in pulmonary NK cells of IAV-infected tissues; virtual TLR3 knockout significantly altered the transcriptional profiles of NK cells related to antiviral defense, cytotoxicity and cytokine signaling, confirming the critical regulatory function of TLR3. This transcriptomic analysis study verifies TLR3 as a direct functional target of andrographolide and identifies a novel NK cell-dependent immune axis, which provides a new mechanistic insight into the immunomodulatory and anti-influenza activity of andrographolide.

items.abstract: Abstract Background Matrix stiffness, a hallmark of the tumor microenvironment, plays a critical role in breast cancer progression by regulating cancer-associated fibroblasts activation and immune remodeling. However, large-scale clinical evidence linking matrix stiffness-related molecular features to CAF heterogeneity, prognosis, and therapeutic response remains scarce. Methods Matrix stiffness-related genes were compiled from MSigDB, literature mining, and a pan-cancer signature. Differentially expressed genes between tumor and normal tissues were intersected with Matrix stiffness-related genes, and univariate Cox regression was used to identify prognostic genes. Consensus clustering was performed to define molecular subtypes. Single-cell RNA-seq (GSE176078) was used to identify stiffness-associated CAF subtypes. Bulk transcriptomic (TCGA-BRCA, GSE96058), and machine learning analyses were integrated to construct a prognostic signature. Immune infiltration and drug response were evaluated. Results A total of 1,695 MSRGs were compiled, finally yielding 40 prognostic genes. Two molecular subtypes were identified: Cluster 1 exhibited enriched ECM remodeling and mechanotransduction pathways, whereas Cluster 2 showed an inflamed, stroma-rich immune microenvironment with elevated immune checkpoint expression and superior survival. Single-cell analysis revealed that CAFs had the highest matrix stiffness scores, with myCAFs as the dominant contributor, driving ECM-related crosstalk with epithelial and endothelial cells. Among 101 machine learning models, the Elastic Net (α = 0.5) signature was optimal, stratifying patients into high- and low-risk groups with distinct survival outcomes (P < 0.0001). The high-risk group was characterized by activated proliferation and metabolic pathways, an immunosuppressive microenvironment with reduced immune infiltration and downregulated immune checkpoints, and broad-spectrum multi-drug resistance. Conclusions This study establishes a matrix stiffness-related prognostic signature and, through single-cell analysis, localizes matrix stiffness to myCAFs. The signature stratifies patients into distinct risk groups with different prognosis, immune microenvironments, and drug responses, providing a rationale for targeting myCAF-mediated matrix stiffness and related pathways in high-risk patients.

items.abstract: Plant regulatory logic emerges from the interaction of cis-regulatory elements, chromatin state, transcription factors, cell identity, and microenvironmental context. This review synthesizes how single-cell and single-nucleus genomics, spatial omics, deep learning, and perturbation frameworks are converging to resolve that logic in plants. We discuss chromatin-first and sequence-informed strategies for discovering candidate cis-regulatory elements, compare major approaches for inferring single-cell gene regulatory networks, and evaluate the promise and limitations of interpretable deep learning and foundation models in data-limited plant systems. We then examine how spatial biology reconnects regulatory inference to tissue geometry, signaling context, and microenvironmental structure, and how perturbation platforms, reporter assays, CRISPRa/i, and programmable promoter engineering can be used to functionally test regulatory predictions. Together, these developments support a transition from descriptive atlases toward iterative design-test-learn frameworks in which candidate elements, networks, and perturbations can be prioritized, validated, and refined across molecular, cellular, and tissue scales.

items.abstract: Persistent subacute neuroinflammation limits tissue repair after spinal cord injury (SCI), yet how macrophage state heterogeneity is organized within lesion-centered inflammatory niches remains unclear. We integrated time-resolved mouse single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics with trajectory analysis, regulatory network inference, ligand activity analysis, exploratory in silico Spp1 perturbation, and interpretable machine learning, followed by tissue-level and donor-recipient validation. Time-resolved profiling revealed early neutrophil and monocyte recruitment, subsequent macrophage accumulation, and delayed microglial activation. Macrophage subclustering resolved seven injury-responsive states comprising inflammatory, transitional, tissue-associated, lipid-associated, SPP1-associated, repair-associated, and homeostatic programs. Among these states, SPP1_Mac expanded prominently, peaked at 7 days post-injury, and retained marked inflammatory activity. Spatial mapping localized the SPP1_Mac signature and focal Spp1 expression to lesion-centered regions within a broader Cd44-enriched cellular territory. Regulatory network, ligand activity, communication, and machine learning analyses prioritized SPP1-associated signaling within this state-niche organization. Injured spinal cords showed increased lesion-associated SPP1 and CD44 expression and enrichment of SPP1 within IBA1-positive myeloid regions. In a BV2-to-RAW264.7 donor-recipient system, donor cell Spp1 silencing attenuated recipient cell CD44 and CD86 expression, the proportion of F4/80⁺CD86⁺ cells, and IL-1β and TNF-α secretion following conditioned medium transfer. Together, these findings support a state-niche-communication framework in which SPP1_Mac represents a prominent cellular feature associated with lesion-centered inflammatory persistence during subacute SCI, providing a biological foundation for further stage-informed investigation of the post-SCI inflammatory microenvironment.

items.abstract: Abstract Low-dose CT (LDCT) reconstruction is a critical problem in radiology that has a significant impact on public health. With the rise of deep learning, especially in generative models, we have seen a diverse range of methods for reconstructing LDCT images. However, existing LDCT reconstruction methods are often evaluated under inconsistent experimental settings, including different dataset splits, preprocessing pipelines, and noise-generation procedures, hindering fair comparisons across approaches. In addition, many studies do not explicitly assess 1 generalization across diverse datasets with different acquisition characteristics, limiting the practical relevance of the reported results. Therefore, we present a comprehensive fair study of modern generative models for LDCT reconstructions. Beyond effectiveness on a single dataset, our main goal is to assess the models’ generalization across datasets. Moreover, we propose a new semantic segmentation-based metric, in addition to traditional image quality metrics, to evaluate the effectiveness of the reconstructed images in a medical task. Our results show that diffusion-based models with a small number of iterations out-perform UNet and GAN, especially on out-of-distribution datasets. However, there are still challenges that require further study regarding effectiveness and efficiency.

items.abstract: Abstract Alzheimer’s is one of the most common type of dementia that affects old-age people. It occurs due to the the damage of brain cells in a patient. This damage affects the capability of brain cells to communicate with each other effectively. Since Alzheimer’s is a progressive disease, various other medical conditions may arise over time. There are several research studies that suggest severe concerns in regards to the disease prevalence in the US population. A careful consideration in the context of these studies asserts that it would affect more than 14 million people by the year 2060 in the US region. Therefore it is critically important to diagnose Alzheimer’s at early stages to save the patient's life. In recent era, it is a very problematic task for the researcher to diagnose the disease before it becomes fatal. Many recent works have explored the use of deep learning model for diagnosis of Alzheimer stages but most of the state-of-the-art deep learning models are computationally expensive and suffer from over-fitting and vanishing gradient problem. Also, some of techniques are weak in accurately diagnosing the early stages and utilize imbalance dataset and small dataset.while existing models require high computational resources yet they do not work well with all datasets .The study proposes a lightweight deep learning model for accurate multistage Alzheimer diagnosis. This study we propose a light weight Xception Attention Network(XAtten-Net) model with only 1.2 million parameters which uses separable convolutions instead of standard convolution to reduce the parameter count. The proposed model consists of two datasets i.e. Oasis and Kaggle.The first dataset acheived 95\% accuracy, 96\% recall, 92\% precison and 0.99 F1-Score on the OASIS dataset, while Kaggle attained 91.63\% accuracy, 91.63\% recall, 87\% precision and 0.98 F1-score.

items.abstract: BackgroundIn the context of the growing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into radiology, AI-assisted systems are increasingly presented as tools for improving diagnostic accuracy, workflow efficiency, and clinical decision-making. Yet discussions of AI in radiology often focus on technical performance or clinician perspectives, while patients' attitudes toward these technologies remain less well understood.ObjectiveThis study aimed to cross-culturally adapt the Artificial Intelligence Attitude in Radiology Scale (AIARS) for patients into Turkish and evaluate the psychometric properties of the modified Turkish version among patients receiving radiology services.MethodsThis cross-sectional validation study included 659 adult patients aged 18-69 years ( M ag e = 34.50, SD = 11.21). The factor structure was examined using exploratory factor analysis (EFA) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA). Measurement invariance was tested across age groups, gender, and educational level using multi-group CFA.ResultsEFA supported a modified four-factor, 23-item structure derived from the original 39-item, five-factor AIARS. CFA confirmed that the four-factor model was a good fit for the data, χ 2 (224) = 640.16, p < .001, CFI = .985, TLI = .983, RMSEA = .075, 90% CI [.068, .082], SRMR = .072. The total scale demonstrated high internal consistency, with α = .87 and ω = .88. Test-retest reliability was excellent (total-scale ICC = .97, 95% CI [.94, .99]). Measurement invariance was supported across age, gender, and educational level.ConclusionThe modified Turkish version of the AIARS demonstrated acceptable psychometric performance at the total-scale level and may be used to assess patients' attitudes toward AI in radiology. However, the Worries and Ethical Concerns factor requires further evaluation.

items.abstract: Objectives Effective application of artificial intelligence (AI) in musculoskeletal (MSK) radiology depends on targeting unmet clinical needs rather than technical feasibility. This Society of Skeletal Radiology (SSR) position statement identifies and prioritizes the most impactful AI applications and value propositions for MSK radiologists. Methods The SSR AI Committee (n = 18) used structured brainstorming to compile lists of AI-based applications and value propositions. After deduplication, standardization, and categorization using a 12-component MSK radiology value cycle, refined lists were distributed as electronic surveys to 122 SSR committee members; 103 (84.4%) and 102 (83.6%) completed the applications and value propositions surveys, respectively, scoring each item on a 5-point Likert scale. Top 10 lists were generated from summed scores. Results Brainstorming generated 208 AI application and 126 value proposition ideas, condensed to 138 and 56 unique items, respectively. Fourteen AI applications and 13 value propositions shared the top 10 ranks (tied scores). Top-ranked AI applications were within dictation and reporting (5 items), archiving and presentation (2), diagnostic imaging (1), follow-up imaging (2), quality/safety (2), and protocoling (2). Top-ranked value propositions were within dictation and reporting (4), diagnostic imaging (3), ordering (3), protocoling (2), and quality/safety (1). The highest-ranked application was AI-assisted comparison study retrieval (mean 3.17/4.0) and the highest-ranked value proposition was increased reporting efficiency (mean 3.30/4.0). Conclusions This position statement provides a demand-driven roadmap for AI development in MSK radiology. Workflow and reporting tools were prioritized over disease detection algorithms, highlighting a gap between clinical needs and current commercial AI offerings.

items.abstract: Purpose of review Prostate-specific antigen (PSA) screening reduces prostate cancer (PCa) mortality but is limited by poor specificity, unnecessary biopsies, and overdiagnosis. This review summarizes current evidence for blood-, urine-, and genetics-based biomarkers that refine risk prediction before magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) or biopsy. Recent findings Blood-based biomarkers (Prostate Health Index, 4Kscore, Stockholm3 (incorporating SNP-based genomic risk), and IsoPSA) and urine biomarkers (PCA3, MyProstateScore, SelectMDx, and ExoDx) generally improve risk stratification for clinically significant PCa (csPCa) compared with PSA alone and reduce unnecessary biopsies in men with elevated PSA, while missing 1-13% of csPCa. Stockholm3 has randomized screening-trial validation; 4Kscore has been evaluated as a post-PSA reflex test within screening trials; and ExoDx has randomized evidence in the diagnostic setting. The polygenic risk score, an investigational PSA-independent screening strategy, has shown promising results and is currently being evaluated in the ongoing TRANSFORM trial. Further emerging biomarkers, including PSA glycoforms, proteomic profiles, DNA methylation, cell-free DNA fragmentomics, microRNAs, mRNA profiling (PROSTest), and metabolomic profiles (volatile organic compounds), remain investigational. Summary A new generation of molecular biomarkers holds promise to reshape PCa early detection by complementing PSA with individualized risk assessment. Clinical implementation requires prospective comparative studies, validation in diverse populations, cost-effectiveness analyses, and machine learning algorithms combining biomarkers, imaging, and clinical data.

items.abstract: Abstract Background: Applications of deep learning models in neuroimaging have significantly advanced translational neuroscience, offering substantial benefits to human health. However, recent cybersecurity threats have undermined the reliability of digital neuroscience tools, posing challenges to the clinical neuroscience community. A critical issue is the automated semantic segmentation of malignant or premalignant brain tumors, essential for neurosurgery and radiotherapy planning. New methods: This study investigates the robustness of customary deep learning models such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and more recent Vision Transformers (ViTs) in semantic segmentation against adversarial attacks. We assess the performance of CNNs and ViTs under ideal nonhostile conditions and then under cybersecurity threats. Results: Our findings reveal that while CNNs perform well in ideal conditions, their efficiency sharply declines under adversarial perturbations. In contrast, ViTs maintain their segmentation performance even when subjected to adversarial attacks. This study is the first to apply Visual Transformers for cybersecurity challenge, leveraging advanced capabilities of VITs to enhance robustness against digital perturbations. Comparison with existing methods: Compared to CNNs, which are widely used for neuroimages but vulnerable to adversarial attacks, ViTs demonstrate superior resilience. Our research highlights that ViTs are as effective as CNNs under ideal conditions but offer enhanced protection from cybersecurity angle, making them a more robust choice for neuroimaging applications. Conclusion: Our results indicate that for large-scale segmentation operation in neuroimaging, such as lesion segmentation tasks, ViT-based models should be preferred over CNN-based models. This shift could provide inherent protection against prevalent digital threats, ensuring more reliable and secure neuroimaging diagnostics.

items.abstract: In-depth, scalable structural interpretation of tandem mass spectra from diverse biological tissues and environmental samples is essential for understanding the molecular diversity of cellular environments and the metabolic architecture of living systems. Although community-driven resources such as GNPS and MassIVE have aggregated massive volumes of tandem mass spectra spanning a wide range of organisms, clinical cohorts and environmental surveys, modeling and interpreting this exponentially expanding spectral corpus to distill molecular information and derive meaningful biological insights poses a fundamental challenge for established computational methods. Here we present UltraMS, a dual-polarity foundation model tailored to decipher the molecular language latent in tandem mass spectra through large-scale pretraining on more than 160 million spectra encompassing both positive and negative ion modes. Our findings illustrate that UltraMS is capable of effectively decoding the chemical semantics of molecules underlying mass spectra via self-supervised learning, achieving superior performance across a variety of downstream tasks, including elemental detection, molecular identification, molecular property profiling, and metabolic landscape characterization. Remarkably, UltraMS enables conducting molecular identification with fine-grained spectral interpretability, simultaneously elucidating molecular structures from untargeted MS/MS spectra and providing peak-by-peak substructural attributions via annotation transfer. Deployed on a clinical cohort of human plaque samples, UltraMS demonstrates significant potential in discovering previously unrecognized phenotype-linked metabolites supported by structurally grounded fragment-ion formation pathways, while effectively correcting likely misannotated clinical markers. Furthermore, building on the structure-aware spectral representations learned by UltraMS, we construct UltraAtlas, a chemical-property-resolved map that organizes millions of experimental spectra into a unified coordinate system, enabling millisecond-scale molecular profiling and offering practical guidance for exploratory navigation across vast chemical space. Applied to human scalp metabolomics, UltraAtlas effectively captures distinct metabolic variations across individuals, highlighting phenotype-specific chemical signatures while shedding light on the chemical niches of the resident microbiome. Together, UltraMS and UltraAtlas constitute a generalizable framework for structural elucidation and biological discovery from tandem mass spectra, empowering the comprehensive exploration of the largely undeciphered metabolomes across different domains of life.

items.abstract: IMPORTANCE Monitoring hemoglobin oxygen saturation is a cornerstone of patient care across a wide range of clinical settings, with pulse oximetry remaining one of the most widely used technologies. Recent studies have identified skin pigmentation-related inaccuracies in these measurements; however, the biological and optical mechanisms underlying these limitations remain incompletely understood. OBJECTIVE To investigate the tissue compartments and wavelengths that drive skin pigmentation-related bias in oximetry using depth-resolved optoacoustic (OA) imaging. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS Prospective observational imaging study of n=46 healthy volunteers representing all 6 Fitzpatrick skin types (FST). EXPOSURES OA imaging of the tibialis anterior region during physiological oxygenation challenges induced by vascular occlusion, reperfusion, and exercise. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES A total of 3016 spatially resolved scans were obtained. Tissue compartments were segmented using a pretrained neural network. OA spectra, oxygen saturation estimates, responses to physiological interventions, and associations with skin pigmentation were evaluated across 41 wavelengths from 700 to 1100 nm. RESULTS Skin OA spectra closely mirrored the optical absorption characteristics of melanin, and OA signal intensities were strongly associated with FST, demonstrating a substantial influence of pigmentation on superficial oximetry measurements. Epidermal oxygen saturation estimates exhibited minimal changes during physiological interventions, especially in darkly pigmented skin. Skin signals showed pronounced associations with melanin-sensitive wavelengths, enabling FST classification based on optoacoustic skin signals. Pigmentation-related bias was greatest at shorter wavelengths and progressively decreased at longer wavelengths. In contrast, oxygenation measurements obtained from skeletal muscle were less affected by skin type and showed the strongest responses to vascular occlusion, reperfusion, and exercise. Depth-resolved OA imaging demonstrated that physiologically meaningful oxygenation information emerged only after propagation beyond the avascular epidermis into deeper vascularized tissue compartments. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE The combination of appropriate anatomical targeting, optimized wavelength selection, and correction for optical attenuation may represent a promising strategy for mitigating skin-pigmentation-related bias in oximetry.

items.abstract: Background: Ataxia-telangiectasia (A-T) is a rare, childhood-onset neurodegenerative disorder for which sensitive, age-appropriate motor outcome measures are needed to support emerging clinical trials. Clinician-rated ataxia scales are limited by subjectivity, low granularity, and floor and ceiling effects. We evaluated whether at-home wearable accelerometry, combined with machine-learned composite scores derived from submovement features, captures cross-sectional motor impairment and longitudinal disease progression in A-T. Methods: 43 children with classic A-T (median age 9.0 years; IQR 5.7-13.4) and 50 age- and sex-matched controls wore GENEActiv accelerometers on the ankle and wrist during one week of natural behavior at home, repeated at 6- to 12-month intervals. From 85 submovement, activity-intensity, and spectral features per sensor site, we trained composite severity models targeting the Brief Ataxia Rating Scale (BARS) gait subscore (ankle) and BARS total score (wrist). Findings: Ankle composite scores correlated strongly with BARS gait (r = 0.88), BARS total (r = 0.88), and caregiver-reported CPCHILD (r = -0.69); wrist composite scores correlated with BARS total (r = 0.88), BARS arm (r = 0.84), and CPCHILD (r = -0.78). Both models discriminated A-T from controls with large effect sizes (ankle Cohen's d = 2.28; wrist d = 2.98) and demonstrated excellent within-week reliability (ICC = 0.95 ankle; 0.92 wrist). The ankle composite captured disease progression sensitively (Mean-to-Standard Deviation Ratio [MSDR] = 0.98; p < 0.0001). In a matched subset with both sensor and clinical data, ankle composite slopes significantly captured progression (Wilcoxon vs zero, p = 0.0036), whereas BARS total (p = 0.079) and BARS gait (p = 0.30) did not. Interpretation: At-home ankle-based wearable accelerometry provides a sensitive, interpretable, and ecologically valid measure of motor function and disease progression in A-T and may serve as a candidate outcome measure for clinical trials.

items.abstract: Background: The physician global assessment (PhGA) is a core outcome measure in juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) but is incompletely captured, even in clinical registries. We developed a large language model (LLM) approach that extracts explicitly documented PhGA from clinical narratives and infers a score where none is recorded. To our knowledge, this is the first study to address both tasks. Methods: We linked charts from 306 children with JIA at one center to the Childhood Arthritis and Rheumatology Research Alliance (CARRA) Registry (2016-2024). A structured prompt was developed on 100 randomly sampled charts, then evaluated on 400 charts from patients not represented in the development set. Extraction used GPT-5.2 within a HIPAA-compliant Azure environment. Registry-recorded PhGA served as the reference standard, with discordances adjudicated by a pediatric rheumatologist blinded to both sources. Agreement was assessed by intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC(2,1)), exact match, and mean absolute error (MAE). Results: Against registry values, ICC(2,1) was 0.87 (95% CI 0.85-0.89; n=400), with 70.5% exact agreement and MAE 0.363. Agreement was near-perfect for explicit extractions (n=190; ICC 0.99; 95% CI 0.98-0.99) and lower for inferred scores (n=210; ICC 0.72; 95% CI 0.64-0.78). Large discordances (≥2 points) occurred in 7.3% of cases. Against the adjudicated standard, overall ICC(2,1) was 0.96 (95% CI 0.95-0.97), with 77.5% exact agreement and MAE 0.200. All 14 explicit discordances reflected mismatch between the registry and the clinical note, rather than extraction errors (adjudicated ICC 1.00). For inferred scores, ICC rose to 0.90 (95% CI 0.87-0.92). Residual disagreement was concentrated at the inactive/minimally active boundary. Conclusion: An LLM can reliably extract PhGA from clinical notes with high accuracy to support downstream clinical research, offering a scalable approach to mitigating missingness in patient registries.

items.abstract: Ovarian morphology on ultrasonography is commonly used in the assessment of female reproductive health, such as in the diagnostic evaluation of polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) and monitoring of response to assisted reproduction. Standard morphological markers quantified on pelvic ultrasound are ovarian volume (OV) and measures of antral follicle count (AFC) such as follicle number per slice or per ovary (FNPS, FNPO). Manual assessment of these features is operator-dependent, which limits the reliability of these measurements, impacting the delivery of consistent care. To address this, we have developed Ovarify , the first deep learning workflow to automatically characterize ovarian morphology from pelvic ultrasonography across multiple clinical contexts. Ovarify was trained on transvaginal ultrasonographic volumes garnered across three centers and evaluated on a held-out internal test set in addition to three external datasets spanning heterogeneity in image collection protocols, scanner hardware, and populations, across both single frames as well as whole-volumes. Ovarify segmented the ovary and follicles with high fidelity, outperforming U-Net and ResNet-34 baselines (p<0.001). Morphological measurements agreed closely with validated image analysis protocols on an internal test set (OV: Pearson r=0.892, FNPS: r=0.667, FNPO: r=0.770); across external datasets, workflow performance was similar. Ovarify additionally retained performance when evaluated on unseen images of ovaries undergoing controlled ovarian stimulation (FNPS: Pearson r=0.813). Ovarify -derived measurements classified polycystic ovarian morphology with an AUPRC of 0.90 (F1=0.93) using FNPO and 0.80 using OV. Ultimately, Ovarify provides a reproducible, operator-independent characterization of ovarian morphology directly from routinely-acquired pelvic ultrasonograms, generalizing across scanners, acquisition formats, and clinically-distinct imaging contexts. Ovarify automates the assessment of clinically-relevant morphological markers, allowing for the unbiased and consistent evaluation of morphological features.

items.abstract: Abstract Distinguishing Alzheimer's disease (AD) and frontotemporal dementia (FTD) from healthy controls (HC) and from each other, remains challenging due to overlapping symptoms. Electroencephalography (EEG) provides a cost-effective view of neurodegeneration, yet conventional methods often overlook temporal and frequency-specific changes in brain connectivity. We propose a temporal multi-band graph-based framework for classifying AD and FTD from resting-state EEG while identifying informative frequency bands and disease-relevant brain regions. EEG data from 88 subjects were analyzed, with temporal graphs constructed using Granger causality, retaining connections above the 95th percentile. Nodes were represented by 18 statistical, spectral, and information-theoretic features, and the proposed graph neural network architecture employed GraphSAGE for spatial feature extraction and Bidirectional LSTM with temporal attention to capture connectivity dynamics. To integrate frequency-specific information, a multi-band attention layer fused alpha and beta bands. Model performance was evaluated using subject-level stratified 5-fold cross-validation repeated 10 times. The model achieved \((F_1)\)-scores of \((0.8891 \pm 0.0224)\) for HC vs.\FTD, \((0.8646 \pm 0.0172)\) for HC vs.\AD, and \((0.8057 \pm 0.0193)\) for FTD vs.\AD. Lobe-wise analysis identified the temporal lobe as the most discriminative region, nearly matching whole-brain performance. It also aligned well with established clinical evidence, whereas XAI methods showed weaker clinical alignment. These findings show that integrating spatiotemporal and spectral dynamics can support accurate dementia classification and provide neurobiological insight. Lobe-wise analysis further suggested that FTD is more regionally focused, whereas AD shows a more widespread pattern, while current graph-based XAI methods may require further refinement for reliable clinical interpretation.

items.abstract: Abstract Breast cancer remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related morbidity and mortality among women worldwide. Early identification of women at increased risk is essential for timely intervention and improved clinical outcomes. Although machine learning has shown considerable promise in breast cancer prediction, comparative evaluations of diverse machine learning paradigms populations remain limited. This study compared probabilistic, linear, ensemble, and deep learning models for breast cancer risk prediction while incorporating explainable artificial intelligence to improve model interpretability. A clinical and epidemiological dataset of Cuban women was used to build six breast cancer prediction models; Logistic Regression, Naïve Bayes, Support Vector Machine, Random Forest, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Artificial Neural Network. These were trained using inverse class weighting to address class imbalance. Model performance was evaluated using stratified 5-fold and 10-fold cross-validation and an independent hold-out test set. Performance was assessed using ROC-AUC, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, F1-score, and Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC). Statistical differences between models were evaluated using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, while SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) was employed to interpret feature importance. All six models demonstrated excellent predictive performance, achieving ROC-AUC values exceeding 0.97 across both cross-validation strategies. XGBoost consistently achieved the highest overall performance (), followed closely by Random Forest, with both models demonstrating superior stability and generalization across validation folds. These findings demonstrate that ensemble learning methods provide accurate, robust, and interpretable prediction of breast cancer risk and show promise for supporting personalized risk assessment and early detection of breast cancer.

items.abstract: Abstract BACKGROUND The increasing complexity of patients in internal medicine wards limits the applicability of randomized controlled trial-derived evidence and highlights the need for complementary real-world data (RWD). The MED-Cli study was developed to generate real-world evidence to better characterize patient complexity and support more personalized, efficient care. METHODS MED-Cli is a single-centre, prospective observational study enrolling all adults admitted to internal medicine and nephrological wards since 2022 at IRCCS San Raffaele Hospital. MED-Cli relies on a comprehensive RWD pipeline comprising production, collection, integration and analysis. Clinical, laboratory, and administrative RWD are collected via electronic case report forms on the dedicated on-premise data management Cohort Genomic Platform. An additional platform, the San Raffaele Ai CEnter (S-RACE), then allows for integration of collected RWD with further laboratory and imaging data directly acquired from hospital’s data lakes. The large volume of generated RWD can then be analysed using statistical and machine learning techniques to generate RWE in the form of descriptive, predictive and prescriptive statistics. RESULTS Since the beginning of the study, RWD of 1352 admission episodes have been collected. Data completeness was high overall, except for selected variables (e.g., respiratory rate, alcohol intake), and improving over time. Mean outlier percentage was 2.8%, with evident data entry mistake happening in only few variables. CONCLUSIONS By establishing a robust and scalable model for RWD integration in internal medicine, MED-Cli opens new avenues for delivering more timely, personalized, and sustainable care to complex older patients, bridging the gap between clinical practice and data-driven innovation.

items.abstract: Abstract Background Digital mental health tools generate growing volumes of active and passive behavioral data, but integrating these data into clinical care and returning them to patients as usable feedback remains a major challenge. Artificial intelligence (AI), including large language models, are able to interpret such data and draft personalized feedback, offering a potentially scalable way to support this work. Whether AI can be adopted for this purpose, however, may depend less on its technical performance than on whether patients trust and accept it. This study examined how former and current patients in mental health service perceive AI involvement in delivering data-report feedback, comparing fully human (no AI), AI-assisted (hybrid), and fully AI-generated formats. Methods Twenty-five adults who had received outpatient mental health treatment viewed six standardized videos representing two clinical scenarios and the three delivery formats. Participants rated each video using a seven-item acceptability scale, compared the formats, and answered open-ended questions. They were not told which formats used AI until after completing the initial ratings. Results Acceptability differed across formats, F(1.20, 28.7) = 21.22, p < .001. Fully human feedback (mean 6.00) and AI-assisted feedback delivered by a human (mean 5.93) received similar ratings, and both were rated more favorably than fully AI-delivered feedback (mean 4.65). Participants were also more comfortable with AI analyzing their data when a human delivered the feedback than with AI both analyzing and delivering it. Overall, 23 of 25 participants preferred a format that retained human involvement after AI use was disclosed. Participants valued AI for producing clear and thorough summaries but wanted a person to explain and discuss the results. Conclusions Patients accepted AI-generated mental health feedback when a human remained involved in reviewing or delivering it. These findings support using AI to assist with data analysis and report preparation rather than replacing the human interaction involved in mental health care. Larger studies should test this approach in routine clinical settings.

items.abstract: Abstract Purpose Accurate localization of breast tumors in mammographic images is a critical yet challenging task due to low contrast, dense breast tissue and subtle lesion boundaries. These factors limit the performance of conventional computeraided detection systems and lightweight deep learning models. This study aimed to improve tumor localization accuracy and robustness through a data-centric, attention-guided detection strategy. Methods We proposed a heatmap-guided, data-centric object detection framework that leveraged neural attention to improve breast tumor localization in mammographic images. The framework integrated contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization, bilateral denoising and neural heatmap generation derived from intermediate features of a lightweight YOLO-based detector. Unlike conventional augmentation strategies, the proposed approach used the generated heatmaps to guide lesion-aware data augmentation, enabling targeted enhancement of tumor-relevant regions and progressive construction of enriched training datasets. The detector was trained on high-resolution images using a consistent optimization strategy. Model performance was evaluated using standard object detection metrics, including mean average precision, precision, recall and loss convergence. Results The proposed heatmap-guided data augmentation significantly improved detection performance compared with the baseline dataset. Notable gains were observed in mean average precision across multiple thresholds, along with increased precision and recall. Training stability was improved and localization-related losses were consistently reduced, indicating more accurate and reliable tumor detection. Conclusion The results demonstrated that heatmap-guided, data-centric augmentation enhanced the accuracy, robustness and efficiency of lightweight YOLO-based models, providing a practical and interpretable solution for breast tumor localization in clinical mammography.

items.abstract: Abstract Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a progressive, long-term condition characterized by a gradual loss of renal function. It represents a significant global health burden, particularly among elderly populations and specific ethnic groups, including individuals of Black and South Asian descent. Early detection and management are critical to preventing severe complications, yet timely and accurate diagnosis remains a clinical challenge. This study investigates the application of Quantum Machine Learning (QML) for the predictive diagnosis of CKD. The study proposes a hybrid quantum neural network (HQNN) architecture and evaluates its performance against alternative QML configurations and conventional classical machine learning techniques. Employing a benchmark CKD dataset from the University of California, Irvine (UCI) Machine Learning Repository, we implemented a robust preprocessing pipeline comprising data imputation, advanced hybrid feature selection, and data normalization. The proposed hybrid model was trained and evaluated on simulated 5-qubit noisy quantum hardware via FakeManilaV2. It achieved a classification accuracy of approximately 97.5% on the UCI CKD cross-sectional cohort with a high circuit expressivity in the quantum layer. The model performed at baseline for classical models and outperformed some standalone QML techniques evaluated in this study.The findings illustrate the feasibility of integrating shallow hybrid quantum-classical networks for medical diagnostic tasks under current NISQ constraints. The proposed hybrid framework provides an exploratory demonstration of explainable risk estimation for CKD with potential relevance for future clinical decision-support research once validated on larger and more diverse cohorts.

items.abstract: Major histocompatibility complex (MHC) proteins share a characteristic structural platform formed by two α-helices positioned above a β-sheet (α1-α2 domain), which can accommodate ligands and provide an exposed surface for recognition by protein binding partners. This interaction system is best characterized for classical MHC-I molecules presenting peptides to T-cell receptors (TCRs), one of the most extensively studied mechanisms of immune recognition. However, non-classical MHC and MHC-like proteins reveal that the α1-α2 platform is considerably more versatile, supporting a remarkably diverse range of biological functions. Related architectures are also exploited by pathogens, further expanding the diversity of molecular interactions associated with this fold. Yet how this functional diversity relates to structural variation within the shared α1-α2 platform and to the diverse modes of recognition employed by natural and engineered binding partners has not been systematically examined across the broader MHC fold. Here, we systematically mapped MHC α1-α2-like domains across experimentally determined structures in the Protein Data Bank and predicted structures in the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database using Foldseek, and compiled their natural and engineered binding partners. Our comparative analyses revealed substantial heterogeneity across multiple structural layers, including α1-α2 geometry, ligand-binding cavity architecture, and the physicochemical properties and spatial conservation of exposed recognition surfaces, despite the overall conservation of the fold. We further characterized a diverse repertoire of natural and engineered binding partners, revealing distinct structural architectures, interface compositions, and recognition geometries. Together, these findings provide an integrated structural landscape connecting the diversity of the MHC fold with the multiple modes of molecular recognition it supports, offering a comparative framework for understanding these interactions and guiding the engineering of novel MHC-targeting proteins.

items.abstract: Activating mutations in leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 (LRRK2) are among the most common genetic risk factors for Parkinson's disease. LRRK2 phosphorylates a subset of Rab GTPases at a conserved Ser/Thr residue within the switch 2 alpha-helix, disrupting interactions with canonical regulators and effectors while promoting recruitment of phospho-specific effectors, including RILPL1, RILPL2, JIP3 and JIP4. However, the full spectrum of phosphorylation-dependent Rab interactions remains unknown. Here, we used mass spectrometry to characterise the phospho-Rab interactome. Purified pRab1, pRab3, pRab8, pRab12, pRab35 and pRab43, together with pRab7, a substrate of the related kinase LRRK1, were used as baits in cellular pulldowns. Comparison with non-phosphorylated Rab interactomes identified numerous phosphorylation-dependent binding proteins, alongside known and candidate effectors that preferentially bound non-phosphorylated Rabs, consistent with phosphorylation broadly disrupting Rab complexes. A prominent phospho-selective interactor was TBC1D2 which bound to multiple phosphorylated Rabs. TBC1D2 is a Rab7 GTPase-activating protein (GAP) implicated in LRRK1-dependent regulation of endolysosomal dynamics. AlphaFold modeling, mutagenesis, co-immunoprecipitation and biophysical analyses demonstrated that a conserved di-lysine motif within a central coiled-coil domain of TBC1D2 mediates binding to pRab3A and pRab8A. These findings identify TBC1D2 as a phospho-Rab effector and suggest a molecular link between LRRK2-dependent Rab phosphorylation and Rab GAP function. Our phospho-Rab interaction resource provides a foundation for investigating how LRRK2 regulates membrane trafficking.

items.title: 国内首个！蚂蚁阿福医生版上线“循证金标准”UpToDate ，打造全场景医生AI工作台
items.summary: 11月22日，蚂蚁阿福医生版发布PC工作台（电脑端）版本，同时接入威科集团循证医学临床决策支持解决方案UpToDate，成为国内首个接入该专业功能的AI平台。 即日起，全国医生、护士及药师等卫生专业技术人员都可通过阿福医生版限时免费试用UpToDate。 此次升级， 阿福医生版实现了手机App加PC工作台的双端布局， 医生既可以便捷地在手机上借助阿福在线接诊、管理和沟通患者，也能在电脑上借助阿福的AI工具完成整理病历、分析数据、生成医学PPT等较复杂任务，双端打通使用起来更方便。…

items.title: 消息称亚马逊接近以 75 亿美元收购人工智能初创企业 Decart
items.summary: IT之家 11 月 23 日消息，《金融时报》当地时间昨日报道称，Amazon 已就收购 Decart 展开深入谈判， 双方最早可能在本周初达成协议 ，但这笔价值约为 75 亿美元 （IT之家注：现汇率约合 501.1 亿元人民币） 的交易仍有破裂的风险。 Decart 由三位以色列工程师于 2023 年创立，提供跨算力硬件类型的人工智能堆栈优化服务，同时也自主开发世界模型。报道指出，Decart 是 亚马逊 AWS Trainium3 人工智能 ASIC 的早期使用者 之一，在优化亚马逊自研芯片表现上有实际经验。 Decart 在今年 5 月以 40…

items.title: 蚂蚁阿福发布全新 AI 健康手环“福环”和 AI 健康戒指“福戒”
items.summary: IT之家 11 月 23 日现场消息，在今日的蚂蚁阿福医疗健康生态大会上，蚂蚁阿福带来了两款全新的 AI 健康硬件 —— AI 健康手环 · 福环 AI 健康戒指 · 福戒 两款产品均主打健康监测和超长续航 ，主要用来记录睡眠、心率、呼吸、血氧等身体指标，并通过 AI 给出健康报告、改善建议。 IT之家在大会现场了解到， 福环可以选择有屏版、无屏版 ，福戒则是银白色简约戒指造型，蚂蚁阿福表示将向伙伴开放合作。 蚂蚁阿福还透露， 阿福已经与华为、小米、苹果等 18 家智能硬件品牌达成深度合作 ，覆盖血糖仪、呼吸机、体脂秤、手环、运动手表、血压仪等设备品类。

items.title: 蚂蚁百灵医疗健康大模型宣布开源，最轻量版一台笔记本就能部署
items.summary: IT之家 11 月 23 日现场消息，在今日的蚂蚁阿福医疗健康生态大会上， 蚂蚁百灵医疗健康大模型宣布全面开源 。 蚂蚁百灵医疗健康大模型家族包含大语言模型、实时音视频模型、预测模型、安全防护模型，支持疾病未来六年的发病风险预测，疾病种类、准确率超越全球多个专用模型。 IT之家在大会现场了解到，蚂蚁百灵医疗健康大模型带来医生专业个人版多模态模型（124B）、医疗机构版医疗智能体大模型（562B），最轻量版一台笔记本就能部署。

items.title: 谷歌 AI 搜索变现受阻，苹果服务业务收入增长也随之放缓
items.summary: IT之家 11 月 23 日消息，据科技媒体 Appleinsider 昨天报道，苹果与谷歌达成的搜索合作协议，带来的收益已不如从前。如今用户的搜索习惯已经改变，导致市场格局生变。 据报道，苹果与谷歌早已就 Safari 默认搜索引擎达成合作关系。谷歌每年向苹果支付 200 亿美元 （IT之家注：现汇率约合 1,336.27 亿元人民币） ，让 iPhone、Mac 等设备的 Safari 浏览器默认搜索引擎为谷歌， 并且谷歌需要将 Safari 搜索广告所产生的 36% 收入支付给苹果 。…

items.title: 中通快递与阿里云伶鹊达成深度合作，智慧AI打造客服新体验
items.summary: 近日，阿里云伶鹊与中通快递达成深度合作，为中通快递打造企业级AI客服，在小件末端配送场景中落地智能语音热线和智能语音外呼两大能力。上线后“呼入+外呼”日均服务量达数十万通，AI“呼入”热线带来的下单转化率提升近20%。 （AI客服产品示意图） 在“呼入”场景下，用户拨通中通快递客服热线后，伶鹊可以听懂“我要改地址”、“快递显示签收但我没收到”、“到上海要几天”等高频诉求，再结合订单的实时状态，通过多轮对话引导用户修改和确认信息，直到把问题办完。…

items.title: 韩国防 AI 作弊新招：要求考生穿围裙考试、时隔 6 年重新收缴手机
