items.abstract: Abstract Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is clinically heterogeneous, yet genetic studies typically rely on binary diagnoses. We applied a novel machine learning method (DDRTree) to 14 clinical measures from 6,355 autistic children in SPARK to identify ASD subtypes and continuous subtype scores. Using a modified k-nearest-neighbor (k-NN) approach, we projected and validated these subtypes in 2,717 autistic children from the SSC. Three subtypes emerged: high support needs (HSN), characterized by broad developmental impairments; emotional-behavioral support needs (EBSN), characterized by repetitive behaviors and psychiatric comorbidities; and low support needs (LSN), characterized by milder symptoms. Projected subtypes reproduced patterns of service and medication use. SNP heritability was higher for EBSN (0.224) and HSN (0.167) scores than for LSN (0.064). Associations with polygenic scores for psychiatric traits were consistent with the characteristics of each subtype, whereas de novo variants and rare copy-number variants were associated with HSN and EBSN. This transferable framework captures clinically and genetically meaningful dimensions of ASD heterogeneity.

items.abstract: Abstract Purpose To characterize the research landscape, major hotspots, and evolving trends in artificial intelligence (AI) applications in corneal refractive surgery and to examine how these applications differ across surgical procedures. Methods English-language Articles and Reviews published between January 2018 and July 12, 2026 were identified from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC). VOSviewer and CiteSpace were used to examine publication trends, countries, institutions, authors, keywords, thematic clusters, temporal patterns, and citation bursts. AI applications were then compared across SMILE, LASIK/FS-LASIK, and PRK/TransPRK. Results The analysis included 79 publications. Publication activity increased after 2022 and reached its highest level in 2026. China and the United States were prominent contributors and occupied central positions in the international collaboration network. Major research themes included artificial intelligence, deep learning, machine learning, LASIK, SMILE, corneal imaging, and keratoconus. Over time, the research focus moved from refractive surgery safety assessment toward AI-assisted analysis and imaging applications. Across LASIK, SMILE, and PRK, AI research mainly addressed corneal parameter assessment, surgical evaluation, and prediction of postoperative outcomes. Conclusions AI research in corneal refractive surgery has expanded considerably in recent years, with increasing emphasis on deep learning, machine learning, and corneal imaging. Current studies mainly concern LASIK, SMILE, and PRK, covering preoperative assessment, corneal parameter analysis, and postoperative outcome prediction. The present bibliometric analysis maps the main research directions and their development over time and may help identify areas for further investigation and clinical translation.

items.abstract: Combinatorial perturbations are widely used to study genetic interactions and to develop drug combinations, but the number of possible combinations grows quadratically with the number of perturbations, and only a small fraction can be measured in a screen experiment. Despite their growing sophistication, deep-learning and foundation models often fail to outperform a simple additive baseline based on measured single-perturbation responses. This suggests a simpler approach that builds on these measurements and directly learns deviations from additivity at the population level. We therefore developed GAIN, a lightweight model that implements these principles by predicting the pseudobulk response to a combination as the sum of its two single-perturbation responses and a learned interaction term. Across three single-cell datasets of genetic and drug combinations, GAIN corrected deviations from additivity and outperformed the additive model and cell-level methods across generalization settings and metrics, while training 3- to 64-fold faster. Applied to a combinatorial CRISPR screen of leukemia differentiation regulators, GAIN revealed synergy between key regulators of the differentiation block and genes that restrain differentiation but have little effect alone. It also revealed dampening by the histone chaperone FACT, which supports the induction of differentiation genes. These results establish population-level modeling of the deviation from additivity as a simple, accurate and scalable approach to predicting combination responses.

items.abstract: Large-scale single-cell transcriptomic data provide a new avenue for precision medicine by uncovering cellular heterogeneity. However, systematic comparison of remodeling patterns across various biological states remains unavailable. Here, we first developed a computational framework based on a foundation model of single cell biology, Universal Cell Embedding (UCE), to harmonize annotations comprising 36 cell types. Based on an integrated dataset of single cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) with 8,789 human samples comprising more than 59 million cells or nuclei across 614 biological states, we then embedded each state with a 36-dimensional vector in a unified space of cell-composition change and further deciphered states bridges by analyzing the relationships among the 614 state vectors. As a result, 22,161 significant bridges (P < 0.05) between the 614 states were revealed. Moreover, we successfully identified a number of well-known bridges such as bridge between Alzheimer's disease and Parkinson's disease (P = 2.21e-15), suggesting the effectiveness of the proposed framework. More importantly, we uncovered a number of new bridges. Furthermore, analyses of the number of changed cell types (NCC) and Shannon entropy revealed heterogeneous and tissue-dependent patterns of cellular composition remodeling. This study provides a new strategy for identifying disease associations and potential therapeutic relationships by deciphering bridges between biological states from scRNA-seq landscape.

items.abstract: Triple-Negative Breast Cancer (TNBC) represents an aggressive breast cancer subtype that lacks actionable cell-surface receptors, restricting frontline systemic management to cytotoxic chemotherapy. While recent functional epigenomics shows that TNBC progression is governed by non-coding regulatory remodeling at distal super-enhancers, conventional Gene Regulatory Network (GRN) inference methods rely on observational transcriptomic co-expression, which suffers from technical dropouts and confounding correlations that inflate false discoveries (>30%). Here, we present an interventional network inference framework that integrates large-scale single-cell CRISPR-interference perturbation sequencing (Perturb-seq; GSE224986, 95,678 cells across 11,975 sgRNAs) with ENCODE Factorbook ChIP-seq physical transcription factor binding priors across 819 somatic mutation-associated enhancer loci in human TNBC (MDA-MB-231). Our pipeline reconstructed a tripartite network yielding 5,935 physical TF–enhancer edges, 383,757 functional enhancer–gene edges, and 542,760 unique TF–target gene functional pairs across 372 active enhancers. Topological centrality prioritized master transcriptional drivers governing TNBC oncogenic signaling, including CTCF, POLR2A, EP300, JUND, MYC, and FOS, which regulate Hallmark programs for Epithelial-Mesenchymal Transition (p = 1.2 × 10-9) and cell cycle progression. Explainable machine learning (SHAP TreeExplainer) revealed non-linear, thresholded transactivation dynamics for AP-1 and MYC. Quantitative benchmarking against held-out CRISPRi ground truth demonstrated strong discriminatory accuracy (AUROC = 0.8999, AUPRC = 0.8745, Precision = 90.13%, FDR = 9.87%), substantially outperforming GENIE3 (AUPRC = 0.6323, FDR = 35.73%) and co-expression correlation (AUPRC = 0.6814). In silico-simulated driver feature silencing correlated with experimental responses (R2 = 0.473, p < 10-122), and master driver signatures significantly stratified overall survival in the METABRIC (n = 320) and TCGA-BRCA (n = 160; p ≤ 0.019) cohorts. Finally, in silico perturbation modeling indicated that multi-target epigenetic combinations achieved 93% topological disruption of oncogenic regulatory connectivity, nominating prioritized candidate circuits for experimental validation.

items.abstract: Abstract Purpose Cadmium exposure is closely associated with kidney stone development, yet its mechanisms in nephrolithiasis remain unclear. This study aimed to identify high-confidence candidate molecular targets in cadmium-induced kidney stone pathogenesis via integrated multi-omics bioinformatics analysis. Methods Cadmium-related targets, kidney stone targets, DEGs from GSE73680 and key WGCNA modules were intersected to obtain candidate targets. PPI network, GO enrichment and multiple machine learning algorithms were used to prioritize 8 candidates. For IL11, we performed differential expression, GSEA, immune and single-cell localization analyses, together with virtual gene perturbation in fibroblasts and tetracycline–IL11 molecular docking. Results Eight candidate targets were identified: IL11, TNFRSF11B, SPP1, AKR1B1, H19, PDZK1, SERPINA1 and CCK. Six proteins formed a PPI network enriched in cytokine activity. All machine learning methods ranked IL11 as the core target.IL11 expression was significantly upregulated in the plaque mucosal group; genes associated with samples exhibiting high IL-11 expression were primarily enriched in pathways such as lysosomes, focal adhesion, and cell adhesion molecules, and were also associated with the proportion of certain immune cells. Single-cell analysis localized IL11 mainly to fibroblasts, which may regulate inflammation and matrix remodeling. Conclusion Eight high-confidence targets for cadmium-related kidney stones were screened. IL11 is recognized as the core target, offering new insights into the molecular mechanisms of cadmium-induced nephrolithiasis.

items.abstract: Abstract Objective To establish a translational framework linking computational risk modeling, spatial immune exclusion, and therapeutic targets in colorectal cancer (CRC), and to evaluate how the cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF) Krüppel-like factor 2 (KLF2)- cluster of differentiation 73 (CD73) pathway may contribute to an immunosuppressive microenvironment through the spatial and functional suppression of CD8⁺ T cells. Methods Five independent transcriptomic cohorts were integrated. Using the GSE39582 discovery cohort, 45 machine learning algorithms were compared via nested cross-validation to construct the CAF stromal-immune exclusion risk (CMIR) score, which was validated for overall survival (OS) prediction in independent external cohorts (GSE17536, TCGA-COAD). Single-cell transcriptomic data (GSE178341) and multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF) staining (evaluating a 4-protein mIF-based CMIR proxy score representing key model components) were combined to quantify in situ cell infiltration density and spatial physical distances. In primary fibroblasts, lentivirus-mediated KLF2 knockdown and overexpression, pharmacological CD73 inhibition, and ternary co-cultures were used to examine CD8 + T-cell cytotoxic activity. Results A 17-gene CMIR score was constructed with the optimal LASSO algorithm and simplified into an 8-gene parsimonious model. In all OS cohorts, patients with high CMIR scores had significantly shorter overall survival than those with low scores (all P < 0.05), and combining the CMIR score with tumor-node-metastasis (TNM) stage significantly improved the concordance index and clinical net benefit of survival prediction. Furthermore, multi-omics profiling revealed that a high CMIR score was significantly correlated with immune-excluded microenvironment features commonly observed in immunotherapy-unresponsive tumors. In situ multiplex immunofluorescence demonstrated that high CMIR scores were associated with reduced CD8 + T-cell infiltration, increased physical distance between T cells and tumor parenchyma, and elevated KLF2/CD73 expression. Mechanistically, KLF2 promoted CD73 expression in CAFs to suppress CD8 + T-cell cytotoxicity, which was effectively reversed by a small-molecule CD73 inhibitor. Conclusion This study establishes a translational framework connecting prognostic risk stratification, histological spatial immune exclusion, and actionable molecular targets, while an mIF-based 4-protein proxy score recapitulates these spatial features at the tissue level. The KLF2-CD73-CAF axis represents a rational target to modulate stromal immunosuppression and enhance the efficacy of immunotherapy in colorectal cancer.

items.abstract: Accumulating evidence implicates nicotine-derived nitrosamine ketone (NNK) in the pathogenesis of various malignancies, yet the biological pathways underlying its effects on hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) have not been fully elucidated. To characterize the signaling pathways involved in NNK-driven hepatocellular carcinoma, we jointly applied network toxicology, single-cell RNA sequencing, molecular docking, virtual knockout analysis, and in vitro validation. Database mining identified 502 putative NNK-related targets across ChEMBL, CTD, SEA, and SwissTarget, together with 2143 HCC-associated genes retrieved from GeneCards, OMIM, and TTD. Functional enrichment analyses implicated the candidate genes in xenobiotic responses, cell cycle regulation, transcription factor binding, and several cancer-related signaling pathways, particularly the PI3K-Akt, FoxO, and p53 pathways. Following transcriptomic validation in GSE121248 and machine learning prioritization, TOP2A emerged as the leading candidate associated with NNK-related molecular alterations in HCC. TOP2A showed satisfactory discriminatory performance in both GSE121248 and GSE14520, with AUC values exceeding 0.75. Immune cell deconvolution further revealed associations between TOP2A expression and multiple immune cell subsets. In silico gene perturbation analysis identified ORM1 as a candidate gene associated with predicted TOP2A perturbation, suggesting a potential molecular relationship between TOP2A and ORM1 rather than an experimentally established regulatory axis. Subsequent cellular experiments showed that NNK treatment increased growth-related cellular activity and migratory phenotypes in both HuH-7 and Hep 3B2.1-7 cells. NNK exposure was also accompanied by increased TOP2A and ORM1 protein abundance, with consistent western blot findings observed in both HCC cell lines. In summary, this study identifies TOP2A as a potential molecular candidate associated with NNK-related HCC progression and suggests a possible relationship between TOP2A and ORM1 that may contribute to NNK-associated molecular alterations in HCC.

items.abstract: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) shows marked prognostic heterogeneity, partly driven by interactions between regulated cell death and the tumor immune microenvironment. A framework integrating multiple cell-death programs with immune states is still lacking. This study integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomic data to characterize immune-cell-death interactions in DLBCL. Immune-cell-death-related genes were identified by intersecting differentially expressed genes with immune and cell-death gene sets. A cell-death-immune score (CDIS) was constructed using 101 machine-learning combinations and evaluated in three external cohorts. This study assessed immune infiltration, cell-death transcriptional programs, cell-cell communication, ligand-target interactions, pseudotime trajectories, drug connectivity, molecular docking and virtual perturbation. In vitro assays further tested BAFF stimulation and tamoxifen treatment in DLBCL cell lines. We identified 159 immune-cell-death-related genes and selected 16 genes from 25 candidates to construct the CDIS prognostic model; CoxBoost plus random survival forest ranked highest (mean C-index 0.703). High CDIS was associated with suppressed transcriptional programs of immunogenic cell death and an immune-cold microenvironment with M2-like macrophage enrichment. CDIS provides incremental value over International Prognostic Index (IPI), particularly within the IPI 2 stratum, where it significantly further distinguished high- from low-risk patients (5-year overall survival 63.6% vs. 42.7%; log-rank P = 0.012). Single-cell analysis localized model genes mainly to macrophages and identified an M2-like macrophage-BAFF/APRIL-malignant B-cell axis. Exogenous BAFF promoted DLBCL-cell proliferation and reduced apoptosis, whereas tamoxifen inhibited proliferation dose-dependently. CDIS serves as a complementary prognostic model to IPI, refining risk within IPI strata, and reveals a candidate mechanism centered on the M2-like macrophage-BAFF/APRIL-malignant B-cell axis.

items.abstract: Recent advances in video generation have made automated advertising production increasingly feasible. However, an effective advertisement must faithfully represent the product and communicate its selling points through compelling visual storytelling, which requires more than visual synthesis: it calls for deeper product understanding and strategic decisions about how to present product value. Crucially, product research and creative design are closely intertwined, as the information gathered about a product determines which features can be faithfully demonstrated and how they should be presented. In this paper, we introduce AdProducer, the first end-to-end agentic framework for advertising video creation, transforming concise creative briefs into finished advertisements. Our multimodal agent autonomously researches products through web and image search and translates its findings into selling-point-driven storyboards that guide a frozen video generator. To achieve this, we develop a dedicated data construction pipeline that yields two training datasets, AdProducer-SFT and AdProducer-RL, and train the agent through supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning with joint optimization of storyboard- and video-level rewards. We further introduce AdCreation-Bench, comprising 305 advertising briefs across eight domains, with two complementary metrics: PG-Score for product correctness and creative execution, and Ad-Score for overall advertising effectiveness assessed by an independent judge. Experiments demonstrate that AdProducer improves the PG-Score of MiniMax H3 from 17.3 to 51.3 and generalizes to Veo 3.1 without additional training, improving its score from 28.0 to 35.9, with consistent gains in Ad-Score, VideoScore2, and human evaluations. Code, models, and data are released.

items.title: Do learned image captioning metrics generalize? Auditing duplicated samples in human-judgment benchmarks
items.summary: Learned image captioning metrics are trained and tested on human judgments, so their reported correlation is a claim about generalization. We audit this claim for the three most recent collections of such judgments, Polaris, Nebula, and Spica, matching images at the pixel level. items.abstract: Learned image captioning metrics are trained and tested on human judgments, so their reported correlation is a claim about generalization. We audit this claim for the three most recent collections of such judgments, Polaris, Nebula, and Spica, matching images at the pixel level. First, test samples reappear in training sets: the Spica training set contains about two-thirds of the Polaris test set, with identical human ratings. Second, controlled retraining shows that duplicates can inflate a metric: for Pearl, the gain is confined to the duplicated samples and grows with every epoch; for DENEB, it stays below one point. The gain depends on the learner and on how often a training set repeats a sample. Third, Kendall's τ over all samples is the sum of two terms, detecting captions with the lowest human score and ranking the others; the first supplies most of the reported correlation and is nearly saturated. The recent test sets cannot order Polos, DENEB and Pearl consistently, and a ridge regression on frozen features matches or exceeds all three. Fourth, we propose a protocol that ranks a learned metric only with a model trained without test samples, reports both terms, and compares metrics by paired tests. Under it, zero-shot vision--language judges rank first on the three recent test sets, and a fine-tuned judge ranks first on the three earlier benchmarks. The same analysis applies to any evaluator learned from human judgments; filter lists and code are released at https://github.com/morninghut/ic-dataset-audit .

items.abstract: Modern visual generative models operate on tokens, and every visual asset they receive, whether an identity, a scribble, a depth map, or a motion video, is tokenized and appended to the input token sequence. Consequently, conditioning quickly dominates the computation cost. Yet most of these tokens carry redundant spatiotemporal information. Our key insight is that identifying what is genuinely new is exactly the problem that classical video codecs have long solved. Thus, we first introduce a codec-based token pruning method that discards redundant tokens. Then, we propose an on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) strategy to train a DiT adapter capable of learning the codec pruning pattern well without quality degradation. Together, they form On-Policy Codec Distillation (CodecOPSD). We scale CodecOPSD to 16 condition modalities on our own video diffusion model, where it prunes 66% of the condition tokens on average with almost no quality drop. Therefore, denoising becomes 2x faster, and the cache memory shrinks by up to 73% in KV cache mode. CodecOPSD also extends to other state-of-the-art pretrained image and video generative models, where its benefit grows further with more conditions, longer frames, and higher resolution.

items.title: Self-Evolving Evaluation Environments for Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: Computer-use agents (CUAs) are rapidly improving, yet their evaluation remains largely static. Existing benchmarks provide a strong foundation, but fixed difficulty ceilings, limited feature coverage, and coarse aggregate scores progressively weaken their discriminative and diagnostic value. We introduce CUA-SEE, a closed-loop evaluation environment that co-evolves tasks and executable verifiers from rollout…
items.abstract: Computer-use agents (CUAs) are rapidly improving, yet their evaluation remains largely static. Existing benchmarks provide a strong foundation, but fixed difficulty ceilings, limited feature coverage, and coarse aggregate scores progressively weaken their discriminative and diagnostic value. We introduce CUA-SEE, a closed-loop evaluation environment that co-evolves tasks and executable verifiers from rollout evidence. It disentangles three objectives: benchmark evolution expands evaluation scope through cohort-calibrated difficulty and coverage growth; diagnostic evolution increases resolution through agent-conditional capability-boundary probes; and verifier evolution improves precision by translating changing requirements into state-grounded checkpoints with adversarial validation. Across multiple agents, applications, and rounds, CUA-SEE generates challenging, measurable tasks while preserving process-level evidence. Our results position adaptive evaluation as a scalable counterpart to self-evolving agents, continuously tracking what agents can do, where their boundaries lie, and how reliably progress is measured.

items.title: ACAP: Asynchronous Coding Agents for Efficient Robot Control
items.summary: Coding agents can construct and revise robot behavior during execution, but using one agent for the whole robot can delay otherwise independent work. We introduce Asynchronous Coding Agents as Policy (ACAP), an asynchronous framework that organizes one robot as a team of persistent agents. Each member reasons and acts for a configurable control group, such as an arm with its gripper or the torso and chassis,…
items.abstract: Coding agents can construct and revise robot behavior during execution, but using one agent for the whole robot can delay otherwise independent work. We introduce Asynchronous Coding Agents as Policy (ACAP), an asynchronous framework that organizes one robot as a team of persistent agents. Each member reasons and acts for a configurable control group, such as an arm with its gripper or the torso and chassis, enabling asynchronous reasoning and execution. However, different robot components often have physical dependencies that require coordination. To address this challenge, ACAP introduces a hyper-agent that assigns tasks, coordinates dependencies, and dynamically allocates control between the lead and member agents. This allows independent work to progress concurrently while supporting tightly coupled manipulation when necessary. Across 72 real-world rollouts covering 25 task/platform settings, ACAP reduces task-balanced time cost by 28.2% compared with a single-agent Direct Policy, with improvements across Fully Parallel, Parallel-Sequential, and Collaborative tasks. Across all eight Collaborative settings, ACAP also achieves lower mean time cost than Fixed Delegation, where only member agents can control their assigned groups. An additional 90-rollout study shows lower mean 30-minute-capped time cost than Direct on all six tasks. We further demonstrate mobile manipulation using the same member interface for chassis and torso control. We present the framework and a real-world rollout dataset containing observations, generated programs, actions, and feedback to support research on how coding agents reason and act in the physical world.

items.title: Rewirable Circuits in Transformers with Loom Attention
items.summary: We propose loom attention, which allows a Transformer to dynamically rewire its circuits at every token by interweaving a head's vertical attention over the outputs of earlier heads (to obtain its query, key and value) with its horizontal attention over tokens. items.abstract: We propose loom attention, which allows a Transformer to dynamically rewire its circuits at every token by interweaving a head's vertical attention over the outputs of earlier heads (to obtain its query, key and value) with its horizontal attention over tokens. We instantiate vertical attention efficiently with normalized and gated linear attention over a per-token matrix memory, which stores the compressed head outputs and serves as a second residual stream. This yields LoomFormer, a dual-stream architecture that splits control and content between the vector and matrix streams. Across model sizes and training token budgets in language modeling and downstream tasks, LoomFormer matches Transformers trained with over 3x compute and recent residual-stream baselines (HC/mHC, MUDDFormer, AttnRes) trained with ~1.7-2.8x. For example, trained on the same 300B tokens with only 2% extra FLOPs, LoomPythia-2.8B achieves ~1.6x the average downstream gain of mHC-Pythia-2.8B over Pythia-2.8B, and matches (0-shot) or surpasses (5-shot) Pythia-12B. Code is available at https://github.com/Caiyun-AI/LoomFormer

items.title: Escriba-OCR: A 1B Vision-Language Model for Error-Preserving Transcription of Handwritten Portuguese Essays

items.abstract: Feedback tools and research on learner writing need transcriptions of handwritten essays that keep exactly what the student wrote: misspellings, line breaks, struck-through words and insertions. Vision-language models (VLMs) read handwriting well, but they also tend to rewrite it into correct language. We measure this on BRESSAY, 1,000 handwritten Brazilian Portuguese essays, with a benchmark that adds error preservation, invented errors, edit-markup precision and recall and line structure to the character error rate (CER) and uses paired bootstrap confidence intervals. We restrict the study to open-weight models that schools can run on their own hardware. Of 22 open baselines, the best, Qwen3-VL 235B-A22B, reaches 5.6% CER on the 199 test pages; none reproduces the edit markup reliably, and every VLM replaces 39-78% of the words absent from a Portuguese dictionary with dictionary words. We fine-tune LightOnOCR-3-1B on the 647 training pages in 85 minutes on one GPU. The resulting Escriba-OCR-1B reaches 2.06% CER, 3.5 points below the best baseline (95% CI [-4.2, -2.9]); under the ICDAR 2024 competition metric it reaches 2.1% CER, below the best published page-level results (2.2-2.4%). It recovers 67% of insertions and 77% of illegible deletions, and reproduces the line structure of 97% of the pages, but still normalises 60% of likely misspellings. Three seeds agree within 0.04 CER points, and quantised to 4 bits the model runs on an ordinary CPU at about one minute per page. On 40 letters of another corpus it matches its base model (without that model's appended comments) but misreads unseen words more often; weight interpolation recovers half the gap. A teacher's review finds that 45% of the judgeable apparent corrections are errors in the BRESSAY ground truth, so dictionary-based scores likely understate preservation. We release the model, the benchmark code and the review data.

items.title: RoomTokens: Masked Diffusion over Structured Tokens for Indoor Scene Synthesis
items.summary: Generating 3D indoor scenes requires a representation that captures object semantics, instance identity, height structure, and orientation while respecting room geometry. Methods that model scenes as sequences of object vectors learn spatial constraints implicitly, leaving collisions and boundary violations to losses or post-processing; semantic-map methods make occupancy explicit, but collapse instance and…
items.abstract: Generating 3D indoor scenes requires a representation that captures object semantics, instance identity, height structure, and orientation while respecting room geometry. Methods that model scenes as sequences of object vectors learn spatial constraints implicitly, leaving collisions and boundary violations to losses or post-processing; semantic-map methods make occupancy explicit, but collapse instance and directional structure. We introduce RoomTokens, a sliced structured-token representation in which each token stores semantic class, instance-color identity, and facing field. This representation allows a scene to be generated as a discrete grid while preserving cues for instance grouping, orientation estimation, and 3D extent prediction. To learn the RoomToken distribution, we propose MDIRT (Masked Diffusion over RoomTokens), a masked discrete diffusion model that denoises semantic/instance-color/facing channels jointly with a shared cross-slice backbone. Architectural tokens are clamped as explicit floor- plan constraints, so the model samples furniture layouts that respect room geometry while retaining instance and object-attribute structure. Experiments on 3D-FRONT show that RoomTokens with MDIRT improve layout fidelity and physical consistency over sequence/vector- and map-based methods, suggesting structured spatial tokens as a practical choice for discrete 3D scene synthesis.

items.title: LeadVLA: Learning Follower-Aware Route Execution for Robot Leading
items.summary: Robot leading requires executing a route while continuously adapting to a designated follower. Existing robot-leading systems often mediate follower understanding and physical route execution through explicit states, planners, or modular interfaces; directly learning this coupling through end-to-end trajectory prediction can instead entangle route execution with follower response. We introduce LeadVLA, a structured…
items.abstract: Robot leading requires executing a route while continuously adapting to a designated follower. Existing robot-leading systems often mediate follower understanding and physical route execution through explicit states, planners, or modular interfaces; directly learning this coupling through end-to-end trajectory prediction can instead entangle route execution with follower response. We introduce LeadVLA, a structured multimodal policy that preserves the route as an explicit Path reference while learning a Pace for route progress and a Residual for local follower- and scene-conditioned adaptation. To make this problem trainable and measurable, we develop LeadInfra, a configurable Unreal Engine-based closed-loop data-generation infrastructure from which we instantiate an approximately 4M-sample training corpus, and LeadBench, a standardized benchmark with 108 fully held-out closed-loop episodes. LeadVLA achieves the highest task success (39.6%) among evaluated robot policies on LeadBench while maintaining strong route fidelity and follower responsiveness, and transfers to unseen real-world environments without real-world policy fine-tuning. Project Page: https://louiszengCN.github.io/LeadVLA_PAGE/

items.title: LUCID: Statistically Grounded Self-Correction for LLM Reasoning Evaluation
items.summary: Cheap language-model raters grade chain-of-thought reasoning at scale, yet systematic step-rating errors can skew reasoning audits and solution rankings. We introduce LUCID (Loop for Unbiased Calibration via Inference-time Diagnosis), which pairs prompt self-correction with Design-based Supervised Learning (DSL). Without retraining or weight access, LUCID calibrates binary step ratings by aligning predicted and…
items.abstract: Cheap language-model raters grade chain-of-thought reasoning at scale, yet systematic step-rating errors can skew reasoning audits and solution rankings. We introduce LUCID (Loop for Unbiased Calibration via Inference-time Diagnosis), which pairs prompt self-correction with Design-based Supervised Learning (DSL). Without retraining or weight access, LUCID calibrates binary step ratings by aligning predicted and expert soundness rates. From a small expert-labeled set, LUCID summarizes rater bias in plain text and prompts the rater to re-grade unseen steps. For example, on PRM800K, GPT-5-mini grades too strictly, under-rating computation, verification, and late-trace steps most acutely. In one pass, LUCID shrinks GPT-5-mini's calibration gap from 7.8 to 0.9 percentage points in absolute predicted-expert rate difference. LUCID also halves false alarms (sound steps rated unsound) and lifts error-detection F1 on unsound steps by 32%. LUCID retains these gains with 1,000 diagnostic steps or overall-gap feedback alone. The loop also transfers across models and domains: it applies GPT-5-mini's bias profile to lift GLM-5.2's PRM800K accuracy, and it narrows calibration gaps for overly strict but capable raters across math, science, web, and logic benchmarks. Because prompt feedback shifts thresholds without improving class-balanced sound/unsound discrimination, LUCID filters re-grading with pre-/post-checks that skip already calibrated raters and roll back ineffective passes. Finally, we reuse that expert set with raw corpus ratings in DSL for calibration and regression debiasing, and apply DSL to pair-labeled steps for sound-step transitions. DSL's out-of-fold soundness probabilities lift best-of-K selection to match expert labels, while its doubly-robust estimators beat expert-only regression fits at small budgets and cut sound-step transition error by nearly two-thirds.

items.title: Context-Grounded Skill Internalization for Vision-Language Agents
items.summary: Skill internalization offers a way for agents to learn useful behaviors from skills and use them without explicit guidance in context at inference time. A common approach is to generate demonstration trajectories with the skill in context and then fine-tune the same model on its own trajectories with the skill removed. However, this leads to the problem that the model may learn to reference the removed skill, which…
items.abstract: Skill internalization offers a way for agents to learn useful behaviors from skills and use them without explicit guidance in context at inference time. A common approach is to generate demonstration trajectories with the skill in context and then fine-tune the same model on its own trajectories with the skill removed. However, this leads to the problem that the model may learn to reference the removed skill, which we named as context misalignment (CoMi). In this work, we first analyze agent behaviors related to CoMi under this common pipeline. Across ALFWorld, WebShop, and ARC-AGI-1, skill-removed fine-tuning consistently results in CoMi: 12.2-46.0% of test trajectories reference the removed skill. To address this problem, we develop Context-Grounded Skill Internalization (CGSI). CGSI uses a sentence detector to identify unsupported references and then masks or rewrites the selected sentences before fine-tuning. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of CGSI and reveal two key findings. (i) Compared with directly fine-tuning with the skill removed, CGSI reduces CoMi at test time by 72.5-94.6% while preserving task success. (ii) Compared with existing reinforcement learning-based skill-internalization baselines, CGSI achieves comparable performance with substantially less training time. CGSI also significantly reduces processing costs compared with large-scale trajectory auditing and correction.

items.title: Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation
items.summary: Visual creation demands expressive imagery together with precise control over text, layout, and structure. We introduce Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation, an agentic framework that connects these capabilities through Pixel as Code. Raster images are represented by learned discrete visual tokens, while structured artifacts use explicit programs. A shared generation-and-rendering interface connects these representations to…
items.abstract: Visual creation demands expressive imagery together with precise control over text, layout, and structure. We introduce Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation, an agentic framework that connects these capabilities through Pixel as Code. Raster images are represented by learned discrete visual tokens, while structured artifacts use explicit programs. A shared generation-and-rendering interface connects these representations to visual feedback across images, vector graphics, webpages, and documents. A Nemotron-native harness coordinates planning and raster candidate selection, with targeted repair for editable structured and hybrid artifacts. To support this interface, we develop Nemotron-Labs-Image-Tokenizer, the autoregressive raster generator Nemotron-Labs-Image-30B-A3B, and the structured-code model family Nemotron-Labs-VisionCode. On approximately 178K images spanning six visual domains, our tokenizer improves reconstruction PSNR from 26.08 to 29.57 dB over Emu3.5 IBQ. It also provides 7.13x faster encoding and 10.93x faster decoding at batch size one on A100. In standalone evaluation, one Nemotron-Labs-VisionCode variant surpasses Kimi K3.1 Pro on the aggregate across Chart2Code, MMSVG, Design2Code, and Image2Struct. At the system level, the Nemotron-native configuration raises GenEval2 Soft-TIFA GM from 31.71 to 52.56 using the same raster generator. With our best setting, Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation achieves performance competitive with GPT Image 2 and Nano Banana Pro across most benchmarks with available comparisons.

items.title: Let Vision-Language Models Generate Images through Their Representations
items.summary: Recent unified multimodal models aim to combine visual understanding and generation within a single model, yet effectively integrating the two capabilities remains challenging. Leveraging pretrained vision-language models offers a way to build on already learned multimodal knowledge, but making this knowledge effectively accessible to visual generation remains nontrivial. We find that a central challenge lies in the…
items.abstract: Recent unified multimodal models aim to combine visual understanding and generation within a single model, yet effectively integrating the two capabilities remains challenging. Leveraging pretrained vision-language models offers a way to build on already learned multimodal knowledge, but making this knowledge effectively accessible to visual generation remains nontrivial. We find that a central challenge lies in the heterogeneous visual representations used for understanding and generation. To address this challenge, we introduce Integral, which converts a pretrained vision-language model into a unified multimodal model by constructing a shared visual representation space across the two capabilities. Integral implements this design through two complementary components. Abstraction Fusion constructs shared visual tokens by aggregating hierarchical representations from the frozen vision encoder, while Block-wise MoT introduces a lightweight generative stream that interacts with the vision-language model only at block boundaries. Our approach effectively preserves the pretrained understanding capability while extending it to strong visual generation. Controlled comparisons further demonstrate that sharing visual representations between understanding and generation substantially improves generative learning compared with using a separate visual representation space, despite comparable reconstruction fidelity. These results suggest that representations learned by pretrained vision-language models already provide an effective foundation for visual generation.

items.title: PixelOne: From Options to Pixels in a Single Forward for GUI Grounding
items.summary: GUI grounding requires precise clicks at low latency. Recent models such as GUI-Decisions and GUI-Swift predict coordinates in one forward pass using fixed global bins with local refinement. However, screenshot downsampling removes detail needed to locate small controls, while fixed bins cover larger pixel ranges at higher resolutions. We introduce PixelOne, which transfers spatial knowledge from a search teacher to…
items.abstract: GUI grounding requires precise clicks at low latency. Recent models such as GUI-Decisions and GUI-Swift predict coordinates in one forward pass using fixed global bins with local refinement. However, screenshot downsampling removes detail needed to locate small controls, while fixed bins cover larger pixel ranges at higher resolutions. We introduce PixelOne, which transfers spatial knowledge from a search teacher to a student that predicts clicks directly from screenshots at native resolution. The teacher uses VideoJEV's text-option scorer to select rows and columns and progressively zoom into candidate regions. The student inherits the teacher's parameters and matches its distributions over explored regions through spatial distillation alongside box supervision. At inference, the same decision head selects a visual token, and a lightweight pixel head predicts the click within it, all in one forward pass. A click-aligned loss encourages pixels inside the target box to score above those outside. Across four benchmarks, PixelOne-Pro-35B-A3B achieves 83.8% mean accuracy, the highest among the evaluated single-forward grounders, with a mean latency of 0.43 s per target.

items.title: GlanceNav: Efficient Vision-and-Language Navigation with Streaming Memory and Counterfactual Rewind
items.summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have become strong policies for vision-and-language navigation (VLN). items.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have become strong policies for vision-and-language navigation (VLN). However, most of them encode a sample of past frames again at every decision and are trained on isolated decisions, so computation is redundant and the usable history is short. They also learn from their own mistakes through outcome rewards that give one scalar to a whole episode. We ask whether a navigator can encode each frame only once, at a constant cost per step, and still remember what matters and learn efficiently from its mistakes. We present GlanceNav, a streaming navigator built on a hybrid MLLM. Its Gated DeltaNet layers carry a recurrent state through the whole episode, while its attention layers keep a short window of recent observations and a small bank of keyframes, selected by how much each frame changes the recurrent state. This constant-size memory keeps the cost per step fixed and allows training on whole episodes with the same memory as at inference. Because the entire memory can also be copied in constant time, we further propose Counterfactual Rewind (CoRe), a reinforcement learning stage that rewinds a drifting rollout to its closest approach to the goal, lets an expert correct a few actions, and credits decisions by the resulting change in outcome. Trained only on the R2R-CE and RxR-CE training splits, with 1,000 instructions for reinforcement learning, a 4B GlanceNav reaches success rates of 71.9% and 73.6% on R2R-CE and RxR-CE val-unseen. On R2R-CE, it outperforms the strongest previous single-RGB method trained without external data by 9.1 points, while running at 104 ms per step.

items.abstract: Given a single text and a simple zero-shot prompt (no web access, tools, candidate lists, or writing samples), frontier models can answer "who wrote this?" at three increasingly specific levels: (1) whether an AI or human wrote it, (2) if an AI, which lab, and (3) if a human, often exactly who. The latest models (Claude Fable 5.2, GPT-6.1 Sol, Gemini 4 Carbon) match trained detectors like Pangram while also explaining their predictions in natural language, and Opus 5.5 names the correct lab for 98% of texts generated by models from Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google. Most strikingly, Fable 5.2 correctly names the author of 55% of 15K anonymous ICML 2020 reviews that were never made public, and identifies the username behind 69% of comments from active Redditors (with >500 posts over the last year). Accuracy depends on exposure to an author's writing in pretraining data and on reasoning effort, and simply asking a model how familiar it is with someone predicts whether it can identify their writing. For anyone who has published enough writing online, frontier models present a greater threat to anonymity than commonly assumed, and defenses are limited.

items.abstract: Dataset distillation (DD) aims to compress a large dataset into a small synthetic one that remains effective for training neural networks. Despite its success in supervised learning, DD remains underexplored in self-supervised learning (SSL), where distilled data must preserve the information needed to learn representations that remain consistent across augmentations. To bridge this gap, we introduce Mutual Information Prototype Alignment (MIPA), an efficient SSL dataset distillation approach that optimizes synthetic images to preserve augmentation-invariant information. Specifically, MIPA treats synthetic images as learnable prototypes and uses a frozen encoder to assign real samples to them based on feature similarity. A synthetic dataset that preserves such augmentation invariance should yield stable prototype assignments across multiple augmented views of the same real image. MIPA encourages this by maximizing mutual information between cross-view assignments while avoiding trivial solutions in which all real samples are assigned to only a few synthetic prototypes. Evaluations on image classification benchmarks show that synthetic data generated by MIPA yield higher-quality representations than existing distillation approaches while reducing time and storage demands during distillation.

items.abstract: Proprietary news archives assign stories to firms, so reproducing a financial study often requires access to both the articles and the vendor's assignments. CCFinance lets researchers reconstruct firm coverage under different selection rules by recording which version of a story was captured, which issuers it names and how often each appears. From 14.8 million English-language records in Fine News, derived from public Common Crawl News, we identify 5.22 million distinct, consistently dated articles with issuer links. Exact reconstruction requires the restricted snapshot and derived artifacts. We compare GLiNER and Stanza on 250 model-labeled article leads and assess issuer links and story focus against blinded model judgments. Estimated precision among 475 accepted links is 96.8%. Among held-out articles with a detected company, requiring three mentions raises subject precision from 31.9% to 66.1%. Across the 2017-2025 panel, the same rule reduces the number of issuer-years with at least 50 qualifying stories from 13,918 to 8,641. Three reimplementations examine volatility tracking, bank networks and overnight returns. In the network study, bank pairs appearing together rose from 177 to 242 across publishers between January and April 2020, but fell from 50 to 35 within Reuters.

items.abstract: Looped Transformers iterate a shared block of layers to increase computation without adding parameters, offering stronger performance and test-time scaling. However, this power has so far required training from scratch and yielded only modest gains for LLMs. Finetuning existing models into loops is far cheaper, yet also brings only marginal gains over SFT. We propose LoopRes, an effective, scalable, and simple approach that turns loops into significant and consistent gains for pretrained LLMs. Building on Attention Residuals, LoopRes lets each looped layer attend directly to the outputs of earlier loops. Since these outputs are iterates of the same layers and become harder to tell apart, we give each a trainable loop-aware key that encodes its structural identity. Attending to all earlier loops also lets layers skip intermediate ones, so we restrict each layer to a residual window of the latest W loops, forcing every loop to build incrementally on recent ones. Across 6 pretrained LLMs from 3 model families and 9 benchmarks, LoopRes delivers significant and consistent gains: at 2x compute, it improves Qwen3-1.7B-Base by 29.1% over SFT, more than doubling the gain of the state-of-the-art baseline. The gains hold on larger models up to 30B and across all three families. More importantly, from 1.7B to 8B, LoopRes scales more steeply than SFT as compute grows, reaching a higher ceiling while needing less compute on long outputs. These results establish LoopRes as an effective looping approach, delivering both better performance and better test-time scaling.

items.abstract: Massively parallel cytometry (MPC) experiments allow cost-effective quantification of >200 surface proteins at single-cell resolution. The Infinity Flow protocol was developed to measure highly informative protein 'Backbone' markers on all cells in wells distributed across plates, along with well-specific exploratory protein 'Infinity' markers. Backbone markers are then used to impute the Infinity markers using machine learning methods. This protocol offers unprecedented opportunities for more comprehensive classification of cell types. However, the protocol can be improved, particularly in removal of unwanted variation. Here, we propose mapfx.norm, a novel method for removing background noise and batch effects from MPC data. It is developed as part of the MAssively Parallel Flow cytometry Xplorer R package, an end-to-end toolbox for analysing MPC data, including pre-processing and imputing missing Infinity markers in wells where those markers were not measured. Unique features of our method include performing background correction to eliminate the noise from electronic baseline restoration and fluorescence compensation prior to imputation, and removing unwanted variation at the cell level while explicitly accounting for the potential association between biology and unwanted factors. We benchmark our method against alternatives and demonstrate that our approach is better at preserving biological signals, removing unwanted variation, and imputing unmeasured Infinity markers.

items.abstract: Diabetic ulcers (DU) are severe complications of diabetes, and environmental contaminants such as acrylamide (AA) and its metabolite glycidamide (GA) have been associated with metabolic disturbances relevant to diabetes. In this study, public transcriptomic datasets, network toxicology, protein interaction analysis, and machine learning were integrated to identify plausible candidate DU-associated biomarkers overlapping with predicted AA or GA targets. Functional enrichment, immune infiltration analysis, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and single-cell RNA sequencing were further applied to characterize their biological roles and cellular distribution. Eight candidate genes were identified from the intersection of differentially expressed genes and predicted toxicant targets, and PNP and CTSB were ultimately identified as plausible candidate DU-associated biomarkers. These genes were associated with proteasome function, DNA damage and repair, immune dysregulation, and altered cell communication. Single-cell analysis highlighted macrophages and T cells as major cell populations with dynamic plausible candidate biomarker expression. ELISA in streptozotocin induced diabetic ulcer mice further confirmed significantly increased CTSB and PNP protein levels, providing preliminary protein-level support for their association with DU. However, the overlap of PNP and CTSB with predicted AA/GA targets represents hypothesis-generating computational evidence only and does not establish that AA/GA exposure modulates these genes in vivo. These findings support PNP and CTSB as plausible candidate DU-associated biomarkers, while the predicted AA/GA-related associations require direct exposure-based experimental validation.

items.abstract: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is a time-sensitive medical emergency in which rapid recognition of right ventricular (RV) dysfunction by point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) can support early risk stratification. Here, we present HOPE (ecHO-Pulmonary Embolism), a real-world emergency cardiac POCUS video dataset comprising 4,069 patients with suspected PE, and EchoPE, a foundation-model-based video classification framework for detecting PE-associated right-heart phenotypes. HOPE includes five commonly acquired emergency echocardiographic views, with all positive PE cases confirmed by computed tomography pulmonary angiography. EchoPE builds on EchoPrime-pretrained echocardiographic representations and incorporates view recognition, task-specific adaptation, and attention-based interpretability. Experiments suggested that directly transferring EchoPrime representations to this disease-specific task provided limited performance, whereas EchoPE (AUROC 95.2 +/- 0.3) substantially outperformed both EchoPrime with a classification head (AUROC 87.6 +/- 1) and conventional video deep learning baselines. At a fixed sensitivity of 90%, EchoPE achieved a precision of 87.8, compared with 70.7 for EchoPrime. Among adaptation strategies, Low-Rank Adaptation combined with knowledge distillation provided the best balance between PE discrimination and preservation of pretrained echocardiographic semantics. Interpretability analyses showed that the adapted model focused on clinically relevant RV morphological changes, interventricular septal configuration, and informative temporal segments within ultrasound videos. Overall, HOPE and EchoPE demonstrate that echocardiographic foundation models require dataset-specific adaptation to identify PE-related right-heart strain and support the potential use of artificial intelligence-assisted bedside echocardiography for risk warning in acute care settings.

items.abstract: A single brain-age estimate may obscure regional differences in clinical vulnerability. Using voxel-level deep learning, we derived whole-brain and nine regional brain-age gaps (BAGs) spanning cortical, subcortical and cerebellar regions from T1-weighted MRI in 46,254 UK Biobank participants. Genetic correlation estimates in 41,067 participants (rg = 0.56-0.93) exceeded phenotypic correlations across all 45 pairs, yet regional profiles varied across 24 hospital-recorded diagnoses. Oligodendrocyte annotations predominated for whole-brain and cerebellar BAGs, whereas annotations for caudate BAG included astrocyte and vascular classes. In the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative, temporal BAG showed stronger associations with cerebrospinal fluid Aβ42 and cognition than whole-brain BAG when modelled together. A regional model modestly improved discrimination of observed conversion from mild cognitive impairment to Alzheimer's disease during available follow-up compared with a whole-brain model. Polygenic scores showed cross-cohort associations with hypertension and osteoporosis. Regional BAGs provide complementary clinical information within a shared polygenic architecture.

items.abstract: Traditional obesity risk assessment centers on body mass index (BMI); however, marked differences in cardiovascular and cerebrovascular outcomes despite comparable total adiposity suggest that the regional attributes of adipose tissue have independent explanatory value. Consistent evidence from cohort studies and Mendelian randomization (MR) shows that upper-body (abdominal/truncal) fat is positively associated with cardiovascular and cerebrovascular risk, whereas lower-body (gluteofemoral/leg) fat is independently associated with reduced risk at the adipose depot volume level. In a South Indian dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) study, each 1-SD increase in android fat was associated with an odds ratio (OR) for type 2 diabetes of 6.59 (95% CI, 3.17–13.70) in men, whereas the OR for leg fat was 0.42 (95% CI, 0.24–0.74). A dose-response meta-analysis showed that each 10-cm increase in hip circumference was associated with a 10% lower risk of all-cause mortality (hazard ratio (HR), 0.90; 95% CI, 0.81–0.99); after adjustment for BMI and waist circumference, the association strengthened to an HR of 0.78 (95% CI, 0.66–0.90). Data from the UK Biobank showed that, after adjustment for BMI and waist circumference, each 1-SD increase in hip circumference was associated with a 5% lower risk of coronary heart disease (HR, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.93–0.97). A cross-cohort reclassification analysis showed that among individuals with a "normal-weight" BMI, 5% had an elevated waist circumference and 18% had an elevated waist-to-hip ratio; most of these individuals, who were not identified by BMI-based classification, had a 15%–50% increased risk of cardiovascular outcomes. A Chinese population cohort showed that dynamic changes in the weight-adjusted waist index were independently associated with cardiovascular and cerebrovascular mortality, with the group showing the largest increase having a 1.52-fold higher risk than the lowest group. Upper-body fat risk exhibited a dose-dependent pattern: a high visceral adiposity index was associated with a 55% increased risk of cardiovascular disease (risk ratio (RR), 1.55; 95% CI, 1.36–1.76). The causal signal for visceral adipose tissue (VAT) is highly sensitive to exposure definition and inferential framework. Within an MR framework using MRI-measured VAT volume and BMI adjustment, VAT had no robust effect on atherosclerotic outcomes. In contrast, observational associations of BMI-adjusted MRI-defined VAT showed a positive signal. An MR study across multiple vascular beds used MRI-derived fat depots as exposure measures. After BMI adjustment, each 1-SD increase in gluteofemoral adipose tissue (GFAT) volume was associated with 17%, 24%, and 28% lower risks of myocardial infarction, large-artery atherosclerotic stroke, and peripheral artery disease, respectively. These effects attenuated but remained significant after adjustment for lipids. In contrast, causal estimates for waist-to-hip ratio (WHR) and hip circumference were not robust in sensitivity analyses. Sex-specific MR showed that the causal association between WHR and coronary heart disease was significant in women (OR, 1.16; 95% CI, 1.06–1.26) but not in men. At the mechanistic level, paired chromatin landscape analysis of subcutaneous adipose tissue (SAT) and omental visceral adipose tissue (OVAT) showed that OVAT-specific differentially accessible regions were approximately twice as numerous as those in SAT and were enriched at promoters of cardiomyopathy-related genes. AI-driven large-scale clinical phenotyping in 101,243 patients showed that individuals positive for brown adipose tissue (BAT) had a lower prevalence of cardiovascular and psychiatric diseases. Higher BAT activity was associated with lower odds of cardiometabolic disease, and angiotensin receptor blocker use was positively associated with BAT, suggesting that BAT has preliminary druggable-target signals, although causal and hard-endpoint evidence is not yet established. A retrospective cohort of 13,530 patients undergoing PET/CT further showed that BAT positivity was independently associated with a lower incidence of cardiovascular events (P=0.018). Perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT) and epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) influence arterial stiffness, ventricular remodeling, and arrhythmias through paracrine pathways adjacent to target organs. EAT volume was independently associated with new-onset atrial fibrillation (HR per 1-SD increase, 1.29; 95% CI, 1.05–1.58; still significant after adjustment for BMI and left atrial volume). The CT-accessible Fat Attenuation Index has translated the inflammatory phenotype of PVAT into a clinically deployable prognostic tool; pericoronary adipose tissue (PCAT) attenuation was significantly associated with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) risk (HR, 1.58; 95% CI, 1.38–1.81) and all-cause mortality (HR, 1.77), but this effect size was highly sensitive to analytical strategy. Radiomic quantification of EAT volume and the PVAT inflammatory phenotype jointly support the feasibility of opportunistic risk stratification. At the intervention level, several lines of evidence jointly support "distribution improvement" as an independent dimension for evaluating interventions beyond weight loss alone. These include CENTRAL/DIRECT-PLUS, the primary and mediation analyses of SELECT, comparisons of VAT reduction across different intervention pathways, the SUMMIT CMR substudy, the DAPA-EAT trial, and evidence on dapagliflozin and EAT. Heart failure outcomes exhibit heterogeneity by ejection fraction phenotype. A prospective cohort of 428,000 participants in the UK Biobank showed that heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) was independently associated with all adiposity measures (VAT: HR, 1.23), whereas heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) was not independently associated with adiposity measures. EAT was consistently associated with harm in HFpEF/heart failure with mildly reduced ejection fraction (HFmrEF) but showed a paradoxical association in HFrEF. Among patients with HFpEF, 91% had an elevated waist circumference and 85% had elevated VAT, but only 38% met the BMI criterion for obesity. The PARAGON-HF trial further showed that the prevalence of central obesity (waist-to-height ratio (WHtR) ≥0.5) in HFpEF was as high as 96%, whereas BMI-defined obesity was present in only 49%. items.abstract: This study aimed to construct and externally validate a multimodal radiopathomic fusion model for predicting postoperative recurrence in patients with primary liver cancer (restricted to hepatocellular carcinoma, excluding intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma and mixed-type hepatocellular-cholangiocarcinoma) after curative hepatectomy, and to explore its independent prognostic efficacy and clinical utility. A total of 280 primary liver cancer patients from two centers were retrospectively allocated to a training cohort (n = 182) and an independent validation cohort (n = 98). Radiomic features were extracted from preoperative abdominal MRI, while pathomic features were quantified from H&E-stained whole-slide images. Eight machine learning algorithms were screened via fivefold cross‑validation for unimodal model development. The optimal random forest classifier was applied to construct unimodal radiomic‑only and pathomic‑only models, whereas the final multimodal fusion model was built using logistic regression with concatenated pre‑screened radiomic and pathomic features. ROC, SHAP, Kaplan-Meier survival, and logistic regression analyses were conducted to assess model performance, risk stratification, and independent predictors. Baseline characteristics were comparable between the two cohorts. We extracted 3390 MRI radiomic and 1039 pathomic features and then built single-modal and fusion models. The fusion model outperformed unimodal models (AUC = 0.894 training, 0.858 validation). It stratified patients into low-/high-recurrence risk subgroups (HR = 9.93 and 5.32). Multivariable analysis confirmed Fusion_Risk score (HR = 18.73) as the strongest independent recurrence predictor, superior to routine clinicopathological biomarkers. The radiopathomic fusion model showed good calibration and satisfactory net clinical benefit. Compared with unimodal models, it exhibited a trend toward improved predictive performance, suggesting potential value as an independent prognostic tool for individualized postoperative recurrence surveillance in patients with primary liver cancer after curative resection.

items.abstract: Deep learning models for medical imaging often exhibit demographic bias, leading to performance disparities across protected groups such as age, gender, and race. This study proposes a debiasing framework to reduce such disparities while maintaining diagnostic accuracy. We propose a Siamese neural network trained using triplet loss, where demographic attributes are incorporated into triplet selection to encourage separation by disease class while promoting within-class similarity across demographic groups. The method was evaluated on pleural effusion detection using chest X-rays (109,005 images from 41,063 patients) and Alzheimer's disease classification using brain MRI (1494 scans from 348 patients). Performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), precision, and true positive rate, along with equalized odds difference. The proposed method significantly reduced demographic disparities while maintaining or improving overall predictive performance compared with baseline and existing debiasing approaches. In pleural effusion detection, true positive rate gaps were reduced by 32% (race), 8% (age), and 22% (gender). In Alzheimer's disease classification, the true positive rate gap was reduced by 41% (age). Model interpretation indicated clinically meaningful imaging features were used for decision-making. Demographic-aware triplet sampling within a Siamese framework can effectively mitigate demographic performance disparities in medical imaging models while maintaining competitive overall diagnostic performance, suggesting potential for more equitable and clinically reliable deployment of medical imaging AI systems.

items.abstract: Reported accuracy of deep learning mandibular canal segmentation varies widely, and studies differ in how it was evaluated. This systematic review estimated accuracy under explicit validity criteria and described how it varied with evaluation design. Five databases were searched to May 2026 (PROSPERO CRD420261403406). Dice similarity coefficients (DSCs) from three-dimensional, patient-level-partitioned cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) or CT test sets were pooled by random-effects meta-analysis on the logit scale. Public benchmark results were analyzed separately, and test sets whose reference was generated by the evaluated model were not pooled. Fifty-four studies were included. Pooled DSC across 15 studies was 0.826 (95% confidence interval 0.752-0.881; 95% prediction interval 0.444-0.966), close to three previous reviews with different inclusion rules (0.80-0.84). The 16 CBCT studies ineligible for pooling, mostly for two-dimensional slice-level segmentation or fewer than 10 test patients, reported a higher median DSC (0.860 versus 0.803). Two systems on the official ToothFairy test set had a pooled DSC of 0.751. Internal and external estimates did not differ significantly (P = .974), but five external studies cannot establish equivalence. Pooled 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance across seven studies was 1.15 mm, with a prediction interval extending to 6.11 mm. Risk of bias was unclear or high in 14 of 15 pooled studies, and certainty of evidence was very low. Average accuracy is consistent across reviews, higher median values came, descriptively, from less constrained evaluations, and external evidence is too limited to show that performance transfers to new settings. Expert verification and prospective external validation remain necessary.

items.abstract: Transseptal puncture (TSP) is a critical step during atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation, and accurate anatomical understanding of the interatrial septum is essential for individualized procedural planning. Intracardiac echocardiography (ICE) provides real-time visualization of septal anatomy but is limited by its two-dimensional representation and operator dependence. This study developed an artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted multimodal imaging framework integrating preprocedural computed tomography angiography (CTA) with intraoperative ICE to provide patient-specific three-dimensional (3D) anatomical guidance for TSP planning. This single-center study enrolled 700 patients undergoing AF ablation. An AI framework was developed using data from 500 patients to perform automated segmentation, 3D reconstruction, and CTA-ICE multimodal image integration. The framework was evaluated in an independent temporal validation cohort of 200 patients. The primary outcome was the influence of AI-assisted anatomical information on individualized TSP planning, assessed by changes in puncture strategy following AI-assisted assessment. Secondary outcomes included decision confidence, planning time, interreader agreement, and procedural feasibility. The AI framework achieved an overall Dice similarity coefficient of 0.854 for automated anatomical segmentation and a Dice coefficient of 0.862 for 3D left atrial reconstruction. In the temporal validation cohort, at least one AI-recommended adjustment was incorporated into the final TSP strategy in 68 patients (34.0%). The recommendations addressed involved three key components of TSP planning: puncture site category in 52 patients (26.0%), puncture direction in 61 patients (30.5%), and puncture trajectory or angle in 74 patients (37.0%). AI-assisted assessment increased decision confidence (4.3 ± 0.6 vs. 3.4 ± 0.8, p < 0.001), reduced planning time (28.7 ± 10.3 vs. 42.5 ± 15.2 s, p < 0.001), and improved interreader agreement for anatomical assessment. In the temporal validation cohort, acute successful TSP was achieved in 196 patients (98.0%), with a mean transseptal time of 6.8-2.5 min and an overall complication rate of 3.0%. AI-assisted integration of preprocedural CTA with intraoperative ICE provides patient-specific 3D anatomical information that supports individualized TSP planning. The proposed framework demonstrated feasibility and compatibility with anatomical assessment and procedural planning, hopefully contributing to improve procedural or clinical outcomes.

items.abstract: Purpose Three-dimensional (3D) preoperative planning is essential in total hip arthroplasty (THA) to optimize implant alignment and reduce the risk of impingement-related complications such as dislocation. Although recent technological advances, including computed tomography (CT)-based navigation and robotic-assisted surgery, have improved the accuracy of implant placement, variation in preoperative planning among surgeons remains poorly understood. This study aimed to quantify inter-surgeon variation in 3D preoperative THA planning and to evaluate the impact of stem design on this variation. Methods Eleven hip surgeons independently performed 3D preoperative planning for 50 THA cases using a CT-based planning system. The cases included two stem types: tapered wedge stems and anatomical stems. Implant size was fixed, and planning was performed according to the combined anteversion theory. Inter-surgeon variation in implant orientation and position was quantified using the mean pairwise absolute difference (MPD) and intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC). The surgeon-selected cup-stem anteversion combinations were grouped into five categories, and inter-surgeon agreement was assessed using Fleiss' kappa coefficient. Results Angular MPDs ranged from 0.8° to 3.8°, with the greatest variation observed in stem anteversion. Positional MPDs ranged from 0.8 to 2.1 mm, with the largest variation observed along the stem craniocaudal axis. The ICCs ranged from 0.69 to 0.99. Agreement in cup-stem anteversion categories was moderate (kappa = 0.44). When the two stem groups were compared, no significant differences in angular variation were observed, while only limited differences in positional variation were found. Conclusion Inter-surgeon variation assessed by MPD provided a direct measure of the absolute magnitude of differences among surgeons' plans. Our findings demonstrate that noticeable inter-surgeon variation exists in preoperative THA planning despite high agreement coefficients. Quantitative benchmarks derived from these data may be useful for evaluating planning consistency and for validating emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence-based automated THA planning systems.

items.abstract: Rationale and objectives To identify the 5 most well-cited manuscripts written by American radiologists across 5 time periods from 2000 to 2025 within 10 disciplines of radiology and to characterize those manuscripts, authors, journals in which they were published, and institutions of origin. Materials and methods In this cross-sectional bibliometric study, American academic radiology faculty rosters were compiled from 174 institutions, yielding 7366 members. Their 248,754 Scopus-indexed manuscripts were screened, and the most-cited publications in each of 5 windows (2000-2005, 2006-2010, 2011-2015, 2016-2020, 2021-2025) were screened for those publications where radiology faculty occupied first or last author positions. The radiology subspecialty was assigned by manuscript content by subspecialty journal, weighted MeSH (Medical Subject Headings) scoring, and large language model classification-with manual verification of top-ranked articles. The 5 most-cited manuscripts were selected in 10 radiology subspecialties, per timeframe, yielding 250 papers. Results The 250 manuscripts were anchored by 205 radiologists; 49 authors contributed more than one paper, and 4 authors contributed 5 or more top manuscripts. Compared with the full roster, anchor authors were more often full professors (78.1% vs 24.5%), MD-PhDs (17.1% vs 5.8%), and men (73.2% vs 65.9%, P = 0.04). Neuroradiology accounted for the highest cumulative median citation count (1568), double that of the next field, cardiothoracic imaging (739). Radiology published 57 manuscripts, but general medical journals such as NEJM and JAMA yielded higher median citations. Four institutions contributed >10 of the first-authored papers. Conclusion Radiologists' most-cited literature is dominated by senior authors who often publish multiple high-ranking papers, favoring select institutions, topics, and journals.

items.abstract: Background In Ayurveda, bitter (Tikta) formulations are prescribed for the resolution of inflammatory conditions. Genetic variation in the taste receptor TAS2R38 influences both taste perception and inflammatory responses by differentially activating ligands, a phenomenon widely observed in Ayurvedic herbs. Objective Given differences in dosage calibration based on Prakriti, we explored whether Prakriti-based stratification correlates with TAS2R38 genetic variation and bitter taste perception thresholds. Materials and methods A total of 337 Prakriti-assessed healthy individuals were recruited for bitter taste using Phenylthiocarbamide (PTC) with the Bartovation® taste kit on a 0-5 intensity scale, and participants were categorized as non-tasters, recessive tasters, or dominant supertasters (293 phenotyped). Genotyping of three canonical TAS2R38 SNPs (rs713598, rs1726866, and rs10246939) was performed using Sanger sequencing and SNaPshot assays(327genotyped). Haplotypes (PAV-taster; AVI-non-taster) were inferred and analyzed for Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium (HWE), and associations with Prakriti were assessed using chi-square, Kruskal-Wallis, and Cramér's V tests. Additionally, in silico docking of bitter phytochemicals (BitterDB) was conducted using an AlphaFold-derived TAS2R38 structure. Results PTC phenotypes and genotypes were concordant and in HWE. Distribution included 9.8% PAV/PAV, 47.4% PAV/AVI, and 36.1% AVI/AVI, corresponding to taster and non-taster phenotypes. Noteworthy, there was no significant difference between Prakriti groups and within each group the genotypes and phenotypes were in HWE. Docking analysis of bitter compounds selected from IMPPAT plants on TAS2R38 revealed some Ayurvedic phytochemicals that showed potential affinity. Conclusion Genetic variability could confer differences in therapeutic response to Tikta formulations that modulate their effects through TAS2R38, within the same Prakriti group. Integrating taste phenotyping and genetic markers could assist in Dashavidha Pariksha and resolve Upshaya-Anupshaya during diagnosis and treatment and provide evidence-based optimal personalized selection of Tikta medicines.

items.abstract: Biomolecular structure prediction tools such as AlphaFold have achieved remarkable success in predicting structures of single proteins and multiprotein complexes. AlphaFold3 now incorporates the capability to model complexes containing nucleic acids and chemically modified side chains. Investigators can now predict structures of proteins bound to chromatin, where interactions with nucleosomal DNA and histone posttranslational modifications (PTMs) converge to control genome function. To evaluate its robustness in modeling chromatin complexes, we benchmarked AlphaFold3 on 115 structures containing nucleosomes whose coordinates were released by the Protein Data Bank after the training set cutoff date. We find that AlphaFold3 excels at predicting interactions with the histone octamer core and with PTMs. By contrast, AlphaFold3 struggles to predict structures of chromatin factors that primarily engage nucleosomal DNA, notably transcription factors and chromatin remodelers. We also show that AlphaFold3 can faithfully recapitulate known PTM recognition patterns, matching experimentally determined specificity profiles. This assessment of the capabilities and limitations of AlphaFold3 in chromatin structural biology provides a roadmap for its effective application to studies of chromatin regulation and PTM readout, while identifying key areas for future refinement of algorithms for predicting interactions between proteins and nucleic acids.
