items.abstract: Pathogens exploit host cellular machinery through protein-protein interactions (PPIs), often using molecular mimicry to hijack host cellular processes. While there have been thousands of host-pathogen PPIs determined to date, the lack of structural information for these impedes the study of the prevalence of molecular mimicry and convergent evolution of protein interaction interfaces. To address this, we benchmarked AlphaFold2 and 3 for prediction of structures of host-pathogen interactions observing that accurate models can be retrieved when ranking by modelling confidence, despite an overall low performance. We predicted structures for 6,782 pathogen-human PPIs yielding 803 models of higher confidence. Most pathogen proteins interacting with a common human protein are predicted to do so via the same interface, suggesting a high degree of convergent evolution of protein interaction interfaces. When comparing structural models from host-pathogen and host-host interactions, we observe that a majority of pathogen proteins are predicted to target existing human PPI interfaces. We categorized instances of mimicry into different modes, occurring at different frequencies: 1) via the same domain family (least common); 2) via a similar structural motif; and 3) via a similar linear peptide (most common). We selected examples of linear peptide interactions for binding assay testing, confirming 8 out of 12 predicted interfaces, including 3 viral linear peptide interactions. This validates AlphaFold's ability to model some host-pathogen interactions and the mechanisms underlying molecular mimicry. This work showcases the value of large-scale structural modelling to study convergent evolution of host-pathogen interactions and how molecular mimicry may contribute to infection or host defense.

items.abstract: Recent advancements in protein structure prediction methods have ushered in a new era of abundant and accurate structural data, providing opportunities to analyse proteins at a scale that has not been possible before. Here we performed a large-scale analysis of physicochemical properties across 373,779 confident AlphaFold structures. Our analysis revealed systematic variation between proteins from different organisms to such an extent that major features of the tree of life could be recovered from these data. Surprisingly, this relationship persisted even when we restricted our analysis to eukaryotic, cytosolic proteins and proteins from single AlphaFold Database Foldseek clusters. Given the strong functional constraints on protein chemistry, this finding is unexpected and suggests that protein structures have organism-specific physicochemical signatures, which might reveal evolutionary constraints imposed by the cellular environment and could have significant implications for the design and engineering of novel proteins.

items.abstract: Alkanes are ubiquitous in the ocean due to natural seepage, microbial synthesis, and anthropogenic activities. The Alcanivorax lineage is the dominant bacteria in alkane removal and maintaining marine ecological balance, but its alkane adaptation mechanisms remain incompletely explained. Here, we found widespread redundancy of alkane-specific outer membrane transporters (OmpTs) in the upstream of alkane metabolism in the Alcanivorax lineage, which may be a critical adaptive factor. In the representative Alloalcanivorax dieselolei B5, three highly similar OmpT-2 homologs, all with alkane transport function, exhibited functional redundancy; disruption of a single homolog moderately impairs the growth of strain B5 on n -hexadecane, with additive inhibitory effect upon double mutation, but none abolished alkane utilization. Phylogenetic and mobile genetic element analysis indicated that inter-species horizontal gene transfer drove OmpT-2 redundancy in strain B5. Analysis of AlphaFold-derived structures suggests that OmpTs of B5 clustered with the alkane uptake protein A (AupA) from Marinobacter and appear to lack a lateral β-barrel opening, which may imply a plausible vertical alkane transport mechanism instead of the classical FadL-type lateral transport. These results suggest that functional redundancy and distinct transport mechanism of alkane transporters may be one reason for the Alcanivorax lineage being the dominant marine alkane-degrading bacteria. Importance The Alcanivorax lineage constitutes the major group of obligate hydrocarbonoclastic bacteria (OHCB) that mediates alkane cycling in the global ocean, while their molecular adaptive mechanisms remain poorly characterized. This study demonstrates widespread genetic redundancy of the alkane-specific outer membrane transporter (OmpT) across the Alcanivorax lineage. In the model strain Alloalcanivorax dieselolei B5, three OmpT-2 homologs have been shown to exert additive effects on alkane transport. Inter-species horizontal gene transfer potentially drives the genetic redundancy of these genes. We further propose a hypothesis that OmpT transports alkane through a unique vertical mechanism instead of the canonical lateral transport mode of FadL family proteins. Our results provide new molecular insights into the broad adaptation of this lineage to marine alkane metabolism.

items.summary: Abstract Accurate localization of non-palpable breast tumors is a major challenge in breast-conserving surgery, because differences in patient position between preoperative imaging and surgery, together with breast mobility, anatomical variability and tissue deformation, may substantially alter tumor position. The clinically relevant, measurable factors that influence image-to-surgery breast tumor displacement…
items.abstract: Abstract Accurate localization of non-palpable breast tumors is a major challenge in breast-conserving surgery, because differences in patient position between preoperative imaging and surgery, together with breast mobility, anatomical variability and tissue deformation, may substantially alter tumor position. The clinically relevant, measurable factors that influence image-to-surgery breast tumor displacement (IS-BTD) have not been systematically established. We conducted a two-stage modified Delphi consensus among breast surgeons and breast-dedicated radiologists to identify factors perceived as influencing IS-BTD, supported by a focused literature review used to standardize terminology. The ranked features were then reviewed to retain those that were independent, measurable and reproducible. In total, 55 distinct features were identified, scored and ranked. Anatomical, positional and mechanical variables generally received higher weights than tumor-related characteristics; patient position received the highest weight (3.3), followed by breast ptosis (3.1) and breast size (3.0). This consensus provides a prioritized set of measurable features for investigating IS-BTD and a foundation for feature selection in future biomechanical and artificial intelligence-based models for perioperative breast tumor localization.

items.abstract: Vision-language models have become a new kind of describer, writing about almost anything people see, and their descriptions now shape how cultures are known by people and by other models. Descriptions of cultures tend to turn particular things into types, and what a description loses shows what its describer lacks. We introduce Polytropos, a benchmark that measures what model descriptions of cultural objects keep of the particular object by turning each description back into an image and comparing it with the original photograph. On 374 objects from the Metropolitan Museum of Art and the Getty, with 1,870 descriptions from five models and 230 written by curators, reconstructions are recognised as the recorded culture more often than the photographs, at 54.55% to 59.09% against 52.14%, yet 16% to 21% of objects change outcome and only 0.49% of reconstructions are identified as the specific object. On the same objects, models lose recorded cultures at a rate similar to curators but gain more. Model descriptions give each object many faces, each typical of its culture and almost none the object itself.

items.abstract: Touchard and the author asked whether every valued hyperfield, in Krasner's sense with the norm axiom, is of the form H_ρ(K): a valued field K read up to relative error ρ. The question turns on the norm axiom. If a valued hyperfield is a quotient K^times/Tcup{0} of a field, the norm axiom forces T=1+m_ρ for a valuation on K. This completes the proof of a published proposition, and it makes the question equivalent to asking whether every Krasner valued hyperfield is such a quotient. For value group Z we prove directly that it is. Without the norm axiom the answer is negative. Layering a hyperfield over a non-trivial ordered abelian group gives a factor hyperfield exactly when the hyperfield itself is one, so Massouros's hyperfields yield hyperfields with a non-trivial valuation, satisfying all the other axioms, that are not factor hyperfields. The general question remains open.

items.abstract: Current MLLM methods largely focus on whether models attend to the right visual regions, implicitly treating spatial attention map as the primary key of effective visual perception. To examine this assumption, we introduce a medical VQA dataset with paired non-contrast (NC) and contrast-enhanced (CE) images that share corresponding anatomy while providing different cues. We show that this view is incomplete: across paired NC and CE medical images, MLLMs often exhibit similar attention patterns despite producing contrasting answers, while controlled bidirectional interventions induce substantially larger prediction changes on visual values than attention weights. These results identify the visual content retrieved through values as a critical factor in improving perception beyond spatial attention alone. Guided by this finding, we propose VIVID (VIsual Value Intervention Distillation), which uses enhanced visual values to identify and refine teacher corrections aligned with useful visual evidence to improve on-policy distillation from CE to NC images. Across six internal and external test sets, VIVID consistently outperforms existing on-policy distillation methods across different model scales and architectures, requires only NC images at inference, and maintains strong zero-shot performance on general-domain VQA benchmarks. The project page is available at https://qiuzyc.github.io/VIVID.

items.abstract: AI-driven game development holds the potential to transform diverse human inspirations into interactive experiences. However, existing systems and benchmarks primarily focus on explicit development specifications, with limited support for adapting multimodal references and evaluating actual gameplay experiences. We introduce GameAnything, an open-source agentic platform that transforms multimodal inspirations into playable extensions of existing games through iterative development. GameAnything integrates coding agents with an independent playtesting critic, persistent development state, and reusable experience memory to support continuous refinement. We further present GameAnything-Bench, a benchmark spanning diverse reference modalities, game creation objectives, and gaming environments, with exploratory gameplay testing to assess both functional correctness and gameplay quality. Evaluations of nine coding agent configurations reveal that current agents can adapt reference content but still struggle with playable interactions and precise modifications. Moreover, multimodal references improve content fidelity, while iterative refinement yields substantial but varying improvements across agents. These findings highlight both the potential and remaining challenges of inspiration-driven game development.

items.title: A Glimpse of Training VLMs as Foundation Models for Robotic Manipulation
items.summary: Recently, GPT-6 Astra demonstrates strong generalization in robot control, yet limited disclosure of its training leaves open how such capabilities can be reproduced. We introduce nanoAstra, an approach to training vision-language models (VLMs) for generalizable manipulation that combines semantic action modeling with capability-preserving supervised fine-tuning (CP-SFT). nanoAstra represents robot behavior as…
items.abstract: Recently, GPT-6 Astra demonstrates strong generalization in robot control, yet limited disclosure of its training leaves open how such capabilities can be reproduced. We introduce nanoAstra, an approach to training vision-language models (VLMs) for generalizable manipulation that combines semantic action modeling with capability-preserving supervised fine-tuning (CP-SFT). nanoAstra represents robot behavior as semantic steps composed of reusable, parameterized action primitives, guided by explicit progress descriptions. Meanwhile, CP-SFT uses an explicit robot-specific system prompt to constrain manipulation outputs to a structured action space, aiming to focus adaptation on robot-specific contexts and promote specialization while minimizing interference with broader pretrained capabilities. With this formulation, we train nanoAstra on more than 5,000 hours of robot data together with general VQA data. On RoboTwin 2.0's randomized benchmark, nanoAstra-9B achieves a 17.8% zero-shot success rate, substantially outperforming advanced VLA and WAM baselines as well as similarly sized VLMs. With inference faster than the corresponding motion execution on a single H20 GPU, our model supports action-chunk-like streaming execution that overlaps inference with motion, reducing the robot's idle time from 35.0% to 6.9%.

items.title: Predicting long-term tumor response to Gamma Knife radiosurgery in vestibular schwannoma: an integrated model of auto-segmentation, MRI radiomics, and dosimetric parameters.

items.abstract: Vestibular schwannoma (VS) is a common benign intracranial tumor for which Gamma Knife radiosurgery (GKRS) is an important treatment option. However, post-treatment changes in tumor volume vary considerably and can complicate follow-up and response assessment. This study developed a framework that uses deep learning-based segmentation and MRI radiomics to predict long-term treatment response to GKRS for VS. We developed an nnU-Net model to automate VS segmentation on contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI. Patients with long-term follow-up after GKRS were classified into four response patterns: direct regression, delayed regression, stable disease, and growth. A two-stage machine-learning framework was then constructed. Stage 1 distinguishes regression from non-regression, while Stage 2 differentiates direct from delayed regression. Pretreatment MRI radiomics features were combined with clinical and dose-related variables and used to train multiple machine-learning models. The models were evaluated using five-fold cross-validation, and SHAP analysis was used to interpret the results. The nnU-Net model achieved a mean Dice similarity coefficient of 91.16 ± 0.47% on the external test dataset. Among the 155 patients, 53 showed direct regression, 83 delayed regression, 9 stable disease, and 10 tumor growths. In Stage 1, the Balanced Random Forest algorithm achieved accuracy of 74.19 ± 7.21%, an AUROC of 72.43 ± 10.18%, and AUPRC of 93.08 ± 4.27%. In Stage 2, the Support Vector Machine achieved accuracy of 64.05 ± 4.16%, an AUROC of 66.70 ± 6.21%, and AUPRC of 57.10 ± 7.30%. SHAP analysis identified radiomics and dose-related features as important predictors. Deep learning-based segmentation combined with pretreatment MRI radiomics, clinical variables, and dose-related parameters may provide useful information for predicting long-term response after GKRS for VS. This framework could support more individualized follow-up planning and help clinicians distinguish delayed regression from treatment failure.

items.abstract: Cell expansion and manufacturing processes inevitably induce cellular aging across multiple biological facets that compromise therapeutic potency. However, existing monitoring methods are destructive and reduce readouts to a population-averaged value, obscuring the multiple biological facets of aging that differentially affect potency. Moreover, conventional molecular aging markers yield readouts on disparate scales, hindering their integration into a unified and interpretable quantitative metric. Here, an Aging Phenotypic Index (API) is introduced, a label-free, single-coordinate aging metric derived from machine learning integration of nanosensor chemical cytometry (NCC)-based single-cell phenotypes. NCC uses near-infrared (nIR) fluorescent single-walled carbon nanotube sensors to enable label-free quantification of cell size, eccentricity, effective refractive index, and H2O2 efflux from the same individual cell, using cell-induced lensing to extract morphological and molecular features simultaneously. Machine learning integrates these multiplex phenotypes into a continuous API that quantitatively represents a passage-associated phenotypic aging state, and the API, together with molecular aging markers, defines a quantitative aging axis. Across human adipose-derived stromal cells, higher API values are associated with reduced population-level angiogenic and secretory potency. This nanosensor-enabled framework provides non-destructive, population-level potency-linked aging assessment, offering a scalable strategy for quality control and standardization in cell therapy manufacturing.

items.abstract: Understanding a scene requires both geometry and semantics: geometry recovers its spatial structure, and semantics separates it into objects. Current models obtain the two from separate networks or separate passes. We present PINE, a one-step Omni Diffusion Transformer that predicts the point map, the surface normals, and the instance map of an image in one forward pass. PINE treats each map as a token stream, and a stream mask decides which streams interact. A camera-aware ray encoding positions every token by its camera ray rather than its pixel. Grounding attention adds the affinity of pretrained DINOv3 features to the attention logits. Trained on only 139K synthetic images for geometry, PINE achieves state-of-the-art point maps whether or not intrinsics are given and the best average rank on surface normals. It also exceeds SAM on large objects with less than 1 percent of its training images, and it predicts all three maps 5.7x faster than MoGe-3 with SAM.

items.abstract: Representation alignment markedly accelerates diffusion training, but one-step generators raise a question that diffusion does not: which training path should receive the loss? A one-step generator sees two kinds of inputs. Corrupted real images come with their clean counterpart, which provides an instance-paired target. Samples generated from pure noise have no corresponding real image, yet this is where the final model operates. We study this question on Priming, which trains one-step generators from scratch by reconstructing corrupted images and then matching feature distributions with optimal transport. Aligning the generative path, the natural choice, collapses recall (0.45!to!0.15--0.25) in all 17 configurations we test, including five target constructions and loss weights down to 0.05. Aligning the paired reconstruction path with a frozen DINOv2 encoder instead helps in every setting we test. A short analysis explains this asymmetry: when the target carries no instance information about the input, the optimal aligned feature is constant within each class, so the loss pulls samples toward class prototypes. A control confirms this: aligning the paired path to a random same-class image instead of the input's own image removes most of the gain. Inside the generator, paired-path alignment creates an interface block through which post-training routes noise, and the image semantics carried through it predict sample quality across 16 models. The resulting recipe, \method, accelerates both training stages on ImageNet 256!times!256: it matches the 160-epoch baseline with 2times fewer priming epochs, surpasses its final quality with 4times fewer post-training updates, and lowers FID to 1.30 (B) and 1.155 (L) at the standard budget. A joint single-stage variant trains native one-step generators and reaches FID 1.22 with 115M parameters.

items.abstract: Visual agents navigate whole-slide images through magnified observations associated with claimed locations. However, a visually plausible observation does not necessarily originate from its claimed location, particularly across magnifications and in regions with similar tissue structures. We formulate cross-magnification provenance verification (CMPV) to evaluate whether visual evidence supports a claimed spatial association, recover the source when possible, and abstain when evidence is insufficient. We introduce PyraFault, a benchmark of 3.06 million coordinate-supervised examples from 2,200 cases across five TCGA cohorts, covering within-context substitutions, absent-source faults, and geometric perturbations. We further propose ZoomTrace, a claim-independent verifier that estimates the observation's source before evaluating its agreement with the claimed location. It combines physical-scale alignment, visual retrieval, geometric refinement, and reliability estimation using spatially disjoint competing matches. On 503,320 test examples, ZoomTrace achieves 0.969 AUPRC and 0.987 AUROC, compared with 0.789 and 0.903 for Efficient LoFTR. Further evaluations reveal trade-offs in reliability estimation and limitations in vision-language models, cross-dataset retrieval, and calibration. Integrating ZoomTrace into visual agent tool paths reduces exposure to corrupted observations and silent failures, while downstream accuracy improvements depend on the agent and verification threshold.

items.title: PhyCoVE: Benchmarking Physical Counterfactual Video Editing across Diverse Material Dynamics
items.summary: Physical counterfactual video editing turns a source video and a language-specified physical edit at a given execution frame into a counterfactual video that shows how the scene would evolve after the edit. Existing evaluations with counterfactual target videos mainly cover object removal or specific rigid-body motions, although real scenes also involve elastic deformation, fluid flow, and interactions among rigid…
items.abstract: Physical counterfactual video editing turns a source video and a language-specified physical edit at a given execution frame into a counterfactual video that shows how the scene would evolve after the edit. Existing evaluations with counterfactual target videos mainly cover object removal or specific rigid-body motions, although real scenes also involve elastic deformation, fluid flow, and interactions among rigid bodies, elastic solids, and fluids. We introduce PhyCoVE, a benchmark of 533 cases on 110 source videos that covers rigid, elastic, and fluid dynamics in five interaction patterns, with edits that remove an object, change a physical quantity, or insert a new object. For the simulated cases, a language model proposes scene designs, coding agents build them with solvers suited to each material and physically based rendering and then simulate each edit from the source scene state, and humans check every stage. For the real cases, we record continuously from one camera position before and after each edit. We also propose counterfactual fidelity, a metric that applies across materials and their interactions and measures how much of the physical change from the source video to the target video a generated video reproduces. We evaluate seven open-source and commercial video editing models and find that counterfactual fidelity ranks them nearly as human preference does, but even the best model reproduces only about one seventh of the physical change. The models change how a scene looks but rarely how it evolves, whereas a physical edit requires understanding the dynamics that it changes. Physical counterfactual video editing thus remains far from solved, and PhyCoVE provides a foundation for developing and evaluating methods for it.

items.abstract: Efficient AI computation depends on hardware that evolves over time, shifting the strategies needed to implement performant code. For CPU kernels, a key evolving factor is the set of available architectural extensions, which expose specialized hardware instructions that change the techniques used to optimize kernels. We study how effectively coding agents use these new, potentially unfamiliar extensions to write fast code. We introduce KernelShift, a benchmarking pipeline and a set of environments for evaluating coding agents in kernel optimization across evolving CPU architectures. Its agent-assisted, human-verified pipeline turns code repositories into benchmark instances, and its environments let agents optimize code with feedback from the target hardware. Using this pipeline, we construct 99 kernels from real-world, actively developed repositories (ncnn, llama.cpp, Arm SIMD Loops, and KleidiAI), including inference workloads derived from real model executions. KernelShift supports incorporating new kernels and hardware configurations as libraries and processors evolve. We evaluate agents with proprietary and open-weight models across progressively newer architectural extensions (Arm Neon, SVE, SVE2, and SME2), examining how performance changes as hardware evolves. On established extensions, agents beat the auto-vectorized compiler everywhere (2.4-19.8x) and exceed general-purpose libraries such as ncnn (getting up to 2.74x over its Neon kernels), but fall behind Arm's hand-tuned KleidiAI kernels (0.70x). In end-to-end inference of two LLMs, agent-written kernels achieve a 1.3-1.6x prefill speedup over llama.cpp's fast path. However, current agents do not yet reliably adapt to new extensions that require unfamiliar programming models, such as SME2's matrix tiles.

items.abstract: Background Accurate identification of mandibular invasion by oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is important for virtual surgical planning, but manual delineation on CT is challenging and time-consuming. This retrospective proof-of-concept study evaluated automated segmentation of the mandible and radiologically apparent bone invasion and explored centerline-based assessment of longitudinal tumor extent for computer-aided design/computer-aided manufacturing (CAD/CAM) planning. Methods Fifty preoperative CT examinations from 50 patients with histopathologically confirmed mandibular invasion were included. Thirty examinations were used for model development and 20 for independent testing. A three-dimensional MedNeXt architecture implemented within nnU-Net was trained applying expert-reviewed CT reference segmentations. Performance was assessed using Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), precision, recall, average symmetric surface distance and 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance. Spatial localization, longitudinal invasion-span differences and signed centerline-projected endpoint errors were assessed in the holdout cohort. Results Mean mandibular DSC was 0.965 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.961-0.969; median 0.967). Mean invasion DSC was 0.553 (95% CI, 0.425-0.660; median 0.623), with mean precision of 0.742 and recall of 0.483. Predicted invasion overlapped the CT reference in 18/20 examinations (90%); 16/20 (80%) achieved DSC ≥ 0.20. Two cases were completely missed. Among the 18 evaluable cases, the median absolute invasion-span difference was 7.01 mm (interquartile range, 5.08-13.00 mm) and the median symmetric endpoint distance was 5.88 mm (3.19-9.16 mm). Conclusions The present proof-of-concept study demonstrates the technical feasibility of automated CT segmentation of the mandible and radiologically apparent mandibular invasion by OSCC. The approach may support transmission of radiological tumor extent into virtual resection planning. Larger multicenter studies and prospective clinical validation are needed to establish its impact on planning accuracy and workflow efficiency.

items.abstract: The decay exponent α in KV-cache eviction is an intrinsic property of the model: calibrated once on a single corpus, it transfers directly across domains. Attention-based accumulation (H2O) and recency-based sliding windows (StreamingLLM) are two dominant eviction frameworks, often treated as unrelated, but we show that they are the two endpoints of a single power-law family: by scoring each token as s_i = A_i cdot (t-i)^{-α}, where A_i is cumulative attention and α controls the age penalty, H2O and StreamingLLM correspond to α=0 and αtoinfty, respectively (with StreamingLLM additionally hard-coding an attention-sink patch). The no-hair mechanism of xiang2026nohair bounds the admissible range of α, and the measured exponents agree: calibrating once on WikiText yields [0.556, 0.822] for a representative model (Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct). The per-model ranges are consistent across five models (410M--1.5B) and independently match the optimal regions from perplexity sweeps. NoHairCache achieves the lowest perplexity across three datasets (WikiText, PG19, and arXiv) without per-dataset tuning, outperforming both H2O and StreamingLLM (p < 0.05 on all three datasets, with 0.06--0.10 PPL gains over StreamingLLM at budget 512). On downstream four-way multiple-choice QA, it matches or outperforms StreamingLLM across all nine (task, budget) cells, retaining 98.2% of full-cache accuracy on NarrativeQA at 25% retention versus 91.1% for StreamingLLM; per-cell McNemar tests are not significant, so QA is corroborating only. We release our calibration script and drop-in scorer upon publication.

items.abstract: Asking a vision-language model (VLM) to think step by step often makes it worse at spatial questions, even though the image stays in context. We show that short chain-of-thought (CoT) turns a perception problem into a transcription problem. Once a VLM writes a spatial relation, its answer follows that sentence instead of the image, so whether CoT helps or hurts depends largely on whether the written relation is more accurate than answering directly. Studying 15 open VLMs (2B-38B) and six frontier closed models, we rule out token count, turn format, and visual forgetting in open models and trace the failure through three stages. First, writing re-weights visual cues, weakening a "lower is closer" shortcut in all 13 open models tested but also discarding valid cues, which produces false relations. Second, the written text takes over. With the model's own conclusion-removed rationale held fixed, swapping in an opposite-depth image moves the answer by 2-9 points on rendered twins (vs. up to 77 for direct answers) and by 3.0-3.4 points on average on natural photographs (vs. 20.5-69.6). Third, the concluding sentence can invert even a true relation, mainly on converse questions. Together, false relations and conclusion mis-mapping account for four in five CoT losses. Scale does not remove this bottleneck: Qwen3-VL-32B shows the same pattern. Frontier closed models are not hurt: they write relations as accurately as they answer, and three of six re-check the image after writing. The three queried with reasoning off lock in like open models, so re-grounding co-occurs with answer-turn reasoning; we identify answer-step re-grounding as the step open VLMs lack. In a single-model pilot, fine-tuning on fixed rationales with image-determined labels restores it on natural photographs. We open-sourced all our datasets and code at https://ming-zch.github.io/seeing-right-writing-wrong.

items.abstract: How much interaction experience is needed to distill a capable visual agent? We study learning from few tasks and recorded interaction histories. Our framework selects representative trajectories using skill-context coverage and ordered visual-decision similarity. On-policy distillation (OPD) learns through fresh interaction on selected tasks or fresh student responses at fixed histories. Across Navigation, Sokoban, and spatial mapping, even one online training task supports transfer to other tasks. Four fixed trajectories raise a 4B student's success from 49.17% to 82.08% on standard Navigation and from 60.16% to 85.55% on Sokoban, recovering over 90% of the measured gap to a 27B teacher on these panels. On an independent Navigation panel, replay improves success from 45.83% to 76.67%, retaining 91.36% of the same-task online gain without new interaction during optimization. Training repetitions, matched supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and a 9B extension further support the value of compact experience.

items.abstract: Frontier language models can now read and edit the weights of a neural network much like code and thereby improve a small model, an approach known as Weight-Space Programming (WSP). We further explore applying WSP to a language model itself, which we call Self-WSP. Specifically, Qwen3.5-0.8B reads its own weights, proposes an edit, and then continues with the edited weights as both problem solver and editor. We find many cases of genuine self-improvement. Self-edits can raise GSM8K accuracy from 11.8% to 62.2% and MATH500 accuracy from 7.0% to 32.2%, sometimes by changing only 16 parameters, and in some cases repeated self-editing keeps improving the model. A closer look, however, reveals that these gains lack interpretability. The model shows little understanding of the edits it makes, and WSP driven by random search sometimes performs comparably. Self-WSP thus holds promise as a path toward recursive self-improvement (RSI), but realizing this promise requires further exploration.

items.abstract: Cortical spreading depression (CSD) is a slowly propagating wave of near-complete neuronal depolarization underlying migraine aura and implicated in stroke, traumatic brain injury, and subarachnoid hemorrhage. Existing reaction-diffusion models of CSD treat the cortex as a flat Euclidean domain, ignoring its highly folded, individually variable geometry. We develop a fully covariant FitzHugh-Nagumo (FHN) reaction-diffusion system on a smooth compact Riemannian 2-manifold [Formula: see text] representing the cortical sheet, in which the Euclidean Laplacian is replaced by the Laplace-Beltrami operator [Formula: see text]. Three mathematical results are established: (i) local and global well-posedness in [Formula: see text] together with positive invariance of the physiological region via parabolic semigroup theory; (ii) a curvature-corrected eikonal relation [Formula: see text], in which the wavefront speed is modulated by the geodesic curvature of the front; and (iii) a sulcal-trapping theorem giving an explicit criterion under which an excitable wave entering a sulcus (negative Gauss curvature region) remains confined to it. Numerically, we develop two complementary solvers: a discrete exterior calculus (DEC) scheme on triangulated surfaces using the cotangent Laplacian with implicit-explicit (IMEX) time-stepping, and a physics-informed neural network (PINN) surrogate that evaluates [Formula: see text] via the closest-point projection of the ambient Euclidean Laplacian. The PINN framework supports both forward simulation and the inverse identification of excitability fields from sparse observations, and a noise-ablation study quantifies its practical identifiability. The parameters of the slow subsystem and of the coupling functions are inherited from our published, cohort-calibrated thalamocortical model, which was calibrated against 67 paired-pulse somatosensory evoked potential (SEP) recordings from nine analysable animals of a cohort of 14 male Wistar rats (1, 233 sweeps) acquired in the Neuroscience Laboratory of Gazi University, with CSD induced by topical KCl application. We validate convergence on [Formula: see text] with the spectral ground-truth [Formula: see text], exhibit a propagating ring wave with a refractory tail, and verify the eikonal-curvature prediction across two orders of magnitude in geodesic curvature, including the leading correction due to the recovery variable; a mesh-convergence study yields explicit resolution requirements for evaluating the trapping criterion on MRI-derived cortical surfaces.

items.abstract: Vertigo diagnosis has high stakes, since one symptom spans benign positional vertigo to stroke, while common vestibular audiology tools (VOG and CDP) face limitations including dependence on human expertise, high cost, and cross-sectional evaluation. The aim of this study is to critically assess the maturity of AI applications in the detection of vestibular disorders from a clinical audiology perspective, with the criterion of "readiness for clinical use" rather than just algorithmic accuracy. This narrative critical review was conducted, according to SANRA guidelines, based on searches in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and IEEE Xplore (2006-2026) and hand-checking of reference lists of key articles. Nystagmus analysis achieved F1 above 0.97 in rotational nystagmus; vestibular schwannoma segmentation reported a pooled Dice of 0.89 (95% CI: 0.88-0.90) with a meta-analysis of 56 models from 11 studies; and CNN/fuzzy posturography demonstrated 97% accuracy in assessing postural dysfunction after stroke. For ECochG, machine learning has been applied successfully to intracochlear recordings and to MRI-based endolymphatic hydrops assessment, but within the scope of this search we identified no study applying AI to click-evoked extratympanic ECochG waveforms, specifically the summating-potential to action-potential (SP/AP) ratio, for the diagnosis of endolymphatic hydrops in Ménière's disease. The progress of AI in this domain is heterogeneous; some subfields have reached relative maturity, but the ECochG-Ménière gap remains at the intersection of otherwise well-developed areas. Future priorities include multicenter standardization, prospective validation, and addressing the debated role of interpretability. The focus on English-language sources is a limitation of this review.

items.abstract: To evaluate the performance of AI algorithms in reducing gadolinium (Gd) administration in brain MRI by generating synthetic post-contrast images from low-dose inputs. Comprehensive searches of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase were conducted through April 17, 2026. Study screening, eligibility assessment, quality evaluation, and data extraction were performed independently by two reviewers. Pooled peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and structural similarity index (SSIM) values were calculated using a random-effects model. Heterogeneity was quantified using the I² statistic. These analyses were additionally followed by evaluations of the reported qualitative assessments. Twelve studies met the inclusion criteria, most of which used convolutional neural network architectures. The pooled PSNR was 32.91 dB (95% CI: 31.37-34.46; I² = 99.08%) across seven studies, and the pooled SSIM was 91.81% (95% CI: 89.33-94.30; I² = 99.69%) across six studies. Subgroup analyses stratified by contrast-dose reduction level, deep learning model type, and input modality did not identify consistent contributors to heterogeneity. Given substantial between-study heterogeneity, pooled estimates were interpreted descriptively. Across the qualitative assessments, synthetic images were generally rated as diagnostically acceptable or comparable to full-dose images for most tasks, although subtle differences in lesion conspicuity and artifact patterns were reported. AI models demonstrate promising technical performance for generating synthetic post-contrast brain MRI with high voxel-wise similarity to full-dose images at substantial contrast-dose reductions. However, marked heterogeneity, limited external validation, and the lack of clinically oriented diagnostic outcomes limit the interpretability and generalizability of current evidence. Question There is a need to determine how effectively artificial intelligence can reduce gadolinium use in brain MRI by generating synthetic post-contrast images from low-dose inputs. Findings Across 12 studies involving 3846 patients, AI-generated post-contrast brain MRI achieved pooled peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and structural similarity index (SSIM) values of 32.91 dB and 91.81%, respectively, with substantial between-study heterogeneity. Clinical relevance AI-assisted synthetic post-contrast imaging may substantially reduce gadolinium exposure in neuroradiology while preserving diagnostic confidence. However, high heterogeneity highlights the need for cautious interpretation and further multicenter standardization before clinical adoption.

items.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a major global health burden, with highly heterogeneous trajectories ranging from long-term stability to rapid progression towards kidney failure and kidney replacement therapy. Accurate prediction of CKD progression is essential to support personalised monitoring, timely therapeutic intensification, nephrology referral, and preparation for advanced kidney care. Artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and deep learning (DL) approaches may improve risk stratification by modelling complex, nonlinear, and time-dependent patterns in routinely collected clinical data, electronic health records, and potentially multimodal data sources. Nonetheless, it remains unclear how ready these AI-driven models are for clinical use. This structured narrative review aimed to map the current landscape of AI for predicting CKD progression, assess the robustness and clinical relevance of the evidence, and identify methodological and implementation gaps that must be addressed to translate technical accuracy into clinical impact. This review synthesised 35 studies published between 2020 and 2025 that developed and evaluated models to predict CKD progression. Most studies used retrospective cohort designs and electronic health record data, relying mainly on demographic variables, laboratory measures, comorbidities, and clinical history. Tree-based models, random forests, boosting methods, regression-based approaches, and neural networks were the most commonly investigated methods. Overall, the reviewed models often achieved favourable discriminative performance, as measured by AUROC or C-index. Nevertheless, the evidence base remains limited by substantial heterogeneity in study designs, cohort compositions, prediction targets, time horizons, feature engineering, and validation strategies. External validation was reported in only about one-quarter of studies, while calibration, clinical utility, patient-level uncertainty, and implementation-oriented evaluation were inconsistently addressed. Prediction endpoints were predominantly kidney failure-related. Multimodal data, including imaging, genomics, and social determinants of health, were rarely used, and explainability methods were more often applied for model description than for clinician-facing decision support. AI models show substantial promise for predicting CKD progression, particularly when trained on routinely available clinical data. However, the field remains more advanced in model development than in clinical validation and implementation. Future research should prioritise external and temporal validation, systematic calibration assessment, decision-curve or net-benefit analysis, comparison with established clinical risk scores, clinically meaningful prediction horizons, subgroup and fairness evaluation, patient-level uncertainty estimation, and prospective testing of model-informed care. These steps are essential to move from statistically accurate models to reliable, interpretable, equitable, and actionable tools for CKD management.

items.abstract: We present KMed-31B, a medical large language model post-trained from an open-weight model for on-premises deployment with limited hardware. Post-training a model for diverse medical tasks remains difficult, because improving one kind of task can lower performance on another. We attribute this to differences between tasks in expected output and available feedback. Medical question answering and diagnosis prediction have reference answers, whereas clinical inquiry has no single correct response and is judged with rubrics. We therefore divide medical training tasks into four categories by these two properties, train one specialist per category with a reward that its feedback supports, and integrate the specialists into a single student with Multi-teacher On-policy Delta Distillation (MOPD^2). For clinical inquiry, we build Synthetic Health Dialogue, a simulated corpus of consultations with lay users and clinicians whose patient cases span common clinical presentations in primary care. Relative to its base model, KMed-31B raises HealthBench Hard from 22.95 to 41.87 and HealthBench Professional from 37.92 to 50.20 in non-thinking mode, and from 23.80 to 51.48 and from 41.97 to 59.18 in thinking mode, while its scores on four multiple-choice medical benchmarks are maintained or slightly improved. KMed-31B has the highest unadjusted HealthBench Hard score among the compared models, including proprietary ones, and scores higher on HealthBench Professional than every open-weight model we compare, including models with more than ten times as many total parameters. Applied to another base model, Qwen3.8-27B, the same training recipe also raises both HealthBench scores. We describe the training recipe, data construction, and settings in detail so that institutions requiring on-premises deployment can develop medical models from open-weight foundations.

items.title: Don't Sleep, Keep Watch: Proactive Perception for Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: Computer-use agents (CUAs) built on vision-language models are increasingly entrusted with long-horizon tasks in live desktop, web, and mobile environments, where the screen keeps changing on its own. items.abstract: Computer-use agents (CUAs) built on vision-language models are increasingly entrusted with long-horizon tasks in live desktop, web, and mobile environments, where the screen keeps changing on its own. However, current CUAs lack real-time situational awareness: they perceive the environment through discrete snapshots, and the substantial inference latency of VLMs, compounded by highly dynamic interfaces, opens a perception-action gap in which the observed state frequently becomes stale before the corresponding action is executed. To bridge this gap, we present NightWatch, a plug-and-play framework that endows any CUA with continuous, temporally grounded perception without changing the agent's model, prompt, or action space. NightWatch couples the VLM agent with NightWatch-0.8B, a lightweight System-1 model that performs streaming monitoring of the interface state and keeps the agent synchronized with the evolving environment at low computational cost and latency, thereby grounding each decision in the current state rather than an outdated snapshot and reducing both stale actions and idle waiting while preserving task success. Experiments on desktop and dynamic web environments (OSWorld-Verified and DynaCU-Bench) show that NightWatch, driven by a watcher of only 0.8B parameters, reduces non-reasoning wall-clock time by 33% and wasted time by 53% on OSWorld while keeping task success on par, raises success on DynaCU-Bench from 39.5% to 44.2% with the large VLM agent, and is more efficient than passive-watching baselines such as AOI and PUSV under the same screenshot-only input, as well as a System-1 decision model more than 30times its size. Overall, NightWatch demonstrates that the timing of perception is as critical as its content, marking a step toward agents that maintain continuous awareness of their environment rather than perceiving it turn by turn.

items.abstract: Spatial intelligence, the ability to reason about 3D space from visual observations, becomes essential as multimodal large language models (MLLMs) move into the physical world. Beyond perceiving each view, it rests on two cornerstones of human cognition: fusing multiple views into one coherent 3D scene and mentally transforming that scene to new viewpoints as reasoning unfolds. Yet our spatial probes reveal that MLLMs largely lack both capabilities, even after spatial fine-tuning. We therefore present S-Mind, which internalizes multi-view geometry within the MLLM through a compact set of spatial tokens. It supervises these tokens to hold the fused 3D scene and re-emits them to re-express this scene from every viewpoint the reasoning adopts. Across four spatial benchmarks, S-Mind improves its Qwen3.5 backbones by up to 22.26 points and surpasses frontier general models such as GPT-6-Astra (+0.45), Kimi-K3.1-Pro (+1.97), and GLM-5.3-Flash (+7.80) in average accuracy. Moreover, the same probes confirm that it acquires both capabilities, reaching fusion and transformation accuracies of 65.11% and 82.17%, against at most 16.02% and 37.28% for the baselines. At inference, S-Mind also runs about 100x faster than a tool-based agent on the same backbone. Instilled through these spatial tokens during training, spatial capability becomes intrinsic to the backbone and persists even when the tokens are withheld, offering a promising path toward spatial intelligence in MLLMs.

However, they still struggle when queries are deferred until after exploration, requiring them to retain visual evidence before knowing which details will matter. items.abstract: Multimodal large language model (MLLM) agents have shown promising capabilities in task-oriented environments. However, they still struggle when queries are deferred until after exploration, requiring them to retain visual evidence before knowing which details will matter. We introduce EvoViM, a recursively self-evolving framework in which a frozen multimodal model turns its own interaction experience into one visual program for memory and skills. The program retains images and computes directly on pixels, and its operations decide how this evidence is used in each task. During memory evolution, the same model traces failures in its visual trajectories to the operations that lost or misused evidence and revises them. It also rewrites the notes and analysis tools that guide later revisions, which then build on earlier findings and skip changes that have already failed. We evaluate EvoViM with three multimodal models on six tasks covering visual matching, spatial recall, and sequential decision-making, including three tasks with deferred queries. Across the six tasks, EvoViM improves the average score over AutoMem, the strongest baseline in the main comparison, by 31.3-47.6 points on held-out episodes. Programs written once from the initial environment instructions perform substantially worse, highlighting the value of interaction experience in shaping how visual evidence is retained and used. Code and dataset are available at https://evovim.github.io/.

items.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) exhibit strong semantic understanding but remain limited in their ability to reason about metric 3D space in the physical world. items.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) exhibit strong semantic understanding but remain limited in their ability to reason about metric 3D space in the physical world. Existing VLMs typically infer 3D scene structure from one or more images without known camera calibration or cross-view geometric constraints. This makes metric 3D inference inherently ambiguous and leaves it unclear whether their spatial predictions are grounded in visual evidence or driven primarily by semantic priors. In contrast, calibrated stereo provides explicit cross-view geometry that resolves this ambiguity and offers a more reliable foundation for metric 3D perception and geometric generalization. We investigate how VLMs can learn transferable 3D representations directly from calibrated binocular observations. To this end, we introduce StereoVLM, the first geometry-aware binocular VLM for metric 3D spatial reasoning. StereoVLM follows a hierarchical learning paradigm spanning from cross-view correspondence and disparity estimation to calibration-conditioned metric depth perception and semantic spatial reasoning. We further find that disparity supervision generalizes substantially better than direct binocular depth supervision on unseen environments. To evaluate these capabilities, we introduce Stereo3D-Bench, a comprehensive benchmark across three levels, from point-level geometry to object-level spatial reasoning. StereoVLM-8B achieves 95.17% depth accuracy (δ_1) and a 66.98 average object-level score on Stereo3D-Bench. Intervention results further indicate that the model's performance on Stereo3D-Bench benefits from valid cross-view geometry and cannot be explained solely by additional visual tokens or semantic priors. Hierarchical geometric supervision also yields average gains of 3.54 points across five spatial benchmarks and 4.3 percentage points in RoboCasa manipulation success.

items.title: 吃了褪黑素还是睡不好？ 长期失眠的你 可能走错了第一步 很多人失眠了第一反应就是吃褪黑素，或者尝试放白噪音、睡前不刷手机……结果试了几天发现，该睡不着的还是睡不着。 于是开始怀疑是不是褪黑素不管用，或者其他方法不适合自己。 💡褪黑素本质上是一种调节生物钟的激素，并不是直接催眠的药物。它更适合倒时差、短期作息紊乱等情况。 如果你是压力大、焦虑失眠、或者持续了好几个月，靠褪黑素或者普通催眠方法很难起效

items.abstract: Abstract Background The pathogenic fungi Thielaviopsis punctulata and Thielaviopsis paradoxa cause black scorch disease in date palm ( Phoenix dactylifera L.), relying on secreted cell wall-degrading enzymes (CWDEs) to invade host tissues. To test whether Trichoderma secondary metabolites directly block these enzymes, we docked viridin, harzianic acid, trichodermin, and gliotoxin in silico against two modeled T. punctulata targets: a GH45 cellulase (AlphaFold) and a GH11 xylanase (SWISS-MODEL). Simulations were run in AutoDock Vina (exhaustiveness 32; three random seeds) using the native substrates cellobiose and xylobiose as baselines. Results Viridin and harzianic acid showed the strongest binding in both cellulase (− 8.00 and − 7.80 kcal/mol) and xylanase (− 7.67 and − 7.63 kcal/mol), matching substrate affinities (− 7.23 and − 7.10 kcal/mol) within Vina’s error margin despite slightly lower heavy-atom ligand efficiency. Conformational consistency further separated the top candidates: all 27 harzianic acid poses (9 per seed) localized inside the active-site clefts, with top-ranked orientations contacting both catalytic residues and sharing 46% and 81% spatial overlap with the docked substrates in cellulase and xylanase, respectively. Both trichodermin and gliotoxin bound more weakly (− 6.30 to − 6.80 kcal/mol), often missing one of the two catalytic residues. In SwissADME, we recorded only basic physicochemical descriptors, as its oral drug-likeness rules do not apply to fungal toxins like the other three tested metabolites. Conclusions Although rigid-receptor docking cannot replace molecular dynamics or wet-lab work, our results suggest that harzianic acid, and possibly viridin, could compete with native substrates for CWDE active sites, warranting in vitro enzymatic and fungal growth assays. items.abstract: Abstract Carotid atherosclerosis remains a major contributor to cerebrovascular events, with macrophage-driven inflammation playing a pivotal role in disease progression. This study employed an integrative multi-omics approach combining bulk RNA sequencing and weighted gene correlation network analysis to identify critical differential expression genes in atherogenesis. Machine learning algorithms (Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator, random forest and artificial neural network) prioritized Toll Like Receptor 1 as the most significant risk gene. Single-cell sequencing of carotid plaques demonstrated TLR1 was predominantly distributed in macrophages. Experimental validation in mouse bone marrow primary macrophages confirmed that coriander inhibits TLR1-mediated macrophage inflammatory response in carotid plaques. Immune infiltration analysis showed that TLR1 was closely related to neutrophil and macrophage activation. Our findings establish TLR1 as a macrophage-specific diagnostic biomarker and suggest that ingestion of coriander supplementation inhibits the inflammatory amplification circuit in TLR1-mediated advanced atherosclerosis.

items.title: Landscape and Emerging Directions of Single-Cell Genetic Variation Research Revealed by LLM-Assisted Analysis
items.summary: Abstract Background Single-cell genetic variation research has expanded rapidly with advances in sequencing technologies and computational approaches and is increasingly important for investigating cellular heterogeneity, clonal evolution, and disease-associated genomic alterations. However, key methodological and experimental information is often dispersed across full-text publications, limiting systematic…
items.abstract: Abstract Background Single-cell genetic variation research has expanded rapidly with advances in sequencing technologies and computational approaches and is increasingly important for investigating cellular heterogeneity, clonal evolution, and disease-associated genomic alterations. However, key methodological and experimental information is often dispersed across full-text publications, limiting systematic characterization of the field. To address this, we combined large-scale literature analysis with full-text structured information extraction assisted by the large language model (LLM) ChatGPT-4o to characterize technological, methodological, and application trends in single-cell genetic variation research. Results Information on sequencing technologies, variant types, disease applications, species, and variant detection tools was systematically extracted and organized. ChatGPT-4o-assisted extraction achieved a mean correctness of 82.50% and a mean completeness of 83.05% compared with manually curated annotations. Single-cell genetic variation research has expanded rapidly, accompanied by increasing international and institutional collaboration. scRNA-seq remains the predominant technology, while scATAC-seq, scDNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics, and multi-omics combinations are increasingly adopted. Cancer is the major application area, with tumor microenvironment, prognosis, and immunotherapy as prominent themes. SNVs remain the most extensively studied variant type, whereas combined SNV-CNV analyses are becoming more common, particularly in cancer studies. Bulk-oriented tools such as GATK remain widely used, while single-cell-specific methods are increasingly adopted to address low coverage, allelic dropout, and technical noise. Conclusions Single-cell genetic variation research is evolving toward integrated multi-omics, multi-variant analysis, and more specialized single-cell computational strategies. The increasing adoption of multi-omics technologies and single-cell-specific methods reflects the growing complexity and maturity of the field. Combining large-scale literature analysis with LLM-assisted full-text information extraction provides a systematic approach for capturing complex methodological and biological information and identifying emerging directions in single-cell genomics.

items.abstract: FusionGDB has served diverse biological, health, and clinical research communities as a unique functional annotation knowledgebase of human fusion genes. In this study, we report an updated resource of human fusion gene annotation (FusionGDB 3.0), available at https://compbio.uth.edu/FusionGDB/. FusionGDB 3.0 includes substantial content updates: 156K up-to-date human fusion genes established by integrating 216K RNA-seq-based and 100K WGS-based breakpoint events, comprehensive open reading frame annotations, protein domain retention searches, and 1.13 million personalized fusion protein sequences reflecting individual nsSNVs from TCGA and CCLE, as well as N- and C-truncated protein sequences alongside canonical in-frame products. Furthermore, it incorporates 18K potential tumorigenic scenarios, supported by evidence from the literature, spanning drug-targetable gene group fusions, the epigenomic architecture around breakpoint junctions, and therapeutic prioritization scoring. FusionGDB 3.0 establishes a systematic framework for the functional annotation of coding structural variants. FusionGDB 3.0 serves as a pivotal reference knowledgebase for the genomics, oncology, and precision pharmacology communities, while also functioning as a foundational benchmark dataset for training and validating machine learning models, structural biology platforms, and AI-driven therapeutic discovery pipelines.

items.abstract: Acetamiprid (ACE) has been implicated not only in bone metabolic disorders but also in the development of various cancers. Nevertheless, its role in osteosarcoma (OS) and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. We integrated network toxicology, transcriptomics, molecular docking, single-cell analysis, machine learning, and preliminary in vitro experiments to explore potential links between ACE-related targets and OS-associated signatures. We identified 219 ACE-related targets and 3299 OS-associated genes, including 62 overlapping candidates. Functional enrichment analyses highlighted inflammatory pathways, including TNF and IL-17 signaling. Exploratory machine learning analyses prioritized CAT and MPO, with CAT showing comparatively more consistent support across subsequent analyses and MPO showing less consistent cross-dataset performance. CAT demonstrated dataset-level discriminatory performance in the evaluated public transcriptomic datasets. Immune-context and single-cell analyses further characterized associations between candidate-gene expression, inferred immune-cell composition, and cellular distribution. Molecular docking generated computationally plausible ACE-protein binding poses but did not establish direct target engagement. In vitro, ACE treatment altered cellular metabolic activity, wound closure, and CAT expression in U-2 OS cells under the tested conditions. CAT emerged as a prioritized candidate molecular feature associated with ACE-related cellular responses and OS-associated molecular signatures. These findings are exploratory and do not establish a causal relationship between ACE exposure and OS development or progression. Further studies using independent tissue cohorts, mechanistic gene perturbation, direct target-engagement assays, and in vivo validation are required.

items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming drug design by enabling the systematic discovery of therapeutic targets and the prediction of drug response from complex biomedical data. In papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC), lymph node metastasis remains a key determinant of poor outcome, yet targetable drivers and predictive models for metastasis are lacking. Here, we integrate single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and machine learning to identify SPP1⁺ tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) as a functionally validated driver of lymph node metastasis in PTC. Using single-cell and spatial analyses, we show that SPP1⁺ TAMs engage TM4SF1⁺ malignant epithelial cells via the SPP1-CD44 axis within a hypoxic niche, driving tumor stemness, invasion, and metastatic progression. SPP1⁺ TAMs exhibit a hypoxic, M2-polarized phenotype and their abundance correlates with worse overall and progression‑free survival in metastatic PTC patients. We further develop an integrative machine-learning model based on SPP1⁺ TAM‑derived molecular features that predicts lymph node status with high accuracy. Preclinically, pharmacological targeting of SPP1 attenuates tumor cell migration, invasion, and lung metastasis, supporting its candidacy as a therapeutic target. Collectively, this study demonstrates how AI‑driven multi‑omics analysis can jointly identify a functionally validated target and generate a clinically deployable predictive model, illustrating a framework for bridging computational discovery with translational oncology.

items.abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic relapsing inflammatory skin disorder driven by epidermal barrier impairment and keratinocyte dysfunction. Current therapies are limited by insufficient target specificity and high recurrence rates. This study aimed to identify keratinocyte-derived biomarkers and develop novel targeted agents for precise diagnosis and treatment of AD. Single-cell RNA sequencing and weighted gene co-expression network analysis were performed to screen for key AD biomarkers, and machine learning algorithms with ROC curve analysis were applied to evaluate their diagnostic performance. Immunohistochemistry confirmed LYPD3 protein upregulation in AD lesional skin. In silico knockdown simulations at single-cell resolution elucidated LYPD3-mediated signaling pathways. Structure-based virtual screening and molecular dynamics simulations identified candidate LYPD3-targeted compounds, and cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA) and biolayer interferometry (BLI) validated target engagement and direct binding. items.summary: The rapid development of phenotypic screening, omics technologies, and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven drug discovery has accelerated the identification of bioactive small molecules and potential therapeutic targets. However, establishing reliable relationships between small molecules and their functional protein targets remains a major challenge in modern drug discovery. Precise characterization of small…
items.abstract: The rapid development of phenotypic screening, omics technologies, and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven drug discovery has accelerated the identification of bioactive small molecules and potential therapeutic targets. However, establishing reliable relationships between small molecules and their functional protein targets remains a major challenge in modern drug discovery. Precise characterization of small molecule-protein interactions is essential for elucidating mechanisms of action, optimizing lead compounds, improving target selectivity, and minimizing off-target effects. Nevertheless, phenotypic responses or individual binding assays alone are often insufficient to confirm bona fide pharmacological targets and define their functional consequences. This review summarizes current strategies for small molecule-protein target validation, including quantitative biophysical binding analysis, cellular target engagement assessment, stability- and affinity-based target identification, chemical proteomics, and structural characterization of ligand binding sites and key residues. We discuss how complementary approaches, such as surface plasmon resonance, biolayer interferometry, isothermal titration calorimetry, microscale thermophoresis, nuclear magnetic resonance, cellular thermal shift assay, and proteome-based technologies, provide distinct layers of evidence for defining molecular recognition, intracellular target engagement, and functional regulation. In addition, emerging applications of AI-assisted approaches in protein structure prediction, binding pocket identification, virtual screening, affinity prediction, and rational compound optimization are highlighted. We propose that reliable mechanism of action elucidation requires an integrated evidence framework combining computational prediction, biochemical validation, cellular evaluation, structural analysis, mutational studies, and functional confirmation. Such multidisciplinary strategies will strengthen target validation, reduce mechanistic uncertainty, facilitate rational drug optimization, and accelerate the development of safer and more effective therapeutics.

items.abstract: Male infertility (MIF) is a complex reproductive disorder influenced by genetic, lifestyle, and environmental factors. Cigarette smoke (CS) contains numerous reproductive toxicants and has been associated with impaired semen quality and fertility. However, the molecular mechanisms linking CS exposure to MIF remain unclear. Representative toxic constituents of CS were selected based on previous studies, and multiple databases were integrated to identify CS associated targets, which were intersected with MIF associated genes to obtain CS-MIF common targets. Three MIF transcriptomic datasets (GSE6872, GSE34514, and GSE22331) were integrated for differential expression analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA). Candidate genes were identified by integrating CS-MIF targets, differentially expressed genes, and WGCNA-derived key module genes, followed by LASSO and SVM-RFE machine learning analyses. Associations between genetically predicted candidate gene expression and MIF risk were investigated using cis-eQTL-based two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR). Summary-data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR) analysis using testis-derived eQTL data was subsequently performed to provide complementary tissue-specific genetic evidence for FASN. Molecular docking suggested potential structural compatibility between FASN and several representative CS-associated compounds, while MD simulation supported the structural stability of the FASN-benzanthrone complex. Finally, TM4 Sertoli cells were exposed to cigarette smoke condensate (CSC), and FASN mRNA expression was evaluated by RT-qPCR. Four hub genes, including ABCC1, FASN, GAPDH, and SGK1, were identified from 14 candidate genes. MR analysis demonstrated that genetically predicted higher FASN expression was significantly associated with increased MIF risk (IVW: OR = 1.256, 95% CI = 1.109-1.423, P < 0.001; FDR-adjusted P = 0.004). SMR analysis using testis eQTL data further supported the association between FASN expression and MIF (P_SMR = 0.040, P_HEIDI = 0.307). Molecular docking identified benzanthrone as the compound with the most favorable predicted binding affinity for FASN among the 20 selected compounds (- 7.129 kcal/mol). Subsequent 100 ns molecular dynamics simulation suggested structural stability of the FASN-benzanthrone complex under the investigated conditions. Furthermore, exposure of TM4 Sertoli cells to 100 μg/mL CSC for 24 h significantly increased FASN mRNA expression. This study integrated network toxicology, transcriptomics, machine learning, genetic association analyses, structural simulations, and in vitro experiments to prioritize FASN as a candidate gene potentially relevant to CS-associated male reproductive dysfunction. Genetically predicted higher FASN expression was associated with increased MIF risk, while CSC exposure increased FASN mRNA expression in TM4 Sertoli cells. However, these findings do not establish that FASN mediates CS-induced reproductive injury. Further functional investigations are required to clarify its potential mechanistic role.

items.abstract: canSAR (https://cansar.ai) serves as the world's largest public platform for cancer drug discovery and translational research. It serves as an exploration and hypothesis generation platform for drug discovery through (i) fully integrating large, multidisciplinary data from public resources, as well as bespoke curated data, creating a connected, navigable drug discovery knowledge map; and (ii) applying a suite of machine learning and AI tools to generate novel insights. We share the latest updates to canSAR highlighting growth across all data, enhancements to the predictive algorithms, and continued improvements to the user experience. We leverage our latest open science chemical handling and druggability prediction tools to provide traceable insights. An increased focus of the platform is to provide "in-line" support and guidance to drug discovery exploration. We report the first incarnation of our high-fidelity, agentic-AI-generated, context-specific summaries, which we provide across the website for all human proteins to further aid users in synthesis and distillation of key information.

items.abstract: Sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (SA-AKI) involves ferroptotic tubular injury, but the upstream mechanisms controlling ferroptosis susceptibility remain incompletely defined. We investigated whether cytochrome P450 family 1 subfamily A member 1 (CYP1A1) promotes SA-AKI by regulating acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 4 (ACSL4) protein stability. Global and kidney tubule-targeted Cyp1a1 knockout mice underwent cecal ligation and puncture (CLP). HK-2 cells and primary mouse renal tubular epithelial cells were used for complementary validation. Protein stability assays, ubiquitination analyses, interaction assays and AlphaFold 3-guided mutagenesis were used to define the mechanism. Renal-targeted siCYP1A1/Cy5.5@LNP-CLPVASC nanoparticles were evaluated for protective efficacy and tolerability. Renal CYP1A1 was upregulated after sepsis, and its deletion reduced renal dysfunction and tubular injury. Tubule-targeted deletion conferred protection without reducing renal bacterial burden. CYP1A1 deficiency attenuated lipid peroxidation and injury in HK-2 and primary cells, whereas ferrostatin-1 attenuated injury in LPS-stimulated, CYP1A1-overexpressing HK-2 cells. CYP1A1 loss accelerated ACSL4 degradation, while overexpression enhanced its stability. CYP1A1 interacted with ACSL4 through a D393-dependent interface and limited its ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation. Renal-targeted CYP1A1 silencing reduced ACSL4 abundance, lipid peroxidation and renal injury. Nanoparticle administration was well tolerated over 28 days based on histological, biochemical and hematological assessments, with no significant increase in renal inflammation at 48 h. These findings identify a CYP1A1-ACSL4 protein-stability axis that promotes ferroptotic tubular injury and support renal-targeted CYP1A1 silencing as a potential intervention for SA-AKI.

items.abstract: The three-dimensional structure of proteins is a fundamental determinant of their functional roles; however, biophysical properties such as stability, flexibility, and solubility are also critical for the experimental applicability of designed proteins. The generation of protein sequences capable of folding into a desired three-dimensional structure is known as the protein inverse folding problem and represents one of the fundamental computational challenges in protein engineering because of the vast search space involved. Current deep learning-based inverse folding models effectively learn structure-sequence relationships; however, these models largely overlook biophysical properties such as solubility and stability. This is primarily because these models are predominantly trained on natural protein datasets, and although natural proteins are highly efficient in cellular processes, they may not necessarily represent suitable candidates for experimental applications. In this study, 21,668 protein sequences from the CATH 4.3 database that passed the quality-filtering criteria were subjected to multi-objective optimization for stability, solubility, and flexibility using the Heuristic Metropolis-Hastings Optimization (HMHO) approach, resulting in the construction of a biophysically enriched synthetic protein dataset. To evaluate the effect of the data-centric approach independently of model architecture, the PiFold architecture was kept unchanged, and the baseline model trained on natural CATH sequences (PiFold) was compared with the model retrained on the optimized training data (PiFoldOPT) using natural CATH test sequences that had not been modified by HMHO. In accordance with the primary objective of the study, an initial set of 200 proteins was selected from the natural CATH test set using proportional stratified sampling that preserved the protein length distribution, with the aim of evaluating the biophysical properties of model-generated sequences on a representative test subset. In paired analyses conducted on 155 common proteins successfully designed by both models, PiFoldOPT designs exhibited markedly lower instability index values and higher predicted solubility than PiFold designs ([Formula: see text] for both comparisons; effect sizes [Formula: see text] and [Formula: see text], respectively). Furthermore, the proportion of designs classified as stable increased from 65% for PiFold to 81% for PiFoldOPT. To evaluate these biophysical gains together with potential changes in inverse folding performance, sequence-level metrics were also compared on the natural test set. PiFoldOPT maintained sequence recovery performance close to that of the baseline model (0.4270 vs. 0.4286), while showing a limited but systematic reduction in prediction confidence (0.3779 vs. 0.3932). ESM-2-based zero-shot sequence scoring, performed to provide an evaluation independent of the biophysical prediction tools used during optimization, further showed that PiFoldOPT designs achieved more favorable protein language model scores for the majority of proteins. Finally, to evaluate whether the biophysical improvements compromised structural integrity, the initial 200-protein test subset selected using proportional stratified sampling that preserved the protein length distribution was used. Within this subset, 161 proteins for which ESMFold structure predictions were successfully obtained for the natural sequence, the PiFold design, and the PiFoldOPT design were included in the paired structural analysis. To minimize method-dependent comparison bias, all sequences across the three groups were evaluated using the same ESMFold structure prediction protocol. Using structures predicted from the natural sequences as references, PiFold and PiFoldOPT designs exhibited mean TM-scores of 0.784 and 0.792, RMSD values of 2.17 and 2.13 Å, and pLDDT values of 66.34 and 66.37, respectively. In addition to paired statistical comparisons, equivalence and non-inferiority analyses supported that the biophysical gains achieved with PiFoldOPT were not associated with a meaningful loss of predicted three-dimensional structural integrity. Taken together, these results demonstrate that biophysically guided training data enable the design of more stable and soluble protein sequences without modifying the model architecture. These findings reveal that, in protein inverse folding, not only model architecture but also the biophysical composition of the training data is an important determinant of design behavior, and demonstrate that biophysically enriched datasets represent a complementary data-centric strategy for protein design.
