items.abstract: Background HER2 status is an important biomarker in breast cancer, but its assessment primarily relies on core needle biopsy and pathological examination. Therefore, noninvasive preoperative prediction of HER2 status has important clinical value. This study aimed to evaluate the predictive value of models integrating multiparametric MRI deep learning, radiomics, and clinical features for preoperative HER2 status prediction in breast cancer. Materials and methods A total of 257 patients with pathologically confirmed breast cancer were retrospectively enrolled, including 98 HER2-positive and 159 HER2-negative patients. All patients underwent preoperative T1WI, T2WI, DWI, and DCE-MRI. Patients were randomly divided at the patient level into training (n = 174) and internal test (n = 83) cohorts at a 7:3 ratio. Cli, Rad, and DL models were constructed based on clinical, radiomics, and deep learning features, respectively, along with single-sequence fusion models. Subsequently, an mpMRI model integrating radiomics and deep learning features from all four MRI sequences and an mpMRI_Cli model further incorporating statistically significant preoperative clinical features were developed. Model performance was evaluated using the AUC, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, F1 score, Brier score, decision curve analysis, calibration curves, and confusion matrices. DeLong's test was used to compare AUCs between models. Results In the internal test cohort, the AUCs of the T1WI, T2WI, DWI, and DCE-MRI models were 0.666, 0.689, 0.710, and 0.728, respectively. The AUCs of the Cli, Rad, and DL models were 0.571, 0.764, and 0.791, respectively. The mpMRI model achieved an AUC of 0.910 (95% CI: 0.837-0.966), with an accuracy of 0.831, sensitivity of 0.742, and specificity of 0.885. The mpMRI_Cli model achieved an AUC of 0.923 (95% CI: 0.860-0.972), with an accuracy of 0.819, sensitivity of 0.839, specificity of 0.808, and Brier score of 0.122. Although the mpMRI_Cli model had a higher AUC than the mpMRI model, the difference was not statistically significant after Holm correction (P = 0.744). Conclusion Integrating multiparametric MRI radiomics and deep learning features improved preoperative prediction of HER2 status in breast cancer. Further incorporation of clinical features increased the AUC and sensitivity and reduced the Brier score, although the improvement in AUC was not statistically significant. Both models show potential for noninvasive preoperative HER2 prediction, but further validation in independent external and multicenter cohorts is warranted.

items.abstract: Introduction As part of a strategy to increase magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) capacity, the UK government funded the purchase of manufacturer artificial intelligence (AI) MRI image reconstruction software on MRI scanners. It aimed to reduce scan duration without compromising image quality and has been widely installed on clinical MRI scanners across the UK. Methods This is a mixed methods study, using an initial questionnaire to quantify opinions followed by focus groups of responders to further explore their views on technical issues. Patient views on the use of AI in MRI image reconstruction for reducing acquisition times, and more generally in their MRI pathway, were assessed. Results Study participants prefer improved image quality over faster acquisition times. If reducing acquisition times with AI, they feel it should only be used if extremely accurate images can be ascertained. They are uncomfortable with the use of manufacturer AI software for image reconstruction where accuracy is not stated and would like to be told about the use of AI in MRI. Conclusions Many participants felt that manufacturer AI software for MRI image reconstruction may be used only if a high accuracy is demonstrated, and if the training data is representative of the patient population, to not exacerbate health inequalities. This information is not currently given by manufacturers, which made the patient representatives concerned. Implication for practice

items.abstract: Background Although recent artificial intelligence (AI) foundation models have shown superior performance in medical imaging, their high computational demands and reliance on large data sets limit accessibility. These issues are especially pronounced in echocardiography, where integrating complex multiview measurements for individual cases hinders AI development and clinical translation. Vector embedding approaches offer promising solutions by leveraging compact representations in AI applications. Objectives We aimed to develop a transformer-based multiview encoder that integrates multiple echocardiographic videos into unified vector embeddings and uses adversarial learning to reduce reliance on demographic shortcuts. Methods Using the MIMIC-IV-ECHO (Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV-Echocardiography) data set (7,169 studies), we trained a multiview encoder to produce study-level embeddings and evaluated them on 21 binary classification tasks covering echocardiographic measurements and clinical diagnoses. We varied adversarial weights to assess their impact on demographic shortcut reliance and overall performance. Results The multiview encoder raised the mean area under the curve (AUC) across clinical tasks from 0.742 to 0.831 compared with the foundation model embedding (ΔAUC +0.090; 95% CI: 0.078-0.100), with significant gains in 20 of 21 tasks. The embeddings remained robust with a limited number of views (mean ΔAUC +0.071; 95% CI: 0.043-0.113). Adversarial learning reduced sex and race predictability only at strong weights and at substantial cost to clinical performance. Conclusions The multiview encoder framework integrates multiple echocardiographic views into unified study-level embeddings, enabling substantial diagnostic improvements across diverse cardiac tasks. By producing compact, informative embeddings without requiring extensive computational resources, this approach lowers the cost of building echocardiographic AI on an existing foundation model.

items.abstract: Virtual staining (VS) has gained a significant interest for label-free characterization of unstained tissue-sections. The concept of VS lies on translating a label-free imaging technique such as auto-fluorescence for generating an equivalent histologically stained image using deep-neural-networks. Different endogenous fluorophores present in the sample have distinct excitation and emission bands, which can provide stain-free specificity of molecules. However, conventional technique for studying emission of different molecules, restrict molecular specificity in the measurements. The present study explores multiple-spectral (MS) bands in label-free imaging to gain richer information about distribution and diversity of these fluorophores. Our study includes a comparative analysis using MS and single long-pass (SLP)-approach for VS of unstained tissue-sections. It is observed that MS-approach provides a better training input to the model enhancing discriminative power of the neural network, even when trained for lesser epochs. The Structural-Similarity-Index-Measure (SSIM) map shows that use of MS-approach for training the model provides a high-SSIM of 0.94 whereas, SLP-approach provides an SSIM-values of 0.62. The ROC area of a model quantifies the ratio of true-negative and false-positive outputs.The testing results show that MS-approach (ROC ≈ 0.98) outperforms the SLP-approach (ROC ≈ 0.78) even at a smaller training time. The versatility of MS-approach is tested by incorporating it for different tissue sections of multiple thicknesses providing consistently high value of ROC area (>0.92). The proposed approach offers a time-efficient and reagent-free add-on to well-established VS techniques that can be further extended for multiple biomedical imaging applications.

items.abstract: Background To evaluate the clinical performance of a novel artificial intelligence (AI)-based image processing algorithm for two-dimensional angiographic imaging compared with its predecessor across multiple imaging modes, anatomic regions, and endovascular specialties. Materials and methods This retrospective, comparative, randomized, paired, and blinded multicenter reader study included anonymized images acquired during clinically indicated endovascular interventions at 11 institutions in the United States and Europe. A total of 553 image series from 182 patients representing 51 procedure types across interventional radiology, neurointervention, cardiology, and pediatric cardiology were processed using both the AI-based and predecessor image processing algorithms. Thirteen board-certified physicians independently evaluated paired images using five-point Likert scales for overall image quality, contrast of clinically relevant details, noise reduction, and confidence in assessing device and vessel details. The primary endpoint was non-inferiority of overall image quality. Secondary endpoints evaluated superiority across image quality metrics using a predefined hierarchical testing strategy. Results The AI-based image processing algorithm demonstrated non-inferior overall image quality in 98.9% of all evaluations (95% confidence interval [CI], 98%-100%), meeting the primary endpoint across all imaging modes, anatomic regions, and predefined subgroups. Superiority of the AI-based algorithm was demonstrated for overall image quality, contrast of clinically relevant details, noise reduction, and confidence in assessing device and vessel details across fluoroscopy, roadmap, overlay reference, and native acquisition imaging. Overall image quality superiority was not demonstrated for digital subtraction angiography, likely reflecting the intrinsically higher signal-to-noise characteristics of these acquisitions. Inter-reader agreement analysis demonstrated identical ratings in 49.3% of evaluations, with 94.7% of paired ratings differing by no more than one Likert category. Conclusions In this multicenter blinded reader study, AI-based image processing demonstrated non-inferior overall image quality compared with its predecessor across all evaluated imaging modes and patient subgroups, with superior performance for multiple image quality metrics in fluoroscopy, roadmap, overlay reference, and native acquisition imaging. These findings support the clinical utility of AI-based image processing for endovascular imaging and provide a foundation for future studies evaluating its impact on radiation dose and procedural outcomes.

items.abstract: Purpose Focal cortical dysplasia (FCD) is a common cause of treatment-resistant epilepsy and can be difficult to detect on MRI. Although traditionally considered static, lesion visibility may vary across scans. We assessed whether MELD-derived lesional imaging features differ across serial MRI in histologically confirmed paediatric FCD type II. Methods Twenty-one patients with histopathologically confirmed FCD type II underwent paired T1-weighted MRI; 13 also had paired FLAIR imaging. Images were processed using FastSurfer and a modified MELD feature-extraction pipeline. Lesion-mask feature values were compared with anatomically matched contralateral regions, and time-corrected longitudinal lesion-contralateral differences were calculated. Blinded qualitative neuroradiological review was available for 20/21 subjects. Results FCD lesions demonstrated quantitative feature differences from contralateral cortex. In the FLAIR cohort, longitudinal lesion-contralateral differences were consistently positive across sampled grey and white matter depths and remained significant after false discovery rate correction (mean paired differences 0.607-0.737; all pFDR = 0.009). Protocol-restricted FLAIR sensitivity analyses preserved the direction of effect, although restricted subgroups were underpowered. In T1-weighted MRI, longitudinal lesion-contralateral differences were positive across grey matter intensity features, greatest at 75% cortical thickness (mean paired difference 0.185, 95% CI 0.060-0.309, p = 0.006), but no T1 feature survived false discovery rate correction. Neuroradiological review identified possible visually appreciable interval change in a minority of cases, with most apparent change attributed to acquisition-related variation or artefact. Conclusion Quantitative MRI-derived FCD features can vary across serial paediatric MRI. These findings demonstrate longitudinal imaging feature variability, most consistently in FLAIR-derived measures, with implications for repeat imaging and machine learning derived lesion detection.

items.abstract: Drought driven by climate change severely threatens food security, particularly for wheat and barley grown in water-limited regions. A major breeding challenge is the trade-off between drought tolerance and yield. This review synthesises current knowledge of drought adaptation mechanisms in Triticeae crops, focusing on the transcriptional cascades, ABA-centric hormonal signalling and posttranslational modifications (kinases, phosphatases and ubiquitination) that confer resilience while often constraining carbon allocation to developing grains. Recent genomic advances, including genome-wide association study (GWAS), multi-omics integration and single-cell RNA-transcriptomics, have uncovered a wealth of drought-associated loci, although their translational potential is limited by data heterogeneity, environmental dependency and a persistent gap between laboratory validation and field performance. Emerging breeding approaches, such as speed breeding, wild-allele introgression, multiplex CRISPR/Cas9 and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven phenotyping are accelerating the development of climate-smart cultivars. Tissue-specific and inducible expression systems show early promise in uncoupling stress protection from growth penalties. Looking ahead, we propose that overcoming the yield-tolerance trade-off will require integrating synthetic biology, explainable AI, systematic exploration of novel variation and field phenomics coupled with digital twin modelling. Collectively, this review provides a strategic framework for engineering next-generation, climate-smart Triticeae cereals capable of maintaining productivity under intensifying drought conditions.

items.abstract: Although immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed breast cancer treatment, predicting durable clinical benefit remains challenging. Current biomarkers, primarily derived from tumor tissue or peripheral blood, do not directly capture the adaptive immune response at its site of initiation. Tumor-draining lymph nodes (TDLNs) are not passive conduits for metastasis but dynamic immunological hubs where anti-tumor T cell priming and immune evasion converge. In this review, we critically examine the nascent intersection of TDLN immunobiology, high-resolution multi-omics, and artificial intelligence (AI) to evaluate TDLN-derived features as candidate next-generation biomarkers for immunotherapy. We synthesize the complex cellular and molecular architecture of the breast cancer TDLN, including T cell exhaustion, B cell-mediated immunity, and stromal crosstalk, before evaluating the state-of-the-art single-cell and spatial technologies capable of decoding this microenvironment. We assess the application of AI and foundation models in this domain, identifying a major methodological gap: while AI frameworks are increasingly mature for primary tumors, their application to TDLNs remains unvalidated and limited by a severe scarcity of annotated multi-omics datasets. Furthermore, we address pivotal translational considerations, including the immunological implications of axillary surgery in the ICI era. We emphasize that no TDLN-derived biomarker has yet undergone prospective validation as a predictive biomarker for immunotherapy in breast cancer, and that retrospective analyses of trial specimens must account for the timing of tissue acquisition relative to systemic therapy. Finally, we chart immediate research priorities, including establishing TDLN reference atlases and developing clinically feasible specimen collection pathways for biomarker validation. This review provides a conceptual framework and translational roadmap to assess whether TDLN-derived features can complement existing tumor-centric metrics in guiding immunotherapy decisions.

items.abstract: N-(1,3-Dimethylbutyl)-N'-phenyl-p-phenylenediamine quinone (6PPDQ) is a widespread tire-derived contaminant linked to cardiotoxicity and metabolic dysfunction, but its role in cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) remains unclear. Using chronic kidney disease, type 2 diabetes, and ischemic heart disease as surrogate models, we combined network toxicology, multi-omics, machine learning, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to identify candidate common molecular drivers of 6PPDQ toxicity and CMM pathogenesis. LYN, SOCS3, and TIMP2 were consistently dysregulated across the three disorders. Docking and MD simulations indicated plausible 6PPDQ binding and relative conformational stability to all three proteins, without confirming actual binding or quantitative affinity ranking. Single-cell RNA-seq of diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM) and diabetic nephropathy (DN) showed predominant enrichment of these targets in macrophages, while CellChat predicted disease-associated communication patterns (macrophage-fibroblast in DCM; macrophage-endothelial in DN). Dose-response screening identified 20 ng/mL-an estimated high-exposure dose under heavy pollution-as the peak-effect concentration for target-gene modulation and M1-marker (iNOS, CD80) induction; it was used thereafter, although extrapolation to typical exposure warrants caution. At this concentration, 6PPDQ induced RAW264.7 morphological remodeling, intracellular ROS accumulation, and M1-like polarization, characterized by upregulation of iNOS, CD80, LYN, and SOCS3, repression of TIMP2, and elevated proinflammatory cytokines (IL-6, TNF-α, IL-1β). These findings associate 6PPDQ-induced macrophage inflammation and ECM-related changes with coordinated LYN/SOCS3/TIMP2 dysregulation, providing a framework linking 6PPDQ exposure to CMM-related inflammatory-fibrotic signatures.

items.abstract: Objective To develop and evaluate LeakageHunter-SCFM, an evidence-bounded informatics framework for auditing dataset-lineage evidence and calibrating benchmark-independence claims in single-cell foundation model evaluation. Methods LeakageHunter-SCFM extracts accessions, DOIs, URLs, and repository identifiers from manuscripts and related artifacts. The workflow canonicalizes resources, assigns dataset roles, constructs candidate overlap pairs, and applies claim ceilings before reviewer adjudication. We evaluated it in a curated development corpus, a locked retrospective external evaluation set, and a small prediction-blinded prospective proof-of-concept evaluation. Results The development workflow reduced 673 raw candidates to 84 filtered resource entries and 53 candidate overlap pairs. Prediction-visible reviewer forms agreed across all 140 retrospective evidence units; their historical labels yielded F1 0.842 across 132 binary-scored units. Independent prediction-blinded relabeling of all 140 units followed by third-assessor adjudication yielded precision 0.727, recall 0.667, specificity 0.910, and F1 0.696 across 136 binary-scored units. The seven-record, prediction-blinded proof of concept achieved recall 1.000 and precision 0.611 across 52 evidence units. All actionable-positive units came from one record. Restricting this analysis to full article bodies retained 50 units from five records and F1 0.759. Conclusion Evidence-bounded lineage auditing supports biomedical foundation-model benchmark review by separating identifier overlap, actionable review priority, and confirmed exposure. LeakageHunter-SCFM provides a reproducible triage layer for lineage evidence and reserves claims about corpus membership and performance effects for direct supporting evidence.

items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in cardiovascular research where conventional analysis struggles with scale, heterogeneity, and multimodal integration. items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in cardiovascular research where conventional analysis struggles with scale, heterogeneity, and multimodal integration. Its contribution differs across imaging, computational omics, mechanistic simulation, and drug discovery. This narrative review examines substantive applications of machine learning and deep learning while distinguishing them from routine bioinformatics and purely biophysical modeling. We assess independent biological units, validation strategies, and strength of inference in representative studies. Deep-learning imaging systems can provide reproducible quantitative phenotypes, but workflow performance alone does not establish mechanism. In single-cell and spatial studies, clustering, integration, trajectory inference, and network reconstruction generally yield associations or hypotheses unless experimentally supported. Mechanistic interpretation is bounded by the specific effect established through targeted perturbation or rescue with functional testing; lineage tracing and orthogonal readouts provide complementary support, not standalone proof of causation. Hybrid AI-biophysical models may accelerate personalized simulation, whereas heart-on-chip, engineered tissue, and organoid systems without learned components are validation platforms rather than AI methods. In drug discovery, active learning and molecular redesign can prioritize candidates, but predicted reductions in ion-channel liability do not demonstrate biological safety or reduced proarrhythmic risk. Major limitations include pseudoreplication, data leakage, domain shift, batch effects, uncertain labels, few independent hearts, demographic imbalance, incomplete calibration, and limited transfer among animal, iPSC-derived, and adult human systems. AI is most valuable when it produces robust phenotypes or experimentally testable hypotheses within a transparent validation framework, rather than when predictive accuracy is treated as mechanistic evidence.

items.abstract: Deciphering the mapping between biomolecular sequences and complex biological functions is a central challenge in genomics. While existing generative nucleotide models capture sequence distributions, they lack explicit access to gene-associated biological semantics, limiting semantics-guided design. Here, we present GenNA, a generative nucleotide foundation model guided by natural language annotations. Pretrained on a multimodal nucleotide-text corpus spanning 2221 eukaryotic species (∼416 billion characters), GenNA internalizes relationships between sequence syntax and functional semantics within a unified autoregressive framework. Without explicit rule-based supervision, GenNA yields distinguishable perplexity responses to sequence-annotation mismatches, mutational variants, and species-label perturbations. Furthermore, across diverse generation tasks, GenNA produces statistically plausible nucleotide sequences consistent with target semantics, structural constraints, and species contexts. Overall, GenNA provides a versatile framework for controllable nucleotide generation, establishing a practical route to integrate functional descriptions with sequence design.

items.abstract: Right-handed, antiparallel α-helical coiled coils are rare in nature and remain challenging targets for de novo protein design. Here, we combined parametric backbone generation with deep-learning-based sequence design and structure prediction to systematically explore this underrepresented region of coiled-coil structural space. We compared three ProteinMPNN design strategies: repeat-constrained homotetramer design, unconstrained homotetramer design, and unconstrained heterotetramer design. Removing strict sequence repeat constraints increased the fraction of designs satisfying structural confidence and topology criteria approximately sixfold, from 0.44% to 2.80%, while simultaneous optimization of two distinct peptide sequences yielded a success rate of 3.04%. Selected designs were evaluated for assembly using a split-luciferase complementation assay in mammalian cells, followed by circular dichroism spectroscopy and molecular dynamics simulations. Five of six experimentally characterized designs exhibited predominantly α-helical structures, with apparent melting temperatures ranging from 55.2 to 72.5 °C. The crystal structure of the most stable design, Heteromer-2, determined at 1.92 Å resolution, confirmed the intended right-handed, antiparallel architecture, with a backbone RMSD of only 0.45 Å relative to the computational model. Our findings establish a strategy for designing noncanonical coiled-coil architectures by combining precise parametric control of backbone geometry with flexible, AI-assisted sequence optimization.

items.abstract: Astroviruses are commonly grouped using sequences of the capsid-encoding ORF2 region. We examined how these groups correspond to similarities in spike fold and whether structural similarity can guide the assignment of new spike models. We used TM-align to compare 964 spike models predicted with AlphaFold 3 and defined TM_max as the larger of the two chain-length-normalized TM-scores. Complete-linkage clustering used TM_max cutoffs of 0.50 for major groups and 0.65 for subgroups. We compared structural dendrograms with sequence trees built by the same method. For query assignment, a subgroup qualified if every member had a TM_max of at least 0.65 with the query. The best-matching reference determined the assignment when several subgroups qualified. The six major structural groups comprised 25 subgroups. Some subgroups contained members of several of the 35 ORF2 amino acid distance groups. For example, the avian fecal sequence KP663426 and the pig-source reference OP643774 belonged to different ORF2 groups but shared subgroup SG1-03. Their spikes had 20.8% amino acid sequence identity and a TM_max of 0.769. Structural dendrograms and sequence trees differed in their internal splits (normalized Robinson-Foulds distances of 0.801-0.851), although they agreed on 70.11-92.08% of sampled quartets. Of 180 additional queries with accessions distinct from those in the library, 177 (98.3%) were assigned to a subgroup and three (1.7%) remained unclassified. The library provides an astrovirus-specific reference for identifying similar spike folds across ORF2 sequence groups and assigning new spike models to subgroups with an explicit structural criterion.

items.abstract: Although protein structures are increasingly determined by cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM), structure modeling frequently suffers from residue misassignments and sequence register shifts, particularly in regions with ambiguous density. Here, we present DAQplugin, a ChimeraX plugin for real-time evaluation of protein models against cryo-EM density maps using the deep-learning-based residue-wise model quality (DAQ) score. Unlike existing validation tools applied after model construction, DAQplugin enables interactive validation during model building and refinement. DAQ identifies residue assignment errors, including sequence register shifts, as well as local conformational modeling errors. DAQplugin also guides correction of sequence register shifts by suggesting alternative residue placements along the backbone. The plugin is computationally efficient and runs on standard CPUs without requiring GPU hardware, enabling deep-learning-based validation on ordinary laptops during interactive model building, model-map fitting, and refinement. DAQplugin facilitates more accurate interpretation of cryo-EM density maps and improves the reliability assessment of protein structure models.

items.abstract: Experimentation teams must decide which proposed website changes to test with live traffic. We evaluated whether forecasts from simulated shoppers could inform that choice. We screened 412 historical website A/B tests and evaluated four systems on the 318 that ran longer than 21 days. Each system predicted an original win, a variant win, or an inconclusive result. Page roles were masked and recorded outcomes were withheld during inference. Squoosh UX-1, a model fine-tuned on human browsing data, simulated 1,000 shoppers per arm and correctly classified 267 of 318 outcomes (84.0%, 95% Wilson interval 79.5-87.6%, treating experiments as independent). Qwen3 Next 80B, the strongest general-purpose configuration on outcome accuracy, correctly classified 196 of 318 (61.6%). UX-1 favored the variant in 126 experiments. In the live tests, 118 of those variants won (93.7%), four lost, and four had inconclusive results. The remaining 192 experiments included 19 additional variant wins.

items.abstract: Optical neural networks promise fast, energy-efficient computing, but every device departs from its design and must be trained with the hardware. In situ training relies on an expert-built calibrated digital model of each device or on gradient-free trial and error. Coding agents, large language models that write and run programs, have shown an emergent ability to understand and edit the weights of digital neural networks. Here we introduce optics as code, a method in which a coding agent trains an optical neural network from measurements alone, through a harness that returns camera images of its probes and requires a hypothesis per request. We discovered that the agent forms a physical understanding of the optics and reparametrizes the network with interpretable optical elements tuned on the hardware. It outperforms gradient-free methods in classification and image encoding, approaching backpropagation through a calibrated model at a fraction of the cost. Needing neither per-device calibration nor gradients through the hardware, and improving with more capable models, optics as code offers a practical route to large, scalable optical neural networks and a general tool for calibrating and optimizing optical experiments.

items.abstract: Simulated manipulation benchmarks measure policy performance using hand-written success checkers that label each episode as a success or failure. Passing an expert demonstration shows that a checker accepts one way of completing the task. Learned policies, however, may stop after partial progress or complete the task in a different way. A checker may then accept an incomplete execution (phantom success) or reject an execution that satisfies the instruction (silent failure). In this paper, we introduce SimAudit, an LLM-based pipeline that audits success checkers against task instructions. SimAudit analyzes the instruction and checker code to identify scenarios where the two may disagree, recreates those scenarios in simulation, and runs the original checker. Multi-view renderings are then used to verify whether the observed behavior satisfies the instruction. Across RoboTwin 2.0, RoboCasa365, and RoboDojo, 183 simulated test cases produced the predicted checker verdict. Visual verification and deduplication yielded 61 distinct defects across 49 tasks, including 40 phantom successes and 21 silent failures. Most defects in RoboCasa365 accepted incomplete executions, most in RoboDojo rejected valid executions, and both error types were common in RoboTwin 2.0. These findings suggest that validating success checkers requires testing both incomplete executions and valid alternatives to expert demonstrations, and motivate more rigorous evaluation protocols for future benchmarks.

items.abstract: Dense metric mapping from a single camera and IMU remains challenging: visual-inertial odometry (VIO) provides metric motion but sparse geometry, whereas feed-forward depth models predict dense structure without ensuring metric scale. We present Accord, which constructs an accurate online dense metric map from any camera with an IMU. A VIO filter publishes metric poses, a depth foundation model conditioned on them predicts depth for short keyframe windows, and a factor graph fuses the resulting submaps. Recent work has explored several approaches to this problem. What is essential is the multi-view agreement (Accord), which is considered in SLAM as a source of geometric self-consistency. Accord anchors each keyframe window to metric 3D points triangulated from the filter poses, then exploits bidirectional dense depth agreement between co-visible images to estimate and correct per-image scale errors while preserving the metric scale established by the anchors. Context keyframes further improve depth prediction, and the resulting submaps are fused in a factor graph. We evaluate a single mapping configuration across five public camera-IMU setups and a new Phone-rig/GoPro dataset. With nothing tuned per dataset/setup and every map aligned only by Accord's own trajectory, Accord achieves consistently best/second-best mean F-score at 5 cm on every platform. Accord is open-source along with the phone-rig dataset for the benefit of the research community

items.summary: Recent work on human-scene interaction (HSI) generation moves from single interactions to long-horizon interaction, where a language-model agent plans and executes a sequence of interactions in a 3D scene under one instruction. However, existing agents struggle in challenging everyday scenarios (e.g., picking up a toy and throwing it into a basket) because they lack spatial control over the motion and quantitative…
items.abstract: Recent work on human-scene interaction (HSI) generation moves from single interactions to long-horizon interaction, where a language-model agent plans and executes a sequence of interactions in a 3D scene under one instruction. However, existing agents struggle in challenging everyday scenarios (e.g., picking up a toy and throwing it into a basket) because they lack spatial control over the motion and quantitative feedback on its execution, and they often fail to complete the interaction sequence. To address these gaps, we present Inhabitant, a training-free agent framework in which the agent specifies each motion through positions, paths and poses, measures how the executed interaction deviates from its intent, and revises the control specification accordingly. For an extensive evaluation in such scenarios, we build Inhabit, a benchmark of 75 household tasks in 31 furniture layouts of an apartment, in which every task chains one to three goals on movable objects and is carried out by the whole body, excluding fingers. On Inhabit, Inhabitant completes 98.7\% of the tasks with Claude Opus 5.5, and 93.3\% and 82.7\% with Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Gemini 4 Argon, respectively. Ablations confirm that without spatial control the agent fails most tasks, and without quantitative feedback its motion becomes less precise. Code is available on the project page.

To combat the critical public health threat posed by CRAB, bioinformatics and immunoinformatic tools were used in this study to predict potential linear B lymphocyte (LBL), helper T lymphocyte…
items.abstract: The World Health Organization (WHO) has classified Carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB) as a critical-priority pathogen that requires novel antibiotics and strategies, due to its high antibiotic resistance. To combat the critical public health threat posed by CRAB, bioinformatics and immunoinformatic tools were used in this study to predict potential linear B lymphocyte (LBL), helper T lymphocyte (HTL), and cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL) epitopes derived from the Acinetobacter baumannii (A. baumannii) outer membrane proteins AdeK, PirA, and outer membrane protein 22 (Omp22). Subsequently, four combined multi-epitope vaccines (MEVs) designated ABV1-ABV4 were constructed by linking selected LBL, HTL, and CTL epitopes and Pan-HLA-DR reactive epitopes (PADRE) via GGGS and AAY linkers and fusing four different adjuvants to the N-terminus of the constructs with EAAAK linkers to increase immunogenicity. Afterward, the allergenicity, antigenicity, and solubility of ABV1-ABV4 were analyzed. The two non-allergenic candidates ABV3 and ABV4 were further analyzed for physicochemical properties and immune simulation using ExPASy ProtParam and C-ImmSim. ABV4 exhibited superior antigenicity and solubility compared with ABV3, and both ABV4 and ABV3 were predicted to induce similar immune responses; therefore, ABV4 was selected for further structural characterization and subsequent expression. The 3D structure was modeled using AlphaFold 3.0 and refined with GalaxyRefine servers. After refinement, the quality of the 3D structure improved markedly, with 97.2% of the residues in the most favored regions of the Ramachandran plot and an overall Z score of -6.11. Docking scores were -274.02 kcal/mol for ABV4-TLR2 and -302.54 kcal/mol for ABV4-TLR4. MM/PBSA calculations yielded binding free energies of -53.66 kcal/mol for ABV4-TLR2 and -68.93 kcal/mol for ABV4-TLR4. The optimized ABV4 gene was synthesized, cloned and inserted into pET28a, and expressed in E. coli BL21 with a C-terminal 6 × His tag. Immunization of mice with ABV4 induced high titers of anti-ABV4 antibodies and elevated serum IFN-γ and IL-4 levels, suggesting that ABV4 may elicit both humoral and cellular immune responses in mice. Immunofluorescence assay (IFA) and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) revealed that the ABV4 antibody specifically recognized CRAB extracellular proteins without cross-reactivity to E. coli, K. pneumoniae, or P. aeruginosa, confirming that ABV4 is a promising MEV vaccine candidate against CRAB with the potential to induce humoral and cellular immune responses. Overall, ABV4 is a promising vaccine candidate against CRAB, and further experimental research is required to validate the protective efficacy in mice and elucidate the underlying mechanisms.

items.abstract: Breast cancer (BC) is the most frequently diagnosed cancer and the second leading cause of cancer-related death in women. BC is classified into three primary subtypes, of which triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) carries the poorest prognosis because it lacks specific targetable markers. Preclinical studies of TNBC have consistently reported reduced tumor-suppressor activity of PTEN, activating the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway. Notably, published studies have shown that the WWP1 enzyme plays a pivotal role in driving PTEN degradation via ubiquitination, identifying it as a promising therapeutic target for the treatment of TNBC. In search of new WWP1 inhibitors, we combined classical structure-based computational methods with artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted prescreening strategies for the de novo design of peptide-based WWP1 inhibitors and identified a hexapeptide, termed WI23-B, which displayed high-nanomolar binding affinity for WWP1. In TR-FRET enzymatic assays, WI23-B inhibited WWP1 activity with an IC 50 of 11.09 ± 4.59 μM, showing about 9-fold selectivity over the closely related ligase NEDD4. In MCF-7 and MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cell lines, WI23-B exerted promising cytotoxic activity, particularly in combination with the PI3K inhibitor BYL719, both as the free peptide and when loaded into organosilica nanocapsules. Collectively, these findings highlight WI23-B as a promising lead peptide with low micromolar WWP1 inhibitory activity and synergistic antiproliferative effects when combined with PI3K inhibitors. While further structural optimization is required to enhance its potency and pharmacological properties, our results provide a solid foundation for the development of next-generation WWP1 inhibitors. Such agents have the potential to reshape therapeutic strategies for BC and TNBC by enabling more effective and less toxic treatment regimens, ultimately reducing the reliance on high-dose chemotherapy and minimizing adverse effects.

items.summary: In vitro cell-based assays are fundamental tools in biomedical research, supporting investigations of cellular physiology, disease mechanisms, drug discovery, toxicology, regenerative medicine, and precision therapeutics. However, conventional two-dimensional (2D) cell culture models often fail to recapitulate the structural complexity and physiological functions of native tissues, prompting the development of…
items.abstract: In vitro cell-based assays are fundamental tools in biomedical research, supporting investigations of cellular physiology, disease mechanisms, drug discovery, toxicology, regenerative medicine, and precision therapeutics. However, conventional two-dimensional (2D) cell culture models often fail to recapitulate the structural complexity and physiological functions of native tissues, prompting the development of advanced platforms, including three-dimensional (3D) cultures, organoids, organ-on-a-chip technologies, and microphysiological systems. Recent advances in cell viability and cytotoxicity assessment, functional cellular analysis, molecular profiling, clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR)-based functional genomics, high-content imaging, flow cytometry, single-cell and spatial multi-omics, and automated high-throughput screening have expanded the analytical capabilities of cell-based assays. Furthermore, the integration of artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted image analysis and computational biology has enhanced cellular phenotyping, biomarker discovery, and mechanistic investigation, with the potential to improve the prediction of therapeutic efficacy and toxicity. Nevertheless, challenges related to physiological relevance, technical variability, inadequate standardization, high operational costs, scalability, poor reproducibility, cell-line misidentification, batch-to-batch variation, and inconsistent reporting continue to hinder translational applications. Future progress will depend on integrating physiologically relevant models with AI-driven analytics, spatial multi-omics, digital pathology, automated screening, and microphysiological systems. Standardized protocols, harmonized reporting practices, and interdisciplinary collaboration will be essential to improve reproducibility, strengthen regulatory acceptance, advance precision medicine, and reduce reliance on animal experimentation. In this context, this review critically evaluates conventional and emerging in vitro cell-based assays, emphasizing their biological principles, analytical capabilities, translational applications, and practical limitations, while highlighting future opportunities to improve predictive accuracy, reproducibility, and clinical translation.

items.abstract: We introduce Clover-35B-A3B-Preview (Clover), a mixture-of-experts diffusion language model with 35 billion total parameters and 3 billion activated parameters, supporting thinking-mode generation. Clover adapts Gated Delta Networks to block diffusion by combining recurrent memory of previously generated context with bidirectional softmax attention inside the current block. Historical memory readout competes with current-block tokens in a shared softmax, with learnable block-size calibration and a separate, zero-initialized right-context convolution branch. Clover leads the seven evaluated agent metrics, including 73.6 on SWE-bench Verified and 51.7 on Terminal-Bench 2.1. On internal agent workloads, it reaches a reported generation speed of 680 tokens/s using one NVIDIA GB300 GPU at BF16 precision and batch size one. We organize the evaluation around model quality, drafting and verification costs, and deployment under constrained memory. We also describe a decision-model variant that generates answers to related questions in one denoising pass. On an internal set of 500 groups, joint prediction raises question accuracy from 90.37% to 93.88% and all-correct group accuracy from 65.4% to 77.0%.

items.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to follow natural-language instructions, yet still fail frequently in closed-loop flight. Correcting these failures requires repairs, i.e., actions that avoid them at the states the policy itself reaches, which human pilots cannot label at scale and rule-based planners cannot supply reliably. In this paper, we present AeroRSI, a recursive self-improvement framework in which an aerial navigation policy iteratively learns from its own failures. Our key insight is that a failing policy should judge its own repairs by flying on from them. Judged in this way, its sampled actions and even rule-based proposals that hurt it when imitated directly become reliable supervision. Moreover, an episode terminates at its first failure, concealing subsequent failures until the earlier ones are repaired. AeroRSI thus renews its supervision in every round, anchoring the failures of the current policy, verifying repairs by its continuation, and distilling them while keeping its behavior elsewhere. On TravelUAV, three rounds raise the success rate of a supervised 2B-parameter policy from 46.4% to 67.5% and reduce collisions by half, surpassing the previous state of the art by 10.6 points from the same initialization without extra human labels or inference cost. Code and models are available at https://github.com/starsholic/AeroRSI.

To lower cost, build environments in batches, and reduce manual effort, each work trades away part of the environment through its construction choices. We describe these choices along three dimensions: reward coverage, the goal-reaching trajectories the verifier rewards; data coverage, the application data the agent is exposed…
items.abstract: Graphical user interface (GUI) agents are widely trained in executable GUI environments. To lower cost, build environments in batches, and reduce manual effort, each work trades away part of the environment through its construction choices. We describe these choices along three dimensions: reward coverage, the goal-reaching trajectories the verifier rewards; data coverage, the application data the agent is exposed to beyond what the task reads or writes; and feature coverage, the application features beyond what the task uses. Existing works set each dimension on engineering grounds, but they do not measure its effect on training. How complete must an environment be to train a capable agent, and along which dimensions? In MobileGym, we adjust each dimension separately, train Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct, and evaluate every policy in the original full environment. A verifier that rewards only one reference path lowers success by 10.53 points, and removing unneeded records also lowers success. Pruning unneeded features instead raises success from 51.61% to 56.13%, entirely on tasks whose environments it left unchanged. The gain reverses when each episode is weighted equally and vanishes when only episodes on the pruned tasks are balanced. Without pruning, length weighting there reinforces long detour successes that erode skills on other tasks. Following these findings, we build MobileGym-Lite, which keeps reward and data coverage complete and prunes unneeded features. It outperforms Full in the full environment (55.48% versus 51.61% success) with lower construction cost.

items.title: Seeing the Invisible: How Vision-Language Models Read, Predict and Trace Radio Fields
items.summary: Operating in the physical world requires reasoning beyond what cameras directly capture. In a city, radio signals are invisible to the lens, yet their strength is governed by the buildings and streets an image does show. Given only these visible structures, can vision-language models (VLMs) infer the invisible radio field they shape? Probing true physical reasoning requires exact fields in real cities, alongside…
items.abstract: Operating in the physical world requires reasoning beyond what cameras directly capture. In a city, radio signals are invisible to the lens, yet their strength is governed by the buildings and streets an image does show. Given only these visible structures, can vision-language models (VLMs) infer the invisible radio field they shape? Probing true physical reasoning requires exact fields in real cities, alongside controlled interventions where a single physical factor changes. We build a label-free engine that turns any coordinate on Earth into a ray-traceable city, simulates matched single-factor counterfactuals, and computes every answer exactly. This yields RadioVISTA, a benchmark and training dataset for visual reasoning about invisible fields. Physically, a radio field is the sum of its propagation paths, yet across six continents we uncover a striking field-path dissociation: frontier VLMs accurately judge where a field is strong, but fail to tell whether a single direct or one-wall path exists. Open models fail even earlier at reading the field itself, and are systematically wrong, scoring below random guessing even when credited for any of four attempts. On unseen cities, fine-tuning brings a 9B open model close to frontier proprietary models on fields, yet neither supervised nor reinforcement fine-tuning improves path tracing. Supervising only final answers teaches models to approximate the field, yet leaves single-path geometry out of reach.

items.title: From Points to Trajectories: Rethinking Multimodal Alignment for Physical Events
items.summary: Advancing physical artificial intelligence (Physical AI) requires moving beyond static object recognition to ground how real-world mechanics (e.g., impact, friction, and force transfer) unfold over time. While multimodal aligners seek to capture these interactions by matching multi-sensor streams, prevailing architectures compress each temporal sequence into a single pooled embedding. We show that this paradigm…
items.abstract: Advancing physical artificial intelligence (Physical AI) requires moving beyond static object recognition to ground how real-world mechanics (e.g., impact, friction, and force transfer) unfold over time. While multimodal aligners seek to capture these interactions by matching multi-sensor streams, prevailing architectures compress each temporal sequence into a single pooled embedding. We show that this paradigm fails on twin events: distinct physical executions recorded under identical task conditions. Collapsing the temporal dimension averages out transient cross-modal dynamics, effectively reducing physical event alignment to static scene recognition. Formally, we prove that as sequence length increases, any temporally pooled representation converges to the stationary recording condition. Consequently, as windows grow, no choice of loss function or embedding geometry can disambiguate twin events from pooled features alone. Instead, we show that physical events are uniquely identified by the event gap, namely the instantaneous, synchronous co-fluctuations across modalities that are erased by pooling and accumulate only along unpooled trajectories. To recover this signal, we introduce CounterPoint, a lightweight plug-in module that strips out each modality's temporal mean to score frame-level cross-modal agreement. Integrated across four state-of-the-art (SOTA) multimodal aligners, CounterPoint shifts representations from coarse condition matching to fine-grained physical event alignment, consistently outperforming existing temporal alignment methods.

items.abstract: Purpose of review Postoperative acute kidney injury (AKI) significantly impairs short- and long-term clinical outcomes after thoracic noncardiac surgery, including increased mortality and prolonged hospitalization. This review synthesizes current evidence on the incidence, prognostic impact, risk factors, and evolving preventive strategies for AKI in thoracic surgery. Recent findings Intraoperative fluid imbalance and hypotension are robust, modifiable risk factors for AKI. While goal-directed fluid therapy and machine learning-based Acumen Hypotension Prediction Index (Edwards Lifesciences, Irvine, California, USA) monitoring effectively optimize intraoperative hemodynamics and reduce hypotensive episodes, recent clinical trials and meta-analyses indicate they do not directly reduce postoperative AKI rates after general thoracic surgery. However, optimizing drug administration - such as continuous intravenous tacrolimus and shortened vancomycin duration - has demonstrated clinical benefit. Furthermore, evidence outside thoracic surgery demonstrates that the biomarker-guided Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes care bundle significantly decreases moderate-to-severe AKI in high-risk surgical populations, suggesting potential applicability in thoracic surgical care. Summary Given the multifactorial etiology of AKI, single hemodynamic interventions alone are insufficient for prevention. Perioperative care should integrate multimodality strategies, including optimal fluid and pressure management, pharmacological stewardship, and high-risk screening with care bundles. Further studies are needed to establish tailored preventive protocols, particularly for high-risk thoracic procedures such as lung transplantation and pneumonectomy.

items.abstract: Purpose of review More than a century after Jacobaeus, medical thoracoscopy is being reshaped by demands for precise pleural diagnosis, adequate tissue for molecular characterisation, combined local treatment and efficient care. This review uses its historical evolution to examine current indications, instruments, biopsy strategies, anaesthetic design and service models, with emphasis on recent evidence. Recent findings Rigid and semirigid thoracoscopy achieve similarly high diagnostic yield but differ in access, force transmission, tissue size, pain and sedative requirements. Recent studies favour needs-led sampling: standard forceps for most visible lesions, with cryobiopsy or advanced tools when depth, invasion, fibrosis or molecular profiling is limiting. Trials support selective rather than routine use of pleurodesis, indwelling catheters, regional blocks, high-flow oxygen or first-line thoracoscopy for pleural infection. Image enhancement, artificial intelligence, hybrid instruments and single-use platforms remain promising but incompletely validated. Summary Medical thoracoscopy should remain a targeted pleural procedure that preserves spontaneous ventilation while integrating diagnosis, adequate tissue acquisition, selected therapy and pathway efficiency. Technology and anaesthetic intensity should be matched to clinical need and adopted only when they improve measurable patient or system outcomes.

items.abstract: Introduction Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for chronic total occlusions (CTO) remains technically challenging, with lower technical success than non-CTO PCI. Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) and intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) may improve procedural and stent-related outcomes by supporting procedural planning, lesion crossing, and stent optimization. Areas covered A literature search of PubMed, Google scholar, identified randomized trials, registries, observational studies, meta-analyses, and consensus documents on CCTA and IVUS in CTO PCI. CCTA enables three-dimensional assessment of cap morphology, occlusion length, tortuosity, calcification, and distal vessel quality, refining complexity assessment and strategy selection. IVUS provides real-time guidance for proximal cap identification, guidewire position, reentry techniques, vessel sizing, and stent optimization. Artificial intelligence and image co-registration are also discussed. Expert opinion CCTA and IVUS provide complementary information across the stages of CTO PCI. Selective preprocedural CCTA may be most valuable in anatomically complex lesions, whereas IVUS supports lesion crossing and should be strongly considered for stent optimization. Wider adoption will depend on workflow integration, operator training, automated image analysis, and prospective validation of imaging-guided strategies.

items.abstract: We present Xing 4, a series of large language models that extends the TeleChat lineage through coordinated advances in model architecture and training infrastructure on Ascend. This report describes the design principles and systems engineering behind the series, spanning architecture selection, large-scale pretraining, and reasoning and agentic post-training. We study how sparse activation, attention design, model depth and width, and speculative decoding balance model capacity with computation, memory access, and execution overhead. Our pretraining infrastructure builds on MindSpore HyperParallel, combining topology-aware hybrid sharding, efficient distributed optimizer execution, and coordinated management of long-sequence workloads and activation memory. CPU affinity and core isolation further reduce host scheduling interference. Together, these mechanisms support the pretraining of a 285B-parameter model on 8,192 Ascend 910C cards, providing a concrete setting for the architectural and systems studies. For post-training, we introduce TeleGym, a unified agent execution platform that connects execution, evaluation, and trajectory construction to policy optimization. Disaggregated asynchronous execution, bounded oversampling, and partial rollout accommodate heterogeneous task durations while preserving trajectory continuity across policy updates. Together, these advances establish an Ascend-oriented training foundation for the continued development of Xing 4 across model scales and increasingly demanding reasoning and agent workloads.

items.abstract: Autoregressive video diffusion models generate frames based on new observations and inputs, making them a promising medium for interactive visual experiences. However, existing models are orders of magnitude too slow for fluid interaction. This paper introduces FastFrames, a family of fast autoregressive video diffusion models that achieves interactive latency without compromising quality. We profile the inference pipeline of state-of-the-art models and find that operations often treated as fixed implementation details, such as VAE decoding and KV cache updates, in fact account for over half of end-to-end inference latency. We challenge the assumption that these components are indispensable and replace them with lightweight alternatives. Our 1.3B variant runs at 36 ms per frame, or 28 responses per second (RPS), on a single B200 GPU while matching the generation quality of a state-of-the-art model that is nearly 8x slower. Our 14B variant runs at 45 ms per frame, or 22 RPS, on an 8x B200 GPU node and yields significantly better visual quality and realism. We show that FastFrames enables real-time interaction in applications such as camera-conditioned and physics-conditioned video generation.

items.abstract: LLM agents increasingly drive their own learning. Self-improvement methods delegate various components of model optimization to the models themselves. As models become more capable, this motivates a basic question: do these increasingly capable models still need us to specify how they should self-improve? In this paper we study an autonomous paradigm in which, given basic primitives, resources, and a general goal for self-improvement, agents construct their own self-learning algorithm for context-based optimization. Using the setting of gameplay as a testbed, a frozen LLM agent is given a compute budget and tools for collecting experience and updating text documents, and allowed to freely experiment without an externally imposed loop or access to real-world data. We find that sufficiently capable models do self-improve under these conditions, demonstrating strategies that align with classic cognitive frameworks for self-regulated learning and constructs from machine learning literature on self-generated curricula. Furthermore, we study the extent to which the learned text artifacts transfer to external benchmarks, observing improvement across different game horizons, mechanics, and 3D navigation.

items.abstract: Robot manipulation videos provide a rich visual experience, yet recovering robot action and gripper-state annotations from RGB observations still remains challenging. Using the embodiment-agnostic tool-center-point (TCP) pose as the action space, we present TCP4D, a unified model in which a shared 4D scene representation both tracks observed TCP motion and generates future TCP trajectories. Given a monocular video and initial 2D TCP queries, the tracker directly recovers metric TCP poses in SE(3) and gripper states alongside scene geometry and camera parameters. The generator samples local features from the same 4D representation along the recovered TCP tracks, then combines them with robot observations and language instructions to predict future TCP states. Our new cross-embodiment augmentation pipeline converts existing RGB videos into demonstrations for alternative embodiments by retargeting the recovered motion and synthesizing the corresponding observations, without recorded source-robot states. Experiments show that the tracker achieves absolute trajectory errors of 7.60 and 16.07 mm on DROID and RoboLab and adapts to a new embodiment with only ten demonstrations. The generator achieves 69.19% mean success on RoboTwin and outperforms well-established policy models on two real-world tasks, while joint training on source and augmented demonstrations improves target-robot success by 41.5% over augmented-only training.

However, realizing this potential requires coordinated whole-body interactions, coherent long-horizon planning, and precise synchronization across robots. items.abstract: Collaboration promises to extend humanoid capabilities beyond what individual robots can achieve. However, realizing this potential requires coordinated whole-body interactions, coherent long-horizon planning, and precise synchronization across robots. We introduce Heave-Ho, a decentralized framework for long-horizon collaborative multi-humanoid loco-manipulation. At the low level, we develop a multi-agent post-training framework that adapts a humanoid foundation tracking model to physically coupled interactions between humanoids, enabling coordinated decentralized control from local observations alone. At the high level, we train a vision-language planner and design a speech-based leader-follower coordination mechanism to synchronize decentralized execution without network communication. Trained with two identical humanoids, our system scales to teams of up to ten robots and generalizes to heterogeneous teams without retraining. To benchmark these capabilities, we introduce HH-Bench, comprising 12 tasks involving teams of 2 to 10 humanoids, including heterogeneous teams. Systematic evaluations show that Heave-Ho consistently outperforms baseline methods, while real-world experiments demonstrate robust decentralized collaboration across challenging tasks.

items.abstract: π^4 is a unified foundation model for 4D scene perception. From diverse, uncalibrated RGB observations in the wild---a single image, an unordered collection, or a video sequence---it recovers dense geometry, camera poses, and metric scale, together with 2D/3D point tracks and moving-object masks for multi-image inputs. It couples a geometry branch with a geometry-conditioned motion branch, which predicts image-space correspondences that are lifted into 3D using reconstructed target-view geometry. Across diverse benchmarks, π^4 achieves the best overall average rank in geometry evaluation, alongside competitive performance in single- and multiview 2D/3D point tracking and moving-object segmentation. With a shared backbone, the full geometry-and-motion system contains approximately 0.5B parameters---less than half the size of most baselines. It produces joint reconstructions and tracks in one forward pass, including large-scale scenes with thousands of input images despite training with contexts of at most 64 views. We further present the data and training recipe underlying these capabilities, together with empirical studies of key design choices. Code and models are available at https://github.com/yyfz/Pi4.

items.abstract: Standard neural architectures such as the Transformer were chosen because they train well with gradient descent and run fast on GPUs. In weight-space programming, a large language model (LLM) writes target weights by hand without gradient-based training, so those reasons no longer apply. Should we keep the Transformer? Given minimal guidance, ten labeled examples, and a sandbox, mainly on multiple-choice questions, we task three frontier LLMs with either generating the weights of a fixed architecture or designing the architecture themselves. When free to design, all three compile plain-text facts into a sparse table queried by a fixed procedure, reaching up to 54.4% test accuracy. An LLM-designed model achieves higher test accuracy than the most accurate released Transformer that the same LLM wrote while using about 1,800x fewer parameters. Without gradients, they choose a table, in which the LLM can state what each weight means and can find and rewrite a wrong one. Each wrong answer points to one row, and removing a row changes about one other answer. From this, we propose an associative-memory-based model up to 17x faster on GPUs than a same-sized Transformer. We also test pretrained weights, other benchmarks, and tasks where models generate answers. Pretrained LLMs remain more accurate; the claim concerns which structure to build when writing weights.

items.abstract: Identifying essential genes in bacteria is crucial for drug discovery and synthetic biology. Genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs) evaluated via flux balance analysis remain standard, yet they rely on the often-invalid premise that mutant strains optimize for maximum growth. Recent machine learning approaches circumvent this limitation using random forests or graph neural networks on mass flow graphs (MFGs). However, data-driven tools like random forests discard network topology, while graph-based tools like MFGs decompose multi-component biochemical reactions into pairwise interactions, misrepresenting complex stoichiometry and limiting interpretability. Furthermore, existing methods remain largely uncharacterised in data-scarce regimes and cross-environmental conditions. Here, we introduce HyperGenie, a framework that integrates genome-scale metabolic models with directed hypergraph neural networks by representing metabolites as nodes and reactions as hyperedges. Operating directly on wild-type flux features, HyperGenie eliminates post-knockout optimality assumptions, achieves a 13% PR-AUC improvement over prior objective-dependent methods, and matches computationally demanding, state-of-the-art flux-sampling baselines. Using HyperGenie to guide targeted growth curve assays, we identified latent essentiality misannotations across three genes in the benchmark iML1515 dataset, which we then reconciled and validated experimentally via PCR. In data-scarce regimes, HyperGenie retained robust predictive performance (> 90% PR-AUC) when trained on as little as 40% of the data. To isolate the value of hypergraph message passing, we benchmarked HyperGenie against an independent-reaction multilayer perceptron (MLPGenie) across diverse nutrient environments and uptake rates, where HyperGenie's hypergraph inductive bias yielded consistent accuracy gains (> 2% in glucose; > 4% across six alternative carbon sources). Notably, HyperGenie exhibits robust zero-shot cross-nutrient generalization, accurately forecasting gain-of-essentiality phenotypes on novel carbon sources, though loss-of-essentiality remains challenging. Finally, coupling hypergraph representations with SHAP attribution provides actionable mechanistic insights into metabolic rewiring, establishing a data-efficient, interpretable platform for discovering novel antibiotic targets.

items.abstract: Acute lung injury (ALI) and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) are both life-threatening diseases. Sepsis-related ALI frequently presents with complications of sepsis, which are mostly identified by the presence of non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema and refractory hypoxia. Despite the advancements in the field of drug discovery and delivery science, the understanding and management of sepsis-associated ALI are insufficient. WGCNA and differential expression analyses were integrated across multiple transcriptomics database cohorts to determine the core common candidate genes associated with sepsis-associated ALI and PTL. A Lasso model with SHAP interpretability was trained for feature selection. Molecular docking was performed for all candidate targets using PyRx with AutoDock Vina as the docking engine. Intersection of predicted parthenolide (PTL) targets and ALI-associated genes yielded 17 candidate genes. The Lasso algorithm used nested cross-validation, yielding an AUC of 0.827 (95% CI 0.767-0.928) and external validation with AUC values of 0.918 (GSE76293) and 0.667 (GSE10361). Molecular docking analysis indicated that the potential binding energies of the selected targets were - 5.9 to - 8.5 kcal/mol. These computational findings identify candidate PTL-associated molecular targets and provide a structural hypothesis to guide experimental validation.

items.abstract: Foundation models have advanced microscopy image segmentation, but existing models are trained on two-dimensional data, struggle with complex structures in volumetric data, and address only a narrow range of analysis tasks. Here we present Segment Anything for Microscopy 2 (μSAM2), a foundation model that adapts SAM2 to joint 2D and 3D segmentation in light and electron microscopy. Trained on annotations of more than 23 million cells and nuclei and 1.6 million cellular structures, μSAM2 achieves state-of-the-art automatic and interactive segmentation and outperforms generalist and specialist methods on volumetric data. Dedicated models further enable accurate mitochondrion and nucleus segmentation in electron microscopy. Beyond segmentation, μSAM2 supports pixel and object classification from few annotations as well as cell tracking in 2D and 3D time-lapse data. All functionality is available in the user-friendly μSAM napari plugin. We demonstrated the capabilities of μSAM2 on challenging use cases spanning developmental biology, organoid research, cardiac physiology, and histopathology.

items.abstract: The automated segmentation of unstained kidney brightfield microscopy images remains a significant challenge in medical imaging. In conventional histopathology, staining provides crucial structural and molecular contrast, allowing renal compartments and structures to be readily distinguished. The absence of staining markedly reduces this contrast, obscuring the fine architectural details that are essential for diagnosis. Addressing this gap would reduce reliance on staining protocols, reduce technical and interpretive variability, and preserve valuable tissue for downstream molecular or multi-omics analyses. Ultimately, automation of unstained image segmentation could enable faster, more objective tissue analysis while preserving samples for further molecular testing. In this work, we provide a comprehensive review of state-of-the-art segmentation methods applied to renal brightfield microscopy images. Current findings highlight a predominance of Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) based architectures for semantic segmentation approaches while recent trends point to the growing application of transformer-based and instance-segmentation strategies. However, the field is still hampered by the scarcity and poor annotation of publicly available renal datasets. Aiming to further contribute to the enhancement of the field, a dataset of 18 Whole Slide Images (WSIs) of unstained human kidney tissue is made publicly available. Additionally, in the dataset, we provide 543 annotated tiles extracted from the WSIs, facilitating further research into stain-independent segmentation approaches. As a third contribution, we present a preliminary case study, evaluating state-of-the-art deep learning segmentation architectures, including U-Net and Segment Anything Model (SAM). Our preliminary results indicate that deep learning models demonstrate promising segmentation performance in unstained kidney biopsies. In alignment with these findings, advanced customised loss functions and data augmentation were integrated into the supervised training of the promising U-Net, DeepLabv3+, and TransUNet models, achieving significant improvements compared to the baseline experiments. To exploit the abundance of unlabelled data, we further tested FixMatchSeg, a semi-supervised learning method; however, its segmentation performance remained slightly behind the supervised methods. Taken together, these contributions establish a foundation for future research in stain-independent Computational Pathology, demonstrating that unstained brightfield microscopy images can reliably support downstream tissue analysis tasks. Our dataset, validation experiments, and methodological insights provide the community with both resources and benchmarks to advance robust, data-efficient, and generalisable kidney tissue segmentation.

items.abstract: Rapid technological innovation and artificial intelligence (AI) have transformed not only the resolution at which the brain can be observed, but also the questions that can be asked, shifting the field from description toward prediction, regulation and generation. Yet progress has largely advanced along parallel trajectories, and findings at one level rarely inform or constrain the next. Here, we review recent advances in three exemplary domains and propose a future-oriented framework for their integration. First, molecular and cellular neurotechnology, including synaptic proteomics, cryo-electron tomography, super-resolution microscopy, optoacoustic and ultrasound imaging, sonogenetics and molecular MRI, resolves neural processes with unprecedented specificity. Second, AI-based decoding of human brain activity yields precise signatures of complex, subjective conscious experiences in naturalistic contexts and is beginning to inform diagnosis, drug evaluation and individualized neuromodulation in mental disorders. Third, large-scale neural recordings, mechanistic whole-brain simulations, neural foundation models and AI surrogate brains are converging toward individualized digital twin brains. We argue that the next level of progress requires integrating these domains into a closed loop of reciprocal constraints, in which molecular measurements inform model parameters, human signatures define and evaluate what models must reproduce, and model predictions prioritize perturbations that can be tested across domains.

items.abstract: The International Society of Urological Pathology (ISUP) grade upgrading from biopsy to radical prostatectomy (RP) occurs in approximately 30%-40% of prostate cancer patients and may compromise treatment planning. Although multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) improves lesion characterization, prostatitis-like signal changes can mimic clinically significant cancer and confound radiological interpretation; however, no predictive model has incorporated mpMRI-diagnosed prostatitis as a variable for ISUP upgrading. This single-center retrospective study enrolled 503 consecutive men who underwent "12+1"-core transperineal ultrasound-guided systematic biopsy supplemented by cognitive mpMRI-targeted cores followed by laparoscopic RP (from May 2021 to October 2024). Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) logistic regression with 10-fold cross-validation was used for feature selection, and six machine learning classifiers were trained and evaluated on an independent test set (7:3 split). ISUP upgrading occurred in 195 patients (38.8%), and mpMRI-diagnosed prostatitis was significantly more prevalent in upgraded cases (27.2% vs 11.4%, P < 0.001). The random forest model achieved the highest weighted composite score (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [ROC-AUC]: 0.823; average precision: 0.799) and was selected as the final model. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis ranked feature importance as: basal tumor location (mean |SHAP|: 0.145), Prostate Imaging Reporting and Data System (PI-RADS) ≥4 (mean |SHAP|: 0.121), percentage of positive cores (mean |SHAP|: 0.100), maximum tumor diameter (mean |SHAP|: 0.062), and mpMRI-diagnosed prostatitis (mean |SHAP|: 0.040). As one of the first models to incorporate mpMRI-diagnosed prostatitis, this SHAP-interpretable framework showed that such prostatitis adds predictive value beyond PI-RADS scoring. This may help identify patients at heightened risk of undergrading on biopsy.

items.abstract: Manual construction of patient-specific models has limited the use of virtual reality (VR) for case-specific spine surgical rehearsal, and simulator assessments are often not patient-specific. We present a largely automated pipeline that converts routine preoperative CT and MRI into patient-specific 3D models for VR rehearsal of lumbar decompression, paired with case-specific written assessments. CT was segmented with an unmodified vertebral network and MRI with an in-house nnU-Net; volumes were registered and exported for VR. A locally hosted large language model generated per-case assessments from each patient's radiology report; the pipeline ran in approximately two minutes per case, and MRI segmentation reached a mean Dice of 0.870. Eight patient-specific models were prepared, and eleven trainees (undergraduate to fellow) completed a faculty-guided session with pre/post knowledge testing. Knowledge scores increased from 5.82 to 7.27 out of 10 (Wilcoxon $p=0.008$; Cohen's $d=1.01$), with 8 of 11 improving and none declining, and trainees rated educational value favorably. This feasibility study demonstrates a fast, fully private pipeline producing patient-specific VR models and matched assessments; the educational findings are preliminary and uncontrolled, motivating a larger controlled trial.

items.abstract: Abstract Periventricular lesions are central to the diagnosis of multiple sclerosis (MS), but automatic segmentation is the least dependable. Whether a lesion is periventricular (PV) or deep is said by its three-dimensional distance to the ventricles. We show that on a thick-slice clinical MRI this decision depends on the ventricles in adjacent slices and on the slice spacing, so that an in-plane distance would show 30% of PV lesion voxels as deep. We therefore give the geometry explicitly. A 3D distance-to-ventricle map, computed in millimetres on the full volume, is added in as one of the input channel to a 2.5D U-Net that segments ventricles, normal white matter hyperintensities (WMH), PV lesions and deep lesions. On the 100-patient MS3SEG dataset, against an identically trained baseline, the distance model raised held-out Dice for PV lesions from 0.731 to 0.758 and for deep lesions from 0.702 to 0.738 (Holm-corrected p < 0.001) and reduced PV/deep label confusions by 71%, while the pooled lesion Dice was unchanged. Ablation and counterfactual analyses shows that the prior improves the structural assignment of lesions rather than their detection itself.
