items.abstract: Asthma is a common chronic inflammatory airway disease closely associated with dysregulated iron metabolism and oxidative stress. Ferro-aging, a recently described form of cellular senescence driven by iron overload, is characterised by sustained lipid peroxidation, but its gene-level links to asthma remain poorly defined. By intersecting differentially expressed genes from the GEO induced-sputum dataset with a ferro-aging gene set and applying five machine learning algorithms, we identified SETD7 as a hub ferro-aging gene. SETD7 was consistently downregulated in asthma in the discovery cohort and in two independent external cohorts (induced sputum GSE41863 and BALF GSE74986), with AUCs of 0.749, 0.763 and 0.834. Single-cell analysis revealed predominant SETD7 expression in goblet and Club cells, positively correlated with ferro-aging scores. In vitro, house dust mite stimulation reduced SETD7 expression, whereas SETD7 knockdown attenuated HDM-induced TSLP, IL-1β and MUC5AC expression and SETD7 overexpression exacerbated inflammation and promoted senescence through lipid peroxidation. Both trichostatin A and the selective SETD7 inhibitor (R)-PFI-2 attenuated these responses, and SETD7 overexpression partially reversed the protective effect of trichostatin A. Collectively, these findings identify SETD7 as a candidate ferro-aging gene in asthma and provide a theoretical basis for alleviating ferro-aging-associated airway inflammation.

items.abstract: Short therapeutic peptides are often limited by rapid systemic clearance and insufficient in vivo persistence. Although formulation- and carrier-based approaches can improve delivery, intrinsic sequence optimization remains underexplored. Using thymosin α1 (Tα-1) as a clinically validated model, we applied structure-guided intrinsic stabilization to improve apparent systemic persistence while preserving context-dependent immunomodulatory function. An AlphaFold-derived comparative scaffold, FoldX single-site scanning, and DUET cross-validation identified D15 and E27 as stability-permissive engineering sites. D15M showed the most consistent overall improvement, whereas E27R supported E27 as a second optimization site. Both variants retained native-like structural features, resisted serum-associated degradation, and showed prolonged apparent systemic persistence after both subcutaneous and intravenous administration. These gains were accompanied by preserved biological activity in immunosuppressed mice, a tumor xenograft model, murine and human macrophage systems, and donor-derived peripheral blood mononuclear cells. The optimized variants maintained the context-dependent immunomodulatory profile of native Tα-1 rather than producing a broad constitutive increase in intrinsic activity. These findings support structure-guided intrinsic stabilization as a complementary strategy for improving the developability and systemic performance of short therapeutic peptides without compromising biological function.

items.abstract: Xenotransplantation is moving from isolated proof-of-concept procedures toward an engineered biotechnology platform for organ replacement. This review examines how genome-designed donor pigs, recipient-directed immunopharmacology, human-relevant in vitro testbeds, and data-driven decision systems can be integrated to address the remaining barriers to clinical translation. CRISPR-Cas-based engineering enables deletion of dominant carbohydrate xenoantigens, insertion of human complement- and coagulation-regulatory genes, modulation of innate and adaptive immune checkpoints, control of donor-organ growth, and inactivation of porcine endogenous retrovirus sequences. However, donor engineering does not eliminate residual T-cell, B-cell, antibody, complement, natural killer (NK) cell, macrophage, and inflammatory responses. Contemporary immunopharmacological strategies therefore increasingly combine costimulation blockade with complement inhibition, lymphocyte-directed therapy, and selected cytokine- or innate-immune interventions, with future regimens requiring closer integration of pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic monitoring with donor genotype and organ-specific risk. Organoids and microfluidic vascular systems may provide an intermediate testing layer by quantifying antibody binding, complement activation, endothelial injury, coagulation, leukocyte transmigration, cytokine responses, and tissue-specific function under controlled conditions before escalation to large-animal studies. Artificial intelligence may further support xenoantigen discovery, genome-editing design, donor-recipient matching, multimodal rejection surveillance, and ultimately clinician-supervised immunopharmacological decision support. We propose that these components should be connected through a traceable design-build-test-learn workflow linking computational prediction, donor construction, standardized functional testing, non-human-primate validation, and early human data. Durable translation will depend not on any single technological advance, but on reproducible donor manufacturing, precision immune control, validated human-relevant test systems, standardized longitudinal data, pathogen surveillance, organ-specific management, and transparent regulatory governance.

items.abstract: Protein-protein interfaces encode molecular recognition through spatially organized contacts, yet their buried, curved surfaces are difficult to inspect as a whole. Flattening these surfaces can expose interface organization but introduces geometric distortion and may divide individual residues into disconnected regions. We present TopoPPI, a geometry-aware platform that converts interaction surfaces into low-distortion two-dimensional atlases while retaining links to source atoms, residues and contacts. TopoPPI extends OptCuts with a contact-weighted penalty for seam-induced fragmentation of residue footprints-the surface regions assigned to individual residues-jointly balancing continuity, seam length and distortion. In a leakage-controlled benchmark of 2,236 experimental complexes, the geometry-only OptCuts foundation achieved 88.39% lower family-weighted scale-fair distortion than the next-best tested parameterization across 2,209 complete comparable outputs. Across 2,204 exact-domain comparisons, TopoPPI reduced family-weighted residue-footprint fragmentation by 12.81% (95% confidence interval, 11.50-14.05%), with a 2.60% increase in normalized seam length and a 0.061% increase in scale-fair distortion. Continuity gains extended to 1,180 fixed-pose pairs of AlphaFold monomer models and 145 predicted complexes, with fragmentation reductions of 18.60% and 11.65%, respectively. Functionally annotated antibody and colicin-immunity interfaces demonstrated reconnection of the footprints of experimentally characterized binding and specificity residues. Further applications mapped published binding and folding free-energy estimates onto the KRAS-RAF1 interface and compared shared receptor residues across two growth-hormone recognition sites. Available through graphical and command-line interfaces, TopoPPI provides a residue-aware visualization framework for integrating structural contacts and functional annotations within geometrically controlled interface maps.

items.abstract: Our aim is to accelerate autoregressive vision-language-action models (VLAs), which generate robot actions one token at a time. Speculative decoding makes this possible: a lightweight draft model proposes several tokens at once, and the VLA verifies them in a single pass, accepting only those that match its own predictions, so decoding remains lossless. The speedup, however, is limited in robot control, where many different tokens encode nearly the same motion and a draft close to the correct action is still rejected. To address this, our approach, VSpark, is built upon three design choices: (i) rollouts collected with calibrated action noise, which expose the draft to a wider range of robot states; (ii) feature alignment, which trains the draft to match the VLA's hidden features rather than its output tokens alone; and (iii) continuation reuse, which keeps the predictions the VLA has already computed along rejected drafts as candidates for the next verification step, instead of discarding them. On four VLAs with different action tokenizers and four manipulation benchmarks, VSpark achieves 1.28x to 2.10x speedup while keeping the VLA's decoding lossless.

items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have renewed interest in Page Stream Segmentation (PSS), splitting a multi-page file into its constituent documents. Yet published LLM methods still frame the task as boundary classification over one or a few neighboring pages, and commercial document-splitting APIs do not disclose their methods. We reimagine PSS for LLMs as a sequential process over the whole stream and propose RICoT (Recurrent Interleaved Chain-of-Thought), a prompting framework that works through the pages as a reader would: within a sliding window it reasons about each page and commits its boundary decision before moving on, and across windows it carries forward a compact record of what it has read, keeping per-call cost bounded. We also introduce FinancePSS-205, a benchmark of 205 real-world, de-identified financial page streams, to be released publicly. On FinancePSS-205, RICoT matches or outperforms pairwise and windowed prompting with the same backbone for each of three open-weight LLMs; on a TABME test subset, RICoT with GLM-5 reaches document F1 0.847 and boundary F1 0.915, above published zero-shot results. A 2B-parameter student, trained on a larger teacher's decisions with and without the page-level reasoning, performs comparably in both modes and comes within 0.05 document F1 of the strongest prompted model on FinancePSS-205.

items.abstract: Autoregressive vision-language-action (VLA) models predict discrete action tokens with the next-token objective of their vision-language backbone, so the action tokenizer defines the interface between the policy and the robot. In bimanual manipulation, the two arms share a repertoire of movements yet coordinate through complementary roles, and an action representation should capture both. However, most existing tokenizers encode both arms as a single concatenated action vector, in which motion patterns common to the two arms are not shared and cross-arm dependencies remain entangled within each token. The policy must therefore learn both aspects implicitly. We propose Bimanual Coordination Action Tokenization (BiCAT), which shares one motion representation across arms while conditioning each arm's tokens on its partner through symmetric cross-arm attention and a joint decoder. The policy then predicts all tokens of each arm in parallel, generating the left arm first and the right arm conditioned on it. Across ten RoboTwin 2.0 tasks and six real-world tasks on three embodiments, BiCAT achieves the highest success among the compared tokenizers. In simulation, it improves mean success by 17.6 percentage points over the strongest of eight baselines, with the largest gains on tasks that require close coordination between the arms, while requiring only 40.5 ms per action chunk. These results suggest that the action tokenizer is a natural place to model bimanual coordination.

items.abstract: Language models can gain capacity at little computational cost from n-gram embedding tables: large tables of learned vectors for short sequences of consecutive tokens, which are looked up and added to the model's input or to its intermediate layers. Recent designs commonly use a separate n-gram embedding table for each layer, which makes the tables costly in memory and prevents layers from sharing what they learn. Sharing a single table, however, gives every layer the same embedding and leaves no room for layer-wise preferences, and it performs poorly in practice. We propose Chorus, in which one set of n-gram embedding tables serves the whole network and every layer reads it in its own way. Each layer maps the refined embedding through its own projection layer, after rescaling its components by factors computed from its current hidden state. Chorus matches the quality of existing n-gram methods with 87% smaller tables: with 1.2B table parameters it predicts text better than FactorEngram and DeepSeek's Engram do with 9.6B. It outperforms Engram, TN-gram and FactorEngram in every setting where we compared them, across table sizes from 20M to 9.6B parameters. We also show that the recently proposed memory-efficient optimizer Ember works well with Chorus, saving 99.2% of table-optimizer memory compared with AdamW without degrading training performance. These results enable further scaling of n-gram embedding tables along the table-size axis by reducing memory use and allowing shared knowledge to be reused across layers.

items.abstract: We introduce Faithfulness Video Score (FVSCORE), a neuro-symbolic framework for specification-driven video generation evaluation. Existing evaluators rely on holistic MLLM judgments or vision-language metrics, yet aligning their scores with human judgments and tracing them to specific temporal violations remain open challenges. FVSCORE addresses these limitations by compiling each video into explicit propositions capturing prompt requirements and implicit propositions capturing unstated physical, temporal, and cross-modal constraints. It grounds each proposition using specialized perceptual tools and evaluates the resulting confidence traces with soft temporal operators inspired by Linear Temporal Logic. A Significance-Aware Calibration step then aligns verification with human perception by retaining only perceptually significant violations before producing a timestamp- and evidence-grounded report. We conduct extensive experiments across public and complex multi-event benchmarks with the strongest video models to date, demonstrating that FVSCORE outperforms holistic and agent-based evaluators in human correlation while providing highly accurate and interpretable feedback.

items.abstract: Identity matching asks whether two records denote the same identity, yet the answer depends on the target granularity. Two records may match at the base level but not at the variant level: they share an underlying design while differing in attributes such as color or size. Final matching accuracy does not separately characterize the capabilities involved. To study this problem, we use e-commerce as a challenging real-world domain. We introduce PURE, a diagnostic benchmark for multi-granularity multimodal identity matching covering four capability dimensions: Perception, Understanding, Reasoning, and Evidence-grounded Judgment. The benchmark comprises 1,457 multiple-choice questions across 14 tasks, derived from real-world matching pairs and verified by two domain experts. Across ten recent MLLMs, overall scores range from 47.1% to 86.0%. Understanding receives the highest mean score and Judgment the lowest, with weaknesses in visual difference localization and variant-level rule judgment. Modality ablations show that models benefit from multimodal evidence but can incorrectly identify conflicts between matching records. In direct matching, most models recognize matching pairs more reliably than non-matching pairs at the base level, whereas the reverse holds at the variant level. PURE therefore reveals what aggregate matching accuracy hides: not only whether models judge a pair correctly, but where they struggle to interpret evidence and apply matching criteria.

items.abstract: We present the Autoregressive View Model (AVM), which generates a scene as a stream of views without constructing an explicit 3D representation. Through a unified in-context interface, AVM conditions on images or videos to generate short clips along a requested camera path. Visual context grounds reconstruction and interpolation, while a learned prior enables extrapolation into unseen regions. AVM retrieves relevant views from inputs and generated history to form a bounded active context. We fine-tune a pretrained bidirectional video diffusion transformer with flow matching in an N-in-1-out formulation. We then tune a causal model on its own rollouts to improve photorealism, reduce denoising steps, and limit long-horizon drift. We scale training to approximately 8M scenes and video clips. We evaluate generation capacity and scene persistence across benchmarks for camera control, text control, visual quality, dynamics, sparse and 4D reconstruction, and long-horizon consistency. The results demonstrate that AVM adapts to diverse input and output settings through one in-context interface.

items.abstract: Streaming video generation must sustain quality beyond the training horizon while handling self-generated history and growing cache costs. To address these challenges, we present MovieRoll, a base-to-distilled framework that connects streaming fine-tuning, long-rollout distillation, and long-horizon inference. We first establish a robust multi-step base through Window-wise Teacher Forcing (WinTF), which jointly denoises chunks at progressive noise levels with bidirectional attention within each window and causal access to preceding history. To retain historical context efficiently, hierarchical KV-cache compression (HieraKV) exploits layer-wise attention patterns, retaining full history in shallow layers and sink--recent history in deeper layers. This reduces cache memory by up to 78% while improving generation quality. Building on this base, cumulative long tuning with distribution matching distillation (CuLT-DMD) holds parameters fixed throughout each long self-rollout and averages local gradients before updating. Each update therefore combines supervision across temporal positions while retaining only one local computation graph, enabling efficient long-rollout training of a few-step generator. To extend generation beyond the training horizon, KV recomputation bounds context for both models, while guidance annealing (AnnealCFG) reduces guidance toward the clean endpoint to stabilize MovieRoll-Base. Complementing these modeling advances, FBCA attention and PS-VAE decoding support efficient training and streaming output. On HeliosBench, MovieRoll-Base remains competitive at 30s after training on videos of up to 15s, and MovieRoll-Distilled achieves the highest total scores among the compared methods across single- and multi-event evaluations up to 60s, combining sustained naturalness with active motion.

items.title: K2-Horizon: A Frontier Fleet of Open Source Language Models
items.summary: We present K2-Horizon, a fleet of six fully open language models, from a 0.9B dense model to a 375B-A23B MoE, built for general-purpose reasoning and agentic work across math and science, software engineering, deep research, office automation, and beyond. items.abstract: We present K2-Horizon, a fleet of six fully open language models, from a 0.9B dense model to a 375B-A23B MoE, built for general-purpose reasoning and agentic work across math and science, software engineering, deep research, office automation, and beyond. The models lead or are competitive with strong open models of their size on agentic and coding benchmarks. On the modeling side, to strengthen reasoning, we introduce Mixture-of-Value Attention (MoVA), applying MoE to attention value projections, and softplus attention gating, a more flexible, theoretically motivated gate. Our 36B-A4B model uses both and nearly matches a 32B dense model trained on the same data, with one-seventh the active parameters. We also introduce Uno, lossless diffusion adapters that speed up decoding by up to 2.2x without a separate draft model. Our release follows the LLM360 definition of open source for transparency and reproducibility: the full development history, including intermediate checkpoints from every training stage, pre-training data, training logs, and all training, evaluation, and infrastructure code, notably our production-scale xLLM framework for dense and MoE training and the RL360 reinforcement-learning stack. Beyond the data itself, we release and document in detail every pipeline that built it, the part of model development that open releases most rarely disclose. These pipelines produced roughly 10T synthetic pre-training tokens, showing that synthetic data can be a major ingredient of pre-training at scale. Four of the models share one 22T-token pre-training corpus and recipe, revealing consistent scaling behavior and enabling controlled studies of scale and sparsity. All artifacts are available at https://ifm.ai/k2/

items.abstract: Biomolecular foundation models predict the structures of proteins and their complexes accurately, and large language models (LLMs) reason in natural language, but the two remain separate: the abilities of the former are not part of a general-purpose LLM, and the reasoning of the latter does not enter a structure prediction. Calpha aims at one general model that folds proteins and complexes, understands protein sequence and structure, and lets its language reasoning influence the structures it predicts. This report covers the first step, in which an LLM outputs single-chain protein structures. Qwen3.5-9B reads a sequence enriched with ESM2 residue features. It can respond in text or emit a token that invokes a pretrained SimpleFold structure head, which receives information about the protein only through Qwen's residue states. Under a fixed folding request, the head achieves mean TM-scores of 0.808 on the FoldBench-334 development set, 0.635 on CASP16 domains and 0.900 on a CAMEO-style PDB set. We compare these predictions with a baseline in which ESM2-3B encodes the sequence and a fine-tuned SimpleFold-3B head predicts the coordinates. The two systems also differ in trainable weights, training duration and crop length. For chains of 100--299 residues, all three paired confidence intervals include zero. At 300--600 residues, the mean differences are -0.044, -0.160 and -0.025, respectively. In a separate test, four English request types triggered folding on every evaluated example. Protein training reduced accuracy on a 350-item MMLU-Pro subset from 77.4% to 70.3%. An LLM can therefore output single-chain structures from its own states, with lower long-chain scores in the current comparisons and reduced accuracy on the evaluated MMLU-Pro subset. Complex prediction, structure understanding and the effect of language reasoning on the predicted coordinates remain future work.

items.abstract: When high-quality data runs out, a common practice is to train on it for several epochs, but each repeat is worth less than the last. Latent feedback, which feeds each token's top-layer state into the next token's input, is another way to spend that compute, yet it has not been tested against a vanilla Transformer that spends the same compute on more epochs. We run this test across a ladder of model sizes, unique data and epochs, tuning both models at every size and amount of unique data. Latent feedback makes every FLOP and every token count for more except when unique data is scarce relative to model size, a regime that today's models are far from. We find that latent feedback serves as an amplifier: with unique data fixed, it reaches a Transformer's loss with less compute; with epochs fixed, it reaches that loss with less unique data. Furthermore, both savings grow with unique data per parameter and with repetition, and downstream tasks agree. To go beyond our grid, we fit one scaling law to both models, in which latent feedback enters as a Transformer with more parameters; it predicts that both savings keep growing with unique data and repetition. Fitted on models from 60M to 271M parameters, the law predicts the losses at a held-out 778M size to within 0.3% and the gap between the two models to within 0.05%. At most, latent feedback saves 48% of the compute and 47% of the unique data. When data, not compute, is the limit, latent feedback is the better use of a FLOP for a model of a given size.

items.abstract: Abstract Inflammation is a primary immune response categorized into acute and chronic types, with chronic inflammation linked to various diseases such as autoimmune disorders and cancer. Conventional therapies often face limitations due to side effects and therapeutic resistance, prompting the exploration of small-molecule compounds as safer alternatives. In this study we emphasize the integration of machine learning (ML), particularly through structure-activity relationship (SAR) analysis and quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) modeling, to enhance drug discovery. A series of ML-based regression models, including LightGBM, were developed and systematically evaluated. Various feature selection method, were employed to effectively reduce the input dimensionality and improve model performance. The LightGBM model, based on combined Morgan and substructure count fingerprints, achieved strong predictive performance with an R² of 0.75 on the independent test dataset. External validation with FDA-approved compounds affirmed the model's applicability, highlighting key structural features identified through explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) techniques, specifically SHAP and LIME. This study concludes that the AISM-REGBF framework provides a reliable computational tool for predicting the anti-inflammatory potency (pIC₅₀) of small molecules.

items.abstract: Protein flexibility is a key determinant of molecular recognition, catalysis, and regulation, yet remains difficult to characterise at scale. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations provide detailed descriptions of time-dependent dynamics but are computationally expensive. Although recent AI-based structure prediction methods have substantially improved access to high-quality static protein structures, they inherently lack information regarding the dynamic fluctuations essential for functional understanding. There is therefore a need for scalable, structure-based computational approaches that can infer intrinsic protein flexibility without explicit dynamical sampling. We present ProtFlap, a graph neural network framework for predicting relative residue-level flexibility directly from static protein structures. ProtFlap represents proteins as residue interaction graphs and integrates empirical atomic energy features extracted from a single energy-minimised snapshot with structural and sequence-derived descriptors. Central to our approach is the hypothesis that the local atomic energy network encoded in a frozen protein structure contains sufficient information to estimate structural flexibility. Trained using atomic mobility labels, quantified via normalised root-mean-square fluctuation (RMSF) derived from short MD simulations, ProtFlap achieves robust and accurate flexibility prediction across diverse protein domains. Feature attribution analysis reveals that van der Waals-related energy terms are the dominant contributors to the prediction.

items.abstract: Abstract Tunneling nanotubes (TNTs) are actin-supported open membrane conduits that connect remote cells and carry vesicles, organelles, RNAs, and protein aggregates. A recent proteomic study defined the TNT proteome (TNTome) of U2OS human osteosarcoma cells as a set of 1,177 proteins and identified the tetraspanins CD9 and CD81 as non-redundant TNT regulators. Here we performed a proteome-wide computational analysis of the intrinsic disorder and liquid–liquid phase-separation (LLPS) propensity of the TNTome using RIDAO, CH-CDF analysis, D 2 P 2 , FuzDrop, the ELM resource, STRING, AlphaFold, and AFflecto. Of 1,176 proteins with complete predictions, 255 (21.7%) were highly disordered and 443 (37.7%) mostly ordered, with a mean disorder of 27.6 ± 27.2%. Among 253 highly disordered proteins scored by FuzDrop, 219 (86.6%) were predicted LLPS drivers; these drivers formed a dense STRING network (209 proteins, 2,200 edges, 21 hubs led by HNRNPA1, HNRNPC, HNRNPA2B1, SRSF1, NPM1, and FUS) that was strongly enriched in RNA-binding, mRNA-processing and ribonucleoprotein-complex functions. A bilateral deep dive into the 15 most disordered and 15 most ordered proteins, together with a catalogue of 1,647 short linear motifs, suggested a two-tier architecture, in which disordered, phase-separation-competent scaffolds coexist with ordered structural and enzymatic modules, including CD9 and CD81. We emphasize that all disorder predispositions and LLPS assignments are predictive and that, because the TNTome is cancer-derived and no non-cancer TNT proteome exists, the disorder/LLPS enrichment cannot yet be ascribed to TNT biology versus the malignant state. These intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) and intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs) and their predicted condensate behavior represent testable hypotheses for the molecular organization of TNTs.

items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is rapidly changing how scientists, including chemical biologists, conduct research. This review is intended to serve as an introduction for chemical biologists to applications of artificial intelligence in chemical biology. We review how chemical and biological data are featurized, the types of models commonly used in chemical biology applications, challenges in assessing accuracy of artificial intelligence models, and recent developments in agentic artificial intelligence for autonomous research. The applications we will cover include protein structure prediction, ligand discovery, peptide and protein design, prediction of mutational effects, interactomics and gene regulation, and virtual cells.

items.abstract: Abstract X-ray computed tomography can quantify pores inside a material, but noisy and blurred pore boundaries make measurements sensitive to the segmentation procedure. This work evaluates direct regression of pore volume, surface area proxy, sphericity, and elongation from a centered synthetic grayscale crop. We generated 180 independent sphere, ellipsoid, and irregular pore geometries and rendered each under three degradation conditions, yielding 540 crops of size 24 3 . All renderings of each geometry remained in one split. A compact three-dimensional convolutional neural network (CNN) was compared with Otsu thresholding and an Extra Trees regressor using segmentation and intensity features. On 27 held-out geometries at high degradation, volume mean absolute percentage error was 14.76% for the CNN, 67.29% for Otsu, and 3.74% for Extra Trees. Otsu recovered clean discrete volume exactly and had the lowest pooled elongation error. Paired and out-of-domain experiments reveal how size, nearby pores, unresolved features, and sampling affect the results. The contribution is a reproducible synthetic benchmark that identifies conditions under which learned estimation improves on thresholding and conditions where classical measurements remain stronger. Independent industrial scans are needed to assess transfer.

items.abstract: Abstract Deep learning studies on neuroimaging data frequently report accuracies close to 100%, yet such results can arise from data leakage rather than from learned disease signal. This paper is a case study of that failure in the author’s own work. A 3D convolutional neural network (CNN) was trained to separate Alzheimer’s disease (AD), mild cognitive impairment (MCI), early MCI (EMCI) and cognitively normal (CN) participants using 191,428 individual 3D volumes extracted from functional MRI (fMRI) acquisitions in the Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI). Each time frame was treated as an independent image, and the pooled frames were split at random, at the image level, into training and validation sets. The network reached 100% validation accuracy by epoch 14 and made no errors on any of the 191,428 volumes. We show that this outcome is explained by frame-level leakage: frames of the same participant are nearly identical, so a model can recognise individuals instead of disease stages, and a random split places almost every participant on both sides. We document the training signatures that exposed the problem, relate them to leakage patterns reported in the Alzheimer’s literature, quantify why image-level splitting of fMRI frames guarantees subject overlap, and propose a subject-level evaluation protocol. The corrected experiment is left to future work; the contribution of this paper is a transparent, reproducible account of how a plausible pipeline yields an invalid result, and how to detect it.

items.abstract: Abstract Background Previous researches have clarified potential clinical applications of radiomics-based prediction of tumor phenotype. The purpose of our research is to utilize radiomic features in computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) system of prediction for high Fuhrman nuclear grade and low Fuhrman nuclear grade in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (RCC) Methods We selected 110 images from 109 case number of axial contrast- enhanced computed tomography with a pathological diagnosis of clear cell RCC from The Cancer Imaging Achieve (TCIA) portal. After preprocessing and extraction of features of from radiological images, the Weka Experiment Environment was run to compare performance of different classifiers to predict high Fuhrman nuclear grade and low Fuhrman nuclear grade. Results Seventy features and 23 selected features were input into classifiers to predict high Fuhrman nuclear grade and low Fuhrman nuclear grade, respectively. The SVM based on poly-kernel classifier (Accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, area under the receiver operative characteristic curve (AUROC), precision, recall and F1 score were 82%, 82%, 82%, 82%, 82%, 82% and 82%, respectively) and K-Nearest neighbors (Accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, AUROC, precision, recall and F1 score were 90.91%, 91%, 89%, 90%, 92%, 91% and 91.5%. Respectively) showed significant better performance than other classifiers, such as Bagging (Bagging), Naive Bayes (NaiveBayes), Boosting (AdaBoostM1), Decision trees (J48), Bayesian Network (BayesNet), library Support vector machines (LibSVM), Artificial Neural Networks (Multilayer Perceptron), Logistic regression (Logistic), Random Forest Tree (RandomForest),respectively. Conclusions The developed CAD system generated by the optimal machine-learning methods with radiomic features is a non-invasive method of predicting and monitoring tumor-nuclear grading characteristics in image-defined response evaluation in clinical practice of targeted therapy of clear cell RCC. items.abstract: Abstract Objective : This study aimed to automatically detect the human tooth pulp cavity and pulp stones on cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) using deep learning-based semantic segmentation. Methodology : 523 annotated images of teeth from 112 CBCT examinations were used to train and evaluate four established deep learning architectures (U-Net, Attention U-Net, U-Net++, and DeepLabV3+) in segmenting the background, pulp cavity, and pulp stone(s). Subsequently a novel architecture was developed (DACA-DeepLab) and evaluated through an additive study. DACA-DeepLab incorporates DeepLabV3+ with a pyramid channel-spatial attention (PCSA) module, a dual-axis cross-attention (DACA) decoder, and a Sobel-guided boundary-refinement (BFR) head. Results : DeepLabV3+ achieved the best overall Dice performance among the four baseline architectures (mean, 0.775; pulp cavity, 0.838; pulp stone, 0.711). In the second study, combining PCSA and DACA yielded the highest performance (mean Dice, 0.733). Adding the boundary-refinement head reduced performance, suggesting sensitivity to the limited training set. Conclusion : Deep learning-based semantic segmentation can accurately identify human tooth pulp cavity and pulp stone(s) on CBCT. These findings establish a systematic benchmark for CBCT-based pulp segmentation and provide a foundation for AI-assisted endodontic diagnosis and pre-treatment planning.

items.abstract: Background: /Objectives: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a neurological disorder that adversely affects cognition, memory, and overall quality of life. Identifying AD in its initial phase is especially challenging when patients display cognitive impairments. Conventional methods rely on physicians to manually examine patients and analyze images, which is time-consuming and prone to errors. This review examines the use of artificial intelligence (AI) techniques for diagnosing AD using CT scans and MRI brain imaging. Methods: Research papers published from 2018 to 2026 were sourced from Google Scholar, IEEE Xplore, and Semantic Scholar. The techniques that were investigated in this study include Convolutional Neural Networks, 3D Convolutional Neural Networks, transfer learning, Vision Transformers, ensemble models, and multimodal approaches. Five research questions were posed to analyse the practicality of using AI-driven techniques in clinical settings, their novelty, scalability, robustness, and accuracy. Results: This study found that AI models can autonomously extract information from brain images and yield highly accurate results, with numerous researches demonstrating over 90% accuracy. Deep learning applied to MRI imaging is effective, while CT-based techniques can detect brain alterations when MRI is inaccessible. Different data types, including imaging, age, medical history, and vocal characteristics, can provide valuable insights into AD. However, issues remain, such as dataset discrepancies, variations among scanners and individuals, and insufficient testing of complex models on diverse populations. Conclusions: Future efforts should focus on accurate and transparent AI, integration of multiple data types, rapid and secure models, and testing on large datasets from multiple hospitals. AI should be developed to assist physicians in accurately diagnosing AD rather than replacing them.

items.abstract: Multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) improves detection of clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa) but is limited by inter-reader variability. Artificial intelligence (AI) has been increasingly applied to prostate segmentation and lesion detection, with heterogeneous results. Concerns remain regarding generalizability, data set bias, and validation. This review summarizes recent evidence on AI-assisted prostate MRI interpretation, identifies knowledge gaps, and outlines directions for future research. A systematic literature search of PubMed and Google Scholar was performed for studies published between January 2023 and April 2025 evaluating AI-assisted interpretation of biparametric or multiparametric prostate MRI. Reference lists were manually reviewed. Eligible studies assessed diagnostic performance of AI alone or in combination with radiologists. Eighteen studies met inclusion criteria from 157 screened. Standalone AI systems achieved areas under the curve (AUCs) ranging from 0.77 to 0.91, with sensitivities of 65.4% to 96% and specificities of 77.6% to 91%, occasionally outperforming radiologists. Hybrid AI-radiologist models improved inter-reader agreement, reduced interpretation time by up to 50%, and enhanced detection accuracy for equivocal (PI-RADS 3) lesions. AI assistance particularly benefited junior and general radiologists, improving diagnostic performance, confidence, and reproducibility. In active surveillance cohorts, AI demonstrated greater accuracy than radiologists for detecting disease progression (AUC=0.86 vs. 0.69), although specificity limitations persisted. Overall, AI integration into prostate MRI workflows demonstrates substantial potential to improve detection efficiency and standardization. Broader clinical adoption will require large-scale, multicenter validation, harmonized imaging protocols, and rigorous outcome-based evaluation.

items.abstract: Single-cell transcriptome sequencing has been widely applied across the life sciences. It enables accurate and robust identification of cell types in heterogeneous biological tissues through unsupervised clustering, shallow learning, and deep learning. While deep learning does not outperform shallow learning in classification performance, it streamlines cell type identification by eliminating cumbersome preprocessing procedures. However, the availability of training datasets with comprehensive cell type annotations is always limited, so new datasets inevitably contain cell populations that are not pre-defined in the training data. To address this limitation, we integrated unsupervised clustering with transformer-based models to identify cell populations unrecognized by classical methods. Specifically, we developed the Nankai GeneRank Classifier by fine-tuning the pre-trained Geneformer-V1 model, and then clustered cells based on its softmax-normalized class probability matrix (SCPM). Applied to a public colorectal cancer dataset, the new method, named SCPM-based clustering, resolved cell populations that cannot be unambiguously identified by classical methods alone and led to the discovery of novel candidate markers of colorectal cancer stem cells, demonstrating its utility.

items.abstract: Abstract: Background: Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD), a chronic gastrointestinal disorder with two main subtypes, Crohn's Disease (CD) and Ulcerative Colitis (UC), is associated with more aggressive phenotypes and greater diagnostic complexity in pediatric patients. Conventional diagnostic biomarkers, lack sufficient distinguishing power between IBD subtypes. This study aimed to investigate and compare proteomic and metaproteomic profiles of pediatric IBD (PIBD) patients and healthy controls to develop a diagnostic panel capable of accurately diagnose IBD and distinguish its subtypes. Methods: We performed an in-depth evaluation of mucosal luminal interface samples from PIBD patients and healthy individuals, separately analyzing both the human proteome and microbial metaproteome data. The study involved selecting appropriate protein sets, employing feature selection techniques and machine learning across three intestinal regions: the terminal ileum, ascending colon, and descending colon. Results: Notably, panels composed solely of microbial biomarkers outperformed both human-only and combined human-microbial panels, achieving highly accurate results. Furthermore, the ascending colon emerged as the optimal sampling site, a result that aligns with the rich microbial diversity revealed in its taxonomic profile. Conclusions: Using a machine learning-based strategy on combined proteomics and metaproteomics, this study uncovered disease‑relevant signaling pathways and delivered taxonomic as well as functional insights into the microbial dysbiosis of PIBD. A diagnostic panel built around microbial proteins (particularly those originating from the ascending colon) emerges as a promising tool for more precise stratification of PIBD subtypes. Larger, prospective studies are now needed to validate these candidate biomarkers and translate them into clinically deployable diagnostic panels. Keywords: Metaproteome, Biomarker, Pediatric Inflammatory bowel disease, Machine learning, Mucosal luminal interface.

items.abstract: The complex network of mechanisms that surround cellular senescence, such as its precise causes and effects, are not entirely understood at present. Senescence occurs when a cell permanently ceases dividing, halts apoptosis, stops performing its normal functions, and begins secreting chemicals that can induce other cells in its environment to also become senescent. Senescent cells are present in both healthy and unhealthy tissue, but their abundance is positively correlated with disease and age. A better understanding of senescence could lead to healthier aging, improved recovery from chemotherapy, or increased lifespan. This study used novel machine learning algorithms - with guaranteed properties of correctness under broad assumptions - to investigate senescence in human liver tissue by analyzing Visium spatial transcriptomics data. This produced data-driven models of the causes and effects of senescence, both locally and from nearby tissue. This report includes an assessment of whether the data meet key requirements for causal analysis, the transcripts identified by causal analyses as causes and effects of senescence marker genes, and pathway analyses of those gene sets.

items.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) generates substantial transcript signal outside segmented cell bodies, which is generally discarded by analysis tools. This is especially problematic for brain ST data, as neuronal mRNAs can be localized far from somata – in axons, dendrites, and synaptic compartments – and up to half of the transcripts in ST data may lie outside cell bodies. Here, we present SCOUBI, a computational framework that identifies axon-dendrite interfaces from extrasomatic RNA in ST data, revealing a hitherto overlooked layer of molecular function in neural tissues. It first partitions extrasomatic space into axon- and dendrite-enriched compartments based on known marker genes, using a neural network trained to maximize marker specificity and inter-compartment communication signals. It then defines interfaces as loci where predicted axonal and dendritic compartments converge and exhibit ligand–receptor colocalization. Applied to mouse brain, SCOUBI creates maps of axonal and dendritic compartments and their interfaces that align with known spatial patterns of neurite and synaptic distribution. It identifies transcriptomic differences between interfaces and the surrounding extrasomatic space, revealing region-specific signatures of neuronal signaling and synaptic plasticity. By comparing interface transcript enrichment with local somatic expression, SCOUBI identifies genes that preferentially localize at sites of intercellular communication rather than simply reflecting nearby cell bodies. SCOUBI reveals interface-associated transcripts beyond established synaptic genes, with molecular signatures reproducible across independent samples and imaging platforms. In summary, SCOUBI transforms a substantial and often-discarded aspect of ST data into an interpretable readout of subcellular organization and neural signaling.

items.abstract: Understanding how genes coordinate across cells is central to explaining tissue function and disease, yet most existing models still take a single cell as input and therefore emphasize cell-intrinsic regulation. We present the Multicellular Transformer (MCT), a foundation model built around a different assumption: cells function together within tissues, so the appropriate unit of input is not one cell in isolation but a set of cells from the same sample. By jointly modeling multiple cells, MCT learns context-aware gene embeddings that capture gene-gene interactions across the tissue environment. Trained on a large set of tissue samples (>4200) across more than 30 tissue types, MCT recovers ligand-receptor interactions, infers cross-cell signaling programs, and reveals spatial co-localization patterns directly from scRNA-seq data. Its contextual embeddings identify disease-specific rewiring of gene neighborhoods in systemic lupus erythematosus and COVID-19 and predict population-level perturbation effects in cancer without additional training. By linking gene-level regulation to tissue-scale organization, MCT provides a scalable framework for modeling multicellular biology and enables in silico discovery of therapeutic targets and tissue-specific dependencies.

items.abstract: Abstract Motivation Characterizing the intratumoral heterogeneity of Lung Adenocarcinoma (LUAD) from bulk transcriptomics is critical for precision medicine, yet conventional deconvolution methods are limited by high computational latency and sensitivity to transcriptomic noise, hindering their application to large-scale clinical trials. To overcome these barriers, we present a Deep Neural Network (DNN) emulator that shifts the deconvolution task from iterative optimization to rapid functional inference. Results Utilizing a harmonized LUAD single-cell atlas, we engineered a synthetic training environment of 1,000 heterogeneous bulk profiles to train a pathway-guided architecture. By internalizing the complex transformation mappings of marker-based deconvolution, our model reproduces TOAST estimates of four previously defined LUAD cancer cell states on held-out synthetic samples (ensemble mean Spearman ρ = 0.87, MAE = 0.067), agrees with the reference-based method BayesPrism about as well as TOAST itself does (mean ρ = 0.57 for both), and runs at 1.4 ms per sample for a single model and 12.5 ms for the ensemble, similar to TOAST and about 100 to 900 times faster than BayesPrism. We applied this emulator to large-scale clinical cohorts to estimate the proportion of the high-risk, dedifferentiated state, characterized by hypoxia and EMT. The predicted proportion of this state was associated with shorter overall survival in all six cohorts (pooled hazard ratio 1.70, 95% CI 1.49–1.95, for top versus bottom tertile), suggesting that our emulator provides a scalable and biologically grounded framework for patient stratification and the translation of single-cell insights into clinical practice. Availability and implementation The analysis code is freely available on GitHub (https://github.com/bsoni08/emulator_luad_stratification) and implemented in Python using TensorFlow alongside R scripts. Contact Inquiries can be directed to bsoni08@gmail.com, christopher.yau@wrh.ox.ac.uk, or ines.grazina_de_matos@roche.com.

items.abstract: We present a global soybean haplotype map generated from whole-genome sequencing of 1278 Glycine max and Glycine soja accessions, comprising 11.37 million single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) and 2.05 million short insertions and deletions (InDels). This map (GmHapMap-II) captures unprecedented genetic diversity, reflecting the broad extent of the global soybean gene pool. Built on a near-gapless reference assembly and extending beyond the diversity ceiling reached by the earlier, cultivated-only GmHapMap-I, this resource incorporates wild G. soja germplasm to capture genetic diversity across the full breadth of the soybean gene pool. Population structure analyses revealed six geographically distinct subpopulations that affected the linkage and shaped the recombination. The haplotype variation map resolved the previously reported association for crude protein content on chromosome 15 with greater precision than a lower-density SNP array. We further identified a genome-wide significant locus on chromosome 1 for linolenic acid content that is distinct from all known FAD3 desaturase genes and is associated with a haplotype found almost exclusively in wild G. soja germplasm, indicating a source of seed oil quality variation lost during domestication. The constructed haplotype map enabled detailed characterisation of haplotype diversity and copy number polymorphism at the soybean cyst nematode (SCN)-associated rhg-1 and Rhg-4 loci, revealing both novel haplotype structures and germplasm lines with elevated CNV relative to previously characterised genotypes. Integrating haplotype and copy-number data into a machine learning framework for genomic prediction of SCN resistance and cataloguing gene-centric haplotypes in a user-friendly database, this resource supports both trait discovery and applied breeding decisions. The haplotype map will serve as a major genomic resource for trait-based mapping, enhancing efforts in the genomics-enabled development of improved cultivars.

items.abstract: Immune heterogeneity and metabolic remodeling frequently limit the efficacy of immunotherapy in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). To address this challenge, we integrated single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing analyses, pairing machine learning with preclinical models to develop the APOA5-correlated T-cell Signature (ACTsig), which effectively stratifies LUAD patients and predicts immunotherapeutic response. Moreover, We identified apolipoprotein A-V (APOA5) as a previously unrecognized tumor suppressor linking cholesterol homeostasis to the tumor immune ecosystem. Mechanistically, APOA5 deficiency induced intracellular cholesterol accumulation and MIF production. Cholesterol depletion and replenishment established a causal role for cholesterol accumulation in regulating MIF production, while MIF knockdown reversed APOA5-loss-induced T-cell exhaustion and recombinant MIF restored the phenotype. Meanwhile, CXCR4 blockade rescued APOA5-loss-induced T-cell exhaustion, supporting the functional involvement of the MIF receptor CXCR4 in this immunosuppressive phenotype. Finally, in silico drug screening identified fenofibrate, which, in combination with anti-PD-1 therapy, significantly suppressed tumor growth in APOA5-deficient models. Together, these findings establish ACTsig as a predictive biomarker for immunotherapy response and reveal an APOA5-cholesterol-MIF-CXCR4 axis underlying T-cell exhaustion.

items.abstract: Abstract Background: The widespread adoption of generative artificial intelligence in medical education has made the phenomenon of "AI borrowing" in the classroom a direct threat to the evaluation of learning authenticity. Pathogen reasoning tasks in medical microbiology inherently have a strict dependency structure. However, existing AIGC text detectors remain confined to surface features, neural cognitive diagnosis systems stop at knowledge-component-level scores, and educational early warning tools provide only outcome labels. None of these approaches fills the methodological gap between node-level attribution identification and actions that teachers can execute. Methods: This study proposes EduAttr, which introduces three principled innovations. The reasoning commitment consistency test based on counterfactual premise perturbation introduces the intervention semantics of causal inference into attribution identification. The identifiable path signature based on the dependency partial order violation rate uses the downward closure property of knowledge space theory and forms a complementary coupling with the counterfactual probe. The instructional early warning node ranking mechanism integrates dual-channel signals with dependency depth weights and outputs a Top-K list of follow-up questions that teachers can execute. The system was evaluated in a two-arm randomized controlled trial at two medical colleges in China between September 2024 and June 2025, with 240 second-year clinical medicine students in eight intact classes allocated 1:1 to supervised writing without generative AI or to AI-permitted writing whose interaction transcripts anchored node-level attribution labels. The primary outcome was the node-level F 1 score. Results: Across 1,200 reports and 22,362 annotated nodes, EduAttr achieves a node-level F 1 of 0.843, exceeding the strongest surface feature baseline Ghostbuster by 13.0 percentage points. Under severe rewriting attacks, this gap further expands to 29.5 percentage points. Agreement with the adjudicated labels reaches a Cohen's kappa of 0.762, which is statistically indistinguishable from the interteacher agreement of 0.741, the teacher adoption rate is 87.5%, and grading time is reduced by 42.7%. Conclusions: EduAttr advances identification accuracy, robustness, and instructional operability, providing a technical pathway that can be embedded into classroom follow-up questioning workflows in medical education. Trial registration: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2600118749. Registered 2 October 2026 (retrospectively registered).

items.abstract: Abstract Background Embryo selection remains a critical determinant of IVF success. Despite advances in morphology, time-lapse imaging, and preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (PGT-A), implantation failure still occurs in morphologically high-quality and euploid embryos, highlighting limitations in current assessment methods. The current study is a theoretical framework development study based on literature synthesis (2000–2026) from major databases. The proposed Integrated Comprehensive AI-based Implantation Scoring system (ICAIS) comprises three domains: morphology (0–9 points), morphokinetics (0–3 points), and an AI-derived adjustment factor (− 2 to + 3 points), yielding a total score of 0–15.The aim is to develop an integrated, transparent scoring system combining morphology, morphokinetics, and artificial intelligence (AI) to improve prediction of embryo implantation potential. Results The ICAIS model stratifies embryos into low (0–7), intermediate (8–11), and high (12–15) implantation potential categories. The integrated approach demonstrates improved theoretical discrimination between embryos with similar morphology but different implantation potential, and better alignment with known euploidy and developmental competence patterns. Conclusion ICAIS provides a structured and interpretable framework that integrates conventional and AI-based embryo assessment. It has the potential to enhance embryo selection and address unexplained implantation failure, although prospective clinical validation is required.

items.abstract: Abstract Background: Mental health care often requires clinicians to reason over patient journeys: longitudinal patterns of symptoms, diagnoses, treatments, behaviors, social context, and responses to care. Yet these journeys are rarely documented as readily available, explicit timelines. Clinically important temporal information is often embedded in unstructured discharge narratives, where events may be repeated, narrated out of order, or expressed through vague and relative time references. This makes temporal recovery difficult for clinicians and computational systems, and can limit the reliability of downstream summarization. Methods: We present CliniCIRCA, a multi-stage large language model (LLM) framework for Calendar-anchored, Imprecision-aware Reconstruction of Clinical Annals. CliniCIRCA decomposes patient-journey reconstruction into three stages: extracting atomic clinical events from raw discharge summaries, assigning calendar-grounded temporal labels with explicit uncertainty, and rendering the verified timeline as a date-grouped clinical summary. The framework is designed to make temporal reasoning inspectable rather than hidden inside a single summarization step. Results: From 14,882 MIMIC-III mental-health-coded admissions, we construct a benchmark of 52 discharge summaries on which CliniCIRCA produces 15,891 temporally tagged events. Following clinician-defined rubrics, human annotation with clinician adjudication corrects 629 errors, producing verified gold-standard timelines. These corrected timelines then drive a temporally grounded summarization stage that compresses each source 1.52 times into a date-grouped chronological record while preserving temporal labels and uncertainty. We further scale the framework to generate 1,000 silver-standard timelines and evaluate them as supervision for smaller open-weight models. Compared with zero- and few-shot prompting, instruction tuning generally improves five open-weight models across event extraction, temporal tagging, and summarization under both silver and clinician-verified evaluations. Conclusions: Auditable temporal reconstruction can serve as both a clinician-readable representation of complex mental health narratives and a reusable supervision source for smaller models. These findings suggest that intermediate, temporally grounded representations may help bridge clinical summarization, timeline generation, and scalable model adaptation, while preserving the need for expert adjudication in high-stakes clinical natural language processing (NLP).

items.abstract: Abstract Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly utilized to support the early assessment of skin lesions. While numerous studies report high diagnostic accuracy under controlled experimental conditions, considerably fewer integrate technical validation, independent clinical stress-testing, and large-scale real-world evidence (RWE) within a single transparent framework. Objective: To evaluate the capabilities, clinical utility, and operational limitations of a mobile AI-assisted skin analysis system by synthesizing three complementary streams of evidence. Methods: This study integrates: (1) an analysis of longitudinal technical performance metrics and big-data usage patterns from over 6.57 million real-world smartphone assessments; (2) an independent clinical evaluation ((n = 160) analyzed cases) conducted at a specialized tertiary referral dermatology center comparing AI predictions and triage routing against histopathological, cytological, or expert clinical reference standards; and (3) a comparative synthesis with contemporary peer-reviewed literature, including external validation on skin of color. Results: Longitudinal technical validation demonstrated consistent, balanced improvements across sensitivity (97.4%), specificity (93.1%), and overall accuracy (94.2%) by 2026. In real-world consumer usage, common inflammatory conditions (e.g., acne/rosacea, (n = 708,356)) accounted for the largest share of assessments, while preventable image-acquisition errors (poor lighting: 42.0%; poor focus: 28.0%; motion blur: 18.0%) represented the primary modifiable determinants of failure. In the independent tertiary referral cohort - heavily enriched with malignant and diagnostically challenging lesions - exact Top-1 and Top-3 diagnostic agreements were 54.4% and 70.6%, respectively. However, combining Top-3 agreement, correct broader disease-group assignment, and appropriate risk-based routing yielded a clinically useful triage outcome in 80.0% of cases. Conclusions: AI-assisted skin analysis provides clinically meaningful support for early risk stratification and patient referral when deployed as a clinical decision-support tool rather than an autonomous diagnostic system. Comprehensive evaluation of medical AI requires pairing conventional accuracy metrics with triage-oriented clinical endpoints and transparent RWE reporting.

items.abstract: Abstract Background: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into clinical decision-making creates uncertainty regarding responsibility and accountability when adverse outcomes occur. Despite this, data regarding stakeholder perspectives remain scarce, especially quantitative data comparing physician and public views on responsibility allocation and transparency. This study aims to evaluate and compare how physicians and the general population in Sweden attribute responsibility for negative medical outcomes when AI is used to support healthcare decisions in primary care, as well as their views on the necessity of transparently disclosing AI use to patients. Methods: A nationwide, cross-sectional, mixed-methods survey was conducted in Sweden between February and May 2025. The survey targeted two distinct cohorts (N = 500 per group): licensed physicians under 70 years, sampled from the National Board of Health and Welfare register, and adults aged 18 or older sampled from the Swedish population registry. The survey used case vignettes as background for multiple-choice questions, with complementary open-ended free-text responses. The data was evaluated using comparative statistical analysis and reflexive thematic analysis. Results: Physicians were significantly more likely than the general population to assign responsibility to the physician (92\% vs. 74\%) and to favor a shared responsibility model involving the physician (48\% vs. 35\%). In contrast, the general population more frequently selected non-physician actor combinations (26\% vs. 8\%) and assigned greater responsibility to the patient in a scenario involving direct patient-AI interaction without a physician involved. Neither group broadly assigned responsibility to the AI itself (1.3\% physicians vs. 10\% general population). The reflexive thematic analysis reinforced these results, identifying a shared accountability framework where all actors share responsibility, but where the physician serves as the ultimate safeguard. A majority of the general population (68\%) affirmed the patient's right to always know if AI was used, in contrast to only 23\% of physicians who exhibited a polarised distribution. Conclusion: Respondents endorse a shared responsibility model among actors involved in implementing and using AI for medical decisions. The physician is viewed as the essential human-in-the-loop, bearing ultimate accountability for adverse outcomes of AI-assisted medical decisions according to a vast majority of respondents. Divergent perspectives regarding transparency emphasise the need to clarify informed consent standards for AI deployment in healthcare.

items.abstract: Abstract Background Small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) is aggressive and often metastatic at diagnosis, and skeletal-related events such as bone pain, pathological fracture and spinal cord compression alter treatment decisions. Prediction tools for bone metastasis in elderly patients with SCLC remain scarce, and external validation and interpretability analyses are limited. We therefore developed and externally validated an interpretable machine learning model for bone metastasis at initial diagnosis in these patients, using routinely available clinical and staging information. Methods We retrospectively enrolled 1,387 consecutive patients aged ≥ 60 years with SCLC treated at two hospitals (2010–2024), randomly divided 7:3 into training and internal validation sets. Two external cohorts were assembled: 128 patients from another hospital (2010–2024) and 19,561 patients from the SEER database (2010–2015). The outcome was bone metastasis at initial diagnosis. Boruta selected features from 16 candidate variables. Six models—logistic regression, decision tree, random forest, XGBoost, LightGBM and artificial neural network—were compared for discrimination and calibration, with decision curve analysis and SHAP interpretation. Results Boruta confirmed four features: N stage, SCLC stage (limited-stage or extensive-stage), liver metastasis and clinical stage. LightGBM was the most stable across cohorts. SHAP identified clinical stage as the largest contributor, with extensive-stage disease, concurrent liver metastasis and higher N stage increasing the predicted risk. Conclusions A LightGBM model based on four features available at initial diagnosis provides stable, interpretable risk stratification for bone metastasis in elderly patients with SCLC and may support clinical decision-making, although recalibration should precede use in other populations.

items.abstract: Abstract Background: Differentiating between bipolar disorder (BD) and borderline personality disorder (BPD) is an intriguing clinical challenge that has attracted research attention, as the multiple co-occurring symptoms such as mood instability, impulsivity, and emotional dysregulation have made the boundary between the two disorders unclear. Recent research in computational psychiatry has shown promise in leveraging the power of knowledge graphs and large language models to enable accurate and inter­pretable decision-making. Methods: The study developed a hybrid framework, KG-Psy, that combines large language models with dynamic graphs. The system extracts clinical entities through GPT-5 while employing multi-step reasoning to find hidden connections within a psychiatric knowledge graph that weighs its evidence-based content. The system performs four main operations, which include extracting clinical entities, creating dynamic weighted knowledge graphs, using GPT-5 to trace multi-step cognitive pathways, and evaluating customized treatment options. The researchers used 310 anonymized psychiatric case re­ports to test their method. Results: KG-Psy achieved better discrimination between BD and BPD than other methods. The model achieved a maximum Precision (%) of 91.5, an improvement of 19%, 10.3%, and 7.4% over the KG-only, LLM-only, and Hybrid-other approaches, respectively. The system successfully discovered un­known cognitive pathways, which it used to create accurate pathway maps and provide treatment rec­ommendations supported by numerical evidence. The results of ablation experiments showed that LLM reasoning, combined with the knowledge graph structure, led to high performance. Conclusion: The KG-Psy system introduces a novel approach to psychiatry inspired by large-scale language models and dynamic graphs that integrates data-driven linguistic analysis with established symbolic knowledge to enhance the capabilities of differential diagnosis and treatment development for complex mood and personality disorders. Future work could include validation on larger datasets and integration of multimodal clinical data.

items.abstract: Abstract Objective Pakistan has broadened its medical and dental education sphere, yet apprehensions last about undergraduates’ competence, impact of regulation, international acknowledgment of qualifications and retention of the health workforce. This study explored multi stakeholder perspectives on training capacity, quality of education, governance, regulation and acknowledgment of health professions education in Pakistan, and identified prime reforms. Methodology: A qualitative descriptive study was conducted using hybrid focus group discussion held on 4 August 2026 as part of national Health and Education Summit Pakistan (HESP) 2026. Fourteen purposively sampled stakeholders participated in discussion guided by 16 semi structured questions. Data were analysed using Framework Method, and Health Policy Triangle was applied as an interpretive lens. Results Nine themes were identified across three domains. Educational quality and competence : undefined and unenforced competency standards; deficits in clinical training infrastructure; faculty development and continuous quality improvement; and cautious, purpose-specific integration of artificial intelligence. Governance, regulation and recognition : fragmented, input-oriented governance; private-sector representation and public–private imbalance; and international recognition and global alignment. Workforce and equity : equity in workforce planning; and workforce sustainability, security and dignity. Participants identified main barrier to reform is not in an absence of policy but in weak implementation, input based accreditation and poor coordination among regulatory bodies. Conclusion Stakeholders called for a shift from input based to outcome-based accreditation built on a nationally agreed definition of competence, a shared inter agency governance platform, documented clinical supervision and simulation, and workforce protection measures.

items.abstract: Abstract Background Logistic regression remains conventional for identifying correlates of self-reported kidney stone history, but multidimensional comparisons with machine learning—integrating discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility—remain scarce. This study aimed to identify determinants of self-reported kidney stone history among US adults and to compare logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost. Methods We conducted a pooled cross-sectional analysis of six consecutive NHANES cycles (2007–2018), including adults aged ≥ 20 years with complete data on kidney stone history and 16 prespecified candidate predictors. LASSO logistic regression with 10-fold cross-validation selected variables in a 70% training subset. Logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost were trained on the identical predictor set and evaluated on the held-out 30% test set by discrimination (AUC with DeLong's test), calibration (intercept and slope), and clinical utility (decision curve analysis). Survey-weighted sensitivity analysis, collinearity assessment, nomogram, and SHAP analyses. Results Of 25,560 adults, 2,462 (9.6%; survey-weighted 9.99%) reported a lifetime history of kidney stones. LASSO retained 14 of 16 candidates. Eight variables were independently associated with kidney stone history: older age, male sex, lower BMI (inverse), higher waist circumference, elevated blood urea nitrogen, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and current smoking (all 95% CIs excluding unity). BMI and waist circumference showed substantial collinearity (VIFs 7.69 and 7.81). Logistic regression achieved an AUC of 0.644, comparable to XGBoost (0.641; DeLong P = 0.591) and superior to random forest (0.617; P = 0.0005), with the strongest calibration (intercept − 0.147; slope 0.892), followed by XGBoost (slope 0.771) and random forest (slope 0.569). On decision curve analysis, random forest's net benefit fell below the treat-none line within the 15–35% threshold range, whereas logistic regression and XGBoost remained stable. SHAP analysis confirmed age, waist circumference, and blood urea nitrogen as the top contributors; survey-weighted results were consistent. Conclusions Older age, male sex, adiposity-related traits, elevated blood urea nitrogen, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and current smoking were independently associated with prevalent kidney stone history. Logistic regression matched XGBoost in discrimination while showing the best calibration, stable clinical net benefit, and full interpretability. Given the cross-sectional, self-reported design, these findings reflect correlates rather than causal predictors and warrant external validation.

items.abstract: Abstract Objectives: The CARDIO-ML-ED dataset was collected to address the critical shortage of publicly available cardiovascular databases that integrate electrocardiogram (ECG) imagery with comprehensive clinical metadata. Existing ECG repositories lack detailed patient-level information such as laboratory results, vital signs, and medical history—factors essential for developing clinically meaningful machine learning models. We aimed to create a curated, well-labelled, multimodal resource that supports research in automated ECG interpretation, multimodal fusion, and exploratory clinical phenotyping, while promoting reproducibility and innovation in artificial intelligence (AI) driven cardiovascular care. Data description: The CARDIO-ML-ED dataset comprises two complementary components: (1) structured clinical metadata for 582 subjects, and (2) a curated subset of 408 high-resolution ECG images derived from paper-based records digitized through standardized scanning, normalization, cropping, quality filtering, and noise reduction. The dataset includes 82 clinical features per subject—covering demographics, vital signs, laboratory tests (complete blood count, cardiac enzymes, electrolytes, inflammatory markers, arterial blood gases), and medical history. Diagnostic labels were independently assigned by a cardiologist and an emergency medicine physician, achieving substantial interrater agreement (Cohen's kappa = 0.82). This resource offers unique value through its dense integration of ECG data with clinical covariates, enabling multimodal fusion research, unsupervised clustering, imbalanced learning, and predictive analytics.

items.summary: Asynchronous reinforcement learning increases training throughput, but data from stale policies and numerical mismatch between training and inference can destabilize learning. items.abstract: Asynchronous reinforcement learning increases training throughput, but data from stale policies and numerical mismatch between training and inference can destabilize learning. To stabilize off-policy learning, score centering (SC) removes the effect of reward baselines on the expected update. Our gradient diagnostics show less extreme gradients with SC than with importance sampling (IS), but SC can still fail when the learner moves far from the behavior policy that generated the data. To limit this policy mismatch, we introduce Regularized Score Centering (RSC), which adds a reverse Kullback-Leibler (KL) penalty to encourage the learner's next-token distribution to stay close to the behavior policy's next-token distribution. RSC works with or without truncated importance sampling (TIS), which caps token importance weights. Our theoretical analysis supports this approach, showing that KL regularization improves convergence guarantees. We evaluate dense and mixture-of-experts models on mathematical reasoning and agentic tasks, including online shopping, tool use, games, and fully asynchronous software engineering. RSC with TIS substantially improves sample efficiency across all agentic benchmarks, attaining higher training rewards with the same number of sampled responses. In final evaluations, it achieves top performance across all six agentic tasks, improving by 14.3% on AppWorld and reaching 9.9 times the strongest baseline's score on BabyAI.
