items.abstract: We present CompoundingKernel, a self-improving agent system that writes GPU kernels by search. As of 2026-11-11, its generated kernels rank #1 on the public L1, L2 and Quantization boards of SOL-ExecBench (NVIDIA B200). They have held #1 on L1 since 2026-10-27, albeit a short loss on 2026-11-07. All 235 problems have a site-verified correct kernel; on the 209 public-board problems they are 4.40x faster than the benchmark's reference baseline. The search starts from zero: agents get each problem's PyTorch definition but no reference kernels or official scores. A per-problem archive outside the model holds every correct kernel and its lineage. An LLM controller reads it, picks a parent or a new design, and gives each parallel child agent one direction. Checks outside the model decide correctness. At equal wall time, it beat a coded UCB style tree on 35 of 38 problems by making 2.4x as many correct attempts. Over a thousand agents ran at once, and one warm restart fix raised their evaluation rate 3.6x. We find that the rate of reliable measurements, not the number of agents, limits how far such a search scales. Our code and kernels are available on URL.

items.title: Do Probing and Steering Favor the Same Directions Within and Across Language Models?
items.summary: A direction in a language model's hidden state can be used to probe whether a concept is present or to steer the model toward it. Although probe directions are often reused for steering, the direction that best detects a concept need not be the one that best changes it. We study this distinction in three instruction-tuned models from different families. We construct a one-parameter family of directions ranging from…
items.abstract: A direction in a language model's hidden state can be used to probe whether a concept is present or to steer the model toward it. Although probe directions are often reused for steering, the direction that best detects a concept need not be the one that best changes it. We study this distinction in three instruction-tuned models from different families. We construct a one-parameter family of directions ranging from a covariance-adjusted discriminant to the mean difference, and evaluate probing and additive steering, which adds the direction to the hidden state, along the family at a fixed side effect. For truthfulness and sentiment, in every model, the best probe is not the best steering direction: steering consistently favors directions closer to the mean difference. This separation holds across 59 of 60 layer-model-concept combinations in a layer sweep, with matched probe and steering texts in all six model-concept combinations, and under a rotation-based steering operator. The exact steering optimum is less stable: for sentiment, an intermediate direction produces a 27-56% stronger steering effect than the mean difference, but this gain shrinks or disappears with matched texts and depends on the layer and the operator. The two roles also transfer differently across models. A probe transferred by a linear map fitted on neutral text retains 81-91% of the target model's above-chance probing performance, while the transferred mean difference retains less of its steering effect in 11 of 12 model pairs. This is a consistent tendency, although our predefined criteria classify only three pairs, and nine remain inconclusive. Finally, as an application on PopQA, steering toward "unknown" increases abstention by 18-44 percentage points on uncertain errors, versus 2-5 on confident errors, while rarely correcting errors in cases where a correct answer is reachable.

Their cognitive strengths and limitations, however, remain poorly understood. We introduce S1CogBench, a benchmark of 24 established cognitive tasks and 27 evaluation modes, evaluating seven open models and the API model Jev. It combines human-response prediction, autonomous execution,…
items.abstract: Decision-making in humans and AI involves multiple cognitive abilities. System One decision models produce fast, structured choices. Their cognitive strengths and limitations, however, remain poorly understood. We introduce S1CogBench, a benchmark of 24 established cognitive tasks and 27 evaluation modes, evaluating seven open models and the API model Jev. It combines human-response prediction, autonomous execution, and controlled task manipulations to reveal strengths and failures that aggregate scores miss. We find distinct behavioral profiles across the evaluated models. In these models, strong performance on some learning tasks coexists with failures to gather information or adapt to feedback, while high accuracy does not guarantee human-like responses to changing task demands. Shared readout controls show that model rankings depend partly on how choices are extracted. Separate latency comparisons with generative language models show that long responses are much slower than direct decisions, whereas matched one-token generation adds little overhead. To our knowledge, S1CogBench is the first benchmark of System One decision models on established cognitive experiments. It provides a common empirical basis for identifying their capabilities and limitations before integrating them into automated decision systems.

items.summary: 近日，上海灵睿智芯计算技术有限公司（以下简称“灵睿智芯”）宣布完成数亿元Pre-A+轮融资。本轮融资由美团战投领投，京东关联基金、干杯基金、力合算芯基金（东方算芯CVC）、钧犀资本、商汤国香资本、尚颀资本（上汽CVC）、深信服科技的产业投资基金琥珀资本等头部产业资本和众多老股东跟投。至此，这家2025年初才成立的企业，累计融资金额已接近十亿元。 灵睿智芯创始人、董事长兼总经理刘洋表示，本轮融资将主要用于加速智能体CPU内核和芯片产品的的研发迭代与流片验证。…

items.title: A Synthetic Benchmark for Topology-Aware Modeling of Multispecific Antibody Function.
items.summary: Multispecific antibodies (msAbs) offer transformative therapeutic potential by engaging multiple epitopes simultaneously, yet their efficacy is an emergent property governed by complex molecular architectures. items.abstract: Multispecific antibodies (msAbs) offer transformative therapeutic potential by engaging multiple epitopes simultaneously, yet their efficacy is an emergent property governed by complex molecular architectures. Rational design is often bottlenecked by the inability to predict how subtle changes in domain topology influence functional outcomes, a challenge exacerbated by the scarcity of comprehensive experimental data. Here, we introduce Synapse, a biologically inspired synthetic benchmark for topology-aware modeling of msAbs. First, we present a generative method that combines nonlinear per-domain sequence-to-score landscapes with connectivity-dependent synthetic readouts. Second, we propose a graph neural network architecture that explicitly encodes these topological constraints, distinguishing between format configurations that appear identical to the evaluated connectivity-agnostic multilayer perceptron. We demonstrate that this model learns topology-dependent structure-function relationships on synthetic landscapes and evaluate a transfer learning workflow as infrastructure for adaptation to biological datasets. We showcase our framework with a trispecific T cell engager-inspired synthetic topology-dependent optimization task and a constrained ranking of common light chain candidates against a composite objective. This work provides a controlled benchmarking environment for developing and evaluating topology-aware computational tools for msAb modeling. All experiments use synthetic data; no biological validation is performed.

items.title: DxToniaNet: A Neural Network for Estimating the Severity of Leg Dystonia in Children with Cerebral Palsy

items.abstract: Importance: Leg dystonia affects 50-80% of children with cerebral palsy (CP), but severity assessment remains subjective and time-consuming. Objective tools are urgently needed to quantify leg dystonia severity in clinical care and clinical trials. Objective: To develop and validate a deep neural network (DxToniaNet) for leg dystonia severity estimation using 2D clinical video recordings. Design, Setting, and Participants: We retrospectively analyzed video recordings of 298 children with cerebral palsy undergoing a seated hand open-close task as part of routine clinical care (Center 1: 193 videos, 720p/30fps; Center 2: 105 videos, 4K/60fps). Videos were rated for leg dystonia severity by a group of 7 experts using the Global Dystonia Rating Scale (GDRS) leg subscore (range 0-40) which has a minimum clinically important difference (MCID) of 4 points. Videos displaying leg dystonia (median expert GDRS score ≥1) were used to develop and test a machine learning model (DxToniaNet) for estimating leg dystonia severity. Open-source software (OpenPose) estimated bilateral knee, ankle, and toe coordinates, normalized for height and camera positioning, and 69 variance and amplitude features were calculated based on established expert-cited features of leg dystonia. A neural network, DxToniaNet, was developed, trained and validated using 5-fold cross-validation on Center 1 videos before final testing on independent Center 2 videos. Main Outcome(s) and Measure(s): Mean absolute error (MAE), root mean square error (RMSE), and accuracy in differentiating between videos with clinically meaningful differences in GDRS scores were calculated relative to experts' median GDRS scores. Results: When estimating experts' leg GDRS scores in testing data, the proposed machine learning (ML) model yielded a MAE of 1.71 ± 1.68 and RMSE of 2.21 ± 0.34 (significantly less than the GDRS MCID of 4), and 90-94% accuracy in differentiating between videos with greater than a 4-point difference in the GDRS. Conclusions and Relevance: We have demonstrated that DxToniaNet can accurately estimate leg dystonia severity compared to experts' assessments with a small (clinically insignificant) error margin. Our methodology supports generalizability since DxToniaNet was developed and tested using independent videos datasets from different centers, recorded under different conditions. In the future, DxToniaNet may help facilitate standardized leg dystonia severity estimation in clinical care and clinical trials.

items.abstract: Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is the most effective treatment of a range of severe mental dis-orders and is annually given to more than a million patients worldwide. Dosing of the electrical charge is critical for efficacy and side-effect burden; however, it is currently based on manual assessment of seizure quality and exhibits substantial clinical heterogeneity. Here, we collected 1,000 ECT session electroencephalograms (EEG) from 130 individual ECT patients and made an expert-level classification of the EEGs into actionable seizure quality categories (null-response [0], threshold [T], and adequate [A]). We then trained a range of machine learning algorithms on the raw EEG data to classify the EEGs into these categories and tested for classi-fication accuracy. The highest performing algorithm was able to classify the seizures with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curves of >0.9 for both the 0 vs. T and the T vs. A categories corresponding to excellent discrimination. In contrast, the accuracy of predicting seizure quality in subsequent treatments was only moderate. The addition of clinical variables to the models, such as demographics, anesthesia and anticonvulsant exposure, did not improve model performance. These results provide proof-of-concept of machine learning classification of seizure adequacy in ECT based on raw EEG data. The findings could pave the way for the de-velopment of more objective and personalized decision-support tools in ECT.

items.abstract: ClinicalTrials.gov provides valuable information for vaccine research, but fragmented data structures and inconsistent vaccine naming complicate systematic cross-trial analysis. The Study-ExperimentAssay Common Data Model (SEA-CDM) provides a standardized structure for biomedical study data, while biomedical ontologies supply semantic relationships among concepts. We extracted 9,147 vaccinerelated study records from the Aggregate Analysis of ClinicalTrials.gov (AACT) database, mapped their records into SEA-CDM, and linked vaccine products and reported adverse events (AEs) to the Vaccine Ontology (VO) and Ontology of Adverse Events (OAE), respectively. Building on the existing Ontology-based SEA Network (OSEAN), we organized the integrated data into relational tables and a Neo4j knowledge graph while retaining links to original registrations. We evaluated three applications to assess semantic trial retrieval, context-aware AE ranking and trial similarity, and trial design recommendation. First, VO-based query expansion retrieved 41 candidate RNA vaccine trials compared with 16 using exact VO identifier matching. Second, a context-aware AE ranking model incorporating SEA-CDM features and VO-derived vaccine families improved recall@10 from 0.317 to 0.383 over a frequency-based baseline. TransE and CompGCN embeddings achieved Hits@10 of 0.950 and 0.946, respectively, for retrieving trials sharing the same VO identifier within disease-specific candidate sets. Third, an ontology-based clinical trial design recommendation model was developed using several machine learning methods under leave-one-Material-out evaluation across 23 vaccine classes, although performance varied across classes. These findings demonstrate how structural and semantic integration can support multiple clinical trial analyses using vaccine studies as a case study. This framework provides a foundation for extending ontology-supported data integration and analysis to other clinical research domains.

items.abstract: **Background.** Rule derived (weak) labels can enlarge a training set when reported labels are scarce. Their value depends on label quality, on how the extra records shift the training distribution, and on whether the comparison accounts for reported labels set aside for tuning or calibration. **Methods.** We ran an exploratory label-budget experiment on *Escherichia coli* urine cultures from two de-identified electronic health record datasets: Stanford ARMD and UT Southwestern ARMD-UTSW. The task was to predict reported non-susceptibility to cefepime, cefoxitin and ceftazidime (Stanford) and to cefepime and ceftazidime (UT Southwestern). Reported-label budgets of 10%, 25%, 50% and 100% of development patients were drawn over five patient-disjoint outer splits. Logistic regression and histogram gradient boosting were trained with reported labels only, or with added rule-derived labels using equal weights, a tuning-selected weight, class-proportion adjustment or prior-probability correction. These were compared with an all-budget reported-only baseline that used every budgeted reported label for training. Stanford used the inferred labels released with the dataset and a feature set including resistance history. UT Southwestern used researcher-derived labels from Stanford rule text, which were not validated for that site, and an age-only primary model. Brier-score differences were assessed with paired patient-cluster bootstrap intervals. **Results.** All rule-derived labels were susceptible. Equal-weight augmentation lowered mean predicted risk well below observed prevalence (for example, Stanford cefepime at the 10% budget: 0.35% versus 4.85%) and had a higher Brier score than the all-budget baseline in every drug, model and budget summary. The tuning-selected weight did not consistently improve on the all-budget baseline. Its median Brier difference was positive in 38 of 40 drug, model and budget summaries. Its paired intervals lay above zero in 100 of 296 Stanford analyses and 31 of 198 UT Southwestern analyses, and below zero in 3 and 5. The tuning set often selected a weight of zero (146 of 296 and 153 of 198 analyses). At UT Southwestern, the age-only models showed little discrimination (median AUROC 0.49 to 0.54), so those comparisons mainly reflect calibration. **Conclusions.** Under these designs, rule-derived labels did not consistently improve probability prediction over a reported-only model that used the whole reported-label budget for training. Evaluations of weak supervision should include such a baseline and should report calibration as well as discrimination. **Keywords:** weak supervision; limited-label learning; label budget; probability calibration; class imbalance; antimicrobial resistance

items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-based computer-aided detection (CAD) of tuberculosis (TB) on chest X-ray (CXR) may standardize screening and triage in settings with few radiologists but its accuracy in clinical cohorts remains uncertain. We searched five databases (PubMed, ScienceDirect, IEEE Xplore, OpenAlex, Lens.org) on 15 March 2026 for studies published between January 2020 and March 2026, and we appraised these studies using QUADAS-2. Evaluations from clinical cohorts with complete 2 × 2 data and a microbiological or composite reference standard for all participants were pooled using a bivariate random-effects model, with 95% prediction intervals. We accounted for overlapping participants by performing a post hoc analysis with one evaluation per cohort and used GRADE to assess the certainty of the evidence. No protocol was prepared or registered. We included 21 studies (26 evaluations of AI models). Nine evaluations from three independent cohorts were pooled. Pooled sensitivity was 0.896 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.874 to 0.915, prediction interval 0.798 to 0.950) and pooled specificity was 0.689 (95% CI 0.642 to 0.732; prediction interval 0.499 to 0.831). Both confidence intervals include the World Health Organization (WHO) triage thresholds (sensitivity 90%, specificity 70%). When a screening study with partial verification was added, pooled specificity increased to 0.735. Eighteen of 24 assessed evaluations were at high risk of bias and only 1 of 21 studies was prospective, fully verified, externally validated and met the WHO thresholds. Certainty of evidence was low for sensitivity and very low for specificity. A subsequent PubMed search found additional eligible clinical evaluations that were not screened, so the review is incomplete for those studies. In clinical cohorts, AI-CXR sensitivity is close to the WHO triage target, and specificity is close to, but not clearly above, its target. The evidence is pooled across only three cohorts, and specificity varies by product and setting. Thresholds need to be calibrated locally, and prospective, externally validated evaluations are needed before widespread deployment.

items.abstract: Abstract Purpose This study aimed to investigate the impact of utilizing generative artificial intelligence (AI) as a tool for organizing thoughts and rehearsing prior to consulting clinical instructors on nursing students’ psychological safety and stability, thereby addressing psychological barriers experienced during reporting and consultation in clinical practica. Methods An anonymous, self-administered questionnaire survey consisting of 17 items was conducted among second- to fourth-year nursing students at the School of Medicine, Kochi University. Questionnaire responses were retrieved from a total of 178 patients. We analyzed psychological safety during clinical training, the status of generative AI utilization, and student expectations and perceived challenges regarding its use. Comparative analyses were performed across academic years and between two groups stratified by expectation level toward AI utilization (high- vs. low-expectation groups). Results Third-year students, who were commencing domain-specific clinical practica, exhibited the highest anxiety regarding asking questions to clinical instructors. Concurrently, they demonstrated the greatest reduction in perceived burden when formulating nursing care plans using AI, alongside the highest intention for future active AI utilization. Compared with the low-expectation group, the high-expectation group exhibited significantly more positive perceptions regarding psychological safety scores (2.5 vs. 2.9, P < 0.001) and psychological impact scores (2.1 vs. 3.3, P < 0.001). Conclusion These findings suggest that generative AI functions as an effective psychological buffer to lower interpersonal barriers, thereby enhancing nursing students’ psychological safety during clinical training.

items.abstract: Abstract Responsibility for artificial intelligence (AI) assisted medical decisions encompasses both preventing harm and providing a way to respond when harm occurs. These functions are often combined in empirical measures of accountability, making it difficult to identify which safeguards respondents prioritise. This cross-sectional analysis used 385 adult responses to a common questionnaire on AI, health law and patient rights in Bangladesh. Three preventive statements addressed defined responsibility, independent clinical judgement and organisational and developer safety controls. A separate statement addressed access to complaints and remedies; a fifth elicited anticipated trust under clear accountability. Endorsement was compared within respondents using exact McNemar tests with Holm adjustment. Exploratory regression distinguished prevention and redress as correlates of anticipated trust. Redress was endorsed by 311 respondents (80.8%), exceeding endorsement of each preventive statement by 16.6–20.5 percentage points (all adjusted p < 0.001). The adjusted linear association with anticipated trust was positive for the prevention summary (b = 0.205, 95% CI 0.049 to 0.361; adjusted p = 0.020), but attenuated in inference when trust was dichotomised. The redress coefficient was close to zero in the adjusted linear model (b = 0.001, 95% CI −0.112 to 0.114). These findings distinguish broad endorsement of a patient-facing remedy from covariance with a hypothetical trust judgement. They support evaluating complaint access as a governance outcome in its own right. The survey neither verifies actual use of medical AI nor estimates effects of introducing safeguards.

items.abstract: Abstract Background: Acute kidney injury (AKI) affects 20--50% of ICU admissions, and the optimal timing for renal replacement therapy (RRT) initiation remains contested. Methods: We developed and externally validated a leakage-safe, causal-weighted machine learning pipeline predicting 48-hour RRT initiation in patients with KDIGO stage 3 AKI, using harmonized MIMIC-IV and eICU data. A regularized stacking ensemble with inverse-probability-weighted meta-learning combined five base learners (LightGBM, XGBoost, Random Forest, CatBoost, ExtraTrees) via a logistic-regression meta-learner. Results: The model achieved AUC 0.894 internally and 0.807 on an independent, 200+ hospital external cohort, significantly outperforming four of five baseline models (DeLong \((p<0.001)\)) while remaining statistically indistinguishable from a single LightGBM model. Stacking-consistent SHAP identified creatinine and urine output trajectories as dominant risk drivers, 40% of high-risk patients had a feasible short-term recourse below threshold, and fairness assessment showed no clinically meaningful subgroup gaps. Conclusions: A prototype clinical decision support system operationalizes the model for bedside use, motivating prospective evaluation before deployment.

items.abstract: Abstract Background Depressive symptoms are common among people living with HIV (PLHIV) and are associated with poorer antiretroviral therapy (ART) adherence and viral suppression. In rural settings, routine symptom screening may be constrained by counsellor workload and limited specialist mental health capacity. This study developed and internally evaluated ten supervised machine-learning (ML) models for identifying PHQ-9-defined probable depression among PLHIV attending ART clinics in Kadjebi District, Ghana. Methods A facility-based cross-sectional dataset of 264 adults receiving ART was analysed. Probable depression was defined as a Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) score of 10 or above. Fifty-two predictors were engineered from sociodemographic, HIV-clinical, tuberculosis-service, physical-health, psychosocial, stigma and health-system variables; the nine PHQ-9 items were excluded from predictors. Data were partitioned 80:20 with stratification. Imputation and, where required, standardisation were fitted using the training partition, and SMOTE was applied only to the training data. Ten algorithms were tuned using five-fold cross-validation within the training partition. Performance on the untouched held-out test set was treated as the primary split-sample internal validation, with 5-fold x 4-repeat cross-validation of the training partition used as a secondary stability analysis. Performance metrics included AUC, sensitivity, specificity, precision, F1 score, Cohen's kappa, Brier score and calibration slope. Interpretability used permutation importance and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP); decision-curve analysis was exploratory. Results PHQ-9-defined probable depression was present in 100 of 264 participants (37.9%). Random Forest was selected by the training-set cross-validation results. On the held-out test set, it achieved an AUC of 0.870, accuracy of 77.4%, sensitivity of 80.0%, specificity of 75.8%, F1 score of 0.727, Cohen's kappa of 0.536 and Brier score of 0.137. Its secondary repeated-cross-validation AUC was 0.893 (SD 0.041). Differences in cross-validated AUC among the leading algorithms were small relative to fold-to-fold variability, and no formal pairwise superiority testing was performed. Permutation importance and SHAP consistently highlighted comfort disclosing psychological difficulty, belief system, counselling and tailored mental-health service availability, perceived healthcare access and quality, sex, and perceived HIV impact. Exploratory decision-curve analysis suggested potential net benefit of model-guided PHQ-9 administration; at a threshold of 0.40, 48.9% of attendees would receive the PHQ-9 while 94% of PHQ-9-positive cases would be identified. This calculation concerns PHQ-9 administrations only and does not quantify total workflow burden. At the PHQ-9 > = 5 sensitivity threshold, Random Forest had a secondary cross-validated AUC of 0.911. Conclusion Random Forest showed promising discrimination for PHQ-9-defined probable depression in this small, single-district development study, but the findings remain proof-of-concept. Relational and service-related variables contributed strongly to prediction. Threshold analyses suggest that risk stratification could reduce the number of PHQ-9 administrations, but total counselling burden and safety were not established. External validation, development of a more parsimonious routine-workflow model, and prospective evaluation are required before clinical use; a prediction model should not replace assessment of suicide or self-harm risk.

items.abstract: Abstract Background Efficient early identification of individuals at risk of developing psychotic disorders or bipolar disorders is crucial and challenging to improving mental health outcomes in adolescents. Objective neurophysiological and neurobehavioral measures may provide information complementary to conventional symptom-based assessment. Electroencephalography (EEG) and eye-tracking offer non-invasive and relatively accessible measures of neural and behavioral function and may support longitudinal risk detection for psychotic disorders or bipolar disorders. This study aims to prospectively evaluate and develop early recognition models for adolescents at high risk for psychotic or bipolar disorders using EEG and eye-tracking features. Methods This is a prospective, observational, single-centre longitudinal cohort study conducted at Peking University Sixth Hospital. A total of 300 adolescents aged 12–19 years at elevated risk for psychotic or bipolar disorder (BD) will be recruited. Baseline assessments will include diagnostic interviews, clinician-rated and self-report symptom measures, psychosocial functioning assessments, cognitive tasks, and simultaneous EEG and eye-tracking recording. Participants will undergo clinical reassessments at 6, 12, 18, and 24 months. The primary objective is to identify the specific EEG and eye-tracking features associated with adverse clinical progression over 2 years in adolescents at elevated risk for psychotic disorders or bipolar disorder, and to develop and validate the risk-stratification prediction models based on synchronized EEG and eye-tracking data. Secondary objectives include estimating the rate and temporal pattern of diagnostic transition to psychotic disorder or BD, characterizing longitudinal trajectories of psychiatric symptoms and psychosocial functioning, and evaluating the incremental prognostic value of digital phenotype markers beyond conventional clinical assessment. Statistical analyses will include Cox proportional hazards models, linear mixed-effects models, and machine learning approaches with feature selection and internal validation. Discussion This study applies a longitudinal multimodal framework to investigate the developmental trajectories of adolescents at elevated risk for psychotic disorders or BD. By deriving EEG-eye-tracking fusion digital biomarkers, this study aims to clarify whether integrating objective neurophysiological and behavioral measures can improve individual-level prediction of adverse clinical progression beyond traditional clinical assessment. Findings from this cohort may provide preliminary evidence for precision risk monitoring and inform future preventive strategies for severe mental disorders in youth. items.abstract: Abstract Background; Obstetric hemorrhage and hypertensive disorders drive Ethiopia’s high maternal mortality ratio (267/100000 live births), requiring continuous availability of lifesaving maternal commodities (LMCs). Conventional statistics offer retrospective insights rather than facility level risk forecasting. This study developed and validated machine learning classifiers to predict LMC stock outs in Ethiopian primary healthcare facilities using EDHS 2024/2025 data. Methods; A secondary analysis evaluated 1245 primary facilities. The binary outcome measured physical absence, expiration or recent stock outs of any 5 WHO tracer commodities. Nineteen features spanning logistics, human resources and infrastructure were analyzed. Five algorithms Logistic Regression, SVC, MLP-ANN, Random Forest and XGBoost were implemented, handling class imbalance via SMOTE and evaluating performance via ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, Decision Curve Analysis (DCA), probability calibration and SHAP interpretability. Results; Overall, 45.8% of facilities experienced stock outs. XGBoost outperformed other models on the test set, achieving a ROC-AUC of 0.894, Accuracy of 88.8%, Sensitivity of 89.5% and Specificity of 88.1%. It exhibited high reliability (Brier Score of 0.084) and superior net clinical benefit via DCA across thresholds from 10% to 85%. SHAP analysis identified non-functional cold chain equipment, lack of IPLS reporting, absence of APTS auditing, irregular bin card reconciliation and lack of professional pharmacy personnel as the top risk drivers. Conclusion; Supervised machine learning algorithms notably XGBoost accurately forecast maternal commodity stock outs. Integrating this architecture into the national eLMIS enables proactive risk flagging, helping the Ministry of Health and EPSS prioritize cold chain upgrades, digital logistics and staffing in vulnerable facilities.

items.abstract: Abstract Background Endometrial cancer (EC) is strongly associated with metabolic disorders, while glycolytic reprogramming contributes to tumor progression and adverse outcomes. This study aimed to identify glycolysis-related prognostic genes and develop a machine learning-based signature for EC risk stratification. Methods Transcriptomic and clinical data were obtained from The Cancer Genome Atlas. Glycolysis-related genes were collected from KEGG, MSigDB, and Reactome. Differential expression and univariate Cox analyses were used to identify prognostic candidates. Multiple machine learning algorithms and combinations were evaluated to construct a prognostic model. Functional enrichment, immune infiltration, somatic mutation, tumor mutational burden, and drug sensitivity analyses were performed. Single-cell RNA sequencing datasets GSE179640 and GSE173682 were analyzed to characterize CENPA expression across cell types and its clinical relevance. Results Among 5,990 differentially expressed genes, 99 overlapped with 290 glycolysis-related genes, and 16 were associated with overall survival. Among 117 model combinations, random survival forest plus generalized boosted model generated a seven-gene signature comprising CLDN9, CENPA, GPI, TFF3, FBP1, SPAG4, and AURKA. The 1-, 3-, and 5-year AUCs were 0.88, 0.81, and 0.84 in the training cohort and 0.73, 0.77, and 0.76 in the internal validation cohort, respectively. High-risk patients had poorer survival and distinct pathway, immune, and genomic features. Single-cell analysis showed heterogeneous CENPA expression, while elevated CENPA was associated with advanced stage and poorer survival. Conclusions The glycolysis-related signature stratified EC patients by survival risk and was associated with distinct biological features. CENPA emerged as a candidate prognostic biomarker requiring independent external validation and experimental investigation.

items.abstract: Abstract Traffic calming is recognized as a set of physical interventions aimed at reducing vehicle speeds and enhancing the safety of vulnerable road users. However, speed bumps and speed humps can exert considerable adverse effects on patients, occupants, and drivers. This study aimed to conduct multi-scale modeling of the effects of optimizing the number and location of speed bumps and speed humps on these three groups. To this end, a convolutional neural network was employed to determine the optimal number of obstacles across 48 urban roadways. Subsequently, the effects of reducing obstacles on eight patient groups (cardiovascular, spinal, intubated, CPR, post-surgical, pregnant women, osteoporosis, and stroke) and on occupant and driver groups were quantified using biomechanical and clinical models. The results indicated that scenario S5, with 39 speed bumps and 45 speed humps, exhibits the best performance, achieving a 51.3% reduction in the number of speed bumps and a 55.9% reduction in the number of speed humps compared with the existing condition. This reduction led to a 51.7% decrease in the cumulative driver anger index, a 51.3% reduction in zero occupant comfort, a 42.6% reduction in cardiovascular risk, a 66.7% reduction in endotracheal tube displacement, and a 45.5% improvement in CPR quality. Dynamic analysis using the reference vehicle demonstrated that although the road acceleration at speed bumps is 16.8 times that at speed humps, due to suspension damping, the actual acceleration on the vehicle seat is only 22.8 times greater, and the actual VDV is approximately 3.3 times greater. The findings indicate that reducing the number of speed bumps takes higher priority than reducing speed humps.

items.abstract: Abstract Background: Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT) followed by total mesorectal excision is standard for locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC). While tumor regression grade is routinely reported, lymph node regression grade (LRG) is underutilized. We aimed to develop a machine learning model for preoperative LRG prediction. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed 111 LARC patients who underwent nCRT plus surgery between January 2016 and December 2020. LRGmax (grades 0–5) was assessed using Mandard criteria. Elastic Net regression with 10-fold cross-validation was used for feature selection, followed by a Softmax multinomial classifier. Patients were randomly split into training (70%) and validation (30%) sets. Performance was evaluated using AUC, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, and recall. Bootstrap resampling and decision curve analysis assessed calibration and clinical net benefit. Results: The LRGmax distribution was: grade 0 (28.8%), 1 (39.6%), 2 (12.6%), 3 (10.8%), 4 (5.4%), and 5 (2.7%). In the training set, AUC was 0.99. In the validation set, AUC was 0.86 and specificity 0.87. Calibration curves showed high consistency; DCA revealed positive net benefit. Higher LRGmax correlated with increased nodal metastasis count, lymph node ratio, and worse survival (all P < 0.001). LRGmax correlated positively with radiotherapy efficacy ( r = 0.28, P = 0.003) and negatively with 3-year survival ( r = –0.47, P < 0.001). Conclusions: The Elastic Net–Softmax model showed discriminative utility for predicting LRGmax after nCRT in LARC. Despite decreased validation metrics due to limited sample size and class imbalance, the model retained predictive value as a proof-of-concept tool. Multi-center prospective studies are warranted.

items.abstract: Influenza A virus (IAV) populations are characterized by a high prevalence of non-infectious virions, with particle-to-plaque forming unit (PFU) ratios typically ranging from 10 to 1,000. While "multiplicity reactivation" -the process by which incomplete viral genomes (IVGs) establish productive infection through co-infection- has long been hypothesized, its quantitative nature has remained elusive. In this study, we utilized a digital influenza assay to achieve absolute quantification of IAV particles, allowing us to define the particle-based multiplicity of infection (pMOI) for precise evaluation. We combined this approach with a single-cell infection assay using microcompartmentalized containers and machine learning-based automated cell classification to accurately assess infection outcomes across a wide range of pMOIs. Our analysis of the A/Puerto Rico/8/1934 (H1N1) revealed a count-to-plaque forming unit (PFU) ratio of approximately 400, meaning only a tiny fraction of particles possesses infectivity. Remarkably, the infection rate in single-cell infection experiments followed a sigmoidal curve and reached saturation at a pMOI of only 5 to 10. This demonstrates that under high-pMOI conditions, productive infection is predominantly driven by genome complementation among incomplete particles rather than solely by fully infectious virions. On the other hand, mathematical model analysis based on these findings suggested that the functionality of each of the eight genomic segments within a virus particle follows a stochastic process, resulting in a probability distribution for the number of functional segments per particle. This mechanism proved exceptionally robust across multiple strains despite a 20-fold variation in CTPR values. Ultimately, these findings indicate that incomplete particles are not merely biological noise but active contributors to the infection process, significantly enhancing the infectivity and evolutionary flexibility of IAV. This study will provide a more refined understanding of influenza transmission dynamics and risk assessment, particularly in environments where multiple virus particles are present within a single respiratory droplet.

items.abstract: Abnormal mitochondrial respiratory chain (MRC) activity is a pivotal driver in the pathogenesis of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). However, the molecular mechanisms linking it to immune phenotypes and disease progression remain unclear. This study aims to systematically determine core biomarkers of MRC dysfunction in SLE and explore their potential pathogenic mechanisms through multi-scale transcriptomic analysis. Five bulk transcriptomic series from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) were integrated to screen for differentially expressed genes linked to MRC abnormalities. Three machine learning algorithms and SHAP analysis were applied to identify core signature genes. Leveraging these markers, a diagnostic model was developed, along with constructing molecular interaction and regulatory networks. We elucidated the biological functions through functional enrichment, immune infiltration analyzes, and correlation analysis with key therapeutic targets. Furthermore, we integrated three single-cell datasets and applied Seurat clustering, pseudotime analysis, and CellChat to characterize the expression patterns, differentiation trajectories, and interaction networks of core genes within specific cell subpopulations. Our results identified 18 biomarkers, with SCO2 emerging as the primary core gene. The diagnostic model achieved high discriminatory accuracy. Multi-dimensional functional analyzes uncovered a potential role for SCO2 bridging mitochondrial metabolic dysfunction with antiviral innate immune activation. Single-cell analysis localized SCO2 overexpression primarily to monocytes and dendritic cells, showing a downregulation trajectory during myeloid differentiation. We found that SCO2 + myeloid cells exhibit altered interaction networks within the immune microenvironment, characterized by enriched MHC-I/II and MIF signaling. In conclusion, SCO2 is a critical biomarker of MRC activity in SLE, reflecting the mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming that drives immune dysregulation.

items.abstract: Abstract Interfacial contact area between contiguous grains governs macroscopic elastic moduli, stress transmission chains, effective thermal and electrical conductivity, and solid-state diffusion rates in three-dimensional (3D) granular media. Standard characterization of X-ray micro-computed tomography (µCT) volumes relies on 3D Euclidean distance transform seeding and marker-controlled watershed segmentation followed by polygonal surface extraction via the Marching-Cubes algorithm (Lorensen & Cline, 1987). However, Cartesian voxelization introduces severe staircase terracing along curved inter-particle boundaries, inflating surface area measurements by 40% to 80%, while local mesh triangulation scales poorly to assemblies containing thousands of grains. Conducted under the supervision of Prof. Mayank Goswami , this study establishes a comparative benchmark of four data-driven surrogate architectures—an interpretable Random Forest ensemble, a 4-block 3D Convolutional Neural Network (3D CNN) operating on 48 3 binary dual-particle patches, a 3-layer bidirectional GraphSAGE Graph Neural Network (GNN) operating on the global contact graph G = (V, E) , and a multimodal Hybrid GNN + CNN fusion architecture—across 250 synthetic 3D granular phantoms (50,800 particles and 48,750 contact interfaces). Across 38 held-out test specimens (7,466 contact interfaces), we evaluate models under both DEM-coupled (known sphere geometry) and blind tomographic (voxel-only, zero metadata) operating regimes. When coupled with exact inter-particle distance and radius attributes, the 3-layer bidirectional GraphSAGE network achieves a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.158 vx 2 , a root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 0.217 vx 2 , a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 1.91% , and R 2 = 0.99999 at an inference latency of 2.89 ms per phantom , while the Random Forest baseline achieves R 2 = 0.99992 and MAE = 0.409 vx 2 . Crucially, an explicit feature-circularity ablation study demonstrates that removing pairwise distance and overlap features collapses tabular/graph accuracy to R 2 = 0.4387 (MAE = 44.68 vx 2 ), proving that inter-centroid geometry is physically indispensable; however, estimating these quantities 100% blindly from watershed-segmented voxels via principal inertia axes ( R̂ i = L maj,i /2, MAE = 0.048 vx) restores R 2 = 0.9959 (MAE = 3.35 vx 2 ) without ground-truth metadata. Furthermore, the purely image-based 4-block 3D CNN —which requires zero tabular or metadata inputs—achieves R 2 = 0.99788 and MAE = 2.434 vx 2 (166.23 ms/phantom), outperforming classical Marching-Cubes surface meshing (MAE = 42.750 vx 2 , MAPE = 72.24%, R 2 = 0.50471, 3,555.60 ms/phantom) by 17.6× in accuracy and 21.4× in speed. Scaling experiments up to N = 2,000 particles, overlap-depth stratification, per-particle contact area aggregation ( n = 6,879 active test grains), and domain adaptation to mildly non-spherical superellipsoids (3D CNN R 2 = 0.9979, MAE = 2.50 vx 2 ) establish practical guidelines, methodological limitations, and ethical safeguards for deploying AI surrogates in granular mechanics.

items.abstract: Abstract The spatial resolution of a computed tomography (CT) scan, summarised by the frequency at which the modulation transfer function falls to one half (MTF50), depends jointly on focal-spot size, geometric magnification, detector blur and reconstruction voxel size. We built a simulation pipeline that scans an analytic slanted-edge and bar-pattern phantom at 400 acquisition settings and measures the ground-truth MTF with the edge-spread-function method and used it to train two kinds of fast estimators. A Gaussian-process surrogate predicts MTF50 from the four settings with a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.106 lp/mm and R 2 = 0.983 on held-out settings, compared with 1.285 lp/mm for the classical quadrature blur formula and 0.293 lp/mm for a calibrated version of it, about 2,000 times faster than a single simulation. Adding physics-derived blur features improved every model and kept errors low in several extrapolation scenarios in which raw-feature models failed. A small residual convolutional network that sees only a 64 × 64 image patch reached 0.121 lp/mm per setting, close to the surrogate, but its error rose to 0.60 lp/mm on unseen generic phantoms, exposing a clear out-of-distribution limit. Within the studied ranges, magnification and detector blur were the most influential settings. Code, data and trained models are released.

items.abstract: Abstract Purpose Accurate preoperative prediction of pathological complete response (pCR) following neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) is essential for individualized treatment decision-making in patients with breast cancer. This study aimed to develop a multimodal fusion model integrating conventional radiomics, two-dimensional (2D) deep learning features, and clinical risk factors based on the pre-treatment third-phase images of dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI), and to validate its efficacy for predicting pCR in an independent institutional cohort. Methods This retrospective multicenter study enrolled 372 women with breast cancer who received NAC across two centers. The 245 patients from Center 1 constituted the model development cohort and were stratified by pCR status and randomly split at a 7:3 ratio into a training set (n = 171) and an internal validation set (n = 74), whereas the 127 patients from Center 2 served as an independent external test set. A radiologist manually delineated the tumor region of interest on the third contrast-enhanced phase of DCE-MRI, and all delineations were reviewed by a senior radiologist. A total of 1,197 radiomic features were extracted using PyRadiomics; after Spearman correlation-based redundancy removal and dimensionality reduction with least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, 10 features were retained to construct the radiomics model. Six ImageNet-pretrained convolutional neural networks were compared, and MobileNet V2 was selected to build the 2D deep learning model. After dimensionality reduction by principal component analysis, the deep features were early-fused with the radiomic features to develop a deep learning radiomics (DLR) model. Independent clinical predictors of pCR were identified using univariate and multivariate logistic regression and used to construct a clinical model. The predicted probability of the DLR model was further fused with the independent clinical factors using logistic regression to build the combined model, which was presented as a nomogram. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, calibration curves, decision curve analysis, the DeLong test, the integrated discrimination improvement (IDI), and the net reclassification improvement (NRI). Interpretability analyses were conducted using SHAP and Grad-CAM. Results The pCR rate of the entire cohort was 14.2% (53/372), with rates of 17.0%, 21.6%, and 6.3% in the training, internal validation, and external test sets, respectively. Multivariate logistic regression identified ER status (adjusted OR = 0.119, P < 0.001), HER-2 status (adjusted OR = 4.870, P = 0.003), and maximum tumor diameter (adjusted OR = 0.742, P = 0.041) as independent predictors of pCR. In the independent external test set, the combined model achieved the best overall discriminative performance, with an AUC of 0.933 (95% CI: 0.879–0.987), accuracy of 0.843, sensitivity of 1.000, specificity of 0.832, and negative predictive value of 1.000, outperforming the clinical model (AUC = 0.925), the deep learning model (0.825), the DLR model (0.745), and the radiomics model (0.559); its AUC was significantly higher than those of the radiomics model (P = 0.0007) and the DLR model (P = 0.014). The deep learning model showed the smallest cross-center performance degradation (ΔAUC = 0.033), markedly smaller than that of the conventional radiomics model (ΔAUC = 0.278). Relative to the four single-modality models, the combined model yielded positive IDI (0.208–0.482, all P < 0.05) and NRI (0.216–0.683) values, good calibration (Hosmer–Lemeshow test, P = 0.069), and a higher net clinical benefit on decision curve analysis. SHAP and Grad-CAM analyses consistently demonstrated that model decisions focused on intratumoral enhancement heterogeneity and peritumoral regions, with the most contributory features derived from both radiomics and deep learning, indicating complementarity between the two sources of information. Conclusions The multimodal fusion nomogram integrating independent clinical predictors, conventional radiomic features, and 2D deep learning features can accurately and robustly predict pCR after NAC in breast cancer before surgery, with favorable cross-center generalizability and interpretability. It may serve as a noninvasive quantitative tool for evaluating NAC response and supporting individualized treatment decision-making.

items.abstract: Abstract Background: Genetic frontotemporal dementia (FTD) is characterized by substantial clinical and neuroanatomical heterogeneity, making prediction of symptom onset challenging. We evaluated whether deep learning-derived MRI biomarkers could be combined with non-imaging biomarkers in an interpretable framework for diagnosis and phenoconversion prediction in genetic FTD. Methods: We evaluated Multi-ICNN, a multimodal extension of the Interpretable Convolutional Neural Network, using data from the FTD Risk Cohort. Imaging biomarkers derived from T1-weighted MRI were combined with demographic, genetic, and neuropsychological biomarkers in an additive prediction model. We evaluated classification of symptomatic mutation carriers versus genetically confirmed non-carriers and phenoconversion prediction within 2- and 5-year time horizons. Biomarker contributions were examined at the group and participant levels. Results: For diagnosis, Multi-ICNN achieved the highest mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.953, numerically outperforming the single-modality models. For phenoconversion prediction, the deep learning-based models outperformed the conventional volumetric and non-imaging models. The imaging-only ICNN achieved the highest mean AUCs of 0.798 and 0.780 for the 2- and 5-year horizons, respectively. Adding non-imaging biomarkers did not further improve ICNN performance. Neuropsychological measures contributed most strongly to diagnosis, whereas imaging-derived biomarkers dominated phenoconversion prediction, particularly biomarkers involving frontal and temporal regions. The additive model also provided participant-specific biomarker contributions. Conclusions: Interpretable deep learning-derived MRI biomarkers showed promise for phenoconversion prediction in genetic FTD, while the value of multimodal integration depended on the clinical task. The main limitations were the modest sample size and lack of external validation, reflecting the rarity of genetic FTD and the limited availability of comparable longitudinal cohorts.

items.abstract: Background: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a devastating chronic lung disease with an incompletely understood course. Limited quantitative tools complicate consistent patient assessment, and visual evaluation of radiological progression varies between observers. This study aimed to assess baseline and one-year CT scans using artificial intelligence (AI)–assisted 3D quantitative Computed Tomography (QCT), integrating radiological changes with clinical findings to objectively characterize disease progression and examine its association with prognosis. Methods: In this retrospective cohort of 83 patients with IPF, we evaluated patients using an AI-assisted quantitative CT framework for prognostic assessment. Whole-lung segmentation was performed using a pretrained deep learning model (LungMask), followed by semi-automated segmentation of fibrotic abnormalities with radiologist-guided refinement. Quantitative imaging biomarkers, including honeycombing volume, non-honeycomb fibrotic lung volume, preserved lung volume, and the pathological lung volume-to-total lung volume ratio, were derived from 3D QCT analysis. Baseline and one-year measurements and their changes were evaluated in relation to mortality, pulmonary function test, gender, age, physiology score (GAP) index, and composite physiologic index (CPI). Between-group comparisons were performed using the Mann–Whitney U test, paired comparisons using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, and correlations using Spearman’s rank correlation analysis. Statistical analyses were conducted using SPSS version 27.0. Results: A total of 83 patients with IPF were included in the study (mean age: 64.1 ± 8.5 years; 69.9% male). First-year mortality was 14.5% (n = 12), and overall mortality was 37.3% (n = 31) over a median follow-up of 48 months. Compared with the survival group, the mortality group had greater baseline non-honeycomb fibrotic lung volume (1002.2 ml ± 532.3 vs. 628.4 ± 460.2), a higher pathological-to-total lung volume ratio, comprising honeycomb and non-honeycomb fibrosis (0.34 ± 0.16 vs. 0.18 ± 0.15), and lower preserved lung volume (2317.9 ± 961.4 vs. 3531.6 ± 1579.2; all p < 0.001). Over one year, honeycomb and non-honeycomb fibrotic lung volume ratios increased, while the preserved lung volume ratio decreased in both groups (all p < 0.05). Patients with a 10% forced vital capacity (FVC) decline had a greater increase in the non-honeycomb fibrotic-to-total lung volume ratio (0.08 ± 0.10 vs. 0.02 ± 0.20; p = 0.044). The baseline pathological-to-total lung volume ratio correlated with baseline GAP (r = 0.343, p = 0.002), baseline CPI (r = 0.431, p < 0.001), and one-year CPI (r = 0.560, p < 0.001). One-year QCT changes did not differ significantly between the mortality and survival groups. Conclusion: 3D semi-automated, AI-assisted QCT provided an objective assessment of radiological progression in IPF. Greater baseline fibrotic involvement and lower preserved lung volume were associated with mortality, and quantitative imaging measures correlated with GAP and CPI. Although one-year QCT changes did not differ by mortality status, increased non-honeycomb fibrotic involvement was associated with FVC decline. These findings support QCT as a complementary tool for assessing disease extent and progression alongside functional and prognostic indices.

items.abstract: Management of pulmonary nodules detected on computed tomography requires assessment of malignancy risk, treatment suitability and the benefits and harms of available options. This narrative review examines clinical decision-making and continuity of care for screening-detected and incidental nodules. Core searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science and the Cochrane Library covered English-language literature from 2010 through August 2026, supplemented by targeted searches and citation tracing. Evidence was selectively synthesized around management decisions. Nodule type, prior imaging and consistent measurement methods guide risk assessment and surveillance. Surveillance intervals and intervention criteria remain specific to the detection setting, the nodule type and the applicable management framework. Further testing is appropriate when its results could change a feasible management plan; negative or nondiagnostic results require interpretation in light of residual malignancy risk. Treatment selection should balance expected benefit against procedural harm and overtreatment, considering cardiopulmonary reserve, frailty, comorbidity, competing mortality risks and patient preferences. Within the reviewed literature, patient-outcome benefit from artificial intelligence has not been established. Continuity of care requires completion of planned actions, review and communication of results, and clear responsibility for subsequent follow-up. Risk-informed decisions should be linked to reliable follow-up, with reassessment as imaging findings or patient circumstances change.

items.abstract: BackgroundA brain tumor is a medical pathology, whereas biomedical imaging is a key element used to visualize the condition. Brain tumor classification is an essential imaging task for early pinpointing and treatment. Accurate and timely tumor characterization supports appropriate treatment planning, prognosis assessment and better patient outcomes.ObjectiveThis paper aims to develop an efficient hybrid deep learning model for early detection of brain tumors from MRI (Magnetic Resonance Imaging) images.MethodsTo classify tumors, this work proposes a hybrid EfficientNet B7 and Inception V4 (ENETV4) network. The Inception network interprets spatial features for improving classification accuracy, while the EfficientNet B7 framework increases the computational efficiency to maintain high feature extraction ability. A unified feature is created by concatenating the retrieved features from the two models. To improve classification performance, a Figshare dataset comprising glioma, meningioma and pituitary tumor MRI images was used. Optimized hyperparameters enhanced generalization across the 70:20:10 train-test-validation split of the multi-sequence MRI dataset.ResultsThe proposed hybrid ENETV4 networks achieved 98.53% accuracy using an independent dataset, outperforming existing methods when evaluated on the dataset. These results accurately differentiate various kinds of tumors. This paper compares the hybrid ENETV4 model with the traditional models, reaffirming that the hybrid ENETV4 method enables effective classification of brain tumors from medical images, helping clinicians select suitable treatment strategies.ConclusionThe proposed hybrid methods provide accurate tumor classification in an early stage, supporting timely clinical decisions and treatment planning.

items.abstract: BackgroundPhoton-counting computed tomography (PCCT) provides finely sampled morphological images and energy-resolved products that may alter the behavior of artificial-intelligence models developed for conventional CT.ObjectiveThis review synthesizes downstream AI applications in PCCT and determines which study designs support claims of feasibility, transfer, spatial or spectral contribution, scanner advantage, and clinical utility.MethodsA structured narrative search identified original studies evaluating segmentation, detection, classification and characterization, and automated quantification on reconstructed PCCT images. Each analytical configuration was coded by task, effective input, model provenance, development or adaptation strategy, reference standard, comparator, testing independence, and evidence maturity.ResultsTechnical feasibility has been demonstrated across all four tasks. Established conventional-domain models often retained useful local performance on PCCT, while PCCT-native studies explored virtual monoenergetic images, threshold or energy-bin images, material maps, and multienergy feature spaces. However, small cohorts, repeated non-independent observations, incomplete external testing, limited matched PCCT-EID comparisons, and scarce spatial or spectral ablations restrict causal attribution. Prospective workflow evidence remains uncommon.ConclusionsPCCT creates important opportunities for AI-enabled image analysis, but availability of high-resolution or energy-resolved information does not establish its contribution to performance. Claims should be aligned with the comparator, ablation, reference standard, and validation design required to support them.

items.abstract: Objectives To develop deep learning super-resolution (SR) models for enhancing cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT). Methods Seventy CBCT volumes (75 µm voxel size) served as references. Paired low-resolution (LR) volumes (300 µm) were simulated using physics-based degradation. Four architectures were each trained with three loss configurations (L1; L1+edge; L1+edge+perceptual): Swin Transformer for Image Restoration (SwinIR), Hybrid Attention Transformer (HAT), Hybrid Multi-Axis Aggregation Network (HMA-Net), and Dense-Residual-Connected Transformer (DRCT). Performance was assessed with peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), structural similarity index measure (SSIM), learned perceptual image patch similarity (LPIPS), and deep image structure and texture similarity (DISTS). Three dentists ranked the 12 configurations in 28 sets using blinded forced-choice pairwise comparisons. Correlations of metrics and expert ranks were assessed using Spearman correlation. Results All configurations outperformed LR input and bicubic interpolation on every metric (p < 0.05). HMA-Net trained with L1+edge+perceptual loss performed best on LPIPS (0.216) and DISTS (0.186). HAT with L1 loss achieved the highest PSNR (28.79 dB) and SSIM (0.820). Experts ranked DRCT and HAT with L1 loss, and DRCT with L1+edge loss, as the best configurations (p < 0.001 versus others). Expert rank correlated moderately only with PSNR (rho = -0.65) and SSIM (rho = -0.60; both p < 0.05). Conclusions Transformer-based SR improved the perceived quality of clinical CBCT images. HAT and DRCT trained with L1 pixel loss alone, and DRCT trained with L1 and edge loss, demonstrated superior performance. Advances in knowledge Transformer-based super-resolution improved expert-perceived detail of simulated low-resolution in vivo CBCT scans without additional radiation dose, supporting further validation on directly acquired low-resolution scans.

items.abstract: Objective. To eliminate the reliance on large-scale external training datasets and achieve high-precision alignment for complex brain structures by overcoming the prevalent challenges of data scarcity and domain shifts in current deep learning-based registration methods. Approach. We propose a novel Instance-Specific Deep Brain Registration Framework that independently trains a dedicated model for each specific image pair. By reconceptualizing a single image pair as an internal dataset generator, we introduce a Multi-Scale Random Patch Learning strategy to construct a diverse local-to-global sample space. Architecturally, we design a Context-Aware Flow Predictor integrated with a Recurrent Context Transfer mechanism within a coarse-to-fine paradigm. Furthermore, a Topology-Aware Adaptive Optimization strategy is incorporated during the inference phase. By dynamically tracking the local spatial folding status, it adaptively adjusts spatial regularization to effectively suppress topological distortions while maximizing voxel-level accuracy. Main results. Extensive experiments on mono-modal, multi-modal, and pathological brain MRI datasets demonstrate that our method can handle large anatomical deformations without relying on external training datasets. It achieves highly competitive registration performance compared to mainstream population-based and implicit neural representation methods. Crucially, it balances this alignment precision with effective numerical topology preservation. Significance. This framework challenges the traditional population-based learning paradigm, offering a highly flexible, robust, and promising solution for practical neuroimage analysis, particularly in clinical scenarios characterized by extreme data scarcity and complex cross-modality variations.

items.abstract: Objective This study aimed to rationally design, screen, and experimentally validate novel immunoglobulin domain antibodies (IgDAbs) targeting the site II epitope of the respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) fusion (F) protein using generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) driven tools. Method A generative AI tool was employed to generate 250 novel IgDAb sequences optimized for RSV-F site II binding. Candidates were screened computationally using molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations to select hit candidates. The selected IgDAbs were cloned and produced using an E. coli expression system. Purified IgDAbs were characterized for target specificity via ELISA and evaluated for functional viral inhibition using in vitro microneutralization assay against RSV A2 (long strain). Result Computational screening narrowed the library to 05 structurally compatible hit IgDAb with predicted binding affinity. ELISA confirmed specific binding of purified IgDAbs to the RSV-F protein. In vitro microneutralization assays demonstrated neutralization of RSV A2 (long strain), with two 'lead' IgDAbs showing EC 50 of 1.3 µg/mL and 3.5 µg/mL. Conclusion Combining generative AI sequence generation with an integrated in silico and in vitro screening cascade enables the rapid, cost-effective discovery of neutralizing nanobodies against RSV, offering a viable alternative to resource-intensive traditional antibody discovery workflows.

items.abstract: Artificial intelligence-based protein structure prediction provides new opportunities for structure-based drug discovery, especially for targets lacking experimental structures. Determining whether AlphaFold2- and AlphaFold3-derived models can reliably support structure-based virtual screening remains a critical issue. In this study, we systematically evaluated the applicability of AlphaFold2- and AlphaFold3-derived models for structure-based virtual screening and assessed the performance of different VS pipeline configurations that integrate AlphaFold models with diverse docking and scoring combinations. Based on our benchmarking results, we established a hierarchical VS methodology and applied this approach to CLIP1-LTK, an oncogenic fusion protein lacking an experimentally resolved structure. Using this pipeline, a library of approximately three million compounds was virtually screened, leading to the identification of potential inhibitor candidates. Similarity-based analog searching identified QL07, which exhibited an IC 50 value of 524.27 nM. QL07 inhibited CLIP1-LTK downstream signaling pathways and induced apoptosis in transformed Ba/F3-CLIP1-LTK cells. Furthermore, QL07 suppressed the growth of CLIP1-LTK-positive tumors in xenograft models. These findings underscore the utility of AlphaFold models in overcoming structural limitations in drug discovery and demonstrate their feasibility in identifying promising small-molecule inhibitors against protein targets without experimentally-determined structures.

items.abstract: Protein kinases are key cellular regulators of growth, proliferation, and signal transduction, making them important therapeutic targets in precision medicine, particularly for cancer and inflammatory diseases. Although molecular docking remains a central tool in structure-based drug discovery, its predictive accuracy is often limited by rigid receptor assumptions and simplified solvent representation. To overcome these limitations, machine learning models were developed based on Extended Connectivity Interaction Features to predict kinase-ligand binding affinities. A kinase-specific dataset of 2337 complexes from PDBbind 2020 was used to train five regression models, namely Decision Tree, Support Vector Regressor, Gradient Boosting Regressor, Random Forest, and Extreme Gradient Boosting, using a merged descriptor set of 1757 interaction-specific and physicochemical features. Integration of RDKit descriptors consistently improved predictive performance across models. Among the evaluated models, GBR achieved the highest predictive correlation, with a PCC of 0.72 and R 2 value of 0.51, while SVR yielded the lowest mean squared error value of 0.84 with a PCC of 0.71. The XGBoost and RF followed with R 2 values of 0.49 and 0.42, respectively, whereas DT showed the weakest performance, with an R 2 value of 0.25 and a PCC of 0.54. External validation on 5265 complexes further confirmed the robustness of the framework and facilitated the identification of high-confidence binding candidates through consensus prediction. Notably, this strategy accurately predicted binding affinities and enabled prioritization of the top 20 compounds as potential kinase-binding leads, demonstrating a scalable and computationally efficient framework for improved virtual screening and hit prioritization in rational drug discovery.

items.abstract: Natural products derived from traditional medicines are valuable sources of potential geroprotective compounds; however, their translation into therapeutic candidates is limited by chemical complexity, polypharmacology, limited mechanistic resolution, and lengthy experimental validation. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers an emerging framework for integrating chemical, pharmacological, multi-omics, imaging, and literature derived data to accelerate natural product anti-aging research. This review summarizes recent applications of AI in three interconnected areas: drug repurposing, prediction of aging-related targets and signaling pathways, and identification of biomarkers for biological aging and cellular senescence. AI integrates chemical, molecular, omics, and imaging data to prioritize candidate compounds, predict drug-target interactions, identify synergistic combinations, and reveal mechanisms underlying geroprotection. However, computational predictions should not be interpreted as evidence of efficacy or causality. Data heterogeneity, sampling bias, limited model interpretability, inadequate external validation, and insufficient pharmacokinetic and long-term safety assessment remain major barriers to translation. Future progress will require an iterative framework that combines AI prediction with target engagement studies, senescence models, organoids, animal experiments, and clinical biomarker validation. This integrated strategy may improve the efficiency, reproducibility, and translational potential of natural product geroscience research.

items.abstract: AI models such as foundation models and generative models have shown promise for aiding drug discovery alongside traditional cheminformatics and bioinformatics tools and physics-based approaches. In this study, we design a workflow that integrates these AI methods to generate molecules alongside established informatic and predictive filtering approaches to streamline downselection of molecules from the massive and noisy result sets generated by AI. This workflow evaluates generative methods based on validity, reliability, diversity, similarity, hallucination and campaign needs. Analyses are made on the original proprietary dataset to determine molecular property thresholds for screening criteria. Overall, 249 molecules are selected from ~ 5 million generated molecules. 18 molecules are then validated with free energy perturbation simulations. 5 out of 5 retain on target inhibition, with IC 50 values below 1 μM. 1 of the 5 experimentally validated molecules displayed greater inhibition than the corresponding lead molecule. Predictive foundation model MMELON yields Pearson correlation R = 0.72 in blind test, showing potential for future drug discovery campaigns.

items.abstract: Chloroplast protein import components have been well documented in Arabidopsis and Chlamydomonas, but remain largely unexplored in other species. This is also true of the pea (Pisum sativum), a classic model system in which many of the early discoveries were made. This study provides an inventory of the components involved in the import of chloroplast proteins,and characterises the heterotrimeric translocon at the outer membrane of pea chloroplasts (TOC). We have identified a gateway in chloroplasts that is composed of TOC159, TOC75 and TOC34. Genome analysis revealed a single gene for each of TOC75 and TOC34, but multiple homologues of TOC159. This suggests that these genes are the primary determinants of the specificity of preproteins. Quantitative analysis of the chloroplast proteome demonstrates that TOC159-1 is dominant, implying a role in the photosynthesis-associated TOC complex (TOC-P). The TOC-P components are approximately three times more abundant than those of the 1MDa TIC complex. Quantitative mass spectrometry of isolated complexes also shows an excess of TOC-P over the 1MDa TICs, indicating separation of TOC and TIC. In a functional protein import assay, preRbcS co-isolated together with the TOC complex, demonstrating its preprotein receptor activity. AlphaFold 3 modelling suggests that dimers of the GTP-binding domains of TOC34 and TOC159-1 control access to a hybrid β-barrel assembly formed by the TOC75 and TOC159-1 β-barrel domains. These models also predict the presence of a transit peptide-binding groove within the TOC159 GTP-binding domain. Together, these findings contribute to a foundational model for TOC function in land plants.

items.abstract: Objective Ultrahigh-resolution (UHR) coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) using a photon-counting detector (PCD) provides excellent spatial resolution but is limited by increased image noise. We evaluated whether deep learning (DL)-based denoising and contrast enhancement can further improve UHR-CCTA image quality. Materials and methods UHR-CCTA scans from 25 patients with coronary artery disease were retrospectively analyzed. Images were reconstructed at 0.2-mm slice thickness without and with quantum iterative reconstruction (QIR, Q off -Q 4 ), and subsequently processed using a DL tool for denoising and increasing iodine contrast enhancement. Subjective image quality (sharpness, noise, vessel wall delineation, and overall quality) was assessed by three radiologists using a 5-point Likert scale. Objective analysis included signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), and coronary wall sharpness. Differences between image sets were analyzed using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Results DL-based CCTA demonstrated significantly superior subjective image quality across all parameters compared to standard reconstructions, with an overall median image quality ([interquartile interval, IQR]: 4 [3-5] versus 2 [2-3], p < 0.001). SNR and CNR were significantly higher for DL-based CCTA across all QIR levels (all p < 0.001). The highest values were observed for DL-based CCTAQ 4 versus UHR-CCTAQ 4 (SNR: 258.0 ± 147.5 versus 145.2 ± 50.1; CNR: 25.8 ± 17.1 versus 11.1 ± 4.5; both p < 0.001). Coronary wall sharpness was improved for DL-based CCTA for Q 1-4 (all p < 0.027). Conclusion DL-based denoising and iodine contrast enhancement effectively reduce noise and improve anatomic detail in UHR-CCTA, providing incremental value beyond vendor-specific reconstruction, particularly at high QIR strength levels. Key points Question Deep learning reduces noise and enhances contrast in ultrahigh-resolution coronary CT angiography. Findings Image quality improves beyond standard iterative reconstruction methods, and vessel wall sharpness and diagnostic clarity significantly increase. Relevance statement This study aimed to determine at which levels of vendor-specific iterative reconstruction, DL-based denoising and contrast enhancement perform best in UHR CCTA, providing a foundation for future investigations on how these technical improvements may translate into diagnostic benefits.

items.abstract: Rationale and objectives Medical imaging typically generates 12-bit to 16-bit formats, yet conversion to 8-bit is often required. While deep learning has been widely explored in medical imaging, the influence of image bit depth on model performance is not fully understood. This study evaluates the impact of conversion from 16-bit to 8-bit for sex, age, and obesity classification using deep learning. Materials and methods In this retrospective, multi-institutional study, we analyzed 100,002 chest radiographs from 48,047 participants across three institutions. Images were uniformly quantized from the fixed 0-65535 range to 256 levels (0-255) with no additional processing. Three convolutional neural network architectures (ResNet52, EfficientNetB2, and ConvNeXtSmall) were trained on both 16-bit and 8-bit versions of the images. Model performance was evaluated using internal test datasets, randomly split multiple times, and an external test dataset. Statistical analysis included paired comparisons of area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) values, with Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons. Results Across all architectures and classification tasks, differences between 16-bit and 8-bit model performance were minimal (mean differences ranging from -0.218%-0.184%). Statistical analyses revealed no significant differences in AUC-ROC values between bit depths for any model-task combination (all p values > 0.05 after Bonferroni correction). Effect sizes were small to moderate (Cohen's d ranging from -0.415-0.391). Conclusion No statistically significant differences were detected between models trained on 16-bit and 8-bit images in the three evaluated tasks. These findings suggest that conversion to 8-bit images may reduce data storage requirements and improve data processing efficiency. Further research is needed to assess their usefulness in clinical tasks.
