items.abstract: Background and purpose Three-dimensional fast spin-echo MR cisternography (CUBE) of the internal auditory canal (IAC) and cerebellopontine angle (CPA) requires longer acquisition times that can limit clinical throughput. We evaluated whether a deep learning (DL)-based highly accelerated reconstruction technique, Sonic DL`™ (SDL), combined with a commercially available DL denoising reconstruction (AIR™ Recon DL, ARDL), preserves or improves subjective image quality and cochlear anatomy visualization relative to standard CUBE-ARDL while shortening scan time. Materials and methods Consecutive patients underwent brain MRI for suspected IAC pathology at 1.5T and 3T with paired acquisition of standard 3D CUBE-ARDL and an accelerated 3D CUBE-SDL sequence. Both used the same voxel size at 1.5T (0.6x0.6x1.2 mm 3 ) and 3T (0.6x0.6x0.6 mm 3 ). Scan times for CUBE-ARDL versus CUBE-SDL were 2:33 versus 1:41 min at 1.5T and 1:55 versus 1:11 min at 3T. Two independent neuroradiologists blinded to MRI acquisition method scored randomized, de-identified images on a 5-point Likert scale across five domains (overall image quality, noise, sharpness, artifacts, cochlear anatomy visualization). Reader-averaged scores for CUBE-ARDL and CUBE-SDL were compared with paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, with reader-specific and cumulative link mixed model (CLMM) sensitivity analyses and false discovery rate (FDR) adjustment; intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) quantified inter-reader reliability for each technique; Gwet's AC2 and weighted (Conger's) kappa with linear ordinal weights quantified pooled inter-reader agreement. Results After exclusion of 5 training cases per field strength, 49 (1.5T) and 34 (3T) patients were analyzed. CUBE-SDL scored significantly better than CUBE-ARDL for all five domains at both field strengths (all FDR-adjusted P < .001), consistently for each reader and in the CLMM. Inter-reader reliability (ICC) for CUBE-SDL was moderate-to-excellent at 3T (0.63-0.92) and moderate at 1.5T (0.65-0.74), generally exceeding CUBE-ARDL (3T: 0.35-0.61; 1.5T: 0.50-0.71). Pooled inter-reader agreement (Gwet's AC2) ranged from 0.56 to 0.89. Conclusions A combined Sonic DL acceleration with ARDL-denoised reconstruction for 3D T2 CUBE produced significantly higher subjective image quality at both 1.5T and 3T, and, at 3T, higher inter-reader reliability than standard CUBE-ARDL, while shortening acquisition time by 34%-38%. These findings support further evaluation, including diagnostic accuracy studies, of CUBE-SDL as an alternative to CUBE-ARDL.

items.abstract: Objectives Thyroid nodules are common and mostly benign, but 5-15% are malignant. Increasing detection rates may lead to overdiagnosis and unnecessary fine-needle aspiration biopsies (FNAB). We aimed to develop a machine learning (ML) model for thyroid malignancy risk assessment using ultrasound, FNAB, laboratory data and to compare its performance with the EU-TIRADS-PL reporting system. Methods This prospective study included 561 patients who underwent thyroidectomy based on preoperative ultrasound and FNAB results, including 261 malignant nodules (46.5%). Data were divided into training and test sets (3:1). Multiple ML algorithms were evaluated using clinical, sonographic, cytological and biochemical variables verified by histopathology. Results Logistic regression (LR) was selected as the final model because of its good performance and interpretability. The model achieved a test set ROC AUC of 74% and showed better correlation with thyroid malignancy than the EU-TIRADS-PL system. Significant predictors of malignancy included microcalcifications (p=0.002), younger age (p<0.001), male sex (p=0.001),and larger anteroposterior dimension (p=0.026). Larger longitudinal dimension was associated with lower malignancy risk (p<0.001). An anteroposterior-to-longitudinal dimension index was developed, with ROC AUC of 68% (95% CI 62.0-71.0). Conclusions The proposed ML model showed good accuracy and may improve thyroid malignancy risk assessment compared with systems based only on sonographic features.

items.abstract: Background The choroid plexus is essential for brain homeostasis, yet its in vivo morphology remains incompletely characterized. Conventional MRI visualizes only part of the choroid plexus and may therefore misrepresent age- and disease-related structural changes. We aim to develop a 7T contrast-enhanced black-blood imaging (CeBBI) framework for whole-brain visualization and quantitative morphologic characterization of the choroid plexus, and to examine its associations with aging and cerebrovascular disease. Methods We retrospectively included 234 participants referred for evaluation of intracranial atherosclerotic disease who underwent CeBBI. A deep learning model was trained to segment the whole choroid plexus. Choroid plexus volume, centerline-based shape features and cystic components were quantified. Segmentations derived from CeBBI were compared with those obtained using a validated T1-weighted MRI-based method. Associations with age, ventricular size and vascular imaging markers were assessed. Results 7T CeBBI enabled visualization of the choroid plexus across all ventricular compartments. The segmentation model achieved high accuracy (Dice score=0.901±0.013), and recovered more than twice the choroid plexus volume detected by the T1-weighted method. Total choroid plexus volume was not associated with age. However, with advancing age, the lateral ventricular choroid plexus became shorter (left r=-0.250, right r=-0.303, both P<0.001) and showed greater cross-sectional area (left r=0.174, right r=0.176, both P=0.007). Choroid plexus cyst number (r=0.187, P=0.004) and cyst volume (r=0.159, P=0.015) also increased with age. Cerebral microbleeds were independently associated with greater lateral ventricular choroid plexus volume (standardized β=0.178, P=0.012). Conclusions Our method enables robust whole-brain visualization and quantitative morphologic assessment of the choroid plexus. Rather than undergoing simple age-related hypertrophy, the choroid plexus showed complex remodeling characterized by shortening, cross-sectional expansion and cystic change. The association between cerebral microbleeds and larger choroid plexus volume further supports a potential role of vascular dysfunction in choroid plexus remodeling.

items.abstract: Background This study aimed to validate the effectiveness of a deep learning-based point cloud completion method for the reverse reconstruction of the patient-specific anatomy of the knee bone morphology, thereby providing technical support for personalized diagnosis and treatment. Methods A computed tomography (CT) database containing 140 normal knees was constructed. There were 10 clinically common defect patterns (7 femoral, 3 tibial) generated. Multiple deep learning methods were employed to achieve defect point cloud completion. Virtual testing was conducted to compare the morphological consistency (assessed by Chamfer Distance, Density-Aware Chamfer Distance, and F-score) and anatomical parameter consistency between the resulting and original intact models. The optimal point cloud completion method, based on the evaluation results, was selected for preliminary clinical feasibility testing. Consistency between reconstructed affected-side models and the intact contralateral knee models was assessed in patients who have unilateral post-traumatic osteoarthritis. Results In virtual testing, the CRA-PCN deep learning model yielded the best reconstruction performance. For all defect patterns, the reconstructed geometries attained a chamfer distance below 0.45 mm, while deviations of anatomical parameters were limited to within 0.5 mm for linear measurements and 0.2° for angular measurements. In the preliminary clinical feasibility testing, the reconstructed morphology exhibited a chamfer distance of approximately 1.2 mm compared to the contralateral side. The restoration accuracy of the joint line angle was superior in extensive defect patterns, with the optimal deviation being within 0.2° on the femoral side and approximately 0.7° on the tibial side. Conclusion The CRA-PCN model enables reverse reconstruction of defective knee structures with satisfactory anatomical restoration. It provides quantitative anatomical references for personalized arthroplasty and aids identification of deformity origins in osteoarthritis (OA) patients, though further large-scale prospective research is required to verify its clinical value.

items.abstract: Personalised radioligand therapy (RLT) depends on accurate absorbed-dose estimation. Standard dosimetry requires multiple post-therapy single-photon emission computed tomography/computed tomography (SPECT/CT) acquisitions, imposing logistical burdens. Machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) have been proposed to streamline organ segmentation, generate synthetic imaging timepoints, and predict patient-specific doses. We evaluated the performance, methodological quality, and translational readiness of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven dosimetry in the clinical theranostics literature. In this systematic review and meta-analysis, we searched PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and regional databases (Jan 1, 2014, to March 1, 2025). Studies applying AI to dosimetry in human RLT recipients were eligible. Two reviewers screened and extracted data. Risk of bias was assessed with the Prediction model Risk Of Bias ASsessment Tool (PROBAST) and the Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-2 (QUADAS-2). Meta-analyses of organ segmentation (Dice similarity coefficient [DSC]) and dose prediction (concordance correlation coefficient [CCC]) used restricted maximum-likelihood (REML) random-effects models restricted to studies with independent validation sets. CRD420261349805 (https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/display_record.php?RecordID=1349805). 58 studies met inclusion criteria covering 1847 patients (1523 [82%] male, 324 [18%] female). 23 studies with independent validation were eligible for meta-analysis. Pooled DSC was 0·87 (95% CI 0·83-0·90; 16 studies). Pooled voxel dosimetry relative absolute error (RAE) was 6·1% (4·6-8·1%; 12 studies). Pretherapy kidney dose prediction yielded pooled CCC 0·79 (0·72-0·85; 8 studies). PROBAST identified high risk of bias in 71% of prediction studies. Reducing timepoints from ≥3 to 1-2 scans increased RAE by 8·2 percentage points (5·1-11·4). AI reduced median processing time from 180 to 25 minutes. On independent validation data, AI-driven dosimetry shows promising accuracy for organ-level dose estimation and substantially reduces processing time. However, the evidence base remains immature: 71% of prediction studies carry high risk of bias, only four studies report external validation, and most pooled outcomes were graded as low or very low certainty. External multicentre validation and prospective randomised trials comparing AI-guided against fixed-activity RLT are needed before clinical adoption. Current evidence primarily demonstrates technical feasibility rather than proven clinical utility.

items.abstract: Preoperative knowledge of intracranial meningioma grade could significantly enhance surgical planning, but reliable noninvasive prediction remains an unmet clinical need. The aim of this study was to develop and externally validate a machine learning (ML) model incorporating traditional radiomic features, along with novel fractal and topological features, to predict WHO meningioma grade from preoperative MRI using a large multicenter cohort. This retrospective diagnostic study analyzed a cohort of patients in the BraTS Meningioma Challenge. Patient data (n = 909) from 6 academic medical centers were used for model training and internal validation (n = 699) and one-time final external validation (n = 210). Tumors were segmented into three regions and radiomic features extracted across four MRI sequences. Eight different ML algorithms (e.g., based on neural networks, decision trees, clustering, and linear relationships) were tested across a total of 2889 candidate features. The primary outcome was the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) for prediction of binarized WHO grade (1 vs 2 or 3). The final model used a support vector machine algorithm comprising 20 features and achieved an AUROC of 0.824 (95% CI 0.755-0.883) on unseen test data, with favorable calibration. Feature importance analysis revealed that topological complexity added complementary predictive value to conventional radiomics features. The final model is publicly available for anyone to use. This externally validated ML model accurately predicted meningioma grade using routine preoperative MRI, with the potential to guide surgical decision-making and serve as a basis for future imaging-based brain tumor classifications.

items.abstract: Head and neck (HN) cancer survivorship is associated with persistent symptom burden and long-term brain-behavioral health alterations, yet mechanisms underlying brain aging remain poorly understood. We investigated whether HN cancer survivors exhibit accelerated brain aging, whether limbic white matter (WM) pathways contribute to these changes, and whether measures associated with glymphatic function are associated with reduced brain aging. Diffusion MRI and symptom burden data were analyzed in 135 HN cancer survivors and compared with a normative cohort from the Human Connectome Project (n = 1,228). Two machine learning models (elastic net [ENET] and random forest [RF]) using fractional anisotropy (FA) and quantitative anisotropy (QA) from 45 WM tracts were trained to estimate brain age and compute brain age gap (BAG). Glymphatic-related processes were indirectly assessed using diffusion tensor imaging analysis along the perivascular spaces (DTI-ALPS). Moderation analyses examined whether symptom burden influenced associations among DTI-ALPS, BAG, and WM integrity. Survivors showed a negative mean BAG of -1.64 years in the ENET model, indicating a nonsignificant tendency toward delayed brain aging, whereas the RF model showed a positive mean BAG of 3.59 years, indicating accelerated brain aging. The RF model demonstrated stronger external generalizability and greater biological coherence, including associations with ALPS and symptom-related measures. The bilateral fornix and right U-fibers were among the strongest contributors to RF-based brain age prediction. Higher DTI-ALPS index values were associated with lower BAG and greater fornix integrity, particularly in survivors with lower symptom burden and reduced activity-related interference. HN cancer survivorship was associated with accelerated brain aging in the model demonstrating greater external generalizability and biological relevance, alongside alterations in limbic WM pathways. Higher DTI-ALPS was associated with reduced brain aging, with symptom burden modifying this relationship. These findings highlight brain health as an important component of cancer survivorship.

items.abstract: Cystic pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (c-PanNETs) are an uncommon cystic phenotype of well-differentiated pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, accounting for approximately 7-12% of PanNETs in several surgical series, although reported frequencies vary according to the definition of cystic morphology and cohort selection. Retrospective studies suggest that c-PanNETs may exhibit less aggressive clinicopathologic features than their solid counterparts; however, their imaging appearance frequently overlaps with other pancreatic cystic neoplasms, particularly branch-duct intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms, mucinous cystic neoplasms, and atypical serous cystic neoplasms. Accurate preoperative recognition may have important implications for patient management and surgical planning. This review summarizes the imaging features of c-PanNETs across computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging, and magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography, as well as the complementary roles of endoscopic ultrasound and somatostatin receptor PET/CT. Particular attention is given to arterial hyperenhancement of the cyst wall, septations, mural nodules, or residual solid components; assessment of communication with the main pancreatic duct; and integration of complementary imaging findings. Because these features are not specific, their interpretation in combination with lesion morphology and ductal relationships is emphasized. Practical approaches to differential diagnosis and common interpretive pitfalls are also discussed. The review further addresses emerging quantitative imaging techniques, including radiomics and artificial intelligence, while recognizing that evidence specific to c-PanNETs remains limited. A practical diagnostic algorithm and structured reporting checklist are provided to support systematic interpretation and multidisciplinary communication. Recognition of the imaging spectrum of c-PanNETs, combined with systematic assessment of enhancement characteristics, ductal anatomy, and complementary imaging findings, may improve diagnostic confidence and support appropriate patient management.

items.abstract: Achieving tight glycemic control in Type 1 diabetes is challenged by non-linear metabolic dynamics and insulin-stacking risk. Artificial intelligence models offer improved personalization, but their opacity raises safety concerns, particularly for basal insulin dosing, which is often treated as static in existing decision-support systems. We propose a hybrid closed-loop system combining a data-driven LightGBM regressor for basal dose prediction, trained on the T1D-UOM dataset, with a physiologically grounded, rule-based safety layer at the edge. Basal insulin is predicted from cyclical time encoding and glucose rate-of-change; bolus dosing follows carbohydrate intake and correction requirements. A time-bounded insulin-on-board model, an uncertainty-adaptive post-bolus damping factor, and a predictive low-glucose-suspend rule reproducing the Tandem Basal-IQ protocol together suspend or reduce delivery when residual insulin is high or hypoglycemia is projected. The system was evaluated in silico over 60 continuous days under shadow-mode replay and closed-loop reduced-order simulation, including an ablation with bolus delivery suppressed. Under chronological, within-subject validation, the offline basal estimator achieved R2=0.68 and MAE=0.21 U; under strict leave-one-subject-out validation on the same real cohort, performance did not generalize to unseen subjects ( R2=-0.49 , MAE=0.49 U). The hybrid controller maintained Time-in-Range at 62.8% within the reduced-order closed-loop simulation, with no violations of the insulin-on-board suspension or damping rules; suppressing bolus delivery in an ablation within this simulation dropped Time-in-Range to 26.1%, indicating that, within the reduced-order model, bolus delivery is a determinant of simulated glycemic outcome. The proposed architecture demonstrates a safety-audited template for combining machine-learning basal prediction with clinically grounded dosing rules. Validation on real outcome data and physical hardware is identified as the next steps toward clinical translation.

items.abstract: Acromegaly has an insidious onset and prolonged diagnostic delay. Vocal changes are a recognized clinical feature, the diagnostic value of deep learning architectures remains underexplored. We aimed to assess Wav2Vec2.0-based voice analysis as a non-invasive digital biomarker for acromegaly. This single-center case-control study included 70 patients with acromegaly and 68 age- and sex-matched controls. Clinical status was defined by standard biochemical criteria, symptoms, comorbidities, and residual tumor. Voice samples were recorded with a standard mobile phone and resampled to 16 kHz. Wav2Vec2.0 was used to extract high-dimensional embedding vectors. These embeddings, were used to train and validate four different machine learning classifiers using an 80%/20% train-test split with five-fold cross-validation. Model calibration was assessed with the Brier score, and clinical utility with decision curve analysis (DCA). Demographics were similar between acromegaly (mean age 45.5 years; 57.1% female) and control (mean age 47.5 years; 61.8% female) groups. On the internal hold-out test set, Logisitic Regression model maintained high accuracy (AUC 0.84; specificity 0.92; sensitivity 0.71) and showed good calibration [Brier score 0.165 (95% CI 0.057-0.289)]. DCA confirmed that LR provided the highest benefit across a clinically relevant range of threshold probabilities (~ 15-85%). Voice analysis Wav2Vec2.0-based model demonstrates good diagnostic accuracy for acromegaly. These preliminary findings suggest that voice may serve as a promising non-invasive digital biomarker, pending validation in larger and more diverse cohorts.

items.abstract: This study aimed to develop and validate OPXrayNet, an automated deep-learning framework for opportunistic osteoporosis (OP) screening using multi-site skeletal X-ray images, to address the limitations of single-site analysis and poor interpretability in existing methods. This retrospective, multicenter diagnostic study utilized 16,347 annotated X-ray images from 2186 patients. The reference standard was OP diagnosis based on DXA T-score (≤ -2.5). OPXrayNet integrated YOLOv8 for automated region-of-interest detection, a spatial-frequency joint focusing architecture for feature enhancement, a feature pyramid network for multi-scale fusion, and an expert-guided loss module. Diagnostic accuracy was evaluated using accuracy and AUC, comparing performance against models including DeepSeek-VL2 and DCNN via statistical tests on internal and external validation sets. The study included 2186 participants (mean age 69.0 ± 10.5 years; 72.3% female). On the internal test set (n = 3892), OPXrayNet achieved an accuracy of 80.1%; observed accuracy values for baseline models were lower. On the external validation set, it attained an AUC of 0.844 (95% CI: 0.821-0.867); a numerical difference of 3.9% was observed when compared with other models. Feature heatmaps suggest that the model focuses on clinically critical bone structures. OPXrayNet effectively provides accurate, automated, and interpretable opportunistic OP screening from multi-site X-ray images, showing promising performance for scalable clinical application in primary care settings. Question There is a notable absence of automated, interpretable, and highly accurate deep learning methodologies for conducting opportunistic OP screening using multi-site X-ray images. Findings The OPXrayNet model achieved an accuracy of 80.1% and an AUC of 0.844 in automated OP screening across multi-site X-rays in internal and external validation cohorts; numerical differences in performance metrics were observed when compared with baseline models. Clinical relevance This framework offers an accurate, automated, and interpretable screening tool for OP using routine X-rays, presenting substantial potential for scalable clinical application in primary care. It enables early detection without incurring additional costs or radiation exposure.

items.abstract: Spatial proteomics enables high-resolution mapping of protein expression within the tumor microenvironment, but its routine clinical application remains limited by cost, technical complexity and restricted tissue coverage. Here we present Hist2Prot, a deep learning framework that generates single-cell spatial proteomic profiles from routine hematoxylin and eosin histology. Trained on approximately 51 million paired cells from a same-section G4X spatial proteomics dataset, Hist2Prot was evaluated in internal test cohorts, independent same-platform G4X cohorts and external cross-platform datasets comprising approximately 72 million additional cells, showing concordance with measured protein profiles and outperforming established baselines. Hist2Prot-derived virtual proteins preserved immune, stromal and tumor cell phenotypes and recapitulated clinically relevant tumor microenvironment organization. Across seven independent patient cohorts comprising 1,774 patients, virtual spatial proteomics improved molecular biomarker, prognostic and immunotherapy response prediction beyond hematoxylin and eosin morphology alone. Hist2Prot enables scalable single-cell computational spatial proteomics from routine histology for precision oncology.

items.abstract: A new generation of medicines that includes gene therapies, cell-based treatments and gene editors have the potential to treat a vast range of diseases. However, the clinical success of these novel modalities is limited by unwanted immune responses, which can compromise both safety and efficacy. Regulatory agencies have recently emphasized reducing animal testing in preclinical safety studies and envisioned a strategic approach for basing regulatory decisions on scientifically validated new approach methodologies (NAMs). These methods encompass mathematical models, artificial intelligence tools, organ-on-a-chip systems, and advanced in vitro and ex vivo assays. In combination, these approaches seem potentially well suited for assessing unwanted immune responses of the novel modalities. Key challenges to be addressed include predicting the immunogenicity risks from transgene products, delivery vehicles and gene-editing machinery; managing pre-existing immunity; overcoming barriers to repeat dosing; and establishing robust long-term monitoring strategies. In this Perspective, we critically evaluate how the current NAMs toolkit, originally developed for protein therapeutics, can be adapted to assess the unwanted immune responses of novel modalities. We provide a forward-looking framework for developing and validating the next generation of predictive immunogenicity tools required to safely unlock the full therapeutic potential of these revolutionary medicines.

items.abstract: Precision oncology based on the identification of actionable genomic alterations (AGAs) has been transformative in the care of solid tumors, yet optimal treatment selection is often hindered by tissue exhaustion and slow turnaround times. Artificial intelligence (AI) addresses these barriers by predicting AGAs directly from routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained slides. Recent landmark studies, including the prospective EAGLE and ANNAR trials, have demonstrated that deep learning models can identify alterations such as EGFR in non-small cell lung cancer and FGFR in urothelial cancer across diverse global cohorts. By providing near-instant, non-destructive results, AI-based prediction can triage patients for molecular testing or clinical trials at the time of initial diagnosis. This perspective evaluates the maturing evidence base and outlines a pragmatic pathway for integrating these tools into clinical practice. Ultimately, these models offer the opportunity to extract critical molecular information from slides generated in every laboratory worldwide and to significantly improve timely access to the rapidly evolving therapeutic landscape of solid tumors.

items.abstract: Patient-reported outcomes (PROs) are essential to understanding how people live with illness, treatment, and care, and are increasingly promoted for routine use in clinical practice, quality improvement, and value-based health care. PROs are also increasingly relevant in digital health and artificial intelligence applications, both as inputs to predictive models and as outputs reflecting patient-centred aspects of health. Yet, PROs remain difficult to reuse at scale: their implementation is inconsistent across health-care settings, measurement approaches are highly heterogeneous, and PROs are rarely available as large, standardised, analysable datasets suitable for multisite analyses and advanced analytics, including artificial intelligence models. In this Viewpoint, we argue that the central challenge is not a lack of initiatives, but the absence of a coherent, end-to-end approach that connects measurement, routine capture, data standards, and analytic reuse. We propose a practical four-step pathway towards Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable (FAIR) PROs. This pathway focuses on (1) defining the outcome domains that matter and selecting high-quality questionnaires; (2) capturing PROs consistently at the point of care in structured, computable formats; (3) storing them in analysable, shareable data models; and (4) establishing transparent cross-questionnaire linking to enable comparable scores. None of these steps poses major technical challenges in isolation; the primary difficulty is that these efforts are often developed in silos, with minimal coordination across disciplines, from questionnaire development and validation to clinical workflows, informatics standards, analytic infrastructures, and governance. A shared FAIR-PROs approach would allow PROs to become a routine, reusable component of learning health systems and a driver of both person-centred care and data-driven innovation.

items.abstract: Selected laryngeal voice disorders represent a significant clinical challenge, motivating the development of non-invasive, accurate, and interpretable screening support systems. In this study, the proposed framework is developed and evaluated using three dataset-defined voice categories: Laryngocele, Vox senilis (presbyphonia), and Normal. Although recent machine learning approaches have demonstrated strong classification performance, many remain limited by their black-box nature and limited decision-support capabilities. This study proposes a preliminary explainable and decision-oriented Agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) framework for voice screening using selected acoustic features. The methodology integrates acoustic feature extraction from voice recordings with Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) and a Random Forest classifier. To enhance interpretability, the framework incorporates both local and global explainability through Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME) and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), enabling examination of the contribution of acoustic features such as Glottal-to-Noise Excitation (GNE) and fundamental-frequency (F₀) characteristics to model predictions. In addition, counterfactual reasoning is introduced through the Diverse Counterfactual Explanations (DiCE) method to illustrate how hypothetical feature-level modifications can influence predictive outcomes. A key component is the proposed Agentic Voice Disorder Diagnosis Agent (AVDD-Agent), which integrates predictive outputs, explainability, and author-defined rule-based reasoning to provide feature analysis, confidence-based risk assessment, and general voice-health and follow-up guidance. Experimental evaluation demonstrates classification performance across the three investigated dataset-defined categories, supported by statistical analyses using t tests, ANOVA (F = 60.2404, P < 0.001), and chi-square tests. The proposed framework integrates prediction, interpretability, counterfactual analysis, and decision support, demonstrating the feasibility of preliminary explainable Agentic AI-based voice screening within the scope of the investigated dataset.

items.abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into healthcare offers significant potential for enhancing diagnostic accuracy and personalised medicine, yet carries inherent risks including algorithmic bias, opacity, and threats to patient safety and fundamental rights. These concerns demand robust governance frameworks that transcend aspirational recommendations. This article examines the role of ex ante evaluation in ensuring compliance with ethical and regulatory standards for AI systems in healthcare, using the PIO Model (Principles, Indicators, and Observables) as an illustrative case study. The PIO Model on Health provides a structured self-assessment methodology grounded in the European Commission's ethical principles for trustworthy AI while aligning with binding legal obligations under the EU Artificial Intelligence Act, the Medical Devices Regulation, and the General Data Protection Regulation. Built around the operational question "Have we done it?", the Model enables stakeholders to critically evaluate AI systems through a comprehensive checklist organised according to seven ethical principles: transparency; justice and fairness; security and non-maleficence; responsibility; privacy; autonomy; and sustainability. The paper frames AI in healthcare within the human rights framework, examining risks including algorithmic bias, automation bias, erosion of the patient-physician relationship, and challenges posed by generative AI such as hallucinations and data protection concerns. The PIO Model performs an essential ex ante evaluation function, enabling identification of ethical and legislative deficiencies prior to formal conformity assessment or market placement. It facilitates continuous monitoring through medical algorithmic audit, generating metrics including conformity percentages, risk matrices, and improvement catalogues that serve as actionable guides for implementing corrective measures. Designed for collective administration incorporating technical, clinical, legal, and ethics experts alongside patient representatives, the Model synthesises proliferating ethical guidelines and complex regulatory requirements into an operational instrument that transcends minimum legal standards, contributing to developing trustworthy AI systems that safeguard patient welfare and fundamental rights.

items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is advancing nanomedicine development by linking formulation variables and biological context with delivery, therapeutic efficacy, and safety. This review examines AI assisted formulation design, centralized formulation databases, prediction of nanoparticle self assembly, and models of cell and tissue selective delivery, biodistribution, and therapeutic outcomes. Recent advances in predicting nanotoxicity and nanoparticle induced immune responses further emphasize the importance of incorporating safety endpoints into nanomedicine optimization. Beyond nanocarrier engineering, foundation models and multimodal analyses of single-cell and spatial data are expanding biological discovery by characterizing disease associated cellular states, prioritizing therapeutic targets, and predicting treatment responses. Computational approaches also support the design of therapeutic RNA, peptides, proteins, and programmable protein nanomaterials. For example, mRNA sequences generated by GEMORNA and delivered via lipid nanoparticles increased erythropoietin expression in mice by up to 15-fold compared with a benchmark sequence. Integration of biological discovery with biomolecular and nanocarrier design may inform therapeutic cargo selection, targeting strategies, and functional nanomaterial development. AI may connect patient specific biological characteristics with predictions of nanomedicine delivery and therapeutic response to support patient stratification and individualized treatment selection. Integration of histological, imaging, molecular, and longitudinal data may enable treatment strategies to be adapted to differences in tissue characteristics, disease state, and therapeutic response. Emerging approaches based on digital twins and adaptive treatment control may extend the framework toward individualized dosing and dynamic treatment optimization. Major challenges include data heterogeneity, limited model generalizability, and the need for experimental and prospective validation. Progress toward precision therapy will require integrated frameworks that jointly consider delivery, efficacy, selectivity, and safety while clearly distinguishing demonstrated applications from future opportunities.

items.abstract: Objective rare interstitial lung diseases (ILDs) represent a heterogeneous group of disorders characterized by various pathogenic mechanisms, clinical presentations, prognoses, and therapeutic challenges. Among these, acid sphingomyelinase deficiency (ASMD), pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (PAP), and pulmonary Langerhans cell histiocytosis (PLCH) exemplify rare pulmonary diseases driven by distinct biological mechanisms, including lysosomal dysfunction, impaired surfactant homeostasis, and activation of the mitogen-activated protein kinases (MAPK) pathways. Recent advancements in molecular biology, genomics, and translational research boosted the development of precision medicine strategies and disease-specific therapies for these conditions. Study design this narrative review was conducted in accordance with the SANRA guidelines. A thorough literature search of the PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus databases was performed from January 2000 to June 2026. Results significant progress has been made in treating all three diseases. In ASMD, enzyme replacement therapy with olipudase alfa has greatly improved visceral and lung symptoms, while research in gene therapy, gene editing, and metabolic treatments is ongoing. For PAP, inhaled granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF) is now the primary disease-specific treatment, now supported by phase III trial evidence for inhaled molgramostim, complemented by potential therapies such as immunomodulation, macrophage transplantation, and gene-based strategies. In PLCH, the discovery of recurrent MAPK pathway variants has supported the use of genotype-targeted treatments with BRAF and MEK inhibitors. Under these conditions, advances in molecular diagnostics, circulating biomarkers, quantitative HRCT, radiomics, and artificial intelligence (AI) are poised to enhance diagnosis, patient stratification, prognosis, and treatment decisions. Conclusions ASMD, PAP and PLCH are entering into an era of precision medicine, in which disease-specific molecular mechanisms play an increasing role in guiding diagnosis and treatment. Ongoing integration of genomics, biomarkers, advanced imaging, AI, and targeted therapies could revolutionise the management of conditions such as ASMD, PAP, and PLCH, leading to better long-term patient outcomes.

items.abstract: The filamentous fungi Monascus spp. are rich sources of secondary metabolites that include Monascus azaphilone pigments, monacolin K, and γ-aminobutyric acid, making them significant in the food, nutraceutical, cosmetic and pharmaceutical industries. Despite the industrial importance of this fungus, its production of citrinin, a nephrotoxic polyketide mycotoxin, remains a major drawback and limits its commercial application. Recent research studies have shown that the mechanism that governs citrinin biosynthesis highlights the interactions between Biosynthetic Gene Clusters (BGCs), epigenetic modifications, global regulatory networks, and environmental factors. The current understanding of the molecular and epigenetic mechanisms used to mitigate citrinin production in Monascus spp. is discussed in this review. Emphasis is given on histone acetylation and deacetylation, methylation, chromatin remodeling, the velvet complex, and the modulation of toxin biosynthesis through RNA-level gene expression control. The recent advances are critically evaluated for engineering citrinin-free strains, including transcriptomics, proteomics, multi-omics, RNA interference, CRISPR/Cas genome editing, and synthetic biology. The comparative analysis of these approaches shows that integrating epigenetic engineering with advanced genome and metabolic engineering can regulate citrinin while maintaining other important metabolite yields. Combining multi-omics and artificial intelligence-guided strain design with epigenetic interventions will accelerate the development of safe, sustainable, and high-yielding Monascus-assisted bioprocesses.

items.summary: Introduction Synthetic biology is an emerging field that integrates engineering principles, molecular innovations, interdisciplinary methodologies, and designer toolkits to create versatile and adaptable platforms for control, enhance, and reprogram signaling, phenotype, or function in biological systems and living organisms. Advances in mammalian synthetic biology have generated growing interest in its…
items.abstract: Introduction Synthetic biology is an emerging field that integrates engineering principles, molecular innovations, interdisciplinary methodologies, and designer toolkits to create versatile and adaptable platforms for control, enhance, and reprogram signaling, phenotype, or function in biological systems and living organisms. Advances in mammalian synthetic biology have generated growing interest in its translational applications, including cardiovascular drug discovery and disease management. Areas covered This concise report highlights promising synthetic biology-inspired technologies that have been applied or can potentially apply to transgene regulation and disease management in cardiovascular medicine, such as tunable regulatory switches, programmable gene circuits, synthetic sensing modules, and gut-heart axis engineering. We also summarize recent translational progress in the field and discuss remaining obstacles, potential solutions, and future opportunities, with particular emphasis on the progression from laboratory concepts to practical applications in cardiovascular disease. Expert opinion Synthetic biology is steadily advancing toward translation. However, barriers for clinical implementation remain, including non‑mammalian components, immunogenicity, regulatory uncertainty, and broader ethical and safety concerns. Emerging solutions, including humanized molecular components, advanced monitoring strategies, and machine learning, may help mitigate those risks and expand the cardiovascular utility of synthetic biology. Stronger evidence and deeper clinical integration will position the field for future cardiovascular medicine.

items.abstract: Introduction Lipinski's Rule of Five (Ro5) has long framed the characteristics of orally administered drugs; however, many clinically relevant targets, particularly protein-protein interactions and other complex interfaces, require compounds operating in chemical space beyond this rule. Understanding how these drugs surpass classical thresholds while maintaining efficacy and pharmacokinetics is a fundamental aspect of modern drug discovery. Areas covered This narrative review is based on a literature using PubMed/Medline between 2016 and 2026. The DrugBank database was also used as an illustrative, retrospective case study to examine how literature-derived bRo5 principles are reflected in approved drugs. The review focuses on five key modalities: optimized small molecules, natural products, peptides/peptidomimetics, macrocycles, and proteolysis-targeting chimeras. Expert opinion Approved bRo5 drugs illustrate that the classic Ro5 should be reconsidered as a context-dependent guideline rather than a universal filter. In the authors' view, future discovery campaigns targeting complex biological targets should move away from rigid thresholds and adopt a deliberate bRo5 design, prioritizing control of hydrogen bonds, 3D shape, and chameleonicity over simple compliance scores. Integrating high-quality structural data with Artificial Intelligence-driven physics-based models may be particularly valuable for rationally expanding the bRo5 chemical space, reducing reliance on empirical trial-and-error, and addressing inaccessible targets to conventional small molecules.

items.summary: Meetings last up to an hour, and nobody knows in advance how many people will speak. Neural diarizers with a fixed number of output slots, such as Streaming Sortformer and Nemotron-3, are accurate and run online, but they cannot name more speakers than they have slots. items.abstract: Meetings last up to an hour, and nobody knows in advance how many people will speak. Neural diarizers with a fixed number of output slots, such as Streaming Sortformer and Nemotron-3, are accurate and run online, but they cannot name more speakers than they have slots. We remove this limit without retraining. The slot head keeps deciding who is active and when speech overlaps, and speaker embeddings are clustered inside a single slot, with the official e-means algorithm, only after every slot has been used. In the streaming system, re-clustering is confined to a bounded window, labels are revised for a few seconds, and identities are anchored to the slots of the head. The resulting system has no limit on the number of speakers and stays accurate when speakers outnumber the slots, where fixed-slot models break down. On meetings that grow to an hour it stays far more accurate than Streaming Sortformer, which accumulates errors, and its cost per update does not grow with the meeting. The same recipe turns the four-slot Streaming Sortformer into an open-speaker system. Across recordings, e-means makes it affordable to link the speakers of a large archive frame by frame, a task that arises when conversational corpora are prepared, and it reaches the clustering quality of Lloyd's k-means several times faster. The method needs little tuning, and e-means runs with its default recipe from a few hundred to more than a million embeddings.

items.title: JVT: Just Video Transformer makes pixel-space video diffusion simple
items.summary: Direct diffusion modeling of high-dimensional raw video data is challenging, and existing pixel-space methods often rely on specialized architectures. We introduce JVT (Just Video Transformer), a simple large-patch DiT-style Transformer for pixel-space video diffusion, without a pretrained autoencoder, auxiliary detailers, cascaded stages, or U-Net-style skip connections. We systematically examine video patch…
items.abstract: Direct diffusion modeling of high-dimensional raw video data is challenging, and existing pixel-space methods often rely on specialized architectures. We introduce JVT (Just Video Transformer), a simple large-patch DiT-style Transformer for pixel-space video diffusion, without a pretrained autoencoder, auxiliary detailers, cascaded stages, or U-Net-style skip connections. We systematically examine video patch embeddings, register tokens, and adaptive layer normalization to identify design choices that balance generation quality and computational efficiency. The resulting JVT design achieves generation quality competitive with latent diffusion baselines in both class-conditioned and unconditional settings. The pixel-space formulation of JVT also naturally supports joint generation of pixel-aligned modalities. We demonstrate this capability through camera-conditioned RGB-disparity generation, which improves camera following relative to RGB-only baselines and yields explicit scene geometry without an additional reconstruction model at inference. These results highlight the potential of simple DiT-style Transformers for pixel-space video diffusion, and we hope our findings offer useful insights and practical guidance for future research.

items.title: Aligning AI Teams
items.summary: Previous work has shown that alignment training on individual LLM agents can fail to transfer to multi-agent settings. We investigate the underlying mechanisms for this failure, and explore interventions to preserve alignment transfer to multi-agent LLM teams. We focus on two software-engineering tasks (sepsis triage, a news recommender) and ten consulting-proposal generation tasks. We present four findings: (1) The…
items.abstract: Previous work has shown that alignment training on individual LLM agents can fail to transfer to multi-agent settings. We investigate the underlying mechanisms for this failure, and explore interventions to preserve alignment transfer to multi-agent LLM teams. We focus on two software-engineering tasks (sepsis triage, a news recommender) and ten consulting-proposal generation tasks. We present four findings: (1) The single-vs-team safety gap does not show a clear trend with more capable models. We find that Anthropic's Mythos Preview shows the largest gap on one of our tasks but the smallest on another; (2) Many natural interventions, such as having agents critique each other's work or coordinate in a group chat, do not reliably bring agent teams back to single-agent alignment behavior; (3) diffusion of responsibility substantially accounts for the safety gap: agents in teams are less likely to proactively check for system-level safety failures and more likely to ignore, rationalize, or deflect responsibility for issues when they arise; (4) having a designated safety lead agent ensure system-level safety, and having a coordinator agent publish a safety specifications document are effective at restoring single-agent alignment. We also release magelab, a multi-agent LLM orchestration and experimentation framework. Our findings can help practitioners design agent teams that successfully preserve the behaviors expected of aligned individual agents.

items.title: Gamer: A Generalist Vision-Language-Action Foundation Model for Long-Horizon Real-Time Game Agent
items.summary: We introduce Gamer, a generalist agent framework built for long-horizon tasks in complex interactive environments. Its end-to-end architecture combines perception, memory management, and multi-step reasoning. A shared training and deployment pipeline supports interaction with both conventional 2D graphical interfaces and complex 3D simulated worlds. We first continue pre-training on a dataset constructed from tens…
items.abstract: We introduce Gamer, a generalist agent framework built for long-horizon tasks in complex interactive environments. Its end-to-end architecture combines perception, memory management, and multi-step reasoning. A shared training and deployment pipeline supports interaction with both conventional 2D graphical interfaces and complex 3D simulated worlds. We first continue pre-training on a dataset constructed from tens of thousands of hours of device-level keyboard and mouse interaction. These trajectories span simulated games and embodied environments, allowing the model to learn environmental dynamics across both physical and virtual domains. Sparse-thinking instruction tuning then substantially reduces redundant computation while preserving the reasoning needed for complex decisions. We train the policy for long-horizon interaction with a stable multi-turn reinforcement learning method that addresses finite context windows, accumulated rollout errors, and sparse rewards. For real-time interaction, a cloud-edge inference engine serves numerous simulated game environments concurrently, supports unbounded-context execution, and keeps online inference latency low. Across multiple challenging 3D open-world games, Gamer demonstrates solid generalization and operational efficiency comparable to skilled players. It also achieves competitive results on a range of conventional 2D game benchmarks. These results suggest that even repetitive keyboard and mouse trajectories can support substantial gains from scaling data and learning algorithms. Training on these trajectories helps Gamer learn complex skills more steadily in environments with both physical and digital properties. This approach offers a path toward generalist agents that can interact across digital and physical worlds.

items.title: CANTraj: Recovering Vehicle Trajectories from CAN Signals in Naturalistic Driving
items.summary: Open driving releases and usage-based insurance programs often claim to prevent privacy breaches by omitting GPS records when sharing or collecting vehicle data. However, removing GPS coordinates from driving logs does not erase the location information carried by vehicle signals. While prior route-inference attacks have demonstrated that speed, steering, and driving events can be matched to road networks to…
items.abstract: Open driving releases and usage-based insurance programs often claim to prevent privacy breaches by omitting GPS records when sharing or collecting vehicle data. However, removing GPS coordinates from driving logs does not erase the location information carried by vehicle signals. While prior route-inference attacks have demonstrated that speed, steering, and driving events can be matched to road networks to reconstruct trajectories, existing studies rely on inconsistent prior assumptions and evaluation metrics and are tested only on small, restricted datasets, making their results difficult to compare and their real-world effectiveness uncertain. We release CANTraj, a naturalistic driving dataset pairing decoded CAN events with time-aligned GNSS trajectories (3,940 drives, 454 drivers), and CANTraj-Bench for evaluating trajectory recovery (3,675 drives, 431 drivers, 1,380 hours, 85,919 km). On 776 evaluation drives from 94 unseen drivers, we compare six re-implemented attacks and benchmark baselines under explicit information-access protocols, paired comparisons, and metrics incorporating failures. Experiments show that combining steering signals with road-network constraints yields the largest gain: With a known start and heading, adding steering to speed raises the online map filter's five-minute route recovery from 56% to 87%, with a median average displacement error of 43 m versus 921 m for map-free dead reckoning. Offline beam search recovers 88% of test routes with the heading and 81% without it. Because methods fail on different windows, we also evaluate an LLM harness that selects among candidate routes on 659 five-minute windows; its best configuration recovers 79% of routes on test and 83% on few-shot, outperforming the best baseline on test and matching it on few-shot. Data and code at huggingface.co/datasets/HenryYHW/CANTraj and github.com/WangYuHang-cmd/GPS--CAN.

items.title: MEM-SQL: Memory-Empowered Text-to-SQL
items.summary: Text-to-SQL systems translate natural language questions into SQL queries over increasingly complex databases. However, widely used benchmarks evaluate questions independently, overlooking settings where earlier queries over the same database can supply joins or calculations for a new question. We introduce HARE (History-AwaRe Text-to-SQL BEnchmark) to measure the accuracy and cost of adapting historical SQL. HARE…
items.abstract: Text-to-SQL systems translate natural language questions into SQL queries over increasingly complex databases. However, widely used benchmarks evaluate questions independently, overlooking settings where earlier queries over the same database can supply joins or calculations for a new question. We introduce HARE (History-AwaRe Text-to-SQL BEnchmark) to measure the accuracy and cost of adapting historical SQL. HARE comprises 1,600 requests derived from a fixed pool of 823 verified queries across four datasets. Annotations record which components each request preserves and which edits it requires, distinguishing whole-query adaptation from partial reuse. Our method, MEM-SQL (Memory-EMpowered Text-to-SQL), stores whole-query templates, reusable SQL blocks, and mappings from domain concepts to schema elements. MEM-SQL uses a layer only if every requirement assigned to it has a match above that layer's threshold. With On-demand Schema Linking (OSL), MEM-SQL consults the schema only when no layer qualifies or the generator judges retrieved evidence insufficient. Across six language models on HARE, mean execution accuracy rises from 37.1% for Direct Generation without history to 50.0% for MEM-SQL, with 76.6% fewer input tokens and 68.8% lower latency on average. Further analysis shows that requests reusing several verified queries remain a bottleneck, with accuracy falling from 56.7% to 29.7%, most sharply when reused components must be placed in a new query structure or combined with a shared join. Applying OSL to three other memory designs consistently reduces generation cost, while its accuracy benefit depends on the memory design. Verified history can thus make generation both more accurate and cheaper, but its value depends on the evidence retained and when the system consults the schema.

items.title: AI Reviews Are Biased Towards the Appendix
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used by reviewers to highlight weaknesses during the reviewing process, and their outputs often shape the reviews that humans submit. Prior work studies how LLM reviews align with human ones, yet we know little about which parts of a paper these models actually criticize. In this work, we investigate 2,000 papers from ACL, EMNLP, COLM, and ICLR, and show that the latest…
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used by reviewers to highlight weaknesses during the reviewing process, and their outputs often shape the reviews that humans submit. Prior work studies how LLM reviews align with human ones, yet we know little about which parts of a paper these models actually criticize. In this work, we investigate 2,000 papers from ACL, EMNLP, COLM, and ICLR, and show that the latest GPT and Claude models draw about 50% or more of their review weaknesses from the appendix. This behavior holds across the API, coding-agent, and web access methods for using LLMs to review a paper. In contrast, we find that humans draw only 8.4% of their weaknesses from the appendix, and these weaknesses primarily revolve around a paper's presentation and content related to its core idea. Meanwhile, LLMs draw weaknesses from deep in the appendix that concern fine-grained technical details not central to the paper's contributions. We anticipate that our analysis will contribute to the scholarly discourse on AI reviews. Our code is publicly available at: https://github.com/cincynlp/review_appendix.

items.title: Envisioning Agentic Robotics: A New Era of Robotic Systems
items.summary: The release of GPT-6 Astra marks the emergence of a new paradigm in robotics: agentic robotics. Within weeks, frontier models with agentic harnesses matched or exceeded task-specific policies on many embodied benchmarks. Instead of training a dedicated policy for each family of tasks, an agentic robotic system applies a foundation model to open-world embodied tasks. It operates in a closed loop: observing the…
items.abstract: The release of GPT-6 Astra marks the emergence of a new paradigm in robotics: agentic robotics. Within weeks, frontier models with agentic harnesses matched or exceeded task-specific policies on many embodied benchmarks. Instead of training a dedicated policy for each family of tasks, an agentic robotic system applies a foundation model to open-world embodied tasks. It operates in a closed loop: observing the environment, interpreting user intent, reasoning about the task, invoking skills and tools, verifying outcomes, and adapting its strategy. Despite these advances, the community has yet to converge on a shared definition, a reliable evaluation framework, or a research roadmap. We argue that Embodied System 2, realized by a foundation model together with an embodied harness, forms the decision-making core of agentic robotics. Its central challenge is to translate general-purpose reasoning into effective and verifiable actions under physical constraints such as limited reaction time, mechanical limits, unpredictable environment changes, and irreversible consequences. Motivated by this perspective, we propose an evaluation framework that measures both model capabilities and closed-loop system performance. Furthermore, we identify the principles that carry over from digital to physical agents and the challenges that must be addressed to achieve reliable physical autonomy. On top of the Embodied System 2 and the evaluation framework, we envision a research roadmap toward sustained autonomy: the ability to perform work safely and reliably with progressively broader responsibility, from executing individual primitives to fulfilling standing roles.

items.title: PaperCritic: Training AI Reviewers to Assess the Soundness of Papers
items.summary: As AI conference submissions grow rapidly, AI reviewers are being considered as an alternative. However, simply imitating human reviewing is problematic because reviewing serves multiple purposes, including evaluating papers' soundness, interestingness, and clarity, the last two of which are subjective. In this work, we focus solely on evaluating soundness, the most important and objective criterion, and define the…
items.abstract: As AI conference submissions grow rapidly, AI reviewers are being considered as an alternative. However, simply imitating human reviewing is problematic because reviewing serves multiple purposes, including evaluating papers' soundness, interestingness, and clarity, the last two of which are subjective. In this work, we focus solely on evaluating soundness, the most important and objective criterion, and define the learning objective as jointly maximizing (1) precision, based on the soundness and substantiveness of review points, and (2) recall, the coverage of high-quality reference review points. Under this problem formulation, we construct a quality-labeled review point dataset, PaperSound-23K, using 1K ICLR submissions and 23K human-written and LLM-generated review points. Using this dataset, we train an AI reviewer model, PaperCritic, through reinforcement learning with the F1 score of precision and recall as the reward. Our experiments show that PaperCritic outperforms frontier models and models trained with other AI reviewer training methods on an in-domain test set. Surprisingly, learning to review ICLR submissions also transfers to reviewing Nature-family papers and even to out-of-domain reviewing tasks (e.g., code review, legal contract review, and feedback on story writing).

items.title: Restoring Diversity in Distilled Image and Video Generators by Probing Activations
items.summary: Distilling diffusion models into few-step student models substantially reduces sampling latency, but induces severe diversity collapse: samples generated from different random seeds show minimal variation. In this work, we investigate the root cause of this failure by probing the internal representations of student models relative to their teachers. We find that distilled students maintain total activation variance…
items.abstract: Distilling diffusion models into few-step student models substantially reduces sampling latency, but induces severe diversity collapse: samples generated from different random seeds show minimal variation. In this work, we investigate the root cause of this failure by probing the internal representations of student models relative to their teachers. We find that distilled students maintain total activation variance comparable to their teachers, but concentrate it into substantially fewer directions. This directional collapse is localized to an identifiable intermediate block at the initial denoising step. Consequently, diversity collapse stems from a misallocation of activation variance rather than an inherent loss of generative capacity. Guided by this finding, we propose ReDiverse to reinstate the missing variance directions. At training time, ReDiverse-FT fine-tunes a lightweight adapter that regresses student activations onto the teacher's, reviving the teacher's feature variance characteristic. At inference time, ReDiverse-TF introduces a training-free mechanism that steers activations along precomputed teacher principal directions. Across image and video distillation benchmarks, ReDiverse consistently restores sample diversity while preserving generation quality, further supported by the user study.

items.title: LuthorSQL: A One-Pass Text-to-SQL Model as System 1 for a Slower LLM Agent
items.summary: Frontier LLM agents that query databases with tools are among the most accurate text-to-SQL systems, but per-query calls to a hosted model are slow, costly, and expose sensitive organizational queries to external APIs. For example, a Claude Opus 5.5 agent serving 10,000 queries a day costs over $70,000 a year at list price. To what extent can local hardware already owned by an organization offload this burden…
items.abstract: Frontier LLM agents that query databases with tools are among the most accurate text-to-SQL systems, but per-query calls to a hosted model are slow, costly, and expose sensitive organizational queries to external APIs. For example, a Claude Opus 5.5 agent serving 10,000 queries a day costs over $70,000 a year at list price. To what extent can local hardware already owned by an organization offload this burden without compromising the agent's accuracy? We present LuthorSQL, a non-autoregressive 7B text-to-SQL model that serves as a rapid System 1 gate for a slower LLM agent (System 2), escalating queries only when uncertain. LuthorSQL makes a single forward pass to predict slot scores over a bounded grammar for query plans, compiles and runs up to 32 candidate plans, and chooses an answer using a trained validator. On its own, LuthorSQL reaches 68.03% execution accuracy on BIRD's hidden test set at 0.84 s per question on a single GPU, maintains its accuracy in 9 GB with 8-bit quantized weights, and transfers zero-shot to Snowflake, BigQuery, MySQL, PostgreSQL, and DuckDB within 3.1 points of its native SQLite accuracy. Combined with Claude Opus 5.5 in a pre-registered confidence cascade over 227 questions on databases published after Opus's training cutoff, LuthorSQL answers nearly half of all questions locally and cuts API cost by 33.3% at the same accuracy. Finally, contamination probing shows that Opus reproduces 48-92% of public benchmark gold queries verbatim without seeing the schema; however, its tool-assisted accuracy holds on renamed schemas and reaches 95.6-97.4% on post-cutoff databases. Code and data: https://github.com/IAMIbrahimmemon/luthorsql

items.title: OneSteer: Unlocking Steerable General Humanoid Motion Tracking via One-Step Diffusion Whole-Body Control
items.summary: Deployment objectives often specify desired outcomes without providing revised trajectories, while parts of the original reference must still be followed. We present OneSteer, a one-step diffusion whole-body controller that combines general motion tracking with selective test-time steering. To accommodate new objectives, differentiable task costs guide optimization of the generator's input noise with frozen weights,…
items.abstract: Deployment objectives often specify desired outcomes without providing revised trajectories, while parts of the original reference must still be followed. We present OneSteer, a one-step diffusion whole-body controller that combines general motion tracking with selective test-time steering. To accommodate new objectives, differentiable task costs guide optimization of the generator's input noise with frozen weights, while body-group reference masks relax selected tracking requirements. Predicted state-action plans provide a shared interface for task optimization and feedback-conditioned execution. For nominal tracking, the model trained from scratch achieves the lowest local tracking error among the evaluated baselines on successful held-out AMASS and BONES clips. For steering, one frozen distilled controller adapts across diverse deployment objectives in simulation, raising the clean passage rate under a 1.25 m bar from 2% to 90%. On a physical Unitree G1, OneSteer completes all 27 nominal tracking trials across nine diverse whole-body motion sequences without falling. With a steering cost derived from a signed distance field built using only onboard LiDAR, it also passes under a 1.1 m low bar in four of five attempts and steps over a 12 cm hurdle without falling in all three attempts. Beyond control, prediction variation in the model trained from scratch ranks likely tracking failures without physics rollouts. This scoring method is more than 10x faster than simulation-based scoring with five rollouts per clip and guides targeted fine-tuning. Project page: https://onesteer.github.io

items.title: DySENSE: Dynamic Spatiotemporal ENergy Synthesis and Emulation with Satellite Imagery
items.summary: Cities account for over two-thirds of the world's energy and more than 70% of global carbon dioxide emissions. City energy is essential for achieving the 2050 net-zero target and the UN's Sustainable Development Goals 7 and 11. Although existing studies have made progress, they are limited by data and methodological gaps. Existing studies are largely predictive for existing cities rather than generative for future…
items.abstract: Cities account for over two-thirds of the world's energy and more than 70% of global carbon dioxide emissions. City energy is essential for achieving the 2050 net-zero target and the UN's Sustainable Development Goals 7 and 11. Although existing studies have made progress, they are limited by data and methodological gaps. Existing studies are largely predictive for existing cities rather than generative for future cities; fine-grained, aligned monthly dynamic energy data are scarce; and existing GenAI models struggle to generate dynamic urban functional monthly energy. We present DySENSE, a joint multimodal GenAI framework that synthesizes static urban satellite imagery together with spatially aligned, dynamic monthly building energy consumption maps. We decouple long-term static urban morphology from short-term dynamic energy consumption. By conditioning on static urban land use, DySENSE can generate realistic, diverse and new static urban imagery with aligned energy maps. By conditioning on dynamic monthly and climate prompts, DySENSE can jointly generate dynamic, monthly energy consumption maps while keeping the urban morphology static. Experiments across four cities (New York, Washington, Norfolk, Busan) demonstrated that DySENSE can generate annotated high-fidelity synthetic energy data using less than 25% labelled data, boosting downstream prediction performance by 8% mIoU, and achieving strong energy dynamic consistency. Compared to existing methods, DySENSE significantly improved prediction performance (8.7% accuracy) and reduced prediction error (9%-18% CVRMSE, ASHRAE). DySENSE offers an effective foundation for energy-efficient cities, peak-load analysis, building performance simulation and dynamic demand response for city, energy, and building science. The data and code: https://huggingface.co/datasets/skl24/MUSE2 and https://github.com/kailaisun/DySENSE

items.title: WebArena-Pro: A Heterogeneous, Multimodal, Reproducible Benchmark for Web Agents
items.summary: Web agents powered by large language and vision-language models are increasingly applied to realistic browser work that spans heterogeneous applications, multimodal content, and stateful workflows. However, existing reproducible web-agent benchmarks cover only a small number of web applications drawn from a few software categories, and restrict modality to text and vision. Live benchmarks broaden site coverage but…
items.abstract: Web agents powered by large language and vision-language models are increasingly applied to realistic browser work that spans heterogeneous applications, multimodal content, and stateful workflows. However, existing reproducible web-agent benchmarks cover only a small number of web applications drawn from a few software categories, and restrict modality to text and vision. Live benchmarks broaden site coverage but sacrifice reproducibility, since pages and data drift between runs. Moreover, existing benchmarks do not meaningfully evaluate whether agents can understand and use audio and video content embedded within web tasks. To address these gaps, we introduce WebArena-Pro, a benchmark comprising 300 tasks across 20 self-hosted web applications in six domain categories, spanning distinct interface conventions, workflows, and data models. Across the evaluated agents, the best performance is achieved by both Codex with GPT 6.1 Sol and Claude Code with Claude Opus 5.5 at 62.3%, followed by OpenCode with Kimi 3.1 Pro at 60.7%. The strongest GenericAgent configurations, Gemini 3.1 Pro omni and Gemma4 31B, both achieve 30.3%. Among reproducible, human-curated web agent benchmarks, WebArena-Pro provides the broadest application coverage and the most comprehensive multimodal support to date. The benchmark treats audio and video as core observations alongside text and vision, with dedicated actions for extracting information from each. WebArena-Pro runs each task in isolation and supports reproducible, parallel evaluation. Tasks are authored through a dedicated annotator interface, filtered by LLM-assisted triage, and finally validated by humans before release. Project page: https://webarena-pro.github.io

items.title: G-CAST: Governed Continual Self-Training for E-Commerce Agents under Evolving Demands
items.summary: With the rapid advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs), an increasing number of users are turning to LLM-powered agents for conversational shopping in e-commerce. However, the user needs continue to change as new product categories, procurement scenarios, and feature requests emerge. items.abstract: With the rapid advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs), an increasing number of users are turning to LLM-powered agents for conversational shopping in e-commerce. However, the user needs continue to change as new product categories, procurement scenarios, and feature requests emerge. At the same time, the product's execution harness-including its tools, skills, and operating procedures-continues to evolve to support increasingly sophisticated interactions. These changes create two practical challenges: 1) Demand drift alters the distribution, intent, and complexity of user requests, causing a model trained once to fall behind; 2) Harness evolution requires the model to use newly introduced capabilities correctly without losing behavior that users already rely on. Periodic manual retraining is too delayed and labor-intensive for this setting. To address these challenges, we present G-CAST, a governed continual self-training system that converts daily production evidence under evolving demand and capability contracts into reward-routed, entropy-prioritized training data and governed reward evolution. Governed checkpoint transition under cumulative evaluation controls each model update, enabling the agent to learn newly introduced behaviors without sacrificing previously accepted capabilities. Experiments on a real production e-commerce agent show that G-CAST achieves stronger adaptation to newly introduced demand while better preserving previously accepted behavior compared with a strong autonomous post-training baseline. Ablations further show that both reward-routed, entropy-prioritized data orchestration and governed reward evolution are important to these gains. G-CAST is now deployed in Yuancai(http://cai.1688.com/), a B2B procurement agent on Alibaba's 1688 platform.

items.abstract: World-model video encoders such as V-JEPA learn how scenes change (direction, speed, order, state) from video alone. To answer questions, they are joined to a language model trained on captions and question-answer pairs. But each caption or question names only a few attributes of a clip, so the model learns to retrieve those attributes rather than to read the clip, and the dynamics the encoder carries go unused: on the same items, a linear probe reads speed from frozen V-JEPA features at 87% while the VLM answers at chance. We show where dynamics lives in a frozen encoder: in a subspace shared across videos for predictive encoders such as V-JEPA, but not as a shared component of frame-wise, text-aligned encoders such as SigLIP. We then build counterfactual supervision that makes the language model read it: pixel transformations turn public videos into answer-balanced variants whose answers are set by the transformation and differ only in the change. Trained in a single stage on 4.53M public samples with 32 visual tokens per frame, where open video LLMs use several stages, 9M to 172M samples and 64 to 256 tokens per frame on average, the resulting V-JEPA-LM models (1B to 8B, Qwen3 and Llama) lead every size class in average score across eleven video benchmarks; our 4B model scores 72.1, against 61.1 for the best open 4B and 64.8 for the best open 8B model. A controlled encoder x supervision study shows that the encoder decides what can be read and the supervision what is read: at a matched budget, counterfactual supervision adds 4.5 points on average and 38 on the speed questions of natural benchmarks. Code and models: https://github.com/kkt94/Llama-V-JEPA-LM.

items.title: Do Underwater Image Quality Metrics Agree with Human Perception? A Benchmark with Human Choices, Simple Edits and Generative Drift
items.summary: Underwater image enhancement is challenging to evaluate due to the lack of clean reference images, so researchers rely on no-reference image quality assessment (NR-IQA) metrics. items.abstract: Underwater image enhancement is challenging to evaluate due to the lack of clean reference images, so researchers rely on no-reference image quality assessment (NR-IQA) metrics. However, it remains unclear whether these metrics agree with human judgments. We evaluate 73 handcrafted underwater, learned underwater, vision-language and general-purpose metrics against human preferences on five references: four published opinion-score sets and a new paired-comparison study. For each metric, we measure how often it selects the same image as people when comparing versions of the same scene. We further test whether simple image edits and small adversarial perturbations raise metric scores above the enhancement people preferred, and whether scores decrease as repeated generative edits add noise. Our results show that no metric consistently matches human preferences. The best worst-case Cohen's kappa over the five references is only 0.23 (Q-Align), while two raters in our study agree with a median kappa of 0.41. The widely used UCIQE often favors edits that people reject. On a Nano Banana Pro replica chain that should leave the image unchanged, only 22 of 73 scores decrease at every checkpoint, while noise grows by 2.5 times. We also introduce TrustUIQA, a benchmark that combines the human references, our study choices, the edited, attacked and generated images, and the scores of every metric on every image. The code is available at https://github.com/TrustUIQA/TrustUIQA and TrustUIQA at https://huggingface.co/datasets/TrustUIQA/TrustUIQA.
